# SPEC-065: Durable and Secure Public Chat Processing

**Status:** Specification complete; approved for implementation (launch evidence pending)
**Owner:** Wesley Hansen
**Created:** 2026-07-22
**Related:** SPEC-061, CRM ecosystem E2E launch-prep review

## TLDR

**Key points:**

- Replace the unsafe reply claim stored inside `chat_messages` with tenant-scoped sidecar state and a durable, idempotent worker contract.
- Commit exactly one ordered reply job with each accepted visitor message. Database state is authoritative; bounded queue/scheduler deliveries are wake-ups, never completion evidence.
- Keep anonymous visitor identity unverified. A claimed email never links a public visitor to an existing CRM contact and never unlocks private contact context for an AI prompt.
- New and bootstrapped public sessions store only a SHA-256 digest of the high-entropy visitor possession token. The unmanaged legacy column stores a non-secret `noli-sidecar-v1:<random>` rollback-fence marker, never the raw new token or `NULL`; the bounded `0.5.x` bridge may verify pre-existing plaintext and replaces it with that marker when bootstrap succeeds. Request-time DDL is removed, typing uses the same possession proof, and tokenless legacy conversations fail closed to public callers.
- Serialize provider work per conversation, persist results before metering/publication, and never automatically replay a provider call whose outcome may be ambiguous.

**Scope:**

- Public chat POST/GET and visitor typing contracts.
- Public widget and hosted-page injection/routing hardening.
- Durable per-scope cutover gate, global public-routing locator, tenant-scoped session, visible-message-order, and reply-job entities, generated migrations, snapshot reconciliation, queue worker, recovery schedule, and exact cleanup.
- Exact Customer Service chat result/proposal handling and public-chat-specific allowance ambiguity handling.
- Focused unit, queue, real-Postgres concurrency/recovery, and browser/API regression proof.

**Boundaries:**

- This patch does not migrate or rewrite the unmanaged legacy `chat_widgets`, `chat_conversations`, or `chat_messages` schemas. Greenfield test environments use a clearly test-only legacy-chat fixture.
- This patch does not invent an authenticated user for an anonymous visitor or create a falsely user-bound external GDPR grant.
- This patch does not make ecosystem-wide metering strict. Metering remains intentionally fail-open, but an attempt is awaited and never automatically repeated.
- This patch does not deploy, apply migrations, contact a paid provider, or alter production data as part of verification.

**Concerns:**

- Current customer snapshots omit already-shipped Customer Service entities. Snapshot reconciliation must be separated from the sidecar migration so generated SQL contains no duplicate or unrelated schema churn.
- The GDPR writer trigger is installed by the auth migration only on tables that exist at that moment. The migration runner needs one idempotent unconditional end-of-`dbMigrate` reconciliation after every ordered module pass before the new sidecars can ship.

## Resolved Product Decision

- **Q1 — resolved 2026-07-22:** Every embeddable widget requires an explicit allowed-origin list. The Noli-hosted page's canonical application origin is always allowed. Arbitrary-domain embedding is not supported.
- Existing widgets with no configured origins become hosted-page-only until an administrator adds origins. This is an intentional fail-closed security correction; there is no wildcard compatibility bridge.
- Allowed origins live in the existing widget `config.allowedOrigins` JSON property, avoiding new DDL on the unmanaged legacy widget table. Authenticated create/update routes accept at most 25 unique normalized HTTPS origins; loopback HTTP is accepted only outside production. Userinfo, paths other than `/`, query, fragment, wildcard hosts, opaque/`null` origins, and non-HTTP(S) schemes are rejected.
- Every actual public POST, poll, and visitor-typing request resolves the exact widget and compares the browser `Origin` to the normalized list or canonical hosted-page origin. Successful CORS responses echo only that exact origin and include `Vary: Origin`; wildcard CORS is removed. OPTIONS may validate and echo a syntactically safe origin because it has no body/conversation identity, but authorization is performed again on the actual request.
- A script copied to an unlisted browser origin can render but cannot start, read, append, or mutate a conversation. Non-browser clients can forge `Origin`, so database-backed per-widget and per-organization provider budgets remain mandatory. CAPTCHA remains optional abuse friction and is not a correctness boundary.

## Overview

The public chat surface accepts untrusted, anonymous traffic but currently combines request handling, transcript storage, model orchestration, Customer Service side effects, and retry state in one route. The launch-safe design separates those responsibilities. The route validates and commits local state; the queue wakes an idempotent worker; sidecar rows record exact phase and identity; the worker performs at most one provider attempt and publishes an exact deterministic result.

The target audience is a website visitor who expects a prompt, private response and a CRM operator who needs reliable transcripts, handoff, metering, and deletion behavior. The principal value is not higher throughput. It is a provable contract under duplicate delivery, delayed writers, worker crashes, provider ambiguity, tenant mismatch, GDPR erasure, and hostile browser input.

> **Market reference:** PostgreSQL row locks and `SKIP LOCKED` are the source-of-truth concurrency primitives; PostgreSQL documents `SKIP LOCKED` as suitable for queue-like tables and `clock_timestamp()` as actual advancing database time. BullMQ documents that stalled jobs can be returned to waiting and therefore handlers must be idempotent. Its retry and deduplication options are not exposed by the repository's current queue abstraction, so this design deliberately rejects Redis/BullMQ job state as the correctness boundary. References: <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-select.html>, <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-datetime.html>, <https://docs.bullmq.io/guide/jobs/stalled>, and <https://docs.bullmq.io/patterns/idempotent-jobs>.

## Problem Statement

The checkpoint commit `56056348232801b56ceb4396f1d08b125a7afe2a` is intentionally unsafe and must not ship. Its public-chat draft:

1. Stores a reply claim as `sender_type='__noli_bot_reply_claim__'` inside `chat_messages`. Authenticated transcript readers, list previews, counts, notifications, summaries, and downstream consumers can expose or ingest that operational row.
2. Uses Next.js `after()` as the only scheduler. A terminated request process can strand work.
3. Deletes a claim after a wall-clock TTL even though the provider request has no matching hard completion boundary. A delayed first worker and replacement worker can both spend and reply.
4. Processes only the newest inbound message and drains a bounded list. Rapid messages can be coalesced, reordered, or stranded.
5. Orders equal timestamps by random UUID, which is deterministic only by accident and does not represent admission order.
6. Lets Customer Service publish a random reply, scans for the newest bot row, copies it into the claim, and deletes the source. A concurrent bot writer can be mistaken for the result and deleted.
7. Infers handoff from `[HANDOFF]` in transcript text and then strips the marker, so later work cannot reliably observe the handoff state.
8. Runs `ALTER TABLE` from anonymous GET/POST requests and accepts tokenless legacy conversations.

The antagonistic surface review also found independent launch blockers:

- An anonymous visitor-provided email is treated as verified identity. The route can reuse a real contact and the drafter can inject that contact's email, phone, and lifecycle state into a response for an impersonator.
- `/chat/typing` lets anonymous callers mutate any conversation and select the agent typing fields without possession proof.
- The embeddable script interpolates tenant-controlled greeting text into `innerHTML`, enabling stored XSS in every embedding site's origin.
- Hosted pages look up a globally ambiguous slug, ignore `public_page_enabled`, and can route a visitor and their PII to the wrong organization.
- Public GET sends the possession token in the query string, increasing exposure through access logs and browser history.
- The repository's greenfield migrations do not create the three legacy chat tables even though routes assume them and additional drifted columns.

## Proposed Solution

### Design Decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| One durable job per inbound message | Preserves ordered semantics and makes rapid messages independently observable instead of silently coalescing them. |
| Job and visible-message ordinals allocated by a locked session-row update | Defines provider and transcript order independently of timestamps, UUID order, or queue arrival. |
| Sidecar state only | Operational UUIDs and phases never enter transcripts or transcript-derived consumers. |
| Database state is authoritative | Queue duplicates, losses, local JSON limitations, and BullMQ stalled replays cannot alter correctness. |
| One provider-start transition, no automatic replay after it | Paid provider APIs do not provide the end-to-end idempotency receipt required to prove a retry is safe. |
| Persist result before metering and publication | A crash after generation resumes from stored output without a second provider call. |
| Mark metering attempted before the call | Preserves intentional fail-open metering while preventing duplicate charges after an ambiguous metering outcome. |
| Deterministic reply and CS proposal identities | Publication can use insert-or-verify semantics and never scan/delete a "latest" row. |
| Hashed possession token; header preferred | Raw secrets are returned/accepted but not stored, and new GET requests keep them out of URLs. |
| Anonymous email remains unverified metadata | Knowledge of an email address is not authentication and cannot unlock a contact record or prompt context. |
| Reply job as organization-only external-processing grant, no fake user | The exact nonterminal job plus its organization writer fence survives worker death and blocks erasure without forging user attribution or calling the user-bound external-grant API. |
| Collision-fail-closed hosted slugs | Preserves the stable route while preventing cross-tenant routing; new/updated slugs are globally unique. |
| Explicit per-widget allowed origins | Prevents a copied widget ID from operating on an unrelated browser origin while retaining the Noli-hosted page. |
| Minimal global public-routing directory | Public widget IDs, slugs, and conversation IDs cannot supply trusted tenant scope themselves; a purpose-built global directory resolves only public coordinates before every tenant-table query applies exact organization and tenant predicates. |
| End-of-migration-run GDPR trigger reconciliation | Entity decorators cannot emit the required trigger and module order creates tables after auth migrations. |

### Alternatives Considered

| Alternative | Why rejected |
|---|---|
| Keep claim rows in `chat_messages` and filter every reader | Every present and future consumer would need a perfect denylist; one missed reader exposes state or corrupts behavior. |
| Use BullMQ job ID/deduplication as truth | The repository abstraction generates queue IDs, removes completed jobs, configures no attempts/backoff, and local mode has different semantics. |
| Expire provider claims and retry | A timeout or crash does not prove the provider did not process the request. |
| Reply once to the newest rapid-message batch | Changes product semantics and can discard an earlier visitor question. |
| Link public visitors by claimed email | Enables impersonation, private prompt context disclosure, and contamination of a real contact's history. |
| Add FKs to legacy chat tables | Those tables are absent from greenfield migrations, so the sidecar migration would fail on a clean database. |
| Add or restore DDL in `setup-tables.sql` | Explicitly forbidden; the file is deprecated and not a source of truth. |
| Hand-write the sidecar migration | Violates repository migration rules and leaves snapshots divergent. |
| Change `/chat/page/[slug]` in one release | Route URLs are stable contract surfaces. Collision-fail-closed behavior and global uniqueness harden the existing path without removal. |

## User Stories / Use Cases

- **Website visitor** wants each submitted message accepted once and answered in order, even if the browser retries or a worker restarts.
- **Website visitor** wants a conversation UUID to be insufficient to read, append to, or mutate typing state.
- **Existing customer** wants knowledge of their email address not to let another visitor obtain or influence their CRM data.
- **CRM operator** wants public-chat replies, flagged proposals, handoff, previews, counts, and transcripts to stay exact under concurrency.
- **Operator** wants an ambiguous provider attempt visible for reconciliation and never silently replayed.
- **Privacy operator** wants deletion fences to cover every new table and active/ambiguous work to block erasure until safely resolved.
- **Embedding-site owner** wants tenant-configured chat text rendered as text, never executable HTML.

## Architecture

### Components

1. **Public route** validates a discriminated zod body, resolves a public locator, authenticates possession where applicable, and invokes the public-chat data service.
2. **Public-routing locator** is an explicitly global security directory keyed only by a versioned digest of a public widget ID, normalized slug, or conversation ID. It stores no transcript, token, contact, tenant configuration, or other private data; it returns the exact organization/tenant/resource coordinates needed for the next query. A locator lookup is the only intentionally global public-identifier query. Every subsequent query touches tenant data and therefore includes both returned scope predicates.
3. **Public-chat data service** owns raw cross-table SQL inside the customers module data layer. It verifies locator coordinates against the exact scoped resource and fails closed on absence, collision, drift, or duplicate directory rows.
4. **Session sidecar** stores the token digest, immutable Noli organization binding, job sequence, visible-message ordinal, and explicit bot/handoff state.
5. **Message-order sidecar** maps every newly written public or authenticated chat message to one exact scoped conversation ordinal without altering the unmanaged legacy transcript table.
6. **Reply-job sidecar** stores exact identities, immutable Noli organization binding, phase fence, provider result, metering/publication markers, and bounded CS metadata.
7. **Quota-event ledger** stores only exact scope/resource/source IDs, kind, and database time for session/message/provider admissions. It survives ordinary widget/conversation/link cleanup through the rolling window so delete/recreate cannot reset spend/storage limits; it contains no token, identity, transcript, prompt, result, address, or provider secret.
8. **Queue adapter** creates at most one exact post-admission direct-job nudge on `customers-public-chat-replies`, and only for the first acceptance of an active-session processable job. A handed-off admission is born atomically `completed`/`completed_at` with sequence-resolved `no_reply`, no external/execution/dispatch/notification fields, and no dispatch binding/nudge; it exact-verifies but creates no scheduler-desiring source when it is the only would-be work. An exact duplicate retry returns the original acceptance without creating a new dispatch epoch after its original binding settled. The one environment-global recovery pager selects at most one DB-registered organization scope per minute and emits one exact bound sweep; polling, worker completion, deletion, response-loss retry, and sweep yielding never create ad-hoc follow-on nudges.
9. **Customers worker** validates and normalizes direct and pager-bound payloads, then calls the reply processor. One `customers-public-chat-replies` worker retains effective concurrency five but uses five non-borrowable pre-authority slots: four accept only validated bound sweeps and one accepts only validated direct-job nudges. Each invocation processes provider phases sequentially—never `Promise.all` over sweep candidates—so total in-process provider-call concurrency remains five. Short database row locks provide per-conversation transitions.
10. **Recovery authority** has exactly one canonical environment pager, not one BullMQ Job Scheduler per organization. Its strict `ScheduledJob` ID is UUIDv5 under RFC URL namespace `6ba7b811-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8` with exact UTF-8 name `noli:public-chat-recovery-pager:v1:<environmentId>`; it is system-scoped, has null organization/tenant/Noli coordinates, owner `customers.public-chat-recovery-pager.v1`, runs every one minute UTC, and materializes only the static environment pager envelope on `customers-public-chat-sweeps`. Each scheduler-desiring organization instead owns one DB-only strict scope registration with deterministic name `noli:public-chat-recovery-scope:v1:<organizationId>:<tenantId>`, owner `customers.public-chat-recovery-scope.v1`, exact Noli/tenant/organization coordinates, and lifecycle/fairness state. A scope registration never installs a repeatable or Job Scheduler and never carries a next-materialized-execution pair. The first durable desired source atomically reserves a generation-fenced population child and creates/verifies its scope registration; a customers-owned provider returns the classified desired/strict/quota population union from durable sessions, nonterminal jobs, pending lifecycle markers, widget delete intents, erasure operations, existing registrations, and retained population children. Target selection is narrower than registration recovery: only a fresh desired-active member with `strict_lifecycle='active'` is pager-target-eligible. A desired-active or retiring member, or a child with `strict_required=true`, may authorize exact scope-registration creation/repair, but retiring authority may create/repair only a `retiring` row for transport cleanup/finalization and can never create a target. A quota-only or unreleased-processable-only child is inventory/capacity state and never recreates a retired registration or enters the pager candidate view. The independent authority repairs the singleton pager plus any missing/drifted eligible scope registration without visitor traffic. Durable `retiring` and quota-residue population state prevent premature slot reuse while exact scope cleanup/finalization completes.
11. **Reply processor** resolves the exact immutable organization allowance binding, uses the scoped reply-job row as its durable organization-only external-processing grant, performs transitions using database time, invokes at most one provider sequence, persists the result, attempts metering once, and publishes exactly. It never creates a synthetic user or calls the authenticated-user-only `CustomersAiProcessorScope.createExternalGrant` path.
12. **End-of-run fence hook** reattaches the existing GDPR organization/user guard triggers, the locator's custom target-organization guard, and the sidecar-aware legacy-message writer guard once after the complete ordered module migration loop, including runs with no pending migration, and is verified on a fresh schema.

### Message Admission Sequence

1. Parse and bound widget ID, conversation ID, message ID, token, name, email, and message.
2. Resolve the exact widget ID through the global public-routing locator, then load the widget with locator-supplied organization, tenant, and widget predicates. Caller-supplied scope is neither accepted nor queried. Collision, missing locator, or locator/resource mismatch returns the same minimal not-found response.
3. For a new session, generate or accept client-generated high-entropy IDs/token, store only `sha256:<hex>`, and leave `contact_id` null.
4. For an existing session, load conversation and session using conversation ID plus organization plus tenant. Compare token digests in constant time. A token-bearing legacy row can bootstrap sidecars on a successful append; a tokenless row fails closed.
5. Legacy bootstrap locks the exact conversation/session, proves no transcript sentinel or active legacy worker remains, and maps all existing visible messages to ordinals in stable `(created_at, id)` order before accepting a new write. Once a session exists, any visible message without an order row is a reconciliation error rather than a fallback sort.
6. Discard candidate reads, then take pager-admission → quota-environment → exact population/absent-child fence → Noli/user/tenant/organization → widget/conversation/session/job classes in the universal order, revalidate, and only then lock/update the exact sidecar session row with `clock_timestamp()`, increment `last_sequence` and `last_message_ordinal`, capture the current server-owned widget automation, conversation automation, and reply-reservation epochs immutably on the job, and insert the visitor message, message-order row, reply job, quota event, and conversation locator in one transaction. For an active processable session, that transaction also increment-one reserves `reserved_reply_slots`, creates-or-verifies the generation-fenced population child and deterministic DB-only scope registration within the `P=40` environment/`T=4` tenant caps, increment-one charges the environment/child/session outstanding-processable counters with the immutable job reservation tuple, and leaves the job queued. For a handed-off session, it creates no reservation and instead stores the exact `no_reply` outcome, `sequence_resolved_at`, `status='completed'`, and `completed_at` together with all side-effect/lease fields null; it creates no new scheduler-desiring population solely for that terminal job, though any existing registration/population child is exact-verified and retained by the authority provider. An exact existing scope registration preserves its pager/fairness coordinates and `updated_at`; config or population-generation drift is a transaction failure rather than an implicit admission rewrite. The global pager row/transport is never created, changed, or scoped by this transaction.
7. A repeated message ID with the exact same scope, sender, body, and assigned ordinal returns the existing acceptance. A conflicting reuse returns `409` without disclosure.
8. Public chat does not write `inbox_conversations`. That table's active list excludes chat, the chat operator UI reads `chat_conversations` directly, and projecting anonymous claimed identity into its contact/email/phone merge helper creates privacy and idempotency hazards without a launch consumer. Admission and every visitor/bot/agent chat publication write only the exact transcript/order/job/CS entities in their transaction. After the first acceptance of an active-session processable job, make one bounded, job-lease-fenced exact direct nudge; a handed-off `no_reply` admission or exact duplicate retry performs no direct enqueue. Queue failure leaves the committed transcript/job/scope registration authoritative and recoverable by the independent global pager.

### Global writer lock order

`P=40` environment population slots and `T=4` slots per tenant are immutable generated launch constants. Every transaction that can read-for-mutation or change any multiplexed `public_chat_quota_environment` total—quota admission/expiry/GDPR, population creation/deletion, processable-job admission/reservation release, or scope-target bind/settlement—uses one universal order after discarding any candidate read: an already-required sorted class-slot plus job/scope **execution-liveness** advisory-lock bundle, if any, as the explicit earliest class; an applicable role-exclusive daemon/lane singleton lock that no data writer ever acquires; optional environment pager-admission advisory lock; fixed quota-environment counter; complete sorted existing population children or deterministic absent-child fences; applicable sorted Noli and local-user fences; tenant-lifecycle and organization locks; then quota rows, scope registration/binding, session/job, and other later scope rows. It revalidates every coordinate after that order is held. No path may acquire a class-slot or execution-liveness lock after any singleton/pager/counter/data class; no path may enter with a population or later scope/session/job advisory/data-row lock and then acquire the environment counter. That early bundle is not a scope/session/job data lock: it is acquired before candidate authority, may remain across the short globally ordered grant transaction and the one external attempt, and never authorizes a counter or data mutation by itself. A proof path that discovers either an earlier liveness or counter class after taking a later lock must release, restart in the full order, and revalidate. A target runtime first commits its immutable no-more-side-effects or pre-send-rejection proof while holding its execution/session lock, releases that later lock, and only a separate transaction in this environment-first order may clear the binding/lease and decrement the live-target count; retry or maintenance can finish that idempotent settlement. Every transition that could create the first scheduler-desiring source takes the environment pager-admission lock before any Noli/user/tenant/organization lock, locks the fixed quota-environment counter, and insert-or-verifies one generation-fenced `public_chat_scope_population` child keyed by exact Noli/local organization/tenant. The child stores positive generation, `strict_required`, lifecycle reason/generation, exact live quota-row count, and exact outstanding processable-job count. Creation increments the environment live-scope count and is accepted only after indexed `LIMIT 41` environment and `LIMIT 5` tenant proofs; the 41st environment scope or fifth tenant scope returns authenticated `409 public_chat_scope_capacity_exhausted` before public authority/data mutation, while a possessed public path encountering impossible missing authority returns its ordinary nondisclosing unavailable response without a message/job/marker write. Existing-scope cleanup/GDPR uses the already-counted child and is never rejected for capacity. Desired-source creation sets `strict_required=true` and creates/verifies the DB scope registration in the same transaction. Finalization may clear `strict_required` only after an authoritative stable desired/retiring zero proof; deletion of the scope's last quota row decrements the child but cannot remove it while strict authority remains. Only `{ strict_required=false, live_quota_rows=0, outstanding_processable_jobs=0 }` plus zero exact scope registration/binding may generation-CAS delete the child and decrement the fixed environment count. A missing strict row therefore cannot lose its slot to another scope, and quota-only residue prevents enable/burst/disable churn. Cutover prepare and public-widget activation reserve the child/registration before public exposure; admission, close/takeover, deactivation, delete, erasure, seed, and reconciliation exact-verify it. A desired source without a child, over-cap preinstall union, generation mismatch, counter drift, or missing row at cap is corruption/readiness failure—not authority to create `P+1`. Seed/reconciliation exact-match population children against the union of desired sources, strict rows, distinct quota scopes, and every unreleased processable reservation, including outstanding-only retiring/quota-free children and `<=4` per tenant.

Every widget create/update/backfill and admission, authenticated reply/status mutation, provider transition, reconciliation action, deactivation, and deletion uses one lock order, skipping classes it does not touch: any already-required sorted class-slot/execution-liveness session locks as the explicit earliest class; an applicable role-exclusive daemon/lane singleton; the applicable environment pager-admission advisory transaction lock; when any population child is locked or multiplexed quota-environment total can change, the fixed quota-environment counter followed by complete sorted population-child rows/absent-child fences; applicable sorted domain-separated Noli GDPR-fence advisory locks; applicable sorted local-user GDPR-fence advisory locks; sorted tenant-lifecycle advisory locks; sorted local-organization advisory locks; sorted notification-routing advisory locks; sorted locator-digest advisory locks (old and new when changing slug); widget advisory lock; conversation advisory lock; widget row; conversation/session row; then job/message rows. A notification-routing key is the fixed domain-separated tuple of environment, organization, and tenant. Alert grants take it shared after their organization lock; every manifested recipient/routing/connection/ESP/sender/credential writer takes it exclusively through its epoch increment and commit. Cross-scope routing reparent is forbidden, so a writer never discovers a second scope after locking. A child public/link/scheduler writer takes the exact tenant-lifecycle lock in shared mode before its ordinary organization lock and re-reads both active/nondeleted parents after waiting; an organization create takes the tenant lock first. Tenant deactivate/delete/restore takes its one tenant-lifecycle lock exclusively and holds it through the indexed zero-protected-child probe, tenant-row CAS, and commit, so it needs no unbounded child-organization lock set. Organization deactivate/delete/restore takes the tenant lock shared and the exact organization lock exclusively through its zero-child-state probe, organization-row CAS, and commit. The shared parent-lifecycle service sets separate transaction attestations for those modes; reconciled OLD+NEW triggers reject a direct parent or child-authority write without the matching lock-bound attestation and fresh parent re-read. A waiter always discards its pre-lock snapshot. No path may acquire an early class-slot/execution-liveness lock after a daemon/pager/counter/data class, or acquire the environment counter, a population child, tenant, organization, or routing lock after a later class in this order, and multi-parent operations sort each complete class before moving to the next.

Ordinary organization grant/lease/chat writers take the applicable Noli fence lock in shared mode; user-only generic lease creators take the existing shared local-user fence keyed by `localUserId` and never invent a Noli organization. Erasure and every Noli link canonicalize/replace/unlink operation first takes the applicable exclusive Noli fence plus tenant/organization locks and atomically flips a durable **scope-closing authority** before attempting a high-cardinality user proof: bootstrap creates the controller-verified disabled/pending cutover row with `user_barrier_phase='materializing'`; unlink/cancellation sets that phase on the existing cutover operation; organization erasure uses the existing `gdpr_org_subjects` deleting operation and its typed public-chat barrier proof. That commit closes association add/remove/move, notification-subject/routing mutation, organization grants, public work, and every new scope-derived writer. It does not take an unbounded user-lock set. The coordinator then keyset-pages the union of current effective organization associations, both indexed non-null reply-job notification subject columns, and every bound notification/generic user lease in pages of at most 32 UUIDs. For each page it takes only the applicable Noli fence and those sorted user fences, insert-or-verifies one immutable `CustomerPublicChatOperationUserBarrier` per operation/user, and settles or records every pre-existing exact user lease before persisting the bounded cursor/count/high-water/digest in the scope-closing authority. A notification subject remains in the union after association detachment until its role is properly redacted, so detach cannot hide an in-flight/ambiguous personal effect. Under a user's fence, every later user-only lease creator must first make an indexed join from that user to any barrier whose exact cutover/GDPR authority is still active and fail closed if one exists; an operation UUID alone is never authority. After the last page, a stable from-start rescan must exact-match the saved high-water/count/digest and prove every union member has a matching barrier plus zero unresolved lease/grant. Only then may the operation advance. Thus a paused creator either commits before its barrier and is settled, or resumes afterward and sees the active barrier; no transaction ever holds all user fences, and a multi-organization user is blocked by any one active operation.

If OLD is malformed but legacy rows could carry it, the initial scope-closing transaction also includes `crm-gdpr-fence:organization-raw-sha256:<sha256(oldRaw)>`; null OLD adds no raw key, while first-link still locks NEW. Only after that bounded fence and parent lock set is held may code authoritatively read the Organization link/cutover row, and it revalidates the canonical/raw binding immediately before committing the closing authority. `crm_gdpr_create_external_processor_grant` and organization-scoped generic lease creators use their supplied Noli identity (canonical UUID key or raw digest key) to acquire the shared Noli fence **before** reading/locking Tenant or Organization or constructing a lease/grant, then take the parent locks and re-read link/cutover/fence after waiting. User-only lease acquisition instead takes its user fence and checks the indexed active operation-user barrier join before insert, so no row-lock→advisory inversion remains. Final unlink or erasure requires the materialization fingerprint, all expected barriers, fresh stable-union and zero-state proofs. If it can mutate a population or quota-environment total, its O(1) final transaction first takes the fixed environment counter and exact population child, then its bounded Noli/tenant/organization locks; otherwise it starts at those bounded scope locks. In that authority transaction that clears the link/deletes the organization it marks the retained cutover/GDPR operation terminal (or deletes the cutover authority), which logically deactivates every joined user barrier at once. Physical barrier rows are keyset-purged only afterward under at most 32 sorted user fences and exact terminal proof; a crash leaves harmless inactive rows, while premature cleanup is forbidden. Cross-organization global-slug contenders take applicable fence, sorted tenant, and sorted organization locks before the shared slug digest. Multi-widget or multi-conversation operations sort UUIDs before taking the next lock. Lifecycle and exact organization/tenant scope are re-read only after applicable locks are held. Tests deliberately interleave scope-fence commit, every barrier page, stable rescan, O(1) terminalization, and physical purge with admission versus quota expiry, admission versus final organization purge, pager selection versus target settlement, and canonical/raw grant creation, user-only lease acquisition, association/notification change, multi-organization users, concurrent user+organization erasure, high-cardinality scopes, controller crash, tenant lifecycle, cross-org slug writes, provider start, widget/conversation lifecycle, and GDPR, proving no lock-table exhaustion, deadlock, orphan work, hidden subject, or delayed old-Noli write.

The associated-user materialization is protected against phantoms by a database-enforced association-writer contract, not by convention. Before implementation, one generated/fingerprinted auth manifest enumerates every table/column that can add, remove, or change a local user's effective organization scope—including direct user organization, membership/role/ACL mappings, invitations when they become effective, Clerk provisioning/sync, organization move/merge, and future generated auth adapters. Every such REST/Assistant/import/webhook/background writer must call one shared service that resolves candidate OLD/NEW tenant, organization, and Noli coordinates without treating them as authority; takes sorted Noli fences, affected user fences, the complete sorted OLD/NEW tenant-lifecycle lock set shared, and then the complete sorted OLD/NEW organization lock set in the global order; and re-reads both parents, association source, link/cutover, scope-closing phase, and effective authority before mutation. Reconciled OLD+NEW triggers reject direct writes unless the transaction carries the exact association-contract plus tenant-lock attestations and current active/nondeleted, non-closing parent coordinates. The initial closing transaction holds tenant/organization locks through its phase write, so an in-flight association writer commits before the fence or waits and then rejects; later barrier pages need no parent locks and cannot miss a new association. A missing/unfingerprinted source, cursor gap, changed union digest, missing barrier, or active user lease makes reconciliation and cutover verification fail closed. Tests pause invite acceptance, provisioning, sync, role/ACL expansion, user move/removal, notification rebind/redaction, and user-only lease creation before/after the scope fence and every page, including cross-tenant A→B moves, attempted lock inversion, equal high-water inserts, and more than 2,048 users.

### Worker State Machine

`queued -> leased -> provider_started -> result_ready -> metering_started -> publish_ready -> completed`

Additional terminal states are `failed` and `cancelled`. `reconciliation` is deliberately nonterminal and blocks GDPR erasure.

- Under a session-row lock, select the lowest sequence whose `sequence_resolved_at` is null. A later job cannot bypass an earlier unanswered sequence; an earlier job that already published/suppressed its deterministic outcome may remain nonterminal solely as an external GDPR ambiguity barrier without freezing later conversation work.
- Claim `queued` or expired pre-provider `leased` work by CAS with a new `claim_token`, incremented attempt count, and `run_after=clock_timestamp()+lease`.
- Every mutation matches job ID, organization ID, tenant ID, widget ID, conversation ID, expected status, and claim token.
- In one short transaction using the global lock order, revalidate lifecycle, immutable Noli organization binding, and admission budgets. Build a causal provider/CS snapshot by job sequence: each earlier inbound/reply pair in sequence order, authenticated visible messages committed before the current inbound, then the current inbound. A reply from an earlier sequence is included even if its visible ordinal was allocated after the current inbound; any later-sequence inbound/reply is excluded. Freeze that bounded input and provider/config choice, then persist `provider_input_digest`, bounded non-secret config identity, `provider_started`, `provider_started_at`, immutable provider/purpose/provider-attempt binding, `external_phase=provider`, its phase start, and database-time ambiguity deadline. The organization-scoped writer trigger's shared erasure-fence lock is the commit boundary. Then **commit and release every transaction, domain advisory, and data-row lock before provider I/O**; the only lock retained is the dedicated execution-liveness session advisory lock described below, which has no data-lock-ordering role and exists solely to prove whether this exact runtime can still perform a side effect. The worker uses that in-memory snapshot and never re-reads newer transcript/config after commit. A provider call is forbidden inside a database transaction and forbidden before this durable grant exists. Every SDK/client layer receives the same hard 45-second AbortSignal and explicitly sets retries/`maxRetries` to zero; a transient status, `429`, connection failure, timeout, or abort therefore produces exactly one outbound HTTP attempt for the durable provider attempt. The stale-provider visitor-recovery threshold is 75 seconds, and the external ambiguity ceiling remains separately bounded at 4,200 seconds.
- A crash immediately before commit leaves the job pre-provider and safely reclaimable. A crash immediately after commit leaves `provider_started` durable and therefore never permits a second provider call. This commit boundary has explicit fault-injection tests.
- An exact settled provider rejection/error clears the external phase while storing a deterministic local handoff. Timeout, abort, network ambiguity, or crash may publish the same bounded handoff but retains the external phase and `reconciliation` until the ambiguity boundary or an exact cleanup/result receipt; it never replays. A late original worker loses its claim-token CAS, and an erasure fence rejects its delayed writes.
- Persist the generated/public text, model, usage, BYOK flag, outcome, and bounded CS metadata before metering.
- CAS to `metering_started` and persist a unique metering attempt plus external-phase/deadline before calling fail-open metering. The client receives an exact AbortSignal, disables SDK retries, and hard-aborts within 10 seconds. A settled return clears the phase; an ambiguous/crashed attempt is never repeated. Because metering is fail open, an already-persisted public result may still publish and resolve the conversation sequence while the job remains nonterminal reconciliation for GDPR until its boundary. The single external-phase slot is strictly serialized: publication may durably mark a CS alert as pending, but no notification attempt/side effect starts while an ambiguous metering phase remains open.
- Immediately before publication, reacquire the full global lock order and re-read widget, conversation, and session lifecycle. Only an active widget, open conversation, and `active` session whose server-owned widget lifecycle generation, conversation lifecycle epoch, and reply-reservation epoch still exactly equal the immutable values captured by the job—and whose aggregate reservation count is positive—may decrement one reservation, allocate the next `last_message_ordinal`, and publish the deterministic `reply_message_id`, its message-order row, and any deterministic CS proposal rows in one transaction. `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` is followed by exact content/scope/ordinal/reservation verification; mismatch moves to reconciliation. If close/reopen, ordinary deactivate/reactivate, delete, or agent/CS takeover won after provider admission, current-state booleans alone cannot revive the stale attempt: provider usage still meters exactly once but bot/holding/proposal/notification publication is suppressed, the outcome becomes explicit `no_reply` or takeover handoff, and `sequence_resolved_at` is set without decrementing the newer reservation epoch or clearing any external ambiguity. A deterministic proposal already committed before lifecycle wins becomes logically non-sendable immediately and is batch-marked later; approval rechecks exact conversation/widget/session state plus all captured generations.
- For a paused CS result, the publication transaction first sets immutable historical `notification_pending_at` **and `run_after=clock_timestamp()` in the same commit**, so a crash before the immediate notification CAS is schedule-recoverable. If no external phase is open, the current execution may CAS the unresolved pending state to one unique notification attempt plus `external_phase=notification`/deadline before email. If metering remains ambiguous, it performs no email call; after metering is exactly settled or the metering-slot `acknowledge_no_retry` clears only that expired barrier, the same transaction refreshes `run_after=clock_timestamp()`. The notification maintenance selector uses its strict-row `(runAfter,jobId)` cursor and exact partial index to inspect at most 100 due sequence-resolved nonterminal jobs with pending/unsettled/unattempted notification and no external phase, selecting at most one alert per conversation and 25 per sweep. It advances past every inspected/CAS-lost/blocked row, wraps/increments its epoch at EOF, never participates in the ordinary selector, and starts an attempt only under a fresh execution guard.

  Alert delivery is opt-in rather than inferred from the first active mailbox. The managed Customer Service settings entity gains nullable scalar `public_chat_alert_recipient_connection_id` plus nonnegative increment-only bigint `public_chat_alert_settings_epoch`, default `0`; no watched-connection/scenario JSON or timestamp substitutes for them. Setting, clearing, or changing the recipient increments the epoch exactly once and requires the same Customer Service base permission plus `customers.engagement.view` and `customers.settings.manage`, exact organization+tenant scope, and an ActionLog. The cutover row also has nonnegative increment-only `public_notification_routing_epoch`, default `0`. Every create/update/delete/activate/deactivate, purpose/provider reassignment, credential rotation, sender-address mutation, or ownership change in `email_routing`, `email_connections`, `esp_connections`, or `esp_sender_addresses` takes the tenant/organization locks through one shared notification-routing writer, increments this epoch when a cutover row exists, and carries an OLD+NEW trigger attestation; direct or unscoped mutations fail. This makes routing selection phantom-safe and ABA-detectable rather than trusting row timestamps.

  Recipient discovery uses a two-pass protocol to preserve the global order. A first read projects only candidate settings epoch, connection/user IDs, organization, tenant, and routing scalar IDs—including any distinct personal sender owner—never address, token, subject, or content, then releases the transaction. The grant takes sorted Noli/user fences for every distinct recipient/sender owner, shared tenant, organization, and routing locks in global order; re-reads the candidate set; requires the same recipient/settings/routing epochs; and restarts without mutation if any coordinate changed. Under those locks it rechecks the exact job/proposal/action binding, pending/sendable action, CS-pause ownership/reason/manual epoch, widget and conversation lifecycle generations, active/open state, and absence of an approval/lifecycle winner. Before loading any email address or composing a body, it requires the configured recipient connection owner to be an active/nondeleted principal still effectively associated with the same organization+tenant and currently holding the Customer Service/email base plus `customers.engagement.view`. A user-owned sender connection independently requires its exact active/nondeleted owner, same-scope association, current email-send/routing authority, and unchanged ownership; an organization-owned allow-listed HTTP ESP is the only no-user sender case. Association/role/ACL writers share every affected user's fence and parent locks, and a removal/revocation deactivates/unroutes the personal sender or increments routing epoch in the same transaction. It resolves the entire transactional sender chain—`email_routing`, chosen `email_connections` or `esp_connections`, and `esp_sender_addresses` as applicable—with purpose, parent ID, active/nondeleted, organization, and tenant predicates at every hop. An ID-only or organization-only routing/provider lookup is forbidden. Missing/unconfigured/revoked/unauthorized/cross-scope/ambiguous recipient or sender state atomically writes `notification_cancelled_at` with allow-listed no-attempt reason `not_configured` or `recipient_or_sender_unavailable`; it creates no notification attempt/external phase, loads no visitor content, emits no event, and calls no email/ESP provider. Tests revoke/detach each distinct sender owner at both snapshot boundaries.

  An accepted grant persists the exact `notification_alert_settings_epoch` and `notification_routing_epoch` plus frozen recipient/sender/config identities and their paired keyed digests in the notification request identity. While still under the final locks it exact-loads and decrypts only the chosen scoped credential into process memory; the database stores only its keyed proof. It then commits and passes those frozen in-memory values directly to one dedicated alert adapter—there is no post-commit credential reload. An epoch/config/permission change that wins before this grant prevents the call, while a later change cannot create a second attempt.

  The launch allow-list is exact: Gmail REST API, Microsoft Graph mail-send, Resend HTTPS, SendGrid HTTPS, or Mailgun HTTPS through contract-specific adapters/version fingerprints. SMTP/IMAP, SES SMTP, Nodemailer, generic `sendEmailByPurpose`, provider fallback/discovery, and an unknown adapter are rejected before grant as `recipient_or_sender_unavailable`. Gmail/Microsoft require an already-valid access token whose database expiry exceeds the full notification envelope plus 60 seconds; an expired/near-expiry token takes that same no-attempt lane. OAuth refresh, DNS/socket work to tenant-configured hosts, credential/token update, internal SDK retry, redirect, and any other hidden network call are forbidden. Every allowed HTTPS adapter receives the same hard AbortSignal, zero-retry option, fixed provider origin, bounded response reader, and one attempt ID, so the tracked send is the sole external attempt.

  The alert itself is content-minimized: its fixed localized template says only that a website-chat item needs authorized review and links to exactly `new URL('/backend/customer-service', validatedProductionAppOrigin)`, with no job, user, tenant, token, or query data. `validatedProductionAppOrigin` comes only from the startup-validated production `APP_URL` contract below; `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, `VERCEL_URL`, request/forwarded `Host`, routing data, tenant text, and localhost/default fallbacks are forbidden. Its normalized origin, fixed path, and template version are part of the frozen body/request HMACs and must exact-match the controller deployment receipt/runtime-start attestation at grant. A mixed-replica or changed-origin fingerprint fails readiness and the grant before credential/content load or provider construction. Origin rotation uses maintenance demotion plus a new deployment/config receipt and routing/template epoch; old attempts retain their frozen bytes and the old domain/key configuration until they settle. The template contains no visitor name/address, message preview, scenario label/instruction, draft, transcript, or tenant-custom text. A losing or invalidating transaction may resolve the historical pending marker by writing immutable `notification_cancelled_at` plus the one canonical model enum reason only when no notification attempt/phase/user lease exists: manual reply, approval, dismiss, prompt/source-policy invalidation, close, deactivate/delete, missing recipient/sender, user erasure, or organization erasure each has a distinct trigger-verified lane. Once any notification attempt, phase, or user lease exists, no no-attempt cancellation is legal and normal exact settlement/ambiguity proof remains mandatory. The client hard-aborts within 15 seconds. A settled success/failure clears only the external phase while writing immutable `notification_settled_at`/outcome and deleting exact user leases; an ambiguous notification retains its phase/leases and is not automatically resent. The notification-slot `acknowledge_no_retry` clears the exact expired attempt barrier, writes immutable `notification_settled_at` with allow-listed `acknowledged_no_retry`, and deletes the leases, so the historical pending marker is resolved and cannot be reselected. The holding reply/review proposal resolves the conversation sequence while the job remains nonterminal reconciliation for every open barrier/unresolved alert. Tests include every canonical cancellation winner; same-user/two-tenant credentials; same-organization/different-tenant and same-tenant lower-privilege recipient sentinels; poisoned cross-tenant routing/provider/sender IDs; SMTP/SES/generic-fallback rejection; token-expiry/refresh-CAS attempts; recipient reassignment; ABA route/recipient changes with the same IDs; config/permission/connection revocation at both snapshot boundaries; malicious Host/Forwarded/NEXT_PUBLIC/VERCEL values; APP_URL userinfo/path/query/fragment/Unicode/default-port/environment mismatches; mixed valid origins across replicas; exact email-link byte fixtures; publication-crash-before-attempt; ambiguous-meter→CS-publication→schedule-only deferred-notification recovery; more than 25 permanent early blockers; every winner versus notification grant; notification ambiguity→second phase-specific acknowledgment→terminal; notification hang; and late settlement. Every rejected recipient/sender/origin case proves zero content load, foreign credential read/decryption/update, event, hidden refresh, and provider call.
- Direct-dispatch ambiguity is independent of sequence and notifications. Its strict-row cursor keyset-inspects at most 100 due rows from the partial `(dispatch_retire_after,id)` index, selects at most 25 with a live direct lease and matching ended-ambiguous receipt plus sufficient exact-tuple `RedisClientFenceReceiptV1`, or an acknowledged/proven-pre-send result, advances past every inspected/blocked row, and wraps/increments its epoch. It advances the row-owned paged transport cleanup and starts no provider/meter/notification call. Only after the Redis command chain is fully proved and a fresh complete state-independent zero-subject proof under the binding-keyed lock may ID-plus-generation CAS-clear the binding and delete exactly its owning processor lease; runtime death or local socket close alone is insufficient. It then terminalizes only if every other barrier is resolved. Crash resumes from `dispatch_cleanup_progress`; a live/pause/no-proof producer stays pending without starving later rows.
- Stale execution-guard recovery likewise uses its strict-row `(execution_reclaim_after,id)` cursor and partial index, inspecting at most 100/selecting 25 and advancing on lock/proof/CAS failure before wrap. A direct guard may clear only with the matching normal-ended receipt or exact verified `RuntimeTerminationReceiptV1`; its ID-plus-generation CAS deletes exactly the one direct-owned processor lease. A strict-sweep guard is non-owning and may clear only while its still-live schedule binding carries the same-epoch normal end or consumed runtime-termination proof; it never deletes the schedule-owned lease. An already-started provider/meter/notification ambiguity remains independently nonterminal but does not require keeping a dead runtime reference after the exact runtime can no longer act. Missing proof, a live/paused lock holder, newer epoch, or mismatched scope/start attestation blocks only that candidate. Clearing the exact guard records the termination digest where applicable and sets `run_after=clock_timestamp()`. Tests include more than 25 permanent early blockers and crashes before/after each external/local commit.
- Barrier-free terminalization uses its strict-row `(runAfter,jobId)` cursor and exact partial index, inspecting at most 100/selecting 25 and advancing past malformed/CAS-lost rows before wrap. Eligible jobs have resolved sequence, nonterminal status, null external/dispatch/execution barriers, and absent/settled/cancelled notification. Under job/session locks it exact-verifies the persisted outcome/publication-or-suppression proof, then CASes `completed`/`completed_at` without transport or external calls and without touching environment/population/session processable counts. It releases those later locks, then immediately attempts the separate environment-first processable-reservation release; a crash leaves the terminal row conservatively counted and discoverable by its partial release index. Every final barrier settlement/cancellation sets `run_after=clock_timestamp()` in the same transaction. Crash before/after terminal or release CAS is idempotent, and a bad early row cannot starve later completion.
- One sweep applies a fixed bounded fairness cycle rather than draining ordinary work first: at most one ordinary unresolved-sequence job, then one lifecycle-marker batch (at most 25 jobs or five conversations/10,000 rows and a 10-second database budget), one barrier-free terminalization batch (up to 25 rows/5 seconds), one stale-execution-guard item (10-second proof budget), one page for one cleanup-eligible direct-dispatch subject (10-second transport budget), and one due notification attempt (15-second client bound), then repeats while below the **120-second** no-new-work boundary and each per-class cap. Empty classes skip; none borrows another deadline. The first cycle guarantees every due sweep-owned class plus one ordinary reply within a healthy **150-second** invocation; processable-reservation release is deliberately absent from this scope-lock cycle and belongs to the independent global reconciler lane after terminalization's post-lock exact-ID epilogue; later cycles weight ordinary three-to-one without consuming maintenance reserve. Partial cleanup persists its cursor/yields. Sustained mixed backlogs, blocked markers, simultaneous ambiguity, and crash-before-terminalization prove each class progresses across pager-selected sweeps.
- Mark the job completed, advance handoff when applicable, and clear typing without another transport write. Each sweep records a hard deadline equal to the lesser of platform deadline and **150 seconds**. Before any external/local-I/O grant it must retain client/transport timeout plus 15 seconds lock/commit/settlement; grant lock timeout is five seconds and post-I/O settlement budget ten. A 45-second provider grant starts no later than second 90; a 15-second notification or 10-second metering/transport page no later than the shared second-120 boundary, leaving its complete envelope before 150. Without the full envelope, work remains due with no attempt/phase/grant/call. A committed grant reserves the remainder only for execute+settle.

  An exact-job invocation may continue sequentially to the next sequence for at most five jobs only while the next operation passes its envelope gate. The shared 120-second no-new-work boundary is an additional cap; provider work stops earlier. A scope sweep processes candidates sequentially, at most one job per selected conversation, and starts no parallel provider calls. Otherwise the global pager revisits the scope within the 45-minute healthy saturated bound. Boundary tests start each class one millisecond around its gate, inject lock/settlement delay and SIGTERM, and prove no grant/call starts without its full settle envelope.

Authenticated agent reply is an explicit automation takeover only on the first `active` reply, but **every new accepted manual reply** increments the session's monotonic `manual_intervention_epoch`. The interactive global-order transaction remains O(1): it insert-or-verifies the one agent message/order receipt; for the first takeover increment-one advances `reply_reservation_epoch` and sets the superseded aggregate reservations to zero; then allocates its ordinal, increments the manual epoch, changes an active/CS-paused session to `handed_off`/`manual_agent`, writes or exact-verifies one `agent_takeover` lifecycle cleanup marker, and creates/verifies strict recovery authority. It never scans/cancels the conversation backlog. The reservation-epoch CAS lets takeover win safely at 999-visible+1-reserved or 998+2; if 1,000 rows are already visible it returns bounded `409 conversation_capacity_exhausted`. Old jobs retain their diagnostics but cannot publish or decrement the new epoch. The epoch/reason change immediately makes every captured CS action, notification grant, provider publication, and approval non-sendable even though their materialized cancel/status fields are batch-written later. An unresolved binding remains nonterminal until its ambiguity horizon and transport proof. If provider work already started, exact result/usage and any external ambiguity still settle under the job contract, but bot publication is suppressed; after exact metering the generated text is cleared and the job completes as handoff. A later distinct authenticated reply may allocate another exact visible ordinal and increment the manual epoch without restarting automation, rotating reservations again, or replacing the existing marker; an exact network retry does neither. Intervening possessed visitor messages remain human-transcript-only `no_reply` outcomes. `disabled`, closed, inactive, deleting, or retiring state rejects. Agent typing alone does not take over or increment the epoch. Tests cover a 500-job backlog, crash immediately after reply/marker commit, capacity races at 999+1/998+2/1,000 visible, two-plus operator replies with intervening visitor messages, reply-versus-CS-approval ordering, the agent winning before provider commit, takeover waiting on an ambiguous dispatch, the worker committing first, the agent arriving during the call, and a late provider publication CAS losing after takeover.

Every authenticated state-creating **public-chat** path—including legacy bootstrap, agent reply, close-note, conversation reopen, Customer Service approval, widget public activation, Noli link/locator publication, and any future transcript writer—takes the organization lock and requires the strict row not to be `retiring` plus the matching enabled cutover generation before inserting/updating state. The only exceptions are the exact unlinked private-widget-only CRUD contract and the exact linked-disabled operation-bound pre-launch repair contract defined below; neither can create chat state or public authority. All other paths reject or remain private while retirement owns the scope; none races a last-state zero-residual proof.

### Customer Service Contract

The current `handleCsChatMessage(): Promise<boolean>` contract is replaced by two explicit phases:

- `generateCsChatPlan(...)` returns a bounded result containing the exact action (`reply` or `pause`), public text, held draft, model/usage, confidence, and validated flag reasons. It performs no transcript or proposal write. It is a dedicated public-chat prompt profile, not an implicit read of personal Inbox settings.
- `publishCsChatPlan(...)` accepts deterministic reply, proposal, proposal-action, and synthetic-inbox-email IDs derived by domain-separated UUIDv5 from the reply job. For `pause`, it transactionally insert-or-verifies all three exact review rows plus the holding transcript/order row by organization, tenant, conversation/job identity, bounded content digest, explicit `channel='chat'`, and metadata. The synthetic email row is a non-deliverable internal review artifact: generic email inbox/list/search/detail/export/subscription paths exclude it at query time, and only the channel-aware Customer Service reader below can load it. The method returns those exact IDs and never queries/deletes a latest bot or inbox row.

Customer Service approval uses `approval_message_id = UUIDv5(noli-public-chat-cs-approval-v1, <jobId>:<proposalActionId>)`; no random message ID is legal. CS-pause publication stores the session's exact `manual_intervention_epoch`, conversation lifecycle epoch, and widget lifecycle generation on the deterministic proposal/action. One global-order transaction revalidates exact organization/tenant/widget/conversation/job/proposal/action scope, a pending/sendable action, the original `cs_pause` job binding, active widget/open conversation, `handed_off` session with the matching CS-pause reason, unchanged exact manual/lifecycle generations, non-retiring strict/cutover state, and visible-cap capacity. It canonicalizes the approved body, insert-or-verifies the message plus order row and body digest, atomically marks the action/proposal accepted/sent, and resolves an unattempted/unopened pending alert with notification cancellation reason `proposal_approved`. A same-body retry returns the existing result; a changed body or conflicting identity returns `409`; close/deactivate/delete/manual-agent epoch advance or another approval winner blocks. If approval wins the session lock first, its deterministic reply publishes and the notification grant loses; if a notification attempt already won, approval does not claim cancellation and the attempt must settle normally. If the human reply wins, epoch/reason change makes approval a permanent no-send `409`. It creates no inbox conversation/projection. Fault injection between every validation/insert/status step and concurrent same/edited approvals, manual reply, and notification grant proves exactly one approved visible reply at most, no stale review email, and consistent action/proposal/job state.

Dedicated chat dismissal uses the same complete chain, permissions, and locks. It atomically marks only the exact pending action/proposal dismissed/rejected and, when no notification attempt/phase/user lease exists, cancels the pending marker with `proposal_dismissed`; if the notification grant already won, dismissal changes review state but the one content-minimized alert settles normally. An exact retry is a no-op, and a conflicting approval/dismiss winner returns bounded `409`. Separately, the maintenance selector materializes prompt/source drift without requiring any prompt writer to scan jobs: when stored widget/scope prompt epochs, selected-source snapshot, eligibility, model/provider policy, or CS selection no longer exact-match, it marks the held proposal/action non-sendable and cancels an unopened alert with `proposal_invalidated`. If an alert attempt already exists it leaves that attempt/leases to settle. Dismiss/invalidation versus grant, approval, every prompt-source mutation, crash before/after status and cancellation, and autonomous terminalization tests prevent a stranded pending marker.

The FK-less InboxOps review graph is nevertheless an exact security relationship. For every row and every status/deleted state, `inbox_proposal_actions.proposal_id` must resolve to one same-organization/same-tenant `inbox_proposals` row; `inbox_proposals.inbox_email_id` must resolve to one same-scope `inbox_emails` row; `inbox_discrepancies.proposal_id` must resolve to that same-scope proposal; and a non-null `inbox_discrepancies.action_id` must resolve to a same-scope action on that exact proposal. The unmanaged `inbox_notes.inbox_conversation_id` edge must resolve to one `inbox_conversations` parent; because a note has no scope columns, that exact parent's organization+tenant is its sole scope and must be established before note ID/content/user fields are loaded or written. The cutover fingerprints the note table's ID/reference columns, indexes, and actual FK/on-delete behavior; absence skips only note-specific work, while a partial, malformed, or unknown cascade/restrict shape blocks launch and no migration invents DDL for it. A public-chat chain additionally exact-matches one reply job's scalar `cs_proposal_action_id`/`cs_proposal_id`/`cs_inbox_email_id`, its deterministic UUID derivations, and the job's conversation/widget/organization/tenant; the action's bounded reserved channel/job/conversation identity must agree but is never the source of scope authority. Every point read, join, list/count/search/stream/export, mutation, lifecycle batch, and cleanup query predicates each scoped hop by both organization and tenant and each note by its already-scope-validated parent before loading address, subject, participants, summary, discrepancy/note text, user identity, or action payload. Missing, malformed, same-organization/different-tenant, cross-organization, reused-ID, orphan-note, or foreign-inverse edges are hidden from ordinary readers and become typed integrity blockers.

Public-chat review classification is immutable and fail closed. Before a generic InboxOps, Customer Service, integration, Assistant, subscriber, scheduled-send, analytics, or background path loads payload/content or performs a mutation/event/provider call, a shared classifier projects only scalar IDs/scope and checks the reply-job binding above plus any reserved chat-shaped metadata. Exact current bindings classify as `public_chat`; a legacy or malformed chat claim with no valid job is `public_chat_integrity_blocked`, never ordinary email. Generic proposal/action PATCH, accept/accept-all/execution-engine, reject/complete, reply-send, categorize/translate, notification/subscription, scheduled send, email detail/DELETE/reprocess, and any future generic path must hide/no-op these rows or delegate to the dedicated public-chat service with the full Customer Service/email base and engagement permissions, lifecycle epochs, and exact chain checks. The internal CS queue, conscience, proactive-followup, and integration surfaces are in this inventory: fleet/service authentication proves the caller service only and never substitutes for the mapped user's feature/scope authorization. Email reprocess must be fenced before it retires children or emits `inbox_ops.email.reprocessed`/`inbox_ops.email.received`; reply-send, approval learning, and execution paths are fenced before knowledge mutation or recipient/body/provider construction. Caller JSON `channel`, route shape, feature source, or status never declassifies a row. Chat channel/job/conversation identity and every parent scalar are immutable after insertion, and reconciled OLD+NEW guards reject direct reparenting, scope change, or reserved metadata removal. Tests address every generic/internal route by raw action/proposal/email/discrepancy ID, include service-authenticated users lacking each required feature, and require no payload leak, mutation, knowledge learning, event, email/ESP call, or cross-tenant timing distinction.

Database guards make that classifier non-bypassable. Reconciled OLD+NEW triggers on `inbox_emails`, `inbox_proposals`, `inbox_proposal_actions`, and `inbox_discrepancies` reverse-classify by the unique job bindings before accepting a change. For `public_chat` or `public_chat_integrity_blocked`, generic transaction settings reject INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE of every content, recipient, status, active/deleted, execution, translation, metadata, scope, or parent field. Only dedicated attested column-diff lanes exist: atomic CS publication, exact approval, lifecycle/notification cancellation, operation-bound cleanup/GDPR, and disabled cutover repair; each lane revalidates the full graph and may change only its allow-listed fields. Non-chat rows keep their ordinary writers but still must satisfy same-scope parent/discrepancy graph invariants. Delayed ORM flushes and raw future writers therefore cannot preserve the IDs while poisoning bodies, addresses, summaries, participants, statuses, or cleanup identity.

Initial CS-pause publication calls one narrowly granted, fixed-search-path `SECURITY DEFINER` publication routine under the job and graph locks; callers have no direct DML on its protected rows. The routine may set diagnostic `noli.public_chat_cs_publication_contract='spec-065-v1'`, but the deferred guards authorize only its DB-private transaction lane and rederived coordinates, never that caller-settable literal. The email, proposal, action, and job's three scalar IDs may be written in either routine-defined order only inside that transaction; `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` constraint triggers classify the tentative rows as protected and at commit require all three unique job bindings, deterministic IDs, exact scopes, reserved channel/job/conversation identity, and email→proposal→action chain to be mutually complete. No application event/subscriber/provider invocation occurs before commit, and generic readers cannot observe uncommitted rows; after commit their classifier excludes the chain. A crash or failure after any individual insert/job update rolls the entire transaction back, while a conflicting/partial graph fails at commit rather than becoming ordinary Inbox data.

The provider-selection/behavior table is frozen in the `provider_started` transaction:

| Preconditions after lifecycle and ordered max-response check | Exact result |
|---|---|
| Session already `handed_off` | No provider and no dispatch; admission already created a sequence-resolved `no_reply` job for the human transcript. |
| Prior published automated response count reaches normalized `bot_max_responses` | No provider; publish the bounded configured/default handoff message once and set explicit handed-off state. |
| `cs_chat_enabled=true` (regardless of legacy `bot_enabled`) | Customer Service is the sole provider path. No standalone fallback is permitted. |
| `cs_chat_enabled=false`, `bot_enabled=true` | Use the legacy standalone widget prompt profile as the sole provider path. |
| Both toggles false | Resolve `no_reply` locally, keep the session active, and perform no provider/metering call. |

`bot_max_responses` defaults to 25. Legacy finite values are deterministically clamped to `0..50` and rounded up; invalid/null values use 25. The field is read-only compatibility state—new widget/settings writes do not create or update any legacy `bot_*` field. The count covers every prior successfully published automated reply/holding/handoff outcome across the whole exact conversation, not only the latest 50 transcript rows; manual agent messages do not count. `0` therefore hands off before the first provider call. The configured handoff text is trimmed and bounded to the ordinary 4,000-character public-message limit, with empty/invalid values using the current default.

For Customer Service, no matched scenario or only matched `auto_send` scenarios publishes the generated public reply. If any matched enabled scenario is `pause`, pause wins: persist the deterministic held proposal, publish the deterministic bounded holding reply, transition the session to handed-off, and attempt the separately fenced alert; later visitor messages remain human-transcript-only and cannot create repeated proposals. Scenario keys/reasons are allow-listed against the frozen ordered config; first configured matching scenario with instructions controls drafting, while all verified reasons remain recorded. Public chat intentionally ignores Customer Service `enabled`, `reply_mode`, hybrid thresholds, source modes, watched mailbox/SMS settings, and signature—`cs_chat_enabled` alone selects this chat engine. Draft failure, invalid provider output, missing provider/config, or an exactly settled provider error publishes the deterministic configured/default handoff; it never falls through to another provider.

Public CS deliberately passes `criticGate: false`, passes no signature/default sign-off, does not request a thread-summary refresh, and performs exactly one provider call for the durable provider attempt. Its prompt allow-list is only the causal public transcript, active **and explicitly public-chat-eligible** `customer_service_knowledge`, bounded enabled **and explicitly public-chat-eligible** Customer Service flag labels/instructions, and explicitly public widget `business_name`/`description`. It excludes `inbox_ai_settings` knowledge/instructions/tone, `inbox_knowledge`, personal brand-voice settings, contact lookup/context, claimed email/name as identity, any cached private thread summary, every legacy/missing-eligibility knowledge row, and every legacy/missing-eligibility scenario/flag instruction. The standalone profile uses only the causal transcript and bounded legacy widget `bot_knowledge_base`, `bot_personality`, `bot_instructions`, `bot_guardrails`, and handoff behavior. Both profiles treat all stored/customer text as untrusted data, never as authority to weaken system safety rules.

Public eligibility is a separate deliberate publication decision, never inferred from `cs_chat_enabled`, ordinary CS active/enabled state, widget creation, migration, or use in email/SMS. The managed `customer_service_knowledge` entity gains generator-owned `public_chat_eligible boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`; each stored flag/scenario entry gains validated `publicChatEligible`, with missing/legacy/invalid parsed as false. Opt-in or keeping eligibility true while changing any prompt-contributing field requires the existing exact Customer Service knowledge-management permission **and** `customers.settings.manage`, exact organization+tenant scope, an explicit warning in the UI, the normal mutation guard, and a redacted `ActionLog`. Every other knowledge title/content/kind/active mutation or flag/scenario label/instruction/active mutation atomically forces that source's eligibility to false before accepting the new bytes; it cannot silently preserve public status. Organization and tenant coordinates on knowledge/settings rows are immutable: a cross-scope “move” must create an independently authorized destination row with every public eligibility false, then explicitly republish there; the old row is separately disabled/deleted. Reconciled guards compare OLD+NEW scope, so A→B and same-organization/different-tenant reparenting cannot carry public text or policy. This rule is shared by REST, Assistant, import/upload, URL ingest/refresh, approval-learning, background sync, settings replacement, and any future generated writer, with reconciled guards rejecting a direct eligible-row content/scope update. Re-publication is a separate deliberate mutation. There is no bulk automatic opt-in. Public prompt construction filters eligibility in the database before loading title/content or instruction text, bounds the selected knowledge set to 20 rows, and never passes a private row to relevance ranking or the provider.

URL ingest/refresh is also a network trust boundary. Its shared safe-fetch transport resolves every A/AAAA answer, rejects loopback/private/link-local/multicast/unspecified/documentation/metadata and mixed public+forbidden answer sets, then connects through a per-request dispatcher whose lookup returns **only** a selected validated address while preserving the original Host header and TLS SNI/certificate validation; native `fetch` may not perform a second uncontrolled DNS resolution. At most three redirects are followed, and each absolute destination is reparsed, credentials stripped/rejected, DNS-revalidated, and separately pinned before connection. One AbortSignal/deadline covers DNS, connection, headers, redirects, decompression, and the complete body rather than being cleared after headers. The response is streamed with hard compressed and decompressed byte counters and aborts before retaining more than 5 MiB; `arrayBuffer()`-then-slice, unbounded compression, and partial persistence are forbidden. Alternating public→`127.0.0.1`, RFC1918, `169.254.169.254`, private/link-local IPv6, CNAME/redirect rebinding, slow body, oversized chunked body, and compression-bomb fixtures prove zero internal connection and zero content/eligibility persistence.

Customer Service file knowledge ingestion is bounded before allocation or parsing, not only when text is saved. The proxy and route stream at most one file with a 6 MiB total multipart limit and 5 MiB raw-file limit, reject an oversized declared length immediately and a missing/lying/chunked body at byte `limit+1`, and validate allow-listed MIME **and** magic bytes.
