No `request.formData()`/`file.arrayBuffer()` path may buffer an untrusted body. Plain text is decoded incrementally. DOCX parsing rejects encryption/macros/external relationships, more than 1,000 ZIP entries, any entry above 5 MiB expanded, more than 20 MiB aggregate expanded, or expansion ratio above 100:1. PDF parsing has a 200-page/object-work ceiling. PDF/DOCX work runs in a cancellable resource-limited worker with a 15-second deadline and 128 MiB memory ceiling, counts extracted Unicode text during parsing, and stops at 20,000 characters rather than parsing an unbounded tail. Rejection/timeout cancels and drains the request/worker, removes any bounded temporary artifact, writes no knowledge row or eligibility, and leaves the server responsive. Fixtures cover lying/missing length, oversized/chunked multipart, MIME spoof, ZIP/path/entity bomb, pathological/encrypted PDF, parser timeout/crash, cleanup, and concurrent healthy requests. Any shared personal-Inbox helper used by this route must meet the same limits; otherwise the Customer Service route uses its own bounded adapter.

The Customer Service and Inbox Knowledge Base bridge is also fail-closed and bounded end to end; the current whole-corpus `/api/documents/export` plus direct `fetch`/`Response.json()` behavior is not launchable. One shared `PersonalKbBridgeClient` requires an upstream keyset/page API for metadata (`limit<=100`, opaque bounded cursor) and an exact selected-ID content API; if either capability is absent, malformed, or not covered by the deployment capability receipt, both bridge routes are disabled rather than downloading an entire personal corpus. Upstream responses must be `application/json`; `Content-Encoding` is rejected unless the client enforces separate compressed/decompressed counters, and all limits below are **decoded bytes counted before parsing**. `GET` returns at most 100 `{ id, title, alreadyImported? }` items and one bounded cursor, streams and schema-validates at most 256 KiB of upstream metadata, never loads content, and queries imported markers only for the at-most-100 returned page IDs rather than scanning all active `kb:%` rows. `POST` uses the shared bounded JSON reader, accepts 1–20 unique document IDs of 1–128 allow-listed characters in at most 8 KiB, sends only those IDs upstream, and streams at most 2 MiB decoded, 20 returned rows, 20,000 Unicode characters per document, and 400,000 characters aggregate under one 15-second deadline; unknown fields, duplicate IDs, missing selected IDs, oversized strings, a lying/missing length, chunked overflow, redirect, or partial/malformed JSON fails with no partial result. Customer Service imports all selected rows with `public_chat_eligible=false` in one exact tenant+organization advisory-locked transaction with insert-or-verify source markers and an ActionLog; Inbox returns at most 20 bounded documents and its settings writer independently enforces its aggregate knowledge limit. Tests cover a million-document upstream corpus, oversized/chunked/compressed/slow responses, duplicate and adversarial IDs, concurrent imports, response loss, bounded page-marker lookup, and zero partial write/allocation.

The connector is personal-user authority, not organization authority. It requires the server-derived authenticated tuple `(tenantId, organizationId, localUserId, noliUserId)` for one active same-scope user; caller query/body cannot supply identity. The KB response must service-authenticate and echo the exact `noliUserId`, stable KB user ID, and mapping version, all bound to the credential/key ID. It resolves only that tuple's encrypted/revocable credential and never falls back to or reinterprets `business_profiles.pkb_api_key` as a shared team credential. Any legacy shared plaintext key is inventory-only and makes the bridge unavailable until it is removed or migrated through a separate explicit admin-created organization-KB product contract with its own ACL, audit, ownership, epoch, and erasure design. Provisioning uses one fixed validated HTTPS origin, one hard AbortSignal, no redirect, bounded content-type/response reader/schema, and a caller-generated durable idempotency key plus authenticated status recovery; it performs one zero-retry call and never repeats a key-minting POST after `5xx`, exception, timeout, or response loss unless the provider add-or-exact-verifies the same user/source/request and returns the same credential/key ID. A per-user advisory lock and row-lock/CAS re-read of the latest cache make concurrent same- or different-user first use preserve every entry and return one credential; a whole-JSON lost update or remote delete-then-rotate retry is forbidden.

Disconnect/user erasure is itself a durable external side effect. Before revoke, the connector persists the exact provider key ID (never raw key), user/scope/mapping version, operation/idempotency ID, revoke attempt, deadline, and user lease/fence. It makes one bounded zero-retry revoke call; exact `revoked` or provider-authenticated `not_found` for that key settles the attempt, while timeout/response loss/outage remains an ambiguity barrier recoverable only by the same idempotency status endpoint or an authenticated exact-key status lookup. Local binding/cache removal occurs only in the same settlement transaction or after authoritative revoked/not-found proof; a concurrent rotation uses a new key ID and cannot be cleared by the old operation. User GDPR completion waits for settled revoke and lease zero. Missing idempotency/status/revocation support disables auto-provisioning and both pickers before launch. Same-organization users A/B, detached users, wrong echoed identity, legacy shared fallback, concurrent same/different-user mint/cache writes, response-loss mint/revoke, concurrent rotation, provider outage, late completion, erase, and secret-log tests prove one user can never browse/import another user's personal KB or leave a live undiscovered credential.

The provider-start grant is the linearization point for prompt visibility. Under the organization/conversation locks it re-reads every selected row and the sanitized scenario configuration, then persists immutable `public_prompt_snapshot` canonical JSON (at most 8 KiB) containing only the ordered selected row IDs plus keyed title/content/active/eligibility digests, the eligible-scenario configuration digest, and schema version, together with its recomputed `public_prompt_snapshot_digest`; no knowledge or instruction plaintext is duplicated there. The exact frozen plaintext used by the one call must produce those digests and the complete `provider_input_digest`. A disable/delete/edit/opt-out that commits before this grant prevents the provider call. A change that wins afterward cannot retract the already-granted single call, but deterministic publication and every held-proposal approval re-read the exact selected IDs/config and require active eligibility plus byte-equivalent snapshot/input digests. Drift settles/meters the already-started attempt as applicable, suppresses its text to deterministic handoff/`no_reply`, invalidates a held proposal, and returns a safe stale-proposal `409`; it never publicly publishes, approves, or reuses the stale output. Tests include private sentinel exfiltration prompts, explicit public sentinel inclusion, opt-in/out/edit/delete races at grant and publication, scenario eligibility changes, exact-scope permission failures, and approval after revocation.

Every provider profile freezes both prompt-policy generations. Server-owned widget `config.noliPublicPromptEpoch` is a nonnegative increment-only integer initialized beside `noliAutomationEpoch`; mutations to widget-local standalone knowledge/personality/instructions/guardrails/handoff or public business name/description increment it under the organization/widget lock. Organization-wide CS-versus-standalone selection, eligible scenario configuration, and shared model/provider policy instead increment the cutover row's `public_prompt_policy_epoch` once under the organization lock—never by scanning/updating widgets. The provider grant captures both epochs and a canonical digest of the complete bounded profile/config bytes actually used. Deterministic publication and CS approval re-read and require both epochs and the same digest in addition to lifecycle and CS-source snapshot checks; drift settles the already-started call but suppresses stale output to handoff/`no_reply`. Knowledge rows remain covered by their exact source snapshot even when shared by several widgets. Tests edit/remove every source class before grant, during provider I/O, after result persistence, and before approval, including a multi-widget race with global CS selection/model changes, and prove stale output never becomes visible without fan-out work.

All tenant/visitor-controlled dynamic strings in the complete provider input—not merely transcript rows—share the existing 16,000-character ceiling. The current inbound is retained in full first; remaining causal transcript receives up to 8,000 total characters, relevance-ranked Customer Service knowledge up to 4,000, enabled scenario labels/instructions up to 2,000, and public brand or legacy widget configuration uses only the remaining budget up to 2,000. A profile that does not use a bucket may lend its unused capacity without exceeding 16,000. Within each bucket, deterministic documented order and Unicode-safe truncation apply before `provider_input_digest` is computed; an overlong stored scenario list is deterministically truncated and cannot create unbounded prompt work. No hidden helper may append dynamic data or start another model call. The output limits remain 1,024 tokens/4,000 persisted characters.

New widget creation and `cs_chat_enabled` setup occur in one local transaction; CS-settings failure rolls the widget creation back rather than leaving a partially configured public surface. The `0.5.x` bridge may accept and ignore deprecated legacy `bot_*` request keys exactly as current writes do, but never persists them. Toggle/max-response tests cover both-off, legacy-only, CS-only, both-on/CS-wins, null/invalid, `0`, `1`, `50`, above-cap, more than 50 lifetime replies, transition before provider commit, transition during the call (frozen choice wins), and post-agent/CS-pause handoff behavior. Prompt tests prove reply-mode indifference, public allow-list, full-input bound, no sign-off/contact/personal Inbox data, no critic/summary call, causal job-two/reply-one/later-inbound exclusion, and one provider invocation per attempt.

### Allowance and GDPR Contract

- The allowance module splits its existing calculation into a read-only internal resolver that returns `{ resolution: "authoritative" | "unlinked" | "unavailable", gate }`. Existing `checkCustomersAiAllowance`/`withCustomersAiAllowance` callers retain their exact current `AllowanceResult` and behavior: only upstream allowance-lookup ambiguity keeps its existing fail-open treatment; scope, identity, GDPR-fence, and lease denials remain blocked. Only public chat consumes the additive resolution signal.
- Public admission requires the exact widget organization to have a non-null Noli organization binding before any sidecar/transcript write, because the organization writer-fence contract itself requires that binding. An unlinked widget has no public locator and returns the same generic `404` as a nonexistent/inactive widget, with no write or enqueue. This is distinct from a temporarily `unavailable` allowance lookup after a previously valid linked admission.
- Public chat spends a platform key only for an `authoritative` allowed gate. An authoritative BYOK gate uses only that key. `unavailable`, blocked, or missing-provider resolution becomes a deterministic local handoff without provider I/O; `unlinked` cannot reach admission. Admission copies the exact Noli organization ID into the session and job. Any later current binding absence/change is an integrity mismatch: no provider or downstream I/O starts, and one guarded CAS moves the job to reconciliation with immutable `{ storedNoliOrganizationId, observedCurrentBindingOrNullDigest, observedAt, mismatchProofDigest }`; GDPR discovery continues by the stored Noli ID. This typed state is indexed and has one exhaustive exit, `resolve_binding_integrity_to_handoff`, below—never a generic retry or silent terminal.
- Provider and metering never consume a user identity: the public worker does not call the user-bound `CustomersAiProcessorScope.createExternalGrant` API for those phases, and the exact reply-job row is their organization-only external-processing grant. The organization writer trigger serializes it against the erasure fence, the GDPR local proof discovers its immutable `noli_organization_id` plus nonterminal `status`, and it stays nonterminal across any external ambiguity. The optional alert notification is the explicit exception because it consumes a recipient user's address and may consume a distinct sender owner's credential; it uses the dedicated bound-user lease contract below rather than pretending those subjects do not exist.
- Before provider, metering, or notification I/O, the worker persists immutable `external_phase`, provider/purpose/attempt binding, phase start, and `external_ambiguity_until` on the exact scoped job. A settled call clears that phase only while persisting its exact outcome. A timeout, abort, process death, or indeterminate transport leaves the phase and nonterminal row intact. The conservative ambiguity ceiling is 4,200 seconds, matching the existing external-processor grant ceiling; the 75-second stale-provider threshold controls visitor handoff/no-replay behavior but is not GDPR completion proof.

  A notification grant creates one deterministic processor user lease for each distinct recipient/sender owner in the same transaction as its attempt/phase. After the candidate-only first pass, the worker uses its one dedicated execution-lock connection to take every distinct subject's shared user fence/session advisory lock in sorted UUID order, then parent/routing/job locks; it does not allocate a connection per user or lease. It continuously holds that complete session-lock bundle through client call and no-more-side-effects settlement and inserts exact `gdpr_user_write_leases` bound to job, notification attempt, user, runtime instance/generation/start attestation, lease generation, heartbeat, and ambiguity deadline. The reply job stores top-level recipient/sender user and connection IDs plus lease IDs/generations for indexed GDPR discovery; one user occupying both roles owns one lease, while two users own two independently exact leases. A notification call cannot start unless the complete distinct-user lease set and reserved settlement permit committed. Normal settlement/cancellation atomically deletes exactly those leases; a crash releases session locks but leaves leases/phase as barriers until normal end, matching runtime-termination proof, and transport settlement/no-retry adjudication.

  User erasure holds the exclusive user fence and scans both job subject indexes plus lease tables. If it wins before an attempt, the grant loses and the pending marker may be cancelled with `user_erasure`; if an attempt committed, erasure cannot claim completion while the call, ambiguity, or lease can act. To avoid fence/settlement deadlock, an erasure pass that observes a live lease/session lock records/returns `local_writes_in_flight` and releases its exclusive user fence; it never blocks while holding the fence needed by the worker's short post-call settlement. The worker holds the distinct users' shared session-fence locks from final grant through no-more-side-effects settlement, then atomically settles/deletes leases before releasing them. A later erasure pass reacquires exclusive mode and proceeds.

  Only after notification settlement/cancellation and exact lease removal may the operation-bound redaction lane null each matching top-level recipient or sender user/connection pair and write that role's immutable redaction timestamp; if the same user fills both roles it does both together, while distinct A/B erasures in either order leave the other role discoverable. The canonical request identity retains only domain-separated HMAC proofs, never raw user/connection IDs. Configuration of an alert recipient likewise takes the candidate owner's user fence and proves same-scope active membership/permission. User/connection erasure clears a matching settings recipient and increments both settings and routing epochs under the same user/tenant/organization/routing locks, so no durable configuration UUID or delayed grant survives. Tests cover same user in both roles, distinct sender/recipient owners erased A→B and B→A, configure-versus-delete, pause after grant before call, exclusive-fence versus post-call settlement, in-call erasure, crash/ambiguity through 4,200 seconds, runtime termination, per-role post-settlement redaction/index visibility, and no raw subject UUID inside retained JSON.
- Every self-managed reply execution also has a durable execution-liveness guard. A direct invocation obtains a dedicated PostgreSQL session advisory lock keyed by the exact reply job on a dedicated connection **before claim**, then the claim transaction creates/exact-verifies one job-bound processor lease and records its controller-issued runtime instance/generation/start-attestation digest. A strict sweep records the already-live schedule execution lease/generation/start-attestation digest as its guard and reuses that schedule session lock. The guard is held continuously through every provider, metering, notification, publication, and cleanup decision until the handler has durably recorded `execution_ended_at` at its no-more-side-effects boundary; it heartbeats at least every 15 seconds and before each external call. A pause after an external-phase commit but before constructing its client/AbortSignal therefore remains a live barrier. If the lock connection is lost, the handler may perform no new side effect until it revalidates the still-live guard/fence; cleanup may acquire the now-free lock but cannot clear the job merely by age. After `external_ambiguity_until`, operation-bound erasure may clear an ambiguous phase only while holding the same lock and after either an exact normal `execution_ended_at` receipt or a matching `RuntimeTerminationReceiptV1`. SIGSTOP/event-loop pause, connection loss without termination proof, unknown/unattested provenance, or a mismatched generation remains `local_writes_in_flight`. This liveness rule is separate from provider transport settlement: it proves that no delayed local code can initiate a new call, not whether an already-sent call settled.
- A healthy handler that observes a newly active organization-erasure fence is not forced to masquerade as a crashed runtime. While still holding its exact execution/dispatch session lock, it may use the narrowly allow-listed `spec-065-v1` self-quiescence transition: read and bind the active fence operation, exact-match row/lease/runtime/generation, start no new I/O, and update **only** the same-generation no-more-side-effects ended receipt/end code (`fence_observed`) plus clear current runtime fields/delete a direct-owned execution lease as applicable. It cannot clear an external ambiguity, publish, enqueue, meter, notify, mutate transcript/outcome, or settle transport without ordinary proof. Schedule-owned references follow the ownership rule. The organization writer guard permits only this OLD→NEW column diff under the matching self-quiesce attestation; anything broader is rejected. The process may remain healthy for other tenants, while GDPR cleanup can consume the normal ended receipt without a false whole-runtime termination proof.
- The additive worker declaration is exactly `gdpr: { mode: "self-managed-durable-job", organizationSubject: { source: "payload", path: "organizationId" }, userSubjects: "dedicated-notification-leases" }`. `WorkerMeta`, `WorkerDescriptor`, both generated registries, and the CLI preserve and validate that exact value. It means the queue payload itself supplies no user authority and generic recursive UUID scanning remains disabled, while the handler must create/settle the explicit indexed notification leases before that phase. Absence keeps current generic scanning; malformed/unknown metadata fails startup. A queue cannot mix generic and self-managed handlers, and `--all` validates every queue group before starting any. The handler validates the exact durable job row before any side effect. Queue cleanup uses only the declared organization path plus the job's trusted top-level notification subjects and ignores attacker-chosen conversation/message UUIDs; equal-UUID cross-organization cases cannot become barriers or deletion targets.
- The shared scheduler-execution worker retains its generic execution lease semantics for unrelated schedules, but the one strict public-chat pager Job Scheduler uses a validated **static global** subject envelope with the exported owner constant: `{ version: 2, strictOwner: "customers.public-chat-recovery-pager.v1", scheduleId, environmentId, sourceModule: "customers", executionQueue: "customers-public-chat-sweeps", targetQueue: "customers-public-chat-replies" }`. Organization, tenant, Noli, future per-fire lease/generation, scope registration, and reply-job IDs are forbidden in this repeating template. The canonical Job Scheduler materializes it only on `customers-public-chat-sweeps`; the owner-exclusive pager worker alone consumes it, persists the global execution binding/cursor, selects at most one exact DB scope registration, and may then enqueue its deterministic scope-bound target on `customers-public-chat-replies`. The generic scheduler worker can address neither public queue. Schedule/environment/queue fields must match the singleton pager row and normalized firing payload. Generic GDPR discovery classifies the envelope as global infrastructure and never derives an organization subject from it; malformed pager metadata is an unreadable named barrier. Widget/organization cleanup must ignore the shared pager schedule/execution and may select/remove only direct subjects plus a bound target whose stored scope-registration/Noli/organization/tenant/generation exact-match—never a tenant-wide UUID substring or arbitrary scheduler payload. Same-tenant unrelated schedules, other organizations, and attacker-controlled equal UUIDs remain untouched. Payload, database owner, matcher, UUID namespace/fingerprint, registry, and tests import the constants; no duplicate literal is permitted.
- Generic queue execution leases are also made crash-recoverable rather than left as random non-expiring rows. A narrow auth-contract migration adds nullable, all-or-none processor provenance to both local/user lease tables: bounded `queue_name`, immutable `transport_job_id`, positive `attempt_number`, `runtime_generation`, `runtime_instance_id`, `runtime_start_attestation_digest`, `heartbeat_at`, and `reclaim_after`. Before any lock or row, the wrapper resolves only the generated subject paths, enforces the manifested cardinality/lock maximum, sorts the complete lease key set, and uses one dedicated connection to acquire every execution-lifetime PostgreSQL **session** advisory lock nonblockingly/all-or-none. It then inserts/exact-verifies every subject lease atomically, holds that one connection/lock bundle through the handler, heartbeats at least every 15 seconds, and releases rows then locks in `finally`. Recursive UUID discovery, partial lock/lease creation, and a connection per subject are forbidden in production. The 4,200-second horizon is eligibility for repair, not automatic proof: queue absence cannot distinguish a paused local handler or BullMQ-stalled original that may resume.
- Post-crash reclaim is therefore permissioned and proof-bound. The internal authenticated GDPR reconciliation surface exposes `reclaim_generic_execution_lease` only after the horizon, exact discriminated organization/user subject and fence/operation, a successful nonblocking acquisition of the same session lock (held until commit), full exact queue/retry/active proof, and a matching environment-scoped `RuntimeTerminationReceiptV1`. A live/SIGSTOP/event-loop-stalled process retains the session lock or lacks the termination receipt and remains a barrier; connection loss without instance-termination proof is also a barrier. One runtime receipt may be ledger-verified across several exact same-runtime rows, but it supplies only process-death evidence: every per-lease capability independently rederives and locks that lease's organization/user scope, operation, queue state, and start identity, then ID/generation-CAS insert-or-verifies an immutable redacted existing `ActionLog` audit keyed by `(leaseId, runtimeGeneration, terminationReceiptDigest, reclaimKind)` and deletes only that matched lease in the same transaction. A changed, mixed, or caller-selected scope loses; the environment receipt never authorizes a subject by itself. Pre-contract null-provenance rows use the stricter `reclaim_legacy_generic_lease` variant with whole-deployment drain and explicit attestation. Cutover readiness requires zero unbound processor leases for participating scopes. Direct SQL is forbidden. Tests cover durable audit plus deletion crash boundaries, multi-scope/multi-lease fan-out from one death receipt, organization versus user-only scope with no fabricated Noli ID, SIGKILL completion, and SIGSTOP/event-loop stall beyond the horizon followed by resume.
- Link lifecycle exposes a distinct, narrower reuse of that proof—not the GDPR action itself. `reclaim_link_blocking_execution_lease` is authorized only while holding the exclusive OLD/NEW Noli fence locks and by either the fresh signed prebootstrap link-attestation nonce/digest or an exact disabled cutover unlink operation. It uses the same horizon, nonblocking lease session lock, queue/active proof, and exact runtime-termination receipt and may delete only the one matched organization/user lease plus a redacted link-operation receipt. Pre-contract null-provenance leases require the signed whole-environment drain. It grants no erasure, public-chat mutation, or broad user cleanup authority. An expired `gdpr_external_processor_grants` row may be link-operation-deleted only after its 4,200-second bound, under the exclusive fence lock, when every associated generic/self-managed execution lease has normal-ended or exact terminated-runtime proof; a pre-contract grant with no provable lease association additionally requires the whole-environment drain. Thus expiry is necessary but never the sole liveness proof, and no schema fiction about grant runtime provenance is required. Paused-live leases/grants remain blockers; crashed residue has a supported exact cleanup path for bootstrap and unlink.
- Active job statuses remain nonterminal for the GDPR scanner. Only `completed`, `failed`, and `cancelled` cease blocking, and no TTL silently terminalizes `provider_started` or `reconciliation`.

#### Organization-erasure quiesce contract

The existing organization-deletion route is extended; no direct-SQL cleanup runbook is allowed:

1. `crm_gdpr_begin_erasure` flips the exact Noli organization fence first. From that commit onward, ordinary admission, worker, scheduler, operator, and delayed-writer sidecar mutations fail through the organization writer trigger.
2. Before the generic active-lease check, the route resolves the one exact local organization and inventories reply-job direct-dispatch bindings, direct execution guards, strict-sweep job guard references, and the exact **scope-registration** target binding. The environment-global pager install/execution binding is not an organization subject and is neither selected nor altered. Each direct dispatch or direct execution lease has exactly one authoritative owning reply row; a selected-scope sweep processor lease is owned only by its scope registration, while one or more currently processed reply rows may carry verified non-owning references to that exact owner/lease/generation. A reference is never counted as another owner and can be cleared only through its own job-generation liveness proof. Direct-nudge or pre-target possible-send bindings become cleanup-eligible at their 90-second `dispatch_retire_after`, but clearing still requires the binding-keyed lock plus an acknowledged/proven-pre-send result or sufficient exact-tuple Redis client-fence receipt followed by fresh transport reconciliation; runtime termination alone cannot prove a delayed command absent. `scope_target_active` requires the later 300-second/latest-heartbeat horizon, the same lock, target absence, and normal-ended or exact terminated-runtime proof. Reply external execution remains governed by its 4,200-second phase boundary plus its job/scope-binding liveness proof. Every owner/reference must match exact population/scope generation, local organization, immutable Noli organization, `kind='processor'`, generation, phase, and boundaries. A future, malformed, multiply owned, orphan-referenced, unknown, merely old, or connection-lost-without-termination lease remains `local_writes_in_flight`; no age-only bulk deletion is permitted.
3. Organization erasure has highest lifecycle precedence over active state and every widget intent. In one bounded transaction with the exact new-contract GDPR settings plus global locks, the route first revalidates the deleting fence/operation/Noli/local scope and performs a bounded indexed existence probe. If there is no strict row, schedulable public-chat state, binding/lease, or transport subject, it writes `gdpr_org_subjects.public_chat_zero_schedule_proof` (added by the auth-contract migration) as bounded exact JSON `{ version: 1, contract: "spec-065-v1", zeroPredicateVersion: 1, operationId, noliOrganizationId, organizationId, tenantId, writerGeneration, provedAt, canonicalZeroDigest }` and does **not** create a strict row. The digest covers the canonical ordered names and zero counts of every indexed scheduler-desiring/binding/transport predicate, while `writerGeneration` is the cutover generation or the installed migration-contract generation when no row exists. The proof is never trusted as a snapshot epoch: every consumer must hold the organization lock, exact-match operation/scope/generation/schema, and freshly re-run all bounded existence probes immediately before returning desired-absent or finalizing. Any residue atomically clears the proof and creates/repairs the retiring authority; every allowed transition that could introduce scheduler-desiring state uses the same organization lock, so it cannot commit between the fresh probe and decision. A cutover-only row may be removed later by ordinary purge. Otherwise the transaction clears any zero proof and creates if needed or CASes the row to `retiring`, `strict_retire_kind='organization_erasure'`, and operation G. If it was already retiring for widget operation W, it preserves the live binding, lease, epoch, retirement boundaries, and bounded evidence; invalidates W-only final proof for a G recheck; and transfers sole finalizer authority to G. The durable organization fence/receipt itself logically supersedes all W intents immediately—this transaction does not scan/update an unbounded widget set. W can no longer pass its guard. Later lowest-widget-ID purge batches mark/delete absorbed intents with G as they encounter them. Sessions are revoked in the ordinary bounded purge, and no new session can pass the fence. The takeover never prematurely clears a binding/lease/row. Tests start G at every W boundary, zero/cutover-only state, and many intents/crash resume, including a delayed allowed state transition after proof creation and after transport proof/before W final commit.
4. At/after each exact dispatch retirement boundary, strict cleanup inventories/removes every exact scope-bound target and direct-nudge job from waiting, delayed, prioritized, paused, waiting-children, completed, and failed states, plus any explicitly inventoried pre-cutover per-scope legacy repeatable/Job Scheduler/materialized execution for that scope. It must exact-prove that the canonical global pager subject is different and leave it untouched. Every shared BullMQ state and legacy scheduler/repeatable inventory is traversed in bounded pages with a receipt-bound `{ inventoryKind, state, start, lastStableKey, pass }` cursor; deletion may restart at page zero because removals shift offsets, but a final complete page-zero-to-EOF pass must observe zero exact scoped matches. Each request obeys the same 240-second operation budget and returns `partial` with its durable next cursor rather than using `getJobs(..., 0, -1)`/unbounded scheduler reads. Active jobs remain named barriers. Local cleanup uses the common bounded queue advisory lock for filtering plus absence proof. Unreadable inventory, unacknowledged removal, residual scoped state, or a late waiter fails closed; retention defaults never exempt a record.
5. Only after transport absence and liveness receipts are exact, operation-bound transactions revalidate row/lease/scope/population generation/boundaries and receipts. A direct execution settlement CAS-clears that job's exact live guard/reference and deletes exactly one direct-owned processor lease; zero/multiple/mismatched deletion rolls back. A strict-sweep job settlement clears only its verified non-owning scope-lease reference. The scope-owned lease is deleted only after every matching job reference is ended/cleared and the scope binding reaches its own no-more-side-effects/terminated-runtime proof. Dispatch bindings follow the same exact owner CAS. The scope registration remains `retiring`; the global pager remains live and unchanged. The route reruns generic active-lease proof; any unknown, orphaned, multiply owned, or residual lease/reference blocks erasure.
6. A second operation-bound quiesce transaction cancels/discards jobs only when they have no active external phase and no live execution guard, or when `clock_timestamp() >= external_ambiguity_until` **and** execution liveness has separately been proved. For a normally ended execution, the route takes the domain-separated job guard lock, revalidates the immutable matching `last_execution_ended_generation` receipt, and proves no live execution fields/lease. For an abnormally live record, it must nonblockingly acquire and hold the same dedicated session lock, exact-verify guard/runtime provenance, and consume a deployment-controller receipt proving that precise runtime instance terminated; connection loss or elapsed age alone is insufficient. A strict-sweep job additionally binds the matching schedule execution guard and cannot be cleared while that guard can resume. Only then may `queued`, pre-provider `leased`, locally persisted results, or expired ambiguous phases be operation-cancelled with generated/result metadata cleared and immutable `erasure_operation_id`/`erasure_cancelled_at` proof. This is the sole post-provider exception to ordinary pre-provider-only `cancelled`; a future/unknown external phase, live/SIGSTOP runtime, missing end receipt, or missing/mismatched termination proof remains a named barrier. Late workers lose generation CAS and cannot write through the fence. After each cancellation transaction commits and releases the execution-liveness/session/job locks, the route invokes the same environment-first exact-ID processable-reservation release capability; a crash or blocked release leaves the terminal job counted and the purge `partial`, never deletable.
7. Public-chat organization purge is operation-bound, bounded, and crash-resumable under the already-flipped fence. It uses deterministic zero-residual rescans rather than a fragile in-memory cursor: each request processes lowest-ID batches of at most 25 terminal jobs or five ordinary conversations/10,000 rows and stops by 240 seconds. Job batches resolve and delete/prove exact deterministic proposal-action/proposal/synthetic-inbox-email rows before the job, but a processable job is purge-eligible only after its immutable reservation-release tuple is present and exact; an unreleased terminal job causes a post-lock exact-ID release attempt and remains the next residual on failure. Conversation batches derive exact IDs from `chat_conversations` with organization+tenant predicates and delete messages/orders in bounded child keysets before their parent/session/active conversation locator; session/parent deletion additionally requires `outstanding_processable_jobs=0` and zero unreleased job tuple. Widget cleanup deletes active widget-ID locators and converts active slug locators to permanent targetless retirement tombstones. A >10,000-row legacy conversation remains as the next lowest parent until every child batch is gone. If any public-chat residual remains, the route returns `partial` with a machine-safe `public_chat_cleanup_remaining` barrier; the same operation retries from the current lowest residual. Only a zero-residual rescan advances to the generic organization purge. Targetless retired-slug tombstones are global anti-reuse state and are not organization residue. The strict row remains `retiring` throughout. The generic organization-table scanner is not expected to discover `chat_messages`, which has no organization column, and broad email/contact matching is forbidden.
8. It re-reads the scoped legacy-scheduler inventories and every exact target/direct queue state, then repeats database job, cleared-dispatch-lease, retiring-scope-registration, active-target locator, legacy-message, quota-event, population-child, and transport proof immediately before the final organization purge transaction. Only that final operation-bound transaction, after candidate reads and completion of the bounded quota-delete and processable-release lanes, takes the optional pager-admission lock then fixed quota-environment counter, the operation's complete sorted at-most-four affected population-child set, current plus sorted historical Noli fences, tenant/organization locks, scope registration, and remaining organization rows in the universal order; it revalidates every proof, requires zero matching quota rows and unreleased processable jobs, clears current `strict_required`, and generation-CAS deletes every affected child that exact-has both counts/registration/binding zero while decrementing the environment scope count once per deleted child together with remaining organization data; it cannot delete/claim the global pager or a targetless retired-slug tombstone. Tests pause admission, quota insertion/expiry, global pager selection, scope reconciliation, local target enqueue, direct nudge, Redis commands, provider/meter/notification calls, result publication, and slug retirement; erasure must either wait with a precise barrier or complete with no delayed scoped recreation, global-pager damage, or slug reassignment.

### Commands, mutation guards, and audit

Authenticated reversible CRUD uses the repository command contract:

- `customers.chat-widget.create`: undo may remove only a still-empty widget with no conversation/session/job; otherwise undo rejects safely.
- `customers.chat-widget.update-settings`: captures the bounded before/after settings, slug, origin, and hosted-page snapshot; undo/redo reruns validation, global slug locking, and exact scope.
- `customers.chat-widget.set-active`: activation is reversible only while no delete intent exists. Deactivation is reversible only after an under-lock preflight proves it changes no session/job outcome and no nonterminal job, dispatch binding, or active/ambiguous external phase exists; otherwise it is a non-undoable orchestration because reactivation affects only future work. Ordinary inactive state never authorizes cleanup.
- `customers.chat-conversation.set-status`: reopening a previously closed conversation is reversible only when it changes no session/job outcome. Closing, with or without a note, is a non-undoable orchestration whenever it cancels, suppresses, hands off, or sequence-resolves work; a close may use the reversible status command only after an under-lock zero-affected-work preflight. Undo at `queued`, dispatch-bound, and `provider_started` boundaries rejects rather than pretending to restore automation.
- `customers.chat-widget.delete`: non-undoable once deactivate-first cleanup begins because transcript/downstream deletion cannot restore the external world.

Public ingestion, visible message send, provider phases, close-with-note, and reconciliation remain non-undoable orchestrations:

- `customers.public-chat.accept-message`: one atomic local transaction; safe duplicate returns existing state.
- `customers.public-chat.process-reply`: worker-only phase machine; retry resumes by state.
- `customers.chat-message.send`: authenticated agent reply atomically bootstraps/allocates the visible ordinal and takes over automation; an appended transcript row is not undoable.
- `customers.chat-conversation.set-agent-typing`: authenticated ephemeral typing mutation with exact scope and expiry; it is not recorded as reversible business CRUD.
- `customers.public-chat.close-with-note`: atomically allocates the final bounded agent-note ordinal and closes the conversation.
- `customers.public-chat.reconcile`: a local authenticated, non-undoable command whose exact CAS persists one immutable slot-specific reconciliation action/actor/time tuple on the job; metering and notification have distinct slots so one job can require both acknowledgments.
- `customers.public-chat.cancel-widget`: exact scoped transaction that writes the reserved durable widget-config delete intent and invalidates safe claims before deletion.

Every authenticated non-undoable create/send/close orchestration is response-loss idempotent, not merely transactionally atomic. Before its first request the updated UI generates and durably retains a canonical lowercase UUIDv7 `requestId`; agent send additionally supplies a random UUID `messageId`, and close-with-note supplies a random UUID `noteMessageId` exactly when a note is present. Widget create never accepts a caller-selected widget ID but does require `requestId`. A request first point-loads the deterministic receipt ID defined below. An existing exact receipt may replay throughout its retained horizon regardless of the UUIDv7 age. If no receipt exists, the server validates against database `clock_timestamp()` that the UUIDv7 embedded millisecond is no more than five minutes in the future and no more than 24 hours old; a stale/future/noncanonical value returns `400` before authorization-dependent mutation or ID allocation. In the same database transaction as the mutation, the service insert-or-verifies one existing `ActionLog` command receipt whose deterministic record ID is UUIDv5 under RFC URL namespace `6ba7b811-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8` with exact UTF-8 name `noli:public-chat-command-receipt:v1:<organizationId>:<tenantId>:<commandId>:<requestId>`, where UUIDs are canonical lowercase and command ID is the exact allow-listed ASCII identifier. The actor is a separately checked nullable coordinate and is deliberately absent from the durable ID; every writer and the deferred database verifier independently rederives the same bytes. The receipt stores a keyed canonical-payload digest, bounded result coordinates (generated widget/message IDs, conversation status, and lifecycle operation ID as applicable), and no message/config plaintext. A first commit preserves that route's native success contract (`201` only for an existing create/send contract that already uses it; close/status remains `200`); an exact retry returns the original allow-listed semantic result with `200` and performs no allocation, epoch increment, marker rewrite, or side effect. Reuse with a changed canonical payload, actor, scope, command, supplied result ID, or note presence returns a minimal `409`. The message-order row and close lifecycle marker exact-match that receipt. Organization erasure deletes the exact scoped command receipts after ordinary data cleanup, and operation-bound user erasure may redact only the actor coordinate; while retained, the scope/request ID is burned so another actor cannot reuse it and a deleted actor cannot authenticate. No digest/result can authorize a request after its scope or resource is gone. The UI reuses the retained IDs after timeout/reload until it receives a terminal response. If the 30-day replay horizon expires first, it surfaces an explicit expired-request outcome and never silently submits the old operation under a replacement ID. Legacy callers missing the required IDs receive `400` before mutation as an intentional security correction. Tests lose each response after commit, race identical and edited requests, retry after process restart, exercise actor/scope/equal-UUID conflicts, and pin every UUIDv7/skew/horizon boundary.

Correctness/security `ActionLog` receipts are explicitly discriminated from ordinary audit logs. Their bounded metadata must exact-match `{ receiptContract:'spec-065-v1', receiptKind, requestOrAttemptId, scopeDigest, payloadDigest, payloadDigestKeyId, resultDigest, resultDigestKeyId, acceptedAt, retainUntil }`, an allow-listed public-chat command, generic-scheduler manual-trigger/undo/redo command, or controller-only legacy-manual-remediation command ID, deterministic record ID, and the corresponding side-effect row; partial/lookalike metadata is ordinary audit data. `acceptedAt` is the canonical database millisecond instant captured by the accepting transaction and `retainUntil` is exactly 30 database-time days later. The manual-trigger receipt additionally freezes the bounded schedule incarnation/revision, target-registry/payload digests, canonical database `requestedAt`, and outbox/result coordinates defined below; undo/redo result receipts freeze original ActionLog ID, action, schedule incarnation, expected/result mutation generation and state digests, and bounded semantic result. Those values are covered by the keyed result digest rather than storing schedule payload. The existing user-GDPR dynamic reference sweep is changed before rollout: for an exact discriminated receipt it takes the user/scope locks and operation-nulls every actor reference column plus any actor display metadata while preserving command/request/attempt, paired keyed payload/result digests, status, reconciliation slot, deterministic ID, and retention coordinates. It must not call the generic whole-row `deleteWholeUserReference` branch for that receipt. Non-receipt ActionLog rows retain the repository's existing user-deletion policy. Message-order and reply-job reconciliation actor columns use the same narrow null-only lane. Tests exercise the real `USER_DELETE_TABLES`/`userReferenceColumns` discovery and final transaction, prove a valid public-chat or manual/undo/redo scheduler receipt survives actor erasure through its bounded replay horizon and prevents duplicate response-loss replay, prove a lookalike/ordinary log follows existing deletion behavior, and prove organization erasure removes the exact scoped receipt only through its indexed reservation locator.

The database-inspectable receipt representation is exact and does not add a table or column. A protected row has `resource_kind='spec065:correctness-receipt:v1'`, `resource_id` equal to the registry-defined request/attempt identifier, `parent_resource_kind` equal to the registry-defined primary effect kind, `parent_resource_id` equal to that corresponding side-effect/outbox/job coordinate, fixed `execution_state='done'`, null undo/deleted/action-label/payload/snapshot/changes fields, plaintext allow-listed `command_id`, and plaintext `context_json` containing only the exact bounded digest/result schema above plus any typed manual-scheduler extension. The generated receipt registry fixes `widget_create -> chat_widgets/generatedWidgetId`, `agent_send -> chat_messages/messageId`, `close_with_note -> chat_conversations/conversationId` plus optional note ID in the validated result, `reconcile -> customer_public_chat_reply_jobs/jobId`, `cancel_widget -> chat_widgets/widgetId` plus delete-intent digest, and `generic_scheduler_manual -> queue_job_outbox/outboxId`; it also fixes `generic_scheduler_undo_result | generic_scheduler_redo_result -> action_logs/originalActionLogId` with command IDs `scheduler.generic.undo | scheduler.generic.redo`, deterministic result-row ID, exact action/request/schedule-incarnation/expected-and-result-generation/state-digest tuple, and deferred exact verification of the final original-log state plus resulting schedule generation/digest. Command-to-receipt-kind substitution fails. Those fields contain no customer text, token, address, display name, or raw payload. The shared ActionLog receipt validator runs before persistence and is also the sole narrow per-row exception in the default encryption subscriber/decryptor and rotation CLI: only a fully exact protected row leaves `command_id`/`context_json` unencrypted and is skipped during rotation; every mapped field on every ordinary or lookalike row retains normal encryption. A `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` PostgreSQL constraint trigger on initial INSERT independently validates at transaction commit the plaintext discriminator/schema, deterministic ID, scope, registry mapping, and final corresponding side effect, so receipt and peer row may be inserted in either order but neither can initially commit alone. After dependency-ordered terminal cleanup removes the peer, immutable stored result coordinates remain the authoritative response-loss tombstone; lookup and exact replay never require that historical peer still exist. The immediate immutability guard rejects a partial/lookalike plaintext row, direct mutation, undo, or soft delete. Its sole actor-null UPDATE validates the OLD protected receipt plus exact actor-only diff without rechecking a potentially retained-expired peer; organization delete is allowed only by its separately proven dependency-zero lane. Receipt fields never rotate; only the operation-bound actor-null lane and dependency-ordered organization delete may change/remove the row. Tests run with field encryption enabled, insert encrypted ordinary and plaintext exact rows together, rotate keys, retry after response loss, reverse receipt/peer insertion order, remove either peer before commit, clean terminal peers after retention, actor-erase and retry afterward, exercise database guards and user/organization GDPR, and prove no invalid discriminator can bypass encryption or persist plaintext.

For this receipt contract, `scopeDigest` is the lowercase SHA-256 of RFC 8785 bytes for exactly `['noli:action-log-receipt-scope:v1',environmentId,scopeKind,organizationIdOrNull,tenantIdOrNull]`; it is unkeyed, rotation-independent, and rederivable only from high-entropy server scope coordinates, while payload/result digests remain HMAC-SHA-256 with explicit key IDs. The exact plaintext exception applies consistently to the encryption subscriber and every encrypt, decrypt, check, and rotate CLI path; an exact protected row is never encrypted or opportunistically rewritten, and every lookalike follows ordinary encryption. HMAC keys rotate no more than once per seven database-time days, the current plus at most five predecessor keys are configured, and a rotation first runs the bounded expired-receipt cleanup and proves zero protected references to the key it would evict. Failure to clean or a live reference blocks rotation/readiness rather than dropping verification authority. Thus a compromised/retired receipt-digest key can leave the bounded six-key ring after its final 30-day reference is deleted; no long-lived organization pins every historical key.

The generated receipt registry has a distinct controller-remediation mapping in addition to ordinary `generic_scheduler_manual`: `generic_scheduler_legacy_manual_remediation` requires command ID `scheduler.generic.legacy-manual-remediation`, actor null, `parent_resource_kind='queue_job_outbox'`, and the exact deterministic remediation outbox ID. Its context extension binds environment, preinstall fence, journal generation/member digest, adjudication outcome/digest, schedule incarnation/revision, target entry key/version/digests, and replacement outbox result. It cannot validate as an authenticated manual receipt, and an ordinary manual receipt cannot substitute for it. The deferred verifier requires the exact bootstrap controller-remediation capacity reservation and frozen journal membership and copies that complete bounded authority/digest into immutable source-outbox and causal-reservation coordinates in the same transaction. The ActionLog row is replay/audit evidence for its 30-day horizon, not the sole later claim authority; after full-guard replacement the dedicated remediation claim capability exact-verifies the frozen source/reservation coordinates and journal-consumption digest even if expiry cleanup has removed the receipt component.

Indexed receipt expiry is autonomous. The manifested retention-daemon role owns the narrow capability in addition to quota and terminal cleanup; no new process/slot/client/fleet budget is added. Its deterministic environment `receipt_retention_window` counter row stores cursor `(retainUntil,receiptRecordId)`, positive wrap epoch, scan time, and oldest-eligible-due coordinate. Every minute with database time, lane B CAS-claims that window, keysets after the cursor, alternates one receipt unit with one terminal unit while both remain eligible, and advances/persists the inspection cursor for every examined child—including try-lock/contention blockers—while only successful releases count toward the 1,000-per-tick receipt ceiling. At EOF it increments epoch and wraps to the minimum; a crash resumes after the last committed cursor and two replicas cannot own one generation. A separate indexed minimum probe refreshes oldest eligible due without resetting the cursor. It sees only typed cleanup coordinates, consumes reserved cleanup work, and cannot read payload/grant effects. Drain stops new units and finishes one transaction. Readiness requires role/command/replica, window/cursor/index/capability fingerprint, the qualified service floor, cursor progress, and oldest-eligible age within the computed backlog drain deadline; key rotation waits for exact zero reference rather than assuming a five-minute universal receipt bound. Crash, 1,000 locked earliest children, continuously eligible terminal work, empty traffic, full capacity, wrap, two replicas, and shutdown prove later receipts progress without duplicate release or cross-lane starvation.

`durability_capacity_reservations` uses exactly three checked row kinds in the same generated table. `counter` rows have deterministic IDs and only the coordinates/usage/fairness fields for one hierarchy level (`environment_physical | family | class | tenant | declared_scope | system | actor_window | generic_schedule_storage | scheduler_release_window | receipt_retention_window | terminal_retention_window | outbox_dispatch_cycle | outbox_dispatch_window | public_chat_quota_environment | public_chat_scope_population`); every counter freezes positive `counter_generation`, its parent counter ID/generation, and a monotonic `next_child_generation`. The `generic_schedule_storage` kind is itself the generation-fenced environment → system-or-tenant → declared-scope hierarchy. Every level owns its non-strict stored-schedule row/byte totals; the fixed environment row owns all-or-none `(tenant_last_inspected_at,tenant_digest,tenant_scan_epoch)`, a tenant row owns `(scope_last_inspected_at,scope_digest,scope_scan_epoch)`, and each system/declared-scope leaf owns `(candidate_materialize_after,schedule_id,schedule_scan_epoch)` plus cleanup cursor/epoch and oldest-eligible tombstone coordinates. These protected lexicographic inspection/service coordinates wrap only after indexed EOF, are separate from cadence authority, and have exact hierarchy/schedule partial indexes. There is no `materializer_*_cursor` counter kind or dedicated row. The retention-window kinds own cursor/epoch/wrap/oldest-eligible-due CAS fields. The one fixed `public_chat_quota_environment` row owns immutable `P=40`, `T=4`, `R=1000`, `Q=120000`, exact nonnegative `live_quota_rows`, `live_scope_count<=40`, `outstanding_processable_jobs<=160`, and `live_scope_target_bindings<=4`. It also owns the global processable-release progress tuple: nullable paired `(processable_release_cursor_completed_at, processable_release_cursor_job_id)`, positive scan epoch, nonnegative wrap count, last-inspected database time, and oldest-eligible-due coordinate; these fields are forbidden on every other counter kind. Each `public_chat_scope_population` child is generation-fenced beneath it and owns immutable environment/Noli/local organization/tenant coordinates, `strict_required`, bounded lifecycle reason/generation, `0<=live_quota_rows<=3000`, and `0<=outstanding_processable_jobs<=4`; unique `(environment_id,noli_organization_id,tenant_id,organization_id)`, environment `(environment_id,id)`, and tenant `(environment_id,tenant_id,id)` partial indexes provide exact membership, `LIMIT 41/5` scope proofs, and bounded tenant outstanding-job sum `<=16`. First desired/quota source allocates the child from the parent's monotonic generation and charges `queue_other_critical`; quota insert/expiry/GDPR changes child+environment live-row counts atomically; processable-job admission/decrement-once reservation release changes child+environment outstanding counts atomically; scope-target bind/settle changes only the environment live-binding count atomically; desired/finalizer changes only `strict_required`/lifecycle; and deletion requires `strict_required=false`, both child counts zero, zero exact scope registration/binding, plus parent generation CAS. Direct DML, caller generation/cap, cross-scope change, negative count, premature child deletion, binding-count drift, or scope-row generation mismatch fails fixed guards; seed/reconciliation exact-match environment totals and the desired/strict/quota/unreleased-processable union, including outstanding-only children. The one fixed environment `outbox_dispatch_cycle` row owns positive generation, next window ordinal, fixed 16-bit serviced bitmap, manifest digest, cycle-start time, and oldest-unserved time. Each fixed `outbox_dispatch_window` owns stable ordinal, `dispatch_family` (`event | ordinary`), destination/class policy, three independent indexed cursor/epoch/wrap/least-recently-served/oldest-eligible coordinate sets for `dispatchable`, already-`visible` recovery, and `detach`, plus protected `next_unit_kind='enqueue | detach'` and nested `next_enqueue_kind='dispatchable | visible_recovery'`. Active-slice ownership is not duplicated. The cycle row owns the all-or-none header `{ slice_generation, active_window_ordinal, active_window_generation, slice_started_at, slice_deadline_at }`, with a positive never-reused generation and database times. The selected window's ordinary sublane cursors/selectors are persistent across slices. Its separate all-or-none active half contains only matching `active_slice_generation`, immutable starting cursor/selector snapshots, and bounded per-sublane inspected/completed counts. One pre-slice transaction locks cycle → selected window and CAS-installs both active halves from the persistent state; each causal-unit transaction locks outbox → selected window only, exact-matches the active generation, and atomically advances that unit's persistent cursor/selector plus active counts without touching the cycle; one final cycle → window transaction exact-matches both halves, clears only active metadata, preserves the progressed persistent cursors/selectors, and sets the cycle serviced bit/next ordinal. A crash resumes from the window's persistent last-committed unit under that exact generation until the persisted deadline, or after the deadline runs only the final two-row CAS; it never restores the immutable starting snapshot or replays a whole slice. Each window also owns exact transport-demand totals—not causal family/class capacity—with hard per-destination maximum 4,096 reserved-or-live outbox rows/32 MiB and an exact rolling database-time maximum of 32 newly reserved destination rows in every 60-second interval. The rate state is a fixed 32-slot ring on that window: protected `rate_head`/`rate_count` plus all-or-none slots `{ rate_token_id, accepted_at }`, where token ID is the domain-separated digest of root reservation ID, destination-component ordinal, and destination-window generation. Under one transaction database timestamp, admission first clears only slots with `accepted_at <= now-60 seconds`, preserving every slot at 59.999 seconds; it exact-verifies already-committed root/component tokens, requires `rate_count + K <= 32` for the `K` new tokens targeting that window, and appends the complete batch in component-ordinal order or appends none. There is no tumbling-window reset, detach/release never refunds a token, an exact root retry creates no token, and a batch with `K>32` is impossible. Root admission freezes every possible destination row/encoded-byte charge and rate-token ID/time, locks the affected deterministic source/outbox fences then sorted destination windows, and atomically reserves the demand/ring tokens before parent mutation; later outbox materialization transfers one named reserved slot→one live outbox charge without seeking headroom, and exact retries consume nothing. Each retained root/component keeps its accepted token coordinates until the causal retention gate, so reconciliation at database time recomputes every nonexpired ring exactly even after transport release; mismatch, duplicate token, noncanonical order, overwritten live slot, clock source other than database time, or a 32→33 boundary disables affected admission/readiness. This transport-demand accounting is separate from 30-day causal retention. Every materialized outbox freezes destination-window ID/generation, one-row/encoded-byte charge, and nullable release time/digest. The final `transport_detached` CAS locks outbox → scheduler release counter when applicable → destination window, decrement-once releases that live transport charge, and writes a domain-separated generation/charge/absence release digest atomically while the detached causal row remains retained. A never-materialized manifest slot releases only when its root proves that outbox can never be created, recording the same named release digest. Reconciliation counts only unreleased reserved slots plus unreleased materialized outboxes; detached retained rows contribute zero transport demand, and generation/digest CAS forbids double release or ABA. Capacity or rate excess rejects/defer-admits the new source before its root/domain event/outbox mutation while settlement, detach, cleanup, and GDPR remain legal. The cycle row forbids capacity totals, and window transport totals never substitute for the hierarchical causal reservation. The launch manifest defines exactly 16 destinations—five event groups plus eleven ordinary queues—and all 17 cycle/window rows plus the quota-environment and fixed generic-storage environment root are precharged inside the fixed 64-row allowance; the at-most-40 population children and at-most-40,000 system/tenant/declared-scope storage children are dynamic critical charged rows, not hidden fixed rows. Unique normalized counter keys/indexes provide O(1) locks/reconciliation, and receipt/root fields are forbidden. One `root` row is unique per accepted parent and stores family/class, exact scope, reserved/consumed/released rows+bytes, and at most 16 pre-reserved receipt components. Each live protected receipt occupies one `receipt_component` child. Their existing uniqueness, transfer, retention, and physical accounting rules remain unchanged.

Receipt release physically deletes the child, so no uncharged tombstone remains. In one transaction the capability exact-deletes ActionLog and child, decrements root plus hierarchical physical row/byte usage by the child's immutable charge, and marks that component terminal in the root's preallocated bitmap/release slot with a domain-separated digest over component ID, receipt ID, release reason, release time, and proof digest. `expired` requires database time at/after `retainUntil`; `organization_gdpr` may be earlier only under the exact operation/scope/dependency-zero proof. A marked slot can never materialize again; retry verifies its release digest and no-ops. Receipt cleanup/scope/actor/oldest-due/HMAC-key indexes select all `reservation_kind='receipt_component'` rows because their existence means live, and key eviction counts only those rows. The sole live-child actor mutation is a user-fenced exact old-user→NULL transition atomically paired with ActionLog/execution actor redaction and actor-window reconciliation; scope/key/other fields remain immutable. Expiry deletes any remaining actor with the child, while claimed manual authority already lives in execution. Unused manifest slots release only when root terminal state proves they can never materialize; a receipt-only root then purges. Checks/fingerprints reject cross-kind fields, unknown/over-16 component, transfer beyond manifest/balance, release without physical child deletion/counter decrement, invalid reason/time/proof, actor rewrite, or bitmap rewind. Tests cover two differently timed/keyed receipts, pre-horizon GDPR, expiry, live actor redaction, long-lived causal root, physical row/byte reconciliation, key zero-reference, and partial-index plans.

Every protected `ActionLog` receipt is capacity-accounted and exactly discoverable without an ActionLog scope scan. Acceptance creates or consumes the deterministic live child under a root, and generated child indexes are `(environment_id,organization_id,tenant_id,retain_until,receipt_record_id)` and `(environment_id,actor_user_id,retain_until,receipt_record_id) WHERE reservation_kind='receipt_component'`. The deferred INSERT verifier requires same-transaction root/component transfer plus effect peer; neither receipt nor child commits alone. Retry point-loads ActionLog. Expiry keysets children and follows the receipt-before-root/component protocol. For authenticated manual, cleanup takes actor fence and schedule/source locks; an unclaimed/no-grant source is terminal-cancelled and unused causal capacity released before receipt+child deletion, while existing execution/grant remains authoritative. Controller-remediation receipt expiry never cancels its copied causal authority. First claim and cleanup serialize. The ActionLog expiry DELETE requires database time at/after `retainUntil`, exact live child/keys, root release-ledger update, physical child/counter release, any manual cancel, and no drift; organization-GDPR uses its separate pre-horizon reason/proof lane. An absent external UUIDv7 older than 24 hours is rejected, while internal reconcile/remediation rechecks domain/journal authority. Erasure/redaction enumerates children then point-loads ActionLog; no audit scan occurs. A local public command creates root+child; manual creates root with receipt and causal bounds; later public reconciliations materialize distinct named children. Cleanup is permitted at capacity and required before key retirement. Tests cover timing, plural transfer/release, physical accounting, cleanup crashes, claim/retry races, stale keys, claimed/granted/remediation survival, actor/organization GDPR, rotation, and bounded plans.

Every custom authenticated widget, message, conversation-status, agent-typing, and reconciliation write calls `validateCrudMutationGuard` before mutation and `runCrudMutationGuardAfterSuccess` when requested. Public anonymous ingestion/typing cannot use that user-bound guard and has a documented exception: it uses origin, possession, database-budget, idempotency, lifecycle, and writer-fence contracts and never fabricates a user. Internal workers are not HTTP CRUD routes.

Reconciliation additionally writes a redacted existing `ActionLog` entry with command ID `customers.public-chat.reconcile`, exact tenant/organization/actor/job, reconciliation slot, expected phase/attempt ID, before/after status, and action. Its record ID is UUIDv5 under RFC URL namespace `6ba7b811-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8` with exact UTF-8 name `noli:public-chat-reconcile-receipt:v1:<jobId>:<slot>:<expectedAttemptId>:<action>`, using canonical lowercase UUIDs and exact allow-listed slot/action ASCII; every writer and the deferred verifier rederive it. Thus retrying one command insert-or-verifies exactly one record while a later notification acknowledgment remains distinct from an earlier metering acknowledgment. The job's slot-specific action/time scalars are immutable correctness audit; only each nullable actor may later be operation-redacted during that user's erasure. No transcript/provider text enters the log. No new workflow event is emitted. New public-chat writes deliberately create no unified-inbox projection.

## Data Models

### CustomerPublicChatCutoverState (`customer_public_chat_cutover_states`)

This is the durable fail-closed authority for mixed-version rollout. It is operational state with no CRUD/query-engine route, search/export surface, or public/authenticated response serialization.

- Identity/scope: `id`, `organization_id`, and `tenant_id` UUIDs plus immutable `noli_organization_id` stored as text but required to be the canonical lowercase UUID string accepted by the GDPR request contract; unique `(organization_id, tenant_id)` and indexed `(noli_organization_id, organization_id, tenant_id)`.
- Gate: `state` is exactly `disabled | ready | enabled`, default `disabled`; `contract_version` and immutable `required_runtime_contract_id` are exactly `spec-065-v1`; `writer_generation` is a UUID created once for this contract cutover and remains stable across compatible forward deployments. Exact deploy/build revisions are mutable verified deployment claims rather than immutable contract identity. `cutover_operation_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `ready_at`, `enabled_at`, nullable `disabled_at`, nullable `maintenance_operation_id`, and nullable allow-listed `disabled_reason` (`initial | verification_invalidated | compatible_upgrade | emergency_forward_fix | noli_link_invalid | noli_link_cancellation`) are explicit scalars. A future incompatible writer/schema contract requires its own versioned migration and explicitly designed generation transition; this release never rotates generation in place over live state.
- Shared prompt policy: nonnegative bigint `public_prompt_policy_epoch` defaults to `0` and increment-one advances for every exact-scope organization-wide public prompt selector/policy change, including `cs_chat_enabled`, eligible scenario/flag configuration, and shared provider/model profile. It is never reset by disable/enable, unlink/rebind, or compatible deployment. This one-row epoch avoids fan-out updates across widgets; widget-local prompt bytes use their separate widget epoch.
- Shared notification routing: nonnegative bigint `public_notification_routing_epoch` defaults to `0` and increment-one advances for every exact-scope recipient, routing, provider credential/version, sender-address, purpose, or effective ownership mutation that could change a public-chat alert. It is never reset by disable/enable or an ABA change; the notification grant captures it alongside the settings epoch.
- Receipt bindings: nullable paired `noli_link_receipt_digest`/`noli_link_nonce_digest`, `noli_link_confirmation_receipt_digest`/`noli_link_confirmation_nonce_digest`, `noli_link_cancellation_receipt_digest`/`noli_link_cancellation_nonce_digest`, and `deployment_drain_receipt_digest`/`deployment_drain_nonce_digest`, plus `legacy_schema_receipt_digest`, `locator_receipt_digest`, `legacy_work_receipt_digest`, `legacy_reference_integrity_receipt_digest`, `legacy_cs_receipt_digest`, `legacy_inbox_receipt_digest`, `identity_contamination_receipt_digest`, and `reserved_config_receipt_digest`; every digest is exactly `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` and has its matching database-time verified-at scalar. `noli_link_reservation_id` UUID, positive `noli_link_registry_version`, `noli_link_confirmation_state` (`pending | confirmed | invalid`), and `noli_link_cancellation_state` (`none | requested`, default `none`) are required for every bootstrapped row. Pair members are all-or-none. A confirmation pair is required exactly when confirmation state is `confirmed`; cancellation never erases it. A cancellation pair plus bounded operation/reason is required exactly when cancellation state is `requested`, whether confirmation was pending or confirmed. Deployment claims persisted from the verified signed receipt are bounded `verified_deployment_environment_id`, `verified_runtime_build_id`, `verified_runtime_image_digest`, `verified_service_manifest_digest`, `verified_controller_fence_id`, and `deployment_claims_verified_at`; they are all-or-none in ready/enabled state and can change only through a fresh prepare. Ordinary `ready`/`enabled` entry requires exact confirmed link state, cancellation state `none`, and every launch receipt. One checked transient permits an already-ready/enabled row to carry `cancellation_state='requested'` only with its complete verified receipt/operation tuple; every admission/grant/readiness gate treats that tuple as closed, no prepare/enable can create it, and only quiesce/demotion may leave it. Every post-bootstrap launch receipt binds canonical scope, operation, writer/runtime generation, scanned counts, zero/blocker decisions, and its terminal cursor; no acceptance receipt can substitute for a required zero. The prebootstrap Noli link attestation deliberately binds scope, authoritative Noli registry version/reservation, inventory digest, and nonce rather than the not-yet-created operation/generation; the consuming transaction binds both of its digests to the new row and receipt-consumption ledger, initially pending. Any stage-relevant inventory, Noli reservation, cancellation request, build/image, or service-manifest change invalidates the applicable receipt and downstream ready state. Raw receipt content remains in the bounded operator artifact, not this row.
- Bounded user-barrier authority: nullable `user_barrier_operation_id` UUID, `user_barrier_kind` (`bootstrap | unlink | registry_cancellation`), `user_barrier_phase` (`materializing | sealed | released`), positive `user_barrier_pass`, nullable UUID `user_barrier_cursor`/`user_barrier_high_water`, nonnegative bigint `user_barrier_count`, and `user_barrier_set_digest` are one checked tuple. `materializing`/`sealed` is scope-closing and makes matching operation-user rows active; `released` is permitted for a successfully sealed bootstrap whose canonical link is already committed and makes them inactive while bounded physical purge finishes. Unlink/cancellation remains `sealed` until the O(1) terminal link/cutover transaction. Cursor/count/digest may advance only by the barrier capability under the exact operation and cannot be reset or copied across an operation.
- Future bridge retirement: nullable `token_retirement_receipt_digest` plus `token_retired_at`; these remain null for `0.5.x` and become mandatory before the `0.6.0` query/plaintext bridge is removed.

Only `mercato customers public-chat-cutover`, its shared first-link/unlink binding service, the exact organization-erasure path, the narrow shared public-prompt-policy service, and the narrow shared notification-routing writer mutate this row. The prompt service may increment only `public_prompt_policy_epoch`; the routing writer may increment only `public_notification_routing_epoch`; each uses the exact scope/tenant/organization locks and its required permission/OLD+NEW trigger attestation and cannot change lifecycle, link, receipt, deployment, operation, or generation fields. Launch-only `prepare` owns the `disabled -> ready` receipt-bound CAS after a complete verify artifact; launch-only `enable` owns `ready -> enabled` in one organization-lock transaction that re-runs cheap zero-residual/schema/trigger/generation/deployment checks and fixes `enabled_at`. No request lazily prepares or enables a scope. A receipt or relevant schema/runtime/config change demotes the scope to disabled through an explicit operation; ordinary application code cannot otherwise edit/delete the row, and unlink may delete it only in the same exact zero-state transaction that clears the old Noli link. A new organization with provably zero legacy chat state still receives a row and the same zero-count receipts before its first public activation—absence is not implicit enablement.

Compatible forward upgrades use `maintenance-demote`; there is no implicit enabled-build swap. The controller first enters the global maintenance fence, closes public/authenticated ingress, and puts every side-effect-capable member of the complete manifested data-plane fleet (web app, private control API, MCP, public target worker, combined generic scheduler materializer/worker service, owner-exclusive global pager worker, all five trust-separated worker/event groups, durable outbox dispatcher, strict reconciler, and the retention daemon) into controller-observed **drain mode**, while the isolated host controller remains available only to coordinate and attest the drain: no new queue claim, schedule materialization/fire/install, dispatch, execution guard, child effect, or external-phase grant may start, while already granted handlers continue against still-`enabled` rows. Before the first demotion CAS, the command proves across every enabled scope that all execution/dispatch/schedule bindings and processor leases have reached normal no-more-side-effects end or exact runtime-termination plus transport/reference cleanup; queued database jobs and independently retained external ambiguity may remain, but no old code can still act. A stuck live runtime blocks demotion rather than relying on a disabled-row settlement exception. Only after that global zero-live-runtime proof does the resumable organization-ID pass lock each scope, write one shared maintenance operation, CAS `enabled -> disabled` with reason `compatible_upgrade`, clear ready/enabled deployment receipt/nonce and verified build/image/fence claims (retaining link and still-valid inventory receipts), and leave jobs/schedules intact. No old handler is allowed to continue after its scope CAS, so disabled guards remain strictly fail closed. The controller drain/global gate stays closed if the command crashes between scopes. An external provider ambiguity may remain as a nonterminal database barrier and is resumed without replay by the new compatible build; it is not permission to keep an old runtime live. The contract wrapper then terminates old runtimes, starts the new exact image disabled, reruns idempotent migrations/guards, obtains fresh per-scope deployment receipts, reruns verification for any build-sensitive/config digest, `prepare`s, and re-enables only after live controller comparison. Emergency forward fix uses the same path/reason. Tests pause/stall handlers before drain, prove the CAS cannot occur early, and crash on every demotion page with provider ambiguity, active target, and mixed enabled/disabled scopes; no route admits traffic until all scopes and controller desired state agree.

Startup/readiness uses the persisted verified claims, not unavailable raw operator artifacts.
