Every manifested data-plane runtime exact-matches its controller-issued start attestation's environment/build/image/origin fingerprint against every enabled scope it can serve and calls the controller's read-only manifest-status check for the stored complete-fleet manifest/fence claim. Any enabled-scope mismatch, absent claim, unknown controller state, or mixed old image makes public-chat readiness fail closed and the shared runtime gate return its disabled responses while process health stays available for compatible recovery. It emits an alert and requires the explicit resumable `maintenance-demote`/fresh-receipt path; startup never silently rewrites a row or trusts a receipt digest it cannot interpret.

Every post-cutover public/agent/widget-lifecycle/Customer-Service-approval write, strict scheduler mutation/fire, and queue worker phase enters a narrowly granted guard-owner `SECURITY DEFINER` routine; runtime roles have no protected raw DML. The routine maps authenticated `session_user` to its controller-registered service/deployment generation, rederives scope, locks and re-reads the enabled row, then may set transaction-local `noli.public_chat_writer_generation` and `noli.public_chat_runtime_contract='spec-065-v1'` as diagnostics. Custom guards on the three legacy chat tables authorize only that DB-private function lane and reject a stale/unregistered principal, wrong generation/contract, disabled state, malformed/partial scope, or Noli mismatch; a caller-set GUC has no effect. Maintenance while disabled requires the separate controller/migrator capability bound to the matching cutover operation. There is one narrow compatible-runtime function for ordinary private-widget CRUD while the organization has no Noli link/cutover row: it re-proves OLD+NEW exact scope, no link, no child conversation/locator/sidecar/strict/transport state, `is_active=false`, hosted/public flags false, and zero case-insensitive reserved/security keys. Its diagnostic `noli.public_chat_private_widget_contract='spec-065-v1'` is never authority. It permits only the widget INSERT/UPDATE or empty-widget DELETE; it cannot write conversations/messages, publish a locator, activate, or bootstrap reserved authority. The null→first-link/bootstrap function is separately allow-listed only when OLD link is null, NEW is canonical, the disabled row is created in the same commit, and no locator/public authority is written. All other absent/disabled/ready writes remain fail closed. Public-chat GDPR has one narrower function independent of cutover state, but operation ID or GUC alone is insufficient because old code already sets them. It binds the registered current GDPR runtime/deployment generation and active deleting fence, rederives matching operation/Noli/local-org/tenant, and permits only the allow-listed quiesce/purge mutation; `noli.public_chat_gdpr_contract='spec-065-v1'` remains diagnostic. The held-lock self-quiescence transition above is the sole non-route deleting-state exception and may change only exact runtime/end-receipt columns. When a cutover row exists, every capability invocation must match its required runtime contract/writer generation; for absent state it must match the installed migration contract constant. A paused pre-contract erasure has no current registered database principal/capability and is rejected even if it created the old fence/operation and sets every expected GUC. This works safely for absent, disabled, ready, and enabled scopes and never authorizes an ordinary writer. The widget guard separately prevents an old serializer from adding/changing/removing any case-insensitive reserved `noli*`/security config key or making a widget public. Strict scheduler rows and the six scope-addressable contract customer entities have the applicable generation/operation/fence protection, with only the quota ledger's exact database-time expiry function in addition to operation-bound GDPR DELETE. The seventh/global receipt ledger has its immutable consumer guard; the eighth receipt-policy table has only exact runtime issuance/compaction and reserved control-plane capacity lanes; the ninth/global outbound-ack ledger has only exact reserved terminal-function INSERT plus pending→signed verifier CAS lanes; and the tenth operation-user-barrier table has only bounded materialize/source-union/terminal-proof purge lanes. Narrow guards reject old public-route contact creation (`customer_entities.source='chat_widget'`) and old unbound `contact_timeline_events.event_type='chat'` writes without the current registered generation, closing the pre-conversation side-effect gap.

The immutable receipt ledger has a separate, narrower definer/verifier function because environment-scoped preinstall and runtime-start claims are intentionally reachable before any enabled cutover row. Runtime roles have no direct INSERT. The function may set diagnostic `noli.public_chat_receipt_contract='spec-065-v1'`, but the ledger trigger permits only its DB-private lane and one verified INSERT shape: environment-scoped preinstall during the still-held controller installation fence; a fresh controller-attested runtime-start claim plus exact `session_user`/service/deployment-generation registration; a bootstrap/link claim in the exact absent-to-disabled or disabled pending operation; an operation/generation-bound deployment or link confirmation; an exact-start-bound runtime termination; or the signed never-consumed link-cancellation tombstone below. PostgreSQL never implements Ed25519 or trusts an application verification. Redis client-command registration/fencing therefore uses controller-authored commitments on the owning protected row, not a runtime-asserted digest: the existing registrar principal alone may read the metadata-only `public_chat_redis_client_fence_candidates_v1` and `public_chat_redis_client_reference_candidates_v1` security-barrier unions and execute fixed `public_chat_redis_client_bind_command_v1` / `public_chat_redis_client_fold_result_v1` / `public_chat_redis_client_commit_fence_v1` / `public_chat_redis_client_commit_root_v1`. Every owning command tuple has exactly two pre-effect shapes: `binding_pending`, with the complete immutable subject/runtime/claim/registered-connection/run/client/nonce/purpose/generation/binding-challenge base present and `database_tuple_digest`, `current_command_tuple_digest`, `registered_command_state_digest`, `controller_root_binding_ack_digest`, `controller_root_bound_at`, and all controller fence fields null; and `registered`, with those five binding fields all nonnull and exact-matched to the root-store command registration. Only a database `registered` tuple whose exact prepared root record also has its fsynced commit marker is send-eligible; database registration alone is never send authority. The bind function alone exact-CASes `binding_pending -> registered`; the runtime cannot write, clear, or guess those fields. After a protected acknowledged result exists, `public_chat_redis_client_fold_result_v1` is callable only by the controller after its `reconcile_result` root CAS and exact-CASes the acknowledged tuple into the cumulative database chain while clearing the current tuple; neither the runtime nor the socket request supplies the result, outcome, digest, or chain value. The fence function alone exact-CASes all-or-none `controller_fence_receipt_digest`, `controller_fence_tuple_digest`, `controller_fence_outcome`, and `controller_fence_verified_at` from a verified `RedisClientFenceReceiptV1` whose outcome is one of the three sufficient outcomes. `run_id_changed_unproved` is retained only as replaceable bounded controller/root-status telemetry with a positive attempt generation and cumulative digest; it leaves the immutable database commitment null, so a later exact old-incarnation retirement proof can produce and commit a sufficient receipt without overwriting history. Runtime roles cannot call any of the four functions or write their columns; every later fold exact-matches the immutable controller commitment and carries its digest into the cumulative proof chain. Raw signed artifacts remain in the bounded/compacted root store. Controller binding/fence fields on an owning row are current-command-scoped: the exact result/fence fold hashes their complete digest/outcome into the cumulative chain and atomically clears them with that command tuple before any next generation; immutable history remains in the chain plus root artifact/capsule, not reusable nullable columns. A delayed receipt for generation `N` cannot match or write generation `N+1`, and fixtures fence/fold two successive generations on one row in both orders. A hostile runtime setting a byte-perfect-looking digest/outcome or GUC fails. The isolated controller duplicate-key-parses and schema/JCS/audience/freshness/key/signature-verifies each raw controller or Noli artifact outside the database, then calls only the matching fixed-search-path capability through the disjoint registrar or Noli-artifact principal. That capability authenticates the principal, rederives lock/fence/scope authority, and exact-matches the bounded typed claims before insertion; migration/operator runtimes only coordinate and exact-reference controller-committed digests. A GUC grants no write to this or any other table. UPDATE is rejected except the one start-claim null→database-time CAS; DELETE is rejected during ordinary scope cleanup/GDPR and for every non-runtime kind, with the sole later exception of controller-only zero-reference runtime pair compaction through `public_chat_compact_runtime_receipt_v1` and its policy/root-store CAS. Thus an old process cannot forge or erase a receipt, while first install, bounded runtime retirement, and disabled-compatible startup are not deadlocked behind an enabled-generation guard.

Every **new** admission, activation, dispatch/install/fire/claim, provider/metering/notification grant, proposal approval, or public publication requires cutover `state='enabled'`, link confirmation exactly `confirmed`, and cancellation state exactly `none`. Consuming a link-cancellation request first changes only the separate cancellation fence to `requested`; it may deliberately leave the cutover row `ready`/`enabled` long enough for already-granted work to quiesce, but the shared gate immediately closes every new authority above. For a registry revoke/change, one narrow operation-bound cancellation-settlement lane permits an already-granted current-generation handler to record only the exact in-flight call's immutable direct/authoritative settlement, suppress its not-yet-published outcome, cancel an unattempted notification, close its liveness/binding receipt, and release its exact lease. It may not start another external phase, publish/approve/send/enqueue/install/fire, allocate transcript state, or grant work. Provider completion after cancellation therefore records usage/result diagnostics locally but skips a not-yet-started metering call and resolves the visible outcome to `no_reply`; an in-flight metering/notification call may only settle its existing attempt. The cancellation coordinator waits for every such handler/session lock or exact runtime-termination/transport proof before demotion. Noli organization erasure never uses this registry-revoke lane; it enters the stronger existing erasure fence/self-quiescence/GDPR contract below.

Every anonymous public resolution or possession read has the same stronger live gate as admission. Start, append, poll/status, visitor typing, widget script, and hosted-page resolution require, at the final scoped authorization/serialization boundary, `state='enabled'`, link confirmation `confirmed`, cancellation state `none`, and no exact active `gdpr_org_subjects` deleting fence for the immutable Noli/local organization/tenant tuple. The check occurs after locator/token/origin lookup and again under the applicable scope lock immediately before returning tenant data; a cancellation or erasure commit therefore makes all subsequent anonymous responses the same nondisclosing `404` with `Cache-Control: no-store`, even while the cutover row remains enabled or session revocation is still being batch-materialized. A request racing the fence may return data only if its final serialization transaction acquired the ordered organization lock before the fence transaction; the fence cannot report committed first and then allow the stale response. Authenticated retained-data reads continue only through their ordinary exact-scope retention/erasure authorization and never through public possession. Tests hold poll, typing, widget-script, hosted-page, and token reads across cancellation and begin-erasure commits and prove no post-fence payload, timing distinction, or shared-cache reuse.

Parent Directory lifecycle is part of that live gate. Every public read/admission, authenticated public-chat mutation, provider/publication/approval grant, queue claim, strict desired-provider result, and scheduler install/fire takes the shared tenant-lifecycle lock and organization lock in the global order, then exact-loads the tenant and organization and requires both `is_active=true` and `deleted_at IS NULL`; a missing/inactive/deleted parent closes public authority even if widget/link/cutover rows remain. First link, prepare, enable, and restore use the same lock/re-read contract. Every ordinary organization point read/update predicates the organization ID by the authenticated **stored** tenant ID; a caller-supplied tenant ID is only consistency input and a mismatch is rejected before authorization or serialization. `organizations.tenant_id` is immutable through ordinary create/update/undo commands in this release. A true organization reparent is not implemented here: it requires a separately reviewed platform migration, and operators must create an independently authorized destination organization rather than changing this scalar.

Unauthenticated customer-account signup is also a parent/role writer and cannot trust independent body coordinates. Under the shared tenant-lifecycle and exact organization locks, it loads the organization by `(id,tenant_id)`, requires both parents active/nondeleted and signup enabled, derives the tenant from that row, and selects a default role that is active and belongs to that same tenant/organization scope before creating either user or assignment. Entity constraints/OLD+NEW guards reject a customer user, role assignment, or organization tuple whose stored tenant/organization coordinates disagree. A tenant-A ID paired with an organization-B ID, inactive/deleted parent, cross-organization role, and races with parent deactivation produce no user, credential, session, role assignment, event, or email.

Reconciled OLD+NEW triggers cover `organizations.tenant_id`, Organization **and Tenant** lifecycle columns, and `organizations.noli_org_id`, and require the distinct child-writer, organization-lifecycle, or tenant-lifecycle transaction attestation. Ordinary Directory organization deactivate/soft-delete/undo/redo holds shared tenant plus exclusive organization authority through the final indexed zero-state check and commit. Tenant lifecycle holds the tenant lock exclusively through one indexed relational probe across all child organizations and its row CAS/commit; because every child authority creator holds that same lock shared, a first link/admission/organization create cannot appear between the zero proof and parent commit. It returns `409 public_chat_cleanup_required` while the organization—or any child organization of a tenant—has a Noli link, cutover/locator/sidecar/strict/transport state, public/active widget, or incomplete cancellation/GDPR acknowledgment. This release defines no unbounded tenant fan-out shortcut: each child scope must complete cancellation/GDPR, widget cleanup, and zero-state unlink first; the tenant probe is bounded/index-backed and the parent operation does not mutate children. The exact operation-bound organization-erasure final transaction is the sole guarded delete lane while residue is being removed. Direct SQL, ID-only organization updates, caller-selected tenant authorization, tenant reparenting, opposite-order parent locking, and restoring a parent over stale/deleted authority fail. Tests use a tenant-B manager plus a tenant-A organization UUID against every point/update command, attempt direct and delayed `organizations.tenant_id` mutation, pause tenant/organization zero checks against first link, first admission, widget activation, strict-row creation, and child-organization creation; race multi-organization tenant deactivate/delete/undo with provider return, publication, scheduler recreation, cancellation, erasure, final unlink, and post-erasure restore; and prove a waiting writer re-reads the committed parent and an attempted organization→tenant lock order is rejected without deadlock.

The runtime owner is the compatibility build's shared public-chat gate, not an environment switch in one route. Public start/append/poll/typing/widget/page return the uniform nondisclosing `404` while disabled, link-unconfirmed, cancellation-requested, or covered by an active organization-deleting fence; authenticated public-chat mutations return `409 public_chat_cutover_required` except exact unlinked private-widget-only CRUD and the operation-bound pre-launch repair command; workers/scheduler firings start no side effect and record/defer to the durable gate; authenticated transcript reads remain available only under their retained-data authorization. The build exposes its exact contract/runtime generation separately from process health. Deployment may keep the reconciler/workers alive in degraded mode, but public-chat readiness remains closed until startup verifies all enabled scopes and active schedule receipts. Production Hetzner controller/drain proof must show zero app/MCP replicas, API handlers, scheduler sync/subscriber/local/execute workers, queue workers, GDPR routes, widget/settings/Assistant writers, host/container cron/timers, and callbacks from every pre-contract build before the enable receipt is accepted. The no-rollback boundary is the first successful installation of this contract's persistent writer/Noli/widget/scheduler guards or hooks, even when zero sidecar rows exist: every later recovery is a forward fix using a compatible disabled-gate build. No pre-contract revision may be redeployed after that point.

The generation guards are defense in depth for delayed database writers; signed deployment drain proof remains mandatory because a pre-contract process could otherwise enqueue external transport before reaching a guarded write. The exact preinstall and scoped receipt variants, controller adapters, and launch ordering are defined below; every receipt digest and nonce is consumed through the durable ledger rather than relying on a cutover row that unlink can delete.

### CustomerPublicChatReceiptConsumption (`customer_public_chat_receipt_consumptions`)

This global operational-security ledger is the replay tombstone for signed control-plane artifacts. It has no tenant CRUD/query-engine route, search/export surface, or application response serializer, and it survives cutover-row unlink and ordinary organization cleanup.

- `id`: UUID primary key generated by PostgreSQL.
- `receipt_kind`: exactly `preinstall_drain | bootstrap_drain | deployment_drain | runtime_start | runtime_termination | noli_link_attestation | noli_link_confirmation | noli_link_cancellation_tombstone | noli_link_cancellation_request`.
- `receipt_digest` and `nonce_digest`: required `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` values over the complete canonical signed artifact and RFC 8785 bytes of the injective tuple `['noli:public-chat-receipt-nonce:v1', environmentId, nonce]` respectively. `environmentId` is ASCII matching `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}`. Each nonce is exactly 16 random bytes encoded as exactly 22 base64url-without-padding characters; alternate alphabets/padding/lengths are rejected. Every signed artifact uses its own nonce; a bootstrap-drain artifact binds but never copies the Noli-attestation nonce.
- `issuer`, `signing_key_id`, `environment_id`, and `scope_digest`: bounded required strings. `scope_digest` is domain-separated over exactly one discriminated replay scope: environment-only, organization (`environmentId,organizationId,tenantId,noliOrganizationId`), or user (`environmentId,localUserId`, with no invented Noli organization). Raw tenant, user, Noli, or provider data is not retained here.
- `cutover_operation_id` and `writer_generation`: nullable UUIDs, required together for `deployment_drain` and `noli_link_confirmation`, and forbidden for every other receipt kind.
- Link claims are durable rather than recoverable only from a deletable cutover row. Nullable `noli_link_reservation_id` UUID, positive `noli_link_registry_version`, and `noli_link_attestation_digest` are required together for all four Noli-link kinds and forbidden otherwise. For `noli_link_attestation`, the attestation digest equals `receipt_digest`; confirmation and both cancellation kinds name the exact earlier attestation. A unique partial `(environment_id, noli_link_reservation_id) WHERE receipt_kind IN ('noli_link_attestation','noli_link_cancellation_tombstone')` makes either CRM attestation consumption or a signed never-consumed tombstone the single permanent winner. Confirmation requires the existing attestation row plus pending cutover operation/generation. A tombstone is allowed only when attestation consumption has not won. A consumed-link `noli_link_cancellation_request` instead requires the existing attestation row and additional `link_cancellation_operation_id` UUID plus allow-listed `link_cancellation_reason`; unique `(environment_id,noli_link_reservation_id,link_cancellation_operation_id) WHERE receipt_kind='noli_link_cancellation_request'` preserves one exact signed request across cutover deletion and rejects changed replay without competing with the attestation row. Those two fields are forbidden for every other kind.
- Preinstall claims use two discriminated rows of the existing `preinstall_drain` kind, not an invented receipt kind. Nullable UUID `preinstall_fence_id`, bounded `preinstall_stage` (`migration_authorized | scheduler_cutover_complete`), `preinstall_authorization_digest`, `generic_scheduler_cutover_journal_digest`, `event_fanout_registry_seed_digest`, and `preinstall_guard_fingerprint_digest` are forbidden for every other kind. Fence and stage are required for both preinstall rows. The authorization stage requires all four digest coordinates null. The completion stage requires all four lowercase SHA-256 digests: its authorization digest exact-references the same-environment/same-fence `migration_authorized` row, its journal digest binds the terminal root-controller `generic-scheduler-cutover-v1` state, its fan-out seed digest binds the terminal exact event registry preflight/seed/verify state, and its guard-fingerprint digest is written only by the final first-guard transaction from the exact installed guard/ACL/function family. Both use environment-only scope and forbid operation/writer fields. Unique `(environment_id,preinstall_fence_id,preinstall_stage)` and unique `(environment_id,preinstall_authorization_digest) WHERE preinstall_stage='scheduler_cutover_complete'` prevent a second completion or cross-fence pairing. The customers entity migration, all three snapshots, guard fingerprint, and generated checks/indexes include these columns.
- Runtime claims are retained in typed columns so replay and later fan-out verification do not depend on a caller-supplied raw artifact. Nullable `runtime_instance_id` UUID, positive `runtime_generation`, UUID `runtime_deployment_generation`, bounded manifest `runtime_role`, bounded normalized PostgreSQL `runtime_database_principal`, `runtime_start_attestation_digest`, `runtime_build_id`, `runtime_image_digest`, `runtime_controller_identity_digest`, bounded `runtime_origin_fingerprint`, nonnegative `runtime_redis_client_slot_count`, and `runtime_redis_client_slot_capability_manifest_digest` are required together for `runtime_start` and `runtime_termination` and forbidden otherwise. Data-plane `runtime_start` rows after first guard installation additionally require `preinstall_completion_receipt_digest`, positive `preinstall_consumed_journal_generation`, and lowercase SHA-256 `preinstall_consumed_journal_digest`; they are signed into the controller artifact and exact-reference the same-environment completion-stage row/guard fingerprint. The preinstall migration one-shot requires all three null and has no data-plane capability. The slot count/digest exact-match the signed fixed-cardinality array sorted by manifest ordinal, whose closed entries are `{manifestOrdinal,role,clientSlotId,clientKind,capabilityDigest}`; zero-slot roles use the generated empty-array digest, and raw capabilities never enter PostgreSQL. The origin fingerprint is the schema-versioned SHA-256 digest of canonical origin, fixed operator path/template version, and checked-in policy. A start row also has controller-generated challenge digest plus nullable `runtime_claimed_at`. For `runtime_start`, attestation digest equals `receipt_digest`, scope is environment-only, terminal fields are null, and controller registrar freshly inserts it unclaimed only after exact root `consumed` state for data-plane roles. Its sole update is exact null→database-time claim CAS when `session_user`/challenge/role/deployment match; afterward immutable. Every start gets fresh principal/secret; unique principal and `(environment_id,runtime_instance_id,runtime_generation)` indexes prevent reuse. `runtime_termination` is also environment-only, has unique `(environment_id,runtime_instance_id,runtime_generation,receipt_kind)`, requires the typed terminal fields, and exact-matches the one start including the slot count/capability-manifest digest and three preinstall-consumption coordinates; it proves process death, never a tenant/user authorization. Each consuming capability separately exact-locks and rederives its own subject/scope/fence and may reference that one death row only when its frozen runtime identity matches. Thus a generic-scheduler SQL capability joins its own claimed runtime-start row and proves the controller's post-CAS consumed-root attestation without filesystem/root authority. Crash after consumed CAS but before insertion resumes by re-reading root and issuing one fresh signed start; a pre-CAS, changed-root, cross-completion, or replayed artifact cannot claim.
- `consumed_at`: required database-time timestamp.
- Durable control reservation: every non-runtime receipt additionally requires deterministic `control_reservation_id` plus positive `control_slot_ordinal`; runtime start/termination forbid both. They exact-reference one `policy_kind='control_reservation'` anchor below whose generated slot manifest maps that ordinal to exactly this receipt kind/scope/operation plus `preinstallStageOrNull` and whose consumed bitmap is changed in the same transaction as the INSERT. Unique `(control_reservation_id,control_slot_ordinal)` prevents cross-operation or second-peer consumption. The sole initial-install exception is not unreserved: before entering the preinstall fence, the controller fsyncs a deterministic `PreinstallControlReservationV1` root-store record; after the queue/scheduler/customers tables exist but before any persistent guard/cutover mutation, the one-shot capability atomically creates the matching database control anchor, inserts the authenticated `migration_authorized` preinstall-drain row, and consumes the manifest ordinal whose stage is exactly `migration_authorized` in the same transaction; the other fixed ordinal is exactly `scheduler_cutover_complete`, and every non-preinstall slot has stage null. A root-store/database mismatch, second initial reservation, or crash replay is fatal/exact-idempotent rather than authority to synthesize capacity.

Unique constraints on `receipt_digest` and on `nonce_digest` make differently signed reuse under another valid issuer/key fail across the environment replay domain; the kind-specific claim indexes additionally prevent a fresh signature/nonce from aliasing one runtime generation, database principal generation, or Noli reservation. Controller-only receipt capabilities insert-or-verify the exact ledger row before or in the transaction that creates/restarts a disabled cutover row, stores a deployment receipt, registers a start/termination fact, or accepts a verified Noli artifact; the sole first-guard chicken-and-egg exception is the controller-verified, fenced one-shot migrator lane defined below; a conflict in kind/scope/operation/generation/typed claims is fatal. Runtime roles cannot insert any receipt. `runtime_start` is deliberately stricter: the controller registrar must freshly insert the unclaimed tuple; only its one claim-time null→timestamp CAS is mutable, and any uniqueness/conflict/replayed challenge fails the second process. A downstream strict-sweep job reference may exact-verify an already-committed termination receipt through the schedule's same-epoch proof rather than consuming it again.

Runtime receipts have a bounded controller-only compaction exception; link/preinstall/deployment rows retain their stronger permanent replay policy and ordinary identity erasure/receipt expiry never delete any consumption row. Permanence is finite rather than unaccounted: the one environment control-plane policy row below hard-limits permanent control-reservation anchors to 50,000 rows/100 MiB, non-runtime receipt peer rows to 200,000/800 MiB, and cancellation-acknowledgment peer rows to 50,000/200 MiB; it admits at most 5,000 new anchors, 10,000 new non-runtime receipts, and 5,000 acknowledgments per rolling database-time hour, with exact retries consuming no additional count. Before a link, preinstall, deployment, cancellation, or erasure control operation can expose authority, close ingress, or destructively finalize state, its fixed capability creates one deterministic generation-fenced reservation anchor under the environment registrar lock with immutable kind/scope/operation/manifest digest, exact receipt/ack slot counts, and zero consumed bitmaps. Generated manifests are bounded to eight slots. Preinstall has two receipt slots; each scoped deployment anchor has its exact receipt slots; the consumed-link envelope has exactly four receipt slots (`noli_link_attestation`, `bootstrap_drain`, `noli_link_confirmation`, `noli_link_cancellation_request`) plus one acknowledgment slot; and the mutually exclusive never-consumed envelope has one cancellation-tombstone receipt plus one acknowledgment. Completion/signing/settlement consumes only a kind-matched named slot and remains legal at the cap; a new unreserved control operation fails before its first fence or destructive mutation. Anchor insertion charges its own permanent row plus reserves the full peer row/byte envelope atomically; slot consumption moves that exact peer charge reserved→consumed without seeking capacity. This launch version deliberately performs no compaction of anchors, permanent non-runtime replay tombstones, or signed acknowledgments: 80% usage fails the deployment/link capacity readiness gate with operator warning, and reaching a hard cap requires a separately versioned reviewed compactor/migration before further new control operations while existing reserved completion remains available.

Controller runtime policy separately admits at most ten new runtime generations per manifested role and 100 environment-wide per rolling database-time hour, with exact response-loss retries consuming no additional count. Under the environment registrar lock, each new start reserves one start plus one future termination slot; the runtime class has a hard 160,000-row/640-MiB encoded bound (80,000 starts at the exact 4-KiB per-row maximum), while termination/compaction of already reserved starts remains legal at the bound. The named `customer_public_chat_runtime_receipt_policies` entity below owns fixed runtime-role rows, the one control-plane row, and all 49 immutable Redis-client-lineage rows. Start issuance requires exactly prior `runtime_issued_generation_high_water+1` and atomically advances that never-rewound high-water with rate and reserved/consumed charges before inserting the unclaimed receipt; after issuance, no artifact at or below the high-water can be newly inserted except exact-verifying the still-retained same digest. Only registrar/compaction/control-reservation functions mutate policy. The customers migration adds `(receipt_kind,environment_id,runtime_role,runtime_generation,id)` for bounded runtime candidates plus control-kind/reservation/ack indexes and fingerprints every policy join.

At least 30 database-time days after the later start/termination consumption time, `public_chat_compact_runtime_receipt_v1` may process any indexed generation only when the principal is absent from `pg_roles`, has zero `pg_stat_activity`, the exact start has its one termination row or a controller-aborted-unclaimed proof, and indexed probes prove zero lease, binding, execution, acknowledgment, domain, or same-runtime reference in any scope. An older blocked generation does not prevent later eligible deletion. Before database deletion, the controller root store fsync-CASes a deterministic compaction operation over role, generation, start/termination digests, prior root, and next sequence into its fixed per-role Merkle accumulator. The database transaction exact-matches that root transition, advances policy `runtime_compaction_sequence`/root/count, deletes only the matched start and optional one termination row, releases their reserved physical charge, and advances the sparse inspection cursor; a stale sequence/root or repeated different digest fails. Registrar functions accept a new start only as the next generation above `runtime_issued_generation_high_water`, so deleting unique rows cannot make an older signed artifact or nonce reusable; role/principal names are never recreated. A controller sweep inspects at most 1,000 indexed generations per tick but commits one pair per transaction and advances past live-reference blockers, wrapping its policy cursor. Crash between root-store and database CAS resumes the same operation by exact old/new root and sequence; crash before the root CAS deletes nothing. Thus retained runtime rows are bounded by the 30-day rate envelope and hard capacity while historical replay protection compresses to fixed per-role state without head-of-line blocking. Apart from claim and this exact compaction lane, rows remain immutable and DELETE is forbidden. Tests replay raw nonces/signatures before and after compaction, hit rate/row/byte boundaries, retain the earliest generation through later churn in each scope shape, compact later generations noncontiguously across crashes, reject issued-high-water/root/sequence rollback or cross-role roots, and accelerate more than 30 days of restart churn while bounding receipt rows/root-store/policy state.

### CustomerPublicChatRuntimeReceiptPolicy (`customer_public_chat_runtime_receipt_policies`)

This eighth internal control entity is the bounded mutable owner for runtime-receipt issuance/compaction, permanent control-plane receipt/ack capacity, immutable per-operation reservation anchors, and the database mirror of the Redis-client root journal; it is not a signed-artifact row. It has no tenant CRUD/query/search/export/API serializer, ORM relationship, or FK. Each environment has between 50 and 82 fixed rows—one `policy_kind='runtime_role'` row for each exact generated runtime role (at most 32), exactly one `policy_kind='control_plane'` row, and exactly 49 `policy_kind='redis_client_lineage'` rows for the immutable launch manifest—and at most 50,000 generation-fenced `policy_kind='control_reservation'` rows beneath the fixed control row. The generated customers migration defines and snapshots their columns/checks/indexes only. Under the first-install fence, audited unconditional reconciliation installs the fixed functions and insert-or-exact-verifies all manifest-dependent fixed rows in the explicit uninitialized root shape before any runtime, control, or Redis-client claim; bounded anchors are created only by the reservation capability.

- Identity is UUIDv5 under RFC URL namespace `6ba7b811-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8`. Its exact UTF-8 name is literal `noli:public-chat-runtime-policy:v1:` followed by base64url-no-padding of RFC8785-JCS UTF-8 for exactly `[environmentId,'control_plane']`, `[environmentId,'runtime_role',runtimeRole]`, `[environmentId,'redis_client_lineage',manifestOrdinalDecimal,redisClientRole,redisClientSlotId,redisClientKind]`, or `[environmentId,'control_reservation',reservationGenerationDecimal,operationKind,fenceIdOrNull,scopeDigest,manifestDigest]` according to the checked discriminator `runtime_role | control_plane | redis_client_lineage | control_reservation`. `runtime_role` is required only for a runtime-role row. A Redis-lineage row instead requires immutable generated `redis_client_role`, `redis_client_slot_id`, `redis_client_kind`, and `redis_client_manifest_ordinal` (`1..49`) and forbids every runtime/control/reservation-only field. Unique partial indexes enforce one control row, one row per runtime role, one Redis-lineage row per `(environment_id,redis_client_role,redis_client_slot_id)`, one per `(environment_id,redis_client_manifest_ordinal)`, and one reservation anchor per exact typed operation/fence/scope. Runtime rows own `runtime_issued_generation_high_water`, `runtime_compaction_sequence`, `runtime_compacted_pair_count`, per-role rolling-hour start count, reserved/consumed rows+bytes, and cursor epoch as nonnegative bigints; `runtime_compacted_root_digest` is nullable only before first compaction. The fixed control row owns the environment-wide runtime rolling-hour start count/window, separate anchor/non-runtime-receipt/ack rolling-hour counts, reserved/consumed rows+bytes, monotonic reservation generation allocator, 80%-warning state, immutable hard ceilings, and the Redis mirror columns named below. A reservation row exact-matches its parent control-row generation and requires deterministic ID, positive reservation generation, kind, environment/scope/operation/fence coordinates, manifest digest, `0..8` receipt/ack slot counts, immutable per-ordinal kind+`preinstall_stage_or_null` mapping, reserved peer row/byte charges, zero-or-monotonic consumed bitmaps, and database creation time; every unrelated runtime/Redis/aggregate field is null. Canonical database times own each rate window and runtime last issuance/compaction/cursor; generated golden vectors cover all four names, null fence, delimiter-looking components, ordinal/generation boundaries, and cross-kind non-aliasing; row/byte ceilings and role/control/lineage manifest digests are immutable checked coordinates.
- The control row's Redis mirror uses fixed-width scalar columns only: nonnegative bigint `redis_client_tail_sequence` and `redis_client_checkpoint_sequence`; nonnull lowercase `sha256:` digests `redis_client_tail_root_digest`, `redis_client_checkpoint_root_digest`, `redis_client_checkpoint_lineage_map_digest`, `redis_client_global_state_digest`, `redis_client_capability_delivery_state_digest`, `redis_client_runtime_egress_fence_state_digest`, `redis_client_helper_gate_accumulator_digest`, `redis_client_retirement_state_digest`, and `redis_client_checkpoint_terminal_accumulator_digest`; nonnegative `redis_client_helper_gate_high_water`; boolean `redis_client_root_initialized`, nonnegative `redis_client_keyring_generation`, and nonnull `redis_client_keyring_digest`. Its readiness projection is the all-null or all-nonnull eight-field family: positive bigint `redis_client_readiness_generation`; lowercase `sha256:` digests `redis_client_readiness_verification_digest`, `redis_client_readiness_completion_receipt_digest`, `redis_client_readiness_run_attestation_digest`, and `redis_client_readiness_manifest_digest`; canonical `varchar(40)` `redis_client_readiness_server_run_id`; positive bigint `redis_client_readiness_controller_generation`; and database `timestamptz` `redis_client_readiness_published_at`. All eight are null at genesis and before first publication. Only `readiness_complete` writes/replaces the complete family from the matching helper-control current-attestation object; its prepared transition exact-matches the old family, and the public-chat deployment gate requires every value to equal the controller's current manifest/generation, current Redis run and helper-control digest. Run change or any partial/stale family fails readiness without clearing history. At first-install genesis, `redis_client_root_initialized=false`, keyring generation is zero, keyring digest is the generated uninitialized digest, and both active and retiring key triplets are all null. Initialized state requires `redis_client_root_initialized=true`, positive keyring generation, exactly one active key ID equal to literal `k` plus that generation's canonical decimal in `varchar(20)`, its key digest, and `numeric(29,0)` nonce high-water in `0..79228162514264337593543950335`, plus an all-null or all-nonnull retiring key ID/digest/high-water triplet of the same types; if present, the retiring ID is `k` plus the immediately prior key generation. First activation is a one-shot tail-anchored `0 -> 1` CAS that installs recovery-verified key `k1` at nonce zero and flips initialized true. Rotation is a single tail-anchored CAS that requires initialized state and no retiring key, moves the exact active triplet to retiring, installs fresh key `k<generation+1>` at nonce zero, increments keyring generation, and changes the keyring/global digests; retiring-key removal is legal only after an exact root/database zero-reference proof and clears that whole triplet. A second rotation while a retiring key remains, nonce decrement/reuse/overflow, key-ID/generation mismatch, partial triplet, or digest mismatch fails closed. Every nonce allocation increment-one CASes the exact active key ID/high-water and root tail before bytes can be sealed or returned. The Redis-lineage row likewise contains no JSON/array/TOAST state: nonnegative `redis_client_generation_high_water`; two ordered scalar claim slots, each an all-null or all-nonnull `{claim_id UUID, claim_generation bigint, claim_state, current_state_digest}` family; nullable `redis_client_active_claim_id`; and nonnegative terminal-accumulator sequence/count plus its nonnull root digest, with generated `count=sequence` because every step compacts exactly one claim. Slot 1 precedes slot 2, generations are positive/distinct/increasing and at most the high-water, state is exactly `reserved | registered_current | retired_unproved`, and active ID is null or identifies the sole `reserved|registered_current` slot. With both slots null and no staged terminal capsule, allocation writes generation `highWater+1` into slot 1. With slot 1 `retired_unproved` and slot 2 null, only its immediate successor `highWater+1` may allocate into slot 2; no allocation is legal while slot 2 exists. Terminal compaction atomically advances the accumulator and then: clears a sole terminal slot; clears terminal slot 2 while preserving slot 1; or, when terminal slot 1 is removed while slot 2 remains, copies the complete slot-2 family into slot 1 and clears slot 2 in the same CAS. Active ID follows the moved claim, high-water never rewinds, a hole is never persisted, and allocation cannot race the one-capsule barrier. All 49 launch rows and immutable identity columns are retained forever.
- The registrar creation/issuance capability alone may increment the role generation/rate/capacity fields and the fixed environment runtime-rate counter while atomically inserting the matching start receipt. The compaction capability alone may advance runtime sequence/root/count/cursor and decrement the exact reserved/consumed charge while deleting the matched runtime receipt pair. The control-reserve capability locks the fixed row, allocates the next generation, derives the complete typed slot manifest and exact charge, advances anchor/peer rate and reserved counters, and inserts-or-exact-verifies the deterministic anchor. Disjoint consume capabilities lock that anchor and fixed row, exact-match one zero bit and peer kind/scope/operation/stage (stage null except the two fixed preinstall ordinals), atomically INSERT the receipt/ack with the same reservation ID+ordinal, set that bit, and move its pre-reserved charge to consumed; they can never release/reuse a permanent slot or consume another operation's anchor. Redis root anchoring has a closed database discriminator derived from the authenticated prepared record, never from caller-selected scope: `global_anchor` locks and CASes only the control row and accepts exactly the literal closed global-kind registry below—including all capability, runtime-egress, AEAD/keyring/emergency-credential, helper/readiness/admin, and retirement create/reference/compact variants—with each kind's exact OLD→NEW/null/artifact/changed-path rules; no independently maintained narrower subtype list exists; `lineage_anchor` locks the control row plus the one manifest-derived lineage row for allocation/challenge/identity/retire/close/unproved-fence/per-lineage compaction; `command_anchor` is available only inside the fixed bind/result/fence registrar and locks the control row, then that one manifest-derived lineage row, then the owning protected row; and `checkpoint` locks the control row plus all 49 lineage rows in manifest order. Every variant exact-CASes `(tail sequence,tail root,prepared-record digest and applicable old scalar fields)` to the one authenticated next state, and a null/mismatched owner or any transition that would touch a row outside its fixed variant is rejected. None accepts caller-selected generation, counters, bytes, cursor, envelope, bitmap, digest, role, slot, ordinal, subject, transition kind, or policy kind. OLD→NEW guards, fixed search paths, exact owner/ACLs, and reconciliation reject direct DML, decrement/rewind, manifest drift, cross-kind/role/slot transition, compaction without root-store proof, issuance without its start row, or peer insertion without its anchor transition.
- Indexes are unique policy scope, `(environment_id,runtime_compaction_cursor_generation,runtime_role)` for runtime rows, the two Redis-lineage uniqueness indexes above, `(environment_id,control_reservation_generation)` plus kind/scope/operation/fence indexes for anchors, and unique peer `(control_reservation_id,control_slot_ordinal)` joins on receipt and acknowledgment tables. The generated customers migration creates only the checked enum/null matrix, exact `varchar(20)` Redis client-ID columns on owning entities, and all fixed scalar mirror columns/checks/indexes; all three generated snapshots exact-match that generator-owned DDL. While the controller's first-install fence is held and before any claim capability exists, the audited unconditional reconciliation installs/fingerprints the four fixed SECURITY DEFINER transition functions and insert-or-exact-verifies the one control row, all generated runtime-role rows, and all 49 lineage rows. The seed uses deterministic empty/genesis tail, checkpoint, global, checkpoint-lineage-map, helper, retirement, capability, runtime-egress, and accumulator digests with the explicit uninitialized keyring null shape, all-null eight-field readiness family, generation-zero/null emergency credential+ACL-file state, and readiness-accumulator genesis above; it never invents the controller's first key or emergency credential. After its `KeyringCandidateIntentV1` is fsynced before any recovery write, its exact copy is written/restore-tested, and the intent reaches `material_verified`, the controller fsyncs the one-shot prepared first-key activation and invokes the fenced `global_anchor` CAS to initialize `k1`; only after that commit marker does the exact stopped-Redis `emergency_credential_activate` preparation/file/CAS/start sequence initialize emergency generation 1, and only after its commit marker may the bootstrap admin sequence begin. Neither transition publishes a runtime start/capability or readiness. A crash with database-old/root-prepared discards or exact-retries activation; database-new/root-prepared completes only its commit marker; any partial seed, missing function/fingerprint, mismatched genesis, or initialized database without the matching recoverable root key blocks every claim and readiness. Readiness reconciles every runtime count/charge to retained starts/terminations; the control tail/checkpoint/keyring/global/capability/runtime-egress/helper/retirement/terminal digests to the root-store generation; the stored `redis_client_checkpoint_lineage_map_digest` to the 49-row projection at `redis_client_checkpoint_sequence`, then deterministically replays the anchored tail to require exact equality with the current 49 database lineage rows; environment rate count to all role issuance windows; and every control anchor/bitmap/reserved/consumed charge to the complete permanent receipt/ack ledgers. Tests create every fixed row and anchor kind; crash/retry every DDL/function/seed/first-key/emergency-activation/ACL-file/container-start boundary and prove no claim in uninitialized or partial state; race issuance/reservation/slot consumption and every global/lineage/command/checkpoint transition; lose each response; crash on both sides of every root/database CAS; wrap each nonce/rate window and sparse cursor; hold an old runtime/client generation while compacting later ones; rotate with live retiring-key references and reject a second rotation; exercise nonce high-water boundaries and rollback; reach 80% and each exact hard boundary; exercise the four-plus-one confirmed-link and one-plus-one never-consumed envelopes; prove an unreserved/wrong-slot operation cannot begin; and prove reserved completion/signing remains legal at saturation.

Every signed schema in this contract uses one canonical byte contract. Input is parsed with duplicate-key detection and schema-validated as I-JSON: UTF-8 only, no lone surrogate/non-finite value, no unknown key, timestamps as canonical UTC RFC3339 strings, UUIDs/lowercase digests in their specified textual forms, and numbers restricted to schema-declared safe integers. Signature input is RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme bytes of the exact object **without** the `signature` member; Ed25519 output is exactly 64 bytes encoded base64url without padding in the `signature` member. `receipt_digest` is SHA-256 over RFC 8785 bytes of the complete validated object **including** that signature; `nonce_digest` uses the separately defined domain string. JCS performs no hidden Unicode normalization, so every non-ASCII schema string must already be NFC or is rejected. Unknown/duplicate members, alternate base64 padding/alphabet, noncanonical date/UUID/digest spellings, and cross-kind audiences fail before signature verification. TypeScript and the Noli/control-plane implementation share golden and negative arbitrary-object fixtures, not only one happy-path sample.

### CustomerPublicChatCancellationAcknowledgment (`customer_public_chat_cancellation_acknowledgments`)

This global outbound-control ledger owns acknowledgment bytes across cutover unlink and organization erasure. It has no tenant CRUD/query/search/export surface, no ORM relationship/FK, and can be read only by the fleet-authenticated status service through its exact reservation/operation key.

- Identity/claim: deterministic UUIDv5 `id`, bounded `environment_id`, UUID `noli_link_reservation_id`, positive `noli_link_registry_version`, `noli_link_attestation_digest`, exact consumed `noli_link_cancellation_request_digest`, UUID `cancellation_operation_id`, allow-listed `cancellation_reason`, organization-scope digest, allow-listed terminal `result` (`never_consumed | zero_state_complete | gdpr_complete`), exact `completion_receipt_digest`/database time, deterministic `control_reservation_id`, and positive `control_slot_ordinal` are required. For `never_consumed`, the request digest names the cancellation-tombstone ledger row; otherwise it names the consumed-link request row. The reservation slot must be the one ack ordinal in the matching link envelope and flips consumed atomically with pending INSERT. Unique `(environment_id,noli_link_reservation_id,cancellation_operation_id)`, unique `(control_reservation_id,control_slot_ordinal)`, and unique controller `signing_request_id` prevent takeover.
- Database completion proof: the application cannot supply an opaque completion digest. One audited `SECURITY DEFINER` finalizer owns both the terminal state transition/deletion and pending-row insertion; no caller-managed “insert now, delete later” sequence exists. It derives immutable typed columns `completion_proof_version='spec-065-v1'`, `completion_proof_kind`, operation/reservation/registry/scope/writer-generation coordinates, canonical bounded zero/GDPR count tuple, source tombstone-or-request ledger digest, source GDPR/zero-state proof digest where applicable, `completion_proved_at=clock_timestamp()`, and `completion_receipt_digest` over that exact tuple. For `never_consumed` it proves the mutually exclusive tombstone and absence of attestation/cutover authority. For `zero_state_complete` it proves the consumed cancellation request plus fresh indexed zero counts across every contract/legacy/full-reference/transport predicate under the global locks, inserts the proof/pending row, and itself clears/deletes the exact link/cutover authority. For `gdpr_complete` it proves that request plus the exact completed GDPR operation/fence and every required scanner/downstream/transport zero receipt, inserts proof/pending, and itself performs the final declared scoped authority/organization deletion. Caller-provided values for any derived field are forbidden. If any declared final deletion/update is omitted, conflicts, or leaves same-ID authority, the function raises and no proof row commits. Direct table INSERT privilege is revoked from app roles, and the guard accepts only this function-owned path.
- Pending artifact: `unsigned_artifact` is at most 4 KiB canonical jsonb containing the immutable acknowledgment **base claims** without controller issuer, signing key ID, nonce, or signature, plus recomputed `unsigned_artifact_digest`, random signing request ID, and database `created_at`. It contains the UUID coordinates Noli must verify but no user identity, transcript, prompt, config, or provider data. The never-consumed tombstone transaction or final zero-state/GDPR-completion transaction insert-or-verifies this pending row **before** deleting cutover/organization state; a conflict aborts completion. The row therefore survives even when every scoped ActionLog/cutover row is gone.
- Signed artifact: nullable `signed_artifact`, `signed_artifact_digest`, `controller_unsigned_artifact_digest`, `nonce_digest`, `signing_key_id`, and `signed_at` are all-or-none. The controller deterministically projects the stored base claims into the final signing object by adding its configured issuer, selected active acknowledgment key ID, and one controller-generated 128-bit nonce, then JCS-hashes and signs that object without its signature member. Only the controller principal's `public_chat_ack_commit_signed_v1` capability may CAS the exact pending row once after locking/rechecking fresh terminal evidence and proving the submitted object's base-claim projection byte-equals the stored base and both base/final-unsigned digests, audience, request ID, environment, key, nonce, and completion claims match. Pending insertion consumes the pre-reserved permanent acknowledgment slot; signing requires that same reservation and no new capacity. App/control/MCP/worker/scheduler roles have no CAS EXECUTE or direct DML. Thereafter every column is immutable and DELETE is forbidden in this launch contract. Lost signing responses use controller GET and the exact same request; GET to Noli returns the stored signed bytes, never re-signs or invents a nonce. Until controller-signed storage commits, CRM status remains nonterminal/quiescing.
- The global guard permits only the SECURITY-DEFINER terminal-finalizer/reserved pending INSERT lane and the controller-only pending→signed CAS lane; ordinary/GDPR cleanup cannot mutate it. The controller security-barrier view joins the retained tombstone/request consumption row, recomputes/exact-matches the typed completion tuple/digest, and freshly verifies no same-reservation/scope authority was recreated before returning a candidate. Reservation tombstones/cancellation state make such recreation illegal, but the check remains fail closed. A caller-written digest, row lacking source ledger evidence, or row without its exact pre-reserved control-policy slot is never insertable/signable. Rows are permanently retained in this launch version under the 50,000-row/200-MiB and 5,000-new/hour hard bounds above; key retirement additionally waits for zero verifier trust, and a future deletion/compaction lane requires a separately versioned proof preserving replay and byte identity. Tests call the finalizer then COMMIT/ROLLBACK/savepoint, inject omission/conflict at each final delete, forge completion digest/count/generation, attempt early or unreserved insertion with nonzero residue, crash before/after control reservation and atomic finalizer, race prohibited recreation/controller selection, complete controller signature/CAS at capacity, attempt hostile runtime CAS, lose POST/GET responses, rotate keys, hit rate/row/byte boundaries, and prove exact byte equality forever.

### CustomerPublicChatOperationUserBarrier (`customer_public_chat_operation_user_barriers`)

This tenth internal operational-security table bounds link/GDPR lifecycle coordination without ever holding an organization's complete user-fence set. It has no CRUD/query-engine/search/export/API serializer or ORM relationship/FK.

- `id` is a deterministic UUIDv5 over the exact environment, authority kind, operation ID, local organization/tenant, and local user. Required scalars are bounded `environment_id`, `authority_kind` (`cutover | gdpr_org`), UUID `operation_id`, `organization_id`, `tenant_id`, `local_user_id`, positive `barrier_generation`, bounded source-membership bitset (`association | notification_recipient | notification_sender | generic_lease` combinations), and database `created_at`.
- Unique `(authority_kind,operation_id,local_user_id)` and indexes `(local_user_id,authority_kind,operation_id)` plus `(authority_kind,operation_id,local_user_id)` make both lease admission and materialization/cleanup bounded. Insert is insert-or-exact-verify through the private-control barrier capability while that operation's persisted phase is active. A changed source bitset is monotonic OR under the same function; every other update is forbidden.
- A barrier is logically active only through an indexed exact join: `cutover` requires the same cutover row/operation with `user_barrier_phase IN ('materializing','sealed')`; `gdpr_org` requires the same `gdpr_org_subjects` deleting operation and matching typed `public_chat_user_barrier_proof`. Missing, malformed, ambiguous, or unreadable authority fails closed for a matching user. One terminal O(1) authority transition deactivates every row; physical DELETE is then allowed only through the keyset cleanup function under at most 32 sorted user fences and exact terminal evidence.

The guard owner alone owns the table. Runtime roles have no direct DML or broad SELECT. User-only lease creation calls a narrow existence capability under its authenticated user fence; private control can materialize/verify/purge only its exact current operation page. Tests cover a user in multiple active operations, forged operation/scope/generation, monotonic source union, cursor crash/replay, active-authority deletion rejection, O(1) terminalization with 100,000 barriers, and bounded post-terminal purge.

#### Durable digest contract

All uses of “keyed digest” in this contract share one implementation rather than ad hoc hashing. `PublicChatDigestService` accepts only an allow-listed domain and a schema-validated I-JSON value, NFC-validates strings, prepends the exact domain/version in a typed tuple, RFC-8785-canonicalizes it, and computes HMAC-SHA-256. Persistence is always paired `{ digest: 'hmac-sha256:<64 lowercase hex>', digestKeyId: '<bounded-id>' }`; missing/unknown key ID, alternate canonical bytes, or digest mismatch fails closed. The typed registry has distinct versioned domains for command payload/result, message body, provider input, public-prompt source/snapshot/config, legacy-identity source/result, inbox-rebuild source/result, ActionLog receipt metadata, metering request/account identity, and notification request/recipient/from/provider-account/template/subject/body. Each domain declares its exact discriminated tuple/schema and no raw byte/string shortcut exists, so a digest cannot cross purposes or silently omit an identity field. Raw HMAC keys, canonical customer text/address, and comparison failures are never logged.

Production config supplies a bounded key-ID→32-byte-secret map `CRM_PUBLIC_CHAT_DIGEST_KEYS_JSON` plus `CRM_PUBLIC_CHAT_DIGEST_ACTIVE_KEY_ID` from the CRM secret store. Every manifested role that computes or verifies one of these digests receives the same validated keyring; public/browser/Noli/controller responses never do. Rotation first installs an overlapping keyring everywhere, maintenance-demotes and verifies all roles, then switches the active ID for new rows. Existing rows are always verified with their recorded key ID. Readiness and retirement scan distinct referenced key IDs across message orders; every top-level and nested provider/prompt/metering/notification proof in reply jobs; command receipts; identity/inbox remediation records; and all nonterminal/retained state. The key-reference scanner schema-validates each bounded JSON identity and extracts every nested `digestKeyId`; an unknown/unparseable identity blocks readiness rather than disappearing from the count. An old key cannot be removed until that count is zero or an explicit operation rewrites only a digest whose original canonical source is still authoritatively available and exact-verifies before/after. Golden fixtures cover every typed tuple and nested notification identity across TypeScript roles. Restart, mixed-old/new rows, response-loss retry, in-flight provider/publication/notification, and missing/unknown/revoked-key tests fail closed without duplicating, leaking, or publishing stale work.

Permanent namespace accounting deliberately does **not** depend on a rotatable secret. `slug_owner_scope_digest`, `retired_locator_scope_digest`, and `legacy_collision_set_digest` are `sha256:<hex>` over fixed domain-separated RFC-8785 tuples of high-entropy CRM environment/service, local organization, tenant, widget/operation, and sorted claimant UUID coordinates as applicable; Noli identity is excluded from the owner-budget tuple. These values provide stable equality/accounting, not secrecy, and are never treated as authentication. Public locator digests and high-entropy visitor-token hashes retain their separately defined unkeyed domains. Golden fixtures pin every domain, canonical byte sequence, HMAC/SHA output, and key ID across TypeScript packages and restarts.

Three non-interchangeable signed drain schemas close the authority chicken-and-egg boundaries:

- `PreinstallDrainReceiptV1` is an environment-wide two-stage discriminated artifact and contains no organization, tenant, cutover-operation, or writer-generation field. Both stages' exact bounded canonical JSON contains contract/version/stage/purpose, deployment provider and environment ID, exact audience `crm-public-chat-preinstall-v1`, complete checked-in service-role-manifest digest, required compatible build/commit/image digest, controller-held maintenance-fence ID, sorted observed container/process/systemd-timer/cron/callback identities with build/image and terminal-or-allowed status/time, observation/database-comparison time, `expiresAt` no more than 15 minutes later, a fresh 128-bit nonce, issuer, signing-key ID, and Ed25519 signature. Stage `migration_authorized` contains no scheduler journal or fan-out registry seed digest and is required through `--public-chat-preinstall-drain-receipt <path>` before generated DDL or seed begins. While it is fresh, the root-local controller verifies it, the still-held live fence, and inventory, then atomically creates the root journal's `authorized` state and returns a one-shot peer-bound migration claim. The fence must remain continuously held even if the initial artifact later expires. After the exact scheduler seed/cleanup and fan-out registry seed/verify leaves in the same root journal reach `transport_cleaned` and `registry_verified`, the controller rechecks the same fence, database/migration/registry and zero-transport evidence and issues a fresh `scheduler_cutover_complete` stage whose signed body exact-binds the authorization receipt digest and terminal journal digest plus fan-out registry seed digest. The first end-of-`dbMigrate` guard transaction rechecks live controller state and exact-reads the already-inserted immutable authorization row, then atomically inserts only the fresh `scheduler_cutover_complete` row while consuming only its still-free slot with the complete guard family; the completion artifact, not an expired authorization alone, must still be fresh. This is the sole first-guard chicken-and-egg exception to controller-only database insertion. Raw artifacts are duplicate-key/schema/JCS/audience/freshness/key/signature-verified only over the authenticated root-owned local channel; PostgreSQL receives bounded claims and the fenced `crm_migrator` has no reusable verifier or receipt capability after that transaction. A fully installed exact guard set requires neither stage again. Partial guard state, a caller-supplied typed claim, missing/divergent journal, lost/changed fence, wrong authorization pairing, or replay throws. The controller cannot release the fence or restart an old build until every role in the compatible disabled-gate manifested data-plane fleet is on the required image, has a freshly claimed runtime identity, and passes a second guard/inventory/origin verification.
- `PublicChatBootstrapDrainReceiptV1` is scoped to exact local organization/tenant and the freshly verified Noli link-attestation digest/nonce plus legacy-inventory digest, has exact audience `crm-public-chat-bootstrap-v1`, but deliberately forbids a not-yet-created cutover operation/generation. It otherwise carries the same provider/environment/manifest/build/maintenance-fence/inventory/freshness/signature fields. Operator-only `bootstrap --bootstrap-drain-receipt <path>` forwards the exact duplicate-key-checked raw drain and Noli-attestation bytes to the isolated controller. The controller verifies both, registrar-persists the exact drain receipt first, and then its disjoint Noli-artifact principal calls the one atomic absent-to-disabled function that accepts the attestation, exact-references the committed drain digest, and creates the operation/generation. A crash-stranded drain receipt grants nothing and an exact retry resumes; no application process consumes either raw signature. It is never accepted by guard installation, prepare, or enable. A later organization bootstrap requires a new maintenance window/fence and fresh receipt; there is no request-time or lazy-link shortcut.
- `PublicChatDeploymentDrainReceiptV1` is post-bootstrap and requires exact audience `crm-public-chat-deployment-v1`, scope organization/tenant, cutover operation, writer generation, required/current build/image IDs, the same complete role inventory and maintenance-fence identity, freshness, nonce, issuer/key ID, and signature. The CLI accepts its raw path only as transport: it duplicate-key-checks and forwards the exact bytes plus frozen scope/operation/generation/inventory coordinates to `/v1/receipt/accept-deployment-drain`; the controller verifies the artifact and registrar-commits its typed receipt before returning a digest/status. `verify`/`prepare`/`enable` can only exact-reference that committed digest, rederive every local binding, and perform a fresh provider inventory/fence comparison immediately before enable. A stranded committed receipt grants nothing and may be referenced only by its exact unchanged operation. Any restarted, unknown, unqueryable, changed, stale, or wrong-image role invalidates the receipt and demotes readiness.

No application process chooses, signs, or inserts its own trustworthy runtime identity. The controller first creates a fresh never-reused least-privilege LOGIN+secret for that exact process start, mounts only that DSN into the new container/one-shot, then observes its container ID, host boot ID, cgroup/PID namespace and process start time over the root-owned control path. It increments the workload generation and creates one `RuntimeStartAttestationV1` with exact audience `crm-public-chat-runtime-start-v1`, environment/provider, service role, fresh `runtime_database_principal`, controller-issued instance UUID/generation, observed process identity, start time, build/commit/image, the exact schema-versioned canonical-origin/operator-path/template/config fingerprint, nonnegative `redisClientSlotCount`, exact `redisClientSlotCapabilityManifestDigest` over the fresh sorted ordinal/role/slot/kind/capability-digest array, short registration expiry, nonce, issuer/key ID, and signature. For every data-plane/controller daemon role after first guard installation, the signed schema additionally requires exact `preinstallCompletionReceiptDigest`, positive `preinstallConsumedJournalGeneration`, and lowercase SHA-256 `preinstallConsumedJournalDigest`; they must equal the same-environment completion-stage database row, its required installed-guard fingerprint, and the root controller's current `consumed` state. Those three members are absent and their typed columns null only for the fenced preinstall migration one-shot, whose audience/role cannot claim data-plane authority. **Before readiness**, the controller registrar persists the complete typed tuple as unclaimed; the runtime has no receipt INSERT capability. The production `RuntimeIdentityProvider` calls a separately granted challenge-bound claim function that accepts only its actual `session_user`, exact controller challenge/digest, and that unclaimed tuple. Claim is one-time; any reused principal, already-claimed digest/instance/generation, swapped login, pre-consumption artifact, changed completion/guard/journal binding, slot count/manifest/capability-set mismatch, or origin-fingerprint mismatch fails. Capability functions exact-match `session_user` to its one claimed start and current service/deployment/origin/preinstall-consumption state; historical rows cannot become authority. Restart is controller-orchestrated: old principal goes `NOLOGIN`, grants are revoked, old backends are terminated/zero-proved, a new principal/secret is created, and only then may the replacement start. Docker automatic restart with cached credentials is disabled for these roles. The provider then exposes immutable instance/generation/start digest/origin fingerprint, slot count/capability-manifest digest, and the three consumed-preinstall coordinates. Every local/user lease, reply dispatch/execution guard, and strict schedule binding stores its runtime identity before work; alert authority additionally exact-matches the origin fingerprint. External grants gain no fictitious direct runtime fields; cleanup remains bound to exact associated leases/guards. Missing/test/application-generated/replayed identity fails production readiness; fixtures cover concurrent claim, swapped login, stolen old secret after restart, stale same-build process, same-container restart, pre-consumed artifact replay, changed consumed-root/guard binding, missing/reordered/extra slot, capability-delivery response loss/ack replay, and mixed-origin replicas.

`RuntimeTerminationReceiptV1` is a distinct controller-signed artifact, not an inference from age or a general deployment drain. Its bounded canonical JSON contains contract/version, exact audience `crm-public-chat-runtime-termination-v1`, provider/environment, service role and runtime database principal, the exact start-attestation digest and controller-visible instance UUID/generation/container/host-boot/cgroup identity, build/commit/image, the exact start-attested origin fingerprint, nonnegative Redis client-slot count, exact slot-capability-manifest digest, and three consumed-preinstall coordinates, observed terminal state/reason/time, client terminal-shutdown state when a network send was possible, issued/expiry no more than five minutes apart, its own nonce, issuer/key ID, and signature. Organization, tenant, Noli organization, user, lease, job, and operation fields are forbidden: it proves death of exactly one environment runtime, not authority over a subject. The host controller must persist it first through the registrar-only fixed-search-path termination function, which exact-matches the claimed start/principal/generation/origin/slot-count/slot-capability-manifest/preinstall fingerprint and insert-or-verifies the one immutable typed receipt; application/control/MCP/worker/scheduler roles cannot INSERT or consume a new signed fact. One already committed receipt may then be referenced by multiple rows only when their stored start-attestation digest, instance/generation, role, principal, build, origin fingerprint, Redis slot count, and capability-manifest digest all match. Every lease/reference capability separately locks and rederives its exact subject scope/fence/operation, records the receipt digest, and still requires its own queue/provider/transport settlement; a receipt never selects or clears a row by itself. Strict schedule proof retains the committed digest for same-epoch non-owning reply-job guards. Direct dispatch, reply execution, strict install/fire/target, organization and user generic lease cleanup, link lifecycle, and GDPR tests reject wrong principal/role/start identity/generation/origin/preinstall state, caller-supplied scope, stale/cross-environment/cross-audience receipt, nonmatching fan-out, forged runtime insertion, and terminal-state claims for a still-running container.

Autonomous recovery obtains that proof through an exact controller protocol rather than assuming an operator has a file. A CRM `RuntimeTerminationResolver` uses a separate least-privilege socket credential to request `/v1/runtime-termination` with the stored start-attestation digest and discriminated scope after the database horizon and nonblocking session-lock check. The controller loads its immutable start registration, re-observes Docker/systemd/PID/cgroup and host-boot state, and for an exact terminal identity signs, durably stores, and commits the typed receipt through the registrar function **before** returning only its digest/status; still-running/restarted identity returns typed `409`, and unknown/unqueryable/controller-DB state returns fail-closed `503`. It never terminates a process as part of this read/adjudication call. The resolver has no receipt INSERT/consumer capability; it only asks the relevant guard-owner cleanup function to exact-read the already committed digest for the same runtime/scope during its own row CAS. No raw private key or broad controller credential enters CRM. Normal-ended receipts avoid the call. Issuance/persist/fetch loss at every boundary, credential rotation, controller outage, forged scope, concurrent restart, and cache-crash tests run against a local controller fixture; this review task does not contact the production controller.

CRM production uses the checked-in `hetzner-compose` controller adapter, not Railway. Its exact role manifest covers app, private control API, MCP, nginx ingress/maintenance/control isolation, PostgreSQL and Redis, the migration one-shot, public target worker, combined generic scheduler materializer/`scheduler-execution` worker service, owner-exclusive global pager worker, independent strict reconciler, long-lived retention daemon with quota/receipt/terminal lanes plus explicit timer/cron absence, registrar/ack/Noli-artifact controller roles, every rendered Docker Compose service/image, every Dockerfile build stage/base, the certificate-renewal service/timer, active `crm-deploy*` systemd unit, host/container cron/timers, every generated enabled queue/subscriber worker, GDPR routes, settings/Assistant/MCP writers, and callbacks. It inventories container/image IDs, Git commit, commands/effective concurrency/handler sets, database principals/pools, systemd desired state, host processes, networks/ports, and timers on the canonical Hetzner host and fails if any role is missing or unenumerated. The existing `/root/deploy-crm.sh` is explicitly insufficient because it recreates only `launchos-app` and does not run migrations. The reviewed contract wrapper consumes the already reviewed CI-built immutable digest/provenance graph and never builds or retags on the host, enters nginx maintenance, disables old restart/timer paths, drains/stops the complete runtime fleet, obtains preinstall proof, runs the existing-volume role transition plus generated migrations/first guard reconciliation from a one-shot exact-image container, starts every manifested role on its exact allowed digest with public chat disabled, registers/claims each runtime, and exact-verifies commit/complete image graph/database/Redis/roles/pools/guards/origin/certificate-renewal state before releasing only the install fence. It never applies unreviewed hand-written production SQL. Railway support may remain as a separately tested non-production adapter only when a real CRM environment uses it; it is not launch evidence for Hetzner.

Receipt signing adds explicit control-plane key dependencies. Each environment has a distinct offline/CI-provisioned Ed25519 deployment-controller signing key and a disjoint Noli control-plane attestation key; private keys live only in their respective controller/CI secret stores and never in any CRM data-plane container, logs, repository, or receipt file. Only the isolated controller receives the verification-key maps needed to turn raw controller/Noli signed artifacts into database authority; ordinary runtimes receive only persisted typed claims and digests through their narrow capabilities. Rotation installs an overlapping new public key before issuers switch and proves both old/new fixtures. An old verification key may be revoked only after every unexpired ordinary receipt window and in-progress operation has ended **and** every root-retained `RedisServerIncarnationRetirementProofV1` signed by it has zero raw-byte reference count or has been irreversibly folded into the terminal old-run accumulator. A consumed retirement proof remains verifiable under that key for every later claim fence that exact-references its retained bytes, even after its five-minute first-use window; it is not silently re-signed or invalidated. Emergency revocation immediately disables affected scopes and bars every claim that still depends on an affected retirement proof until an independently sufficient live fence is obtained; it never treats key loss as absence.
