Unknown/revoked keys, cross-environment signatures, reused nonces, early key removal, and proof reissue fail closed. Tests pause every old route/worker/scheduler/GDPR/MCP/mutation class across guard install and `ready -> enabled`, retain and consume a retirement proof before/during/after key rotation, attempt emergency revocation with live references, cover forged/stale/replayed/incomplete receipts, post-signature container/systemd restart, manifest omission, any complete-fleet image/origin mismatch, and maintenance-fence loss, and prove old code cannot mutate reserved state or publish/enqueue.

### CustomerPublicChatLocator (`customer_public_chat_locators`)

This entity is the sole globally addressed security directory, not tenant-owned business data. It is accessible only through the customers public-chat data service; it has no CRUD/query-engine route, export, search index, or response serialization.

- `id`: UUID primary key, generated by PostgreSQL.
- `kind`: text, exactly `widget_id | widget_slug | conversation_id`.
- `locator_digest`: text, exactly `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` over `noli:public-chat-locator:v1:<kind>:<canonicalIdentifier>`. Raw conversation/widget IDs and normalized slugs are public inputs but are not retained in the locator key.
- `routing_state`: text, exactly `active | retired`, default `active`. `retired` is permitted only for `widget_slug` and is an immutable global anti-reuse tombstone.
- `target_organization_id`, `target_tenant_id`, `target_widget_id`: UUID routing coordinates. These names deliberately distinguish global routing coordinates from ordinary tenant-row ownership fields. They are all required for `active` and all null for `retired`.
- `target_conversation_id`: UUID, required only for an active `conversation_id` and forbidden otherwise.
- `target_noli_organization_id`: text storage, required immutable canonical lowercase UUID erasure-fence coordinate for `active` and null for `retired`.
- Widget lifecycle discovery: nullable `lifecycle_operation_id`, database-time `lifecycle_due_at`, and `lifecycle_scan_after` are all-or-none and permitted only on an active `widget_id` locator. They exact-match the server-owned widget deactivation/delete marker and give the strict provider a relational, indexable due coordinate; clearing/replacing them requires consumption or stronger-operation supersession under the same widget/operation CAS.
- Slug ownership/budget: `slug_owner_scope_digest` is the rotation-independent domain-separated SHA-256 coordinate of stable CRM environment/service identity plus local organization and tenant—deliberately excluding the replaceable Noli binding—required for every normal active or retired `widget_slug` row and forbidden for other kinds. A pre-contract ambiguous duplicate retired with reason `legacy_collision_repaired` instead has null owner digest and a required rotation-independent `legacy_collision_set_digest` over the sorted claimant scope/widget UUID coordinates.
- Retired-slug proof: paired `retired_at` database time and bounded allow-listed `retired_reason` (`slug_changed | widget_deleted | organization_erased | orphan_repaired | legacy_collision_repaired`) are required only for `retired`; `retired_locator_scope_digest` is the rotation-independent domain-separated SHA-256 coordinate of the former exact target and operation, carries no raw tenant coordinate, and is immutable.
- `created_at`, `updated_at`: timestamptz, required.

Constraints/indexes are exact: unique `(kind, locator_digest)` across active and retired rows; unique `(kind, target_widget_id)` for active `widget_id`/`widget_slug`; unique `target_conversation_id` for active `conversation_id`; active-only cleanup index `(target_noli_organization_id, target_organization_id, target_tenant_id, target_widget_id)`; slug-budget index `(kind, slug_owner_scope_digest, id) WHERE kind='widget_slug' AND slug_owner_scope_digest IS NOT NULL`; lifecycle index `(target_organization_id, target_tenant_id, lifecycle_scan_after, target_widget_id) WHERE kind='widget_id' AND lifecycle_operation_id IS NOT NULL`; and state/kind-specific all-or-none checks. There are no ORM relationships or FKs to unmanaged chat tables.

Locator state never authorizes a request. Only an `active` lookup provides coordinates; the data service then revalidates exact resource, lifecycle, origin, token, and scope under tenant predicates and locks. Inserts are insert-or-verify and never remap a digest. Widget create, sorted old/new slug update, conversation admission, hard deletion, and locator mutation are atomic with the authoritative tenant change. Normal deactivation retains active locators. Missing, retired, malformed, duplicate, stale, or mismatched rows return the same `404`.

Slug retirement is intentionally stronger than ordinary locator cleanup. A slug change, widget hard-delete, or organization erasure locks the old digest and atomically CASes its active `widget_slug` row to `retired`, clears every raw target coordinate, and writes the database-time retirement proof; widget-ID and conversation-ID locators are still hard-deleted after their scoped cleanup proof. A retired slug row can never be updated, deleted, reactivated, transferred, or reused in this contract, including by launch repair, unlink, GDPR, or an organization claiming the same slug later. New slug admission rejects both active and retired digest conflicts. The targetless tombstone is global pseudonymous security state rather than organization business data, survives scope cleanup, and is explicitly excluded from organization/Noli zero-state inventories. Guard tests pause rename/delete/erasure before and after retirement, then attempt a cross-tenant claim and stale-bookmark access; the old URL remains a uniform `404` forever.

Permanent anti-reuse state is bounded. Under the organization plus candidate-slug locks, creation or change to a previously unseen slug counts all active and retired slug rows carrying the same `slug_owner_scope_digest` and rejects the new slug with `409` at the fixed lifetime limit of 1,000 per scope; a rename consumes one new slot, while active→retired conversion, removal of a slug with no replacement, widget deletion, unlink, and erasure consume none and can never be blocked at the cap. The unkeyed domain-separated local-scope coordinate is stable across Noli A→B unlink/rebind solely for this security budget and is never exposed; historical Noli identity remains only in the separate retirement proof. Launch inventory reserves/counts all normal legacy slug claims against that scope and permits at most 10,000 distinct pre-contract ambiguous-collision digests environment-wide; exceeding either limit is a cutover blocker requiring an explicit later retention/namespace design, not tombstone deletion. Tests rotate rapidly to the edge, race two candidates for the final slot, delete/erase at the cap, preserve zero remaining capacity across A→B rebind, and prove another local scope has an independent cap but cannot reclaim a burned digest.

A public locator is created only when the local organization has one authoritative immutable Noli organization link that parses and reserializes to one canonical lowercase UUID. New or updated widgets may be saved privately while unlinked under the narrow guard above, but cannot be activated publicly and receive no locator; malformed or unattested legacy links remain quarantined and fail cutover readiness because the GDPR route could not address them. Every Noli link mutation routes through the operator-only shared organization-lock binding service; direct `Organization.noliOrgId` flush is removed. In particular, `packages/shared/src/lib/auth/clerk.ts` never creates, canonicalizes, replaces, or clears a link: sign-in may detect missing/mismatched authority and return a safe `noli_link_setup_required` state, but cannot acquire a drain receipt or mutate the organization. A custom `organizations` OLD+NEW trigger independently rejects any link insert/update/delete/replacement without the exact first-link, launch link-repair, or zero-state-unlink transaction attestation, organization lock, canonical UUID, and applicable inventory proof. First valid link establishment may preserve private widget rows, creates a disabled cutover state, and publishes no locator until exact verification.

Launch bootstrap owns the sole recovery for a legacy link before a cutover row exists. A harmless `canonicalize_same_uuid` action is allowed only when parsing OLD and NEW proves the identical UUID and merely reserializes it to canonical lowercase form. A malformed, semantically wrong, or disputed value requires `replace_attested` plus a bounded `NoliOrganizationLinkAttestationV1`: signed canonical JSON containing contract, exact audience `crm-public-chat-link-attestation-v1`, CRM environment/service identity, local organization/tenant, exact target canonical Noli UUID, authoritative Noli registry row/version and pending reservation UUID, CRM request and Noli approval IDs/digests, digest of the old value, legacy-inventory digest, requested action, issued/expiry times no more than 15 minutes apart, nonce, issuer/key ID, and signature from an allow-listed Noli control-plane key. It deliberately does not require not-yet-created cutover operation/generation IDs. After the scoped bootstrap drain proves pre-contract writers terminal, the controller acceptance function takes only the bounded Noli/raw-old, tenant, and organization locks—no associated-user fence set—revalidates no existing cutover/new-contract sidecar/active-target locator/strict/transport authority, then atomically binds the artifact's unique digest/nonce/reservation, writes the canonical link plus disabled pending cutover row and redacted ActionLog, and sets `user_barrier_phase='materializing'`. That first commit is the durable scope-closing fence. The private-control coordinator then runs the at-most-32-user barrier pages and stable rescan above; it reaches `sealed` only after every association/notification/lease subject has a barrier and every pre-existing organization/user lease or external grant has normally ended or has exact termination/settlement proof. Expiry/age alone is insufficient, and a multi-organization user's live/ambiguous lease remains a blocker. Confirmation may be durably accepted while materialization runs, but no locator, cutover apply/prepare/enable, public authority, or barrier release is legal until the sealed fingerprint/zero proof exists; a sealed successful bootstrap may then transition barriers to logically inactive `released` and purge them in pages while retaining the fingerprint. Targetless retired-slug tombstones do not belong to or authorize the scope but still prevent reuse. Missing/conflicting/expired proof or a barrier/lease/grant blocker leaves the scope disabled/quarantined—neither a guessed ID nor direct SQL is accepted. After confirmed bootstrap, unlink/replacement remains forbidden while any active-target locator, public/active widget, conversation, session, message-order, reply job, strict row/binding/lease, transport, organization/user generic lease, external grant, or nonterminal barrier exists. Replacement is never in-place. Tests cover direct/old link flush, same-UUID canonicalization, malformed/wrong signed recovery, forged/expired/conflicting proof, first bounded closing commit, every 32-user page and stable rescan, multi-organization users, cancellation during materialization, sign-in read-only behavior, more than 100,000 subjects with no path above 40 simultaneous locks, retired-slug nonreuse, and erasure precedence.

The authoritative producer is the Noli platform's service-authenticated internal `POST /api/internal/crm/public-chat-link-attestation` endpoint, implemented and versioned in the Noli platform repository. It signs only a pre-existing active Noli-side `crm_scope_bindings` registry row keyed by CRM environment/service identity plus local organization/tenant and pointing to exactly one Noli organization; the fleet service secret authenticates the caller but is never itself mapping authority. Registry creation/change requires dual consent. First, a CRM user holding `customers.settings.manage` for the exact local organization/tenant initiates a one-time binding request through CRM; CRM permission-checks under its organization lock, stores a redacted ActionLog request, and service-authenticates a bounded request to Noli containing the exact source scope, request ID/nonce/digest, expiry, and actor-audit digest. Second, a Noli organization admin accepts that still-fresh request while authenticated inside the target Noli organization. The registry row binds both approval IDs/digests/times, both actors' redacted audit coordinates, the target Noli organization, uniqueness constraints, and a monotonic registry version. Attestation issuance locks that registry/Noli organization and creates a `crm_scope_binding_reservations` row keyed by its unique reservation/attestation nonce/version before signing. Once an attestation has been issued, that pending reservation is itself a link-change and Noli-erasure dependency; expiry ends confirmation eligibility but is never evidence that CRM did not consume it.

Registry change/revoke and Noli-organization erasure take the same registry/organization lock and first CAS every issued pending/confirmed reservation to Noli-side `cancellation_requested`; they cannot delete/invalidate it or finalize the registry/organization locally. Noli then issues a bounded signed `NoliOrganizationLinkCancellationV1` with exact audience `crm-public-chat-link-cancellation-v1`, environment/scope/Noli organization, registry version, reservation/attestation digest, cancellation operation/reason (`registry_change | registry_revoke | organization_erasure`), issued/expiry, nonce, issuer/key ID, and signature. It delivers or polls the CRM service-authenticated reservation-cancellation endpoint until CRM returns one durable operation-bound acknowledgment. If the attestation was never consumed, CRM inserts the mutually exclusive cancellation tombstone in the receipt ledger under the full local lock order, thereby making every later attestation consume fail, and acknowledges `never_consumed`. If consumption won, one local transaction stores the cancellation receipt pair/ActionLog and CASes CRM's separate cancellation state from `none` to `requested` while preserving historical `pending|confirmed` confirmation and while the cutover gate may still be `disabled|ready|enabled`; that state immediately closes new authority but does **not** strand already-granted handlers behind a disabled-row guard.

For registry change/revoke, CRM then runs the operation-bound quiesce coordinator. It closes ingress, scheduler/queue claims, and new external grants for the exact scope; waits for or adjudicates every in-flight dispatch/execution/schedule binding and external attempt through the settlement-only lane; proves zero side-effect-capable runtime/lease/reference under the binding locks; and only then CASes `ready|enabled -> disabled` with `disabled_reason='noli_link_cancellation'`, clearing launch/deployment-ready claims but preserving link/cancellation and ambiguity audit. A crash before that CAS resumes quiescence with new work still fenced; a crash after it resumes only bounded disabled-state cleanup. The ordinary unlink stages may then reconcile retained external ambiguity at its exact boundary, delete all legacy/current state, and return zero-state completion. For `organization_erasure`, receipt consumption instead begins/resumes the existing Noli-scoped CRM erasure operation; its deleting fence, self-quiescence transition, runtime/transport proof, and final GDPR completion own demotion and cleanup. It never uses a link-only clear. The Noli operation may finalize only after validating the exact CRM never-consumed, zero-state-unlink, or GDPR-completion acknowledgment; timeout, CRM outage, ambiguous response, reservation expiry, or local Noli cleanup is not success. Change/revoke still repeats dual authorization; an explicitly documented internal platform-operator recovery requires two-person audited proof of both source and destination and cannot bypass the CRM acknowledgment. Tests deliver cancellation in disabled, ready, and enabled state and pause before/after every provider/meter/notification grant, scheduler install/fire/target enqueue, handler settlement, quiesce proof, demotion CAS, cleanup, and acknowledgment. A Noli admin alone cannot claim guessed CRM coordinates, and a CRM admin alone cannot select an unapproved Noli target. No endpoint trusts email, free-form target UUID, old link value, or Clerk membership as mapping proof. Existing launch mappings must be established through this workflow; absent, expired, duplicated, revoked, singly approved, or ambiguous registry state is an explicit blocker.

CRM's bootstrap coordinator first takes a short organization-lock snapshot to compute the old-link and bounded legacy-inventory digests plus a nonce and exact-verifies the local binding-request ActionLog digest, releases database locks, and calls Noli with the existing CRM↔Noli service credential. It treats the returned attestation as untrusted bytes and forwards those exact duplicate-key-checked bytes plus the paired raw `PublicChatBootstrapDrainReceiptV1` to the controller's kind-specific `/v1/noli-artifact/accept-link-attestation-bootstrap` endpoint; the app/CLI has no Noli verification key and cannot persist a derived signed fact. The controller independently verifies both schemas, JCS bytes, signatures, audiences, issuers, keys, environment, action, freshness, target/version/reservation, both approval digests, local request, and paired drain receipt/nonce. Through the registrar it first insert-or-verifies the drain receipt; through `crm_noli_artifact_controller` it then invokes the bounded Noli/raw-old+tenant+organization transaction that recomputes the snapshot, accepts the attestation, creates the disabled/pending cutover with `user_barrier_phase='materializing'`, and commits the scope fence. It does not snapshot or lock the full associated-user set. Private control resumes the persisted at-most-32-user cursor until a stable complete union/zero proof seals the barrier; confirmation receipt acceptance may occur concurrently but pending→confirmed authority, locator work, prepare/enable, and logical barrier release all exact-require that sealed proof. A crash after drain staging or any barrier page is safe and resumes exact state; the staged drain alone grants nothing. Cutover has unique partial indexes on every non-null attestation, confirmation, and cancellation receipt/nonce digest; the persistent ledger's digest/nonce plus reservation-claim indexes preserve replay and cancellation-winner denial after unlink.

After the local pending bootstrap commit, the CLI calls service-authenticated `POST /api/internal/crm/public-chat-link-confirmation` with the reservation ID, attestation digest, and newly created operation/generation. Noli takes the same registry/organization lock used by cancellation and confirms only an unexpired `pending` reservation whose org is not deleting; `cancellation_requested` always wins and can never confirm. It atomically marks the reservation/registry link confirmed and returns `NoliOrganizationLinkConfirmationV1` signed with exact audience `crm-public-chat-link-confirmation-v1`, environment/scope/Noli org, registry version, reservation/attestation digest, CRM operation/generation, confirmation time, nonce, issuer/key ID, and signature. The CLI forwards the exact raw confirmation/status artifact to `/v1/noli-artifact/accept-link-confirmation`; only the controller verifies it. Through `crm_noli_artifact_controller`, a bounded Noli+tenant+organization transaction atomically inserts the typed confirmation receipt when no cancellation won; if the user barrier is not yet sealed it deliberately leaves local state `pending`. A separate bounded CAS changes `pending -> confirmed` only after exact sealed fingerprint/zero proof, and races before/during/after seal are idempotently tested. Crash before either call is restart-safe through service-authenticated `GET /api/internal/crm/public-chat-link-confirmation/<reservationId>`; an unknown response leaves CRM disabled/pending, never guessed. If Noli confirmation committed before a later erasure/revoke request but CRM has not yet consumed its receipt, the Noli row is already confirmed and therefore follows the same CRM cleanup dependency; it cannot be downgraded to an unconsumed reservation. An exact cancellation response drives the cancellation protocol above, not a link-only shortcut; malformed/conflicting state leaves CRM disabled/quarantined.

Confirmed and consumed-pending mappings are both erasure dependencies. Noli organization deletion must invoke and complete the ordinary CRM deletion contract before clearing either, while confirmed registry change/revoke requires the CRM zero-state unlink completion. Confirmation, cancellation delivery, CRM ledger/cutover commits, cleanup acknowledgments, and Noli finalization each have durable idempotency keys and can be retried independently; there is no atomic cross-database step. Unit/cross-repository tests pause and race attestation issuance, cancellation-before-consume, CRM pending commit, confirm-before/after cancellation, restart, registry change/revoke, CRM cleanup, acknowledgment loss, and Noli erasure at every boundary and prove that no stale link becomes enabled and no linked legacy personal data is orphaned. Production retrieval/confirmation/cancellation and registry mutation are separately approved external actions; missing credentials, mapping, dual approval, reservation, or deployed endpoint evidence is a launch blocker rather than a direct-SQL escape.

An idempotent custom writer trigger checks OLD and NEW `target_organization_id` plus the immutable Noli binding against the organization erasure fence; the unconditional end-of-run reconciliation attaches it. It permits active→retired slug coordinate clearing only under the exact owning lifecycle/GDPR operation and rejects every later tombstone mutation. Organization erasure deletes/proves active widget/conversation locators and retires each active slug by exact stored Noli/local/tenant scope; targetless retired tombstones are neither selected nor counted as residue. The controlled backfill iterates organizations/tenants in bounded exact-scope batches, creates widget-ID and conversation locators, and creates a slug locator only when the normalized slug has neither an active nor retired row; duplicate legacy slugs receive no locator and stay fail closed until an authenticated update resolves them.

The maintenance surface is the module CLI command `mercato customers public-chat-locators`, implemented in `packages/core/src/modules/customers/cli.ts` through a reusable core customers locator data service (the app route imports that service; core never imports app code). Launch bootstrap first creates/reads the exact disabled cutover row. The command requires exact `--organization`, `--tenant`, and current `--cutover-operation`; accepts only `--mode dry-run|apply|repair|verify`; defaults to dry-run; clamps `--batch-size` to `1..500`; and accepts/returns a validated opaque cursor bound to mode/scope/kind/cutover operation/writer+runtime generation/inventory digest/last scalar ID. Every apply batch revalidates that disabled operation before one idempotent transaction using the global lock order and emits a bounded JSON receipt with scanned/created/verified/missing/mismatched/collision counts plus `nextCursor`; it never prints raw tokens, transcript, email/name, or provider/config data. Re-running from the start or last receipt is safe. Dry-run reports domain-separated collision digests and safe widget IDs without mutation; apply never overwrites a conflict; verify exits nonzero for any eligible missing/mismatched locator and separately reports expected quarantined duplicate slugs and unlinked-ineligible widgets.

`repair` requires a local authenticated actor with `customers.settings.manage`, the exact disabled operation, expected old and new scalar coordinates, and one allow-listed resolution. A same-scope stale row uses that scope's operation. If OLD names another existing organization, the command additionally requires `--old-organization`, `--old-tenant`, and `--old-cutover-operation`; the actor must hold `customers.settings.manage` in both scopes, both rows must be disabled, and the OLD+NEW trigger exact-verifies both operation/generation attestations while sorted organization/digest locks are held. If the OLD organization row is truly absent, the narrow `repair_orphan_locator` action instead requires exact old coordinates, a fresh controller-verified/registrar-committed deployment-drain receipt digest, database proof that the organization and every referenced widget/conversation/session/sidecar/transport target are absent, and a transaction-local orphan-repair attestation bound to the new operation/digest; any surviving old organization/resource rejects it. These are the only ways to satisfy both sides of the locator guard. A stale/orphan `widget_id` or `conversation_id` locator may be deleted after that proof, but a `widget_slug` locator is always active→retired with reason `orphan_repaired` and can never be reassigned. Any new authoritative target must use a different unburned identifier. The transaction writes redacted ActionLog receipts in every affected scope atomically.

Ambiguous pre-contract duplicate slugs have no winner because an old bookmark cannot safely select one tenant. `rename_live_slug` requires each claimant's separately authorized bounded replacement slug, locks old/new digests and all involved organizations in sorted order, revalidates actor scope, forces only that widget inactive/hosted-disabled, proves the replacement globally unused and within its lifetime budget, and updates it without publishing authority. It does not assign the old slug to the other claimant. In the same transaction it recomputes all remaining legacy claimants of the old normalized slug; when the last claimant moves or is deleted, it insert-or-verifies one targetless `legacy_collision_repaired` tombstone for the old digest before commit. Thus the digest remains unavailable while claimants exist and permanently unavailable afterward, including across a crash at the last mutation. The other live target is never mutated without its own authorized command, and every claimant must move before verification passes. Missing dual-scope authority or orphan proof leaves the collision quarantined. Repair never accepts an arbitrary target/remap, contact/email evidence, or direct SQL. A changed cutover operation/generation/inventory invalidates its cursor and launch receipt. Tests cover sequential two-claimant rename/delete in both orders, crash before/after last-claimant retirement, orphan repair, then attempted cross-tenant claim and stale-bookmark access.

The companion supported cutover surface is `mercato customers public-chat-cutover`. It requires exact `--organization`, `--tenant`, and `--phase launch|token-retirement|unlink`; accepts `--mode dry-run|apply|verify` plus launch-only `bootstrap|confirm-link|restart-disabled|maintenance-demote|prepare|enable`; defaults to dry-run; and uses a validated opaque cursor bound to phase, stage, scope, cutover operation, writer/runtime generation, and last scalar identity. Launch `bootstrap --bootstrap-drain-receipt <path> --noli-link-attestation <path>` is the sole legal absent-to-disabled initialization for a linked or legacy-link-repair scope. The CLI performs the snapshot→Noli request→controller-forward flow above; only the controller's kind-specific capability re-locks and revalidates the stable runtime contract, generates CSPRNG operation/generation UUIDs exactly once (or exact-verifies the existing disabled row), atomically canonicalizes/attested-replaces the link when needed, accepts the attestation against the registrar-committed drain receipt, and stores pending reservation plus canonical link-validation receipt/nonce on **every** row. It then invokes confirmation outside database locks; `confirm-link` resumes status/confirmation after a crash. Only after the signed confirmation receipt is consumed and the row is `confirmed` does the command emit authority for locator/cutover dry-runs. Pending/unknown returns a bounded pending result and remains disabled; invalid confirmation permits only safe reconciliation/unlink. Arbitrary bounded legacy widgets/conversations/messages are expected and permitted because later stages inventory them while the new gate remains disabled. Bootstrap creates no locator, sidecar, schedule, or downstream launch receipt and fails for ready/enabled state, conflicting contract/link proof, or pre-existing new-contract sidecar/locator/strict-transport authority inconsistent with an absent cutover row. Attested null→first-link may perform this same operator transaction and is an explicit enabled-generation guard exception only for that atomic link+disabled-row write. Batches are `1..500`, one exact transaction each under the global lock order, and output bounded canonical JSON counts/digests/cursors with no raw token, transcript, email/name, config value, or provider material. `apply` requires explicit named resolutions for any destructive/quarantine choice; `verify` never mutates and exits nonzero for every required residual. `prepare --verification-receipt <path> --deployment-drain-receipt <path>` requires confirmed link state, forwards the raw deployment artifact for controller verification/registrar commitment, exact-references only the returned committed digest, validates the bounded local verification artifact, re-derives every cheap inventory/trigger digest under the organization lock, stores the exact receipt/nonce and verified deployment claims, and CASes only the matching `disabled` row to `ready`; mismatch leaves it disabled. An interrupted batch resumes or repeats idempotently, while a cursor/receipt from another stage, scope, operation, generation, or changed inventory is rejected.

Launch phase owns these ordered stages and receipts; no direct SQL substitute is allowed:

0. `bootstrap` creates/exact-verifies the disabled pending operation/generation authority above, and `confirm-link` completes the Noli reservation handshake. Together they are deliberately the only pre-dry-run mutations; locator and launch dry-runs require confirmed state and bind the returned identifiers. Repeating either is status/idempotency-safe and cannot rotate an existing operation. `restart-disabled` may replace only `cutover_operation_id` after proving zero **downstream** launch receipts, sidecars, locators, schedules, transport, and maintenance writers; `writer_generation` remains the immutable contract generation created by the first bootstrap, so delayed-writer fencing never changes in place. The mandatory prebootstrap link-validation/confirmation receipts are excluded from that zero-downstream test. Restart uses the same two-transaction handshake as first bootstrap: the CLI obtains a fresh Noli reservation/attestation plus bootstrap drain and forwards both raw artifacts to the controller; under locks the controller-only acceptance function exact-references the registrar-committed drain, accepts the attestation, writes a new operation ID, replaces the old link receipt pairs, clears prior confirmation/cancellation pairs, and leaves the unchanged canonical registry mapping `pending`; outside database locks it requests confirmation, then `confirm-link` forwards the exact raw status artifact and only the controller acceptance capability consumes the signed confirmation in a second local transaction before exposing the new operation with the unchanged generation. A crash at either boundary resumes by reservation status; no step atomically claims to confirm across CRM and Noli. Restart cannot carry an expired/cancellation-requested reservation or reuse a ledger-consumed nonce.
1. `schema` verifies the version-controlled exact legacy fingerprint in `packages/core/src/modules/customers/data/public-chat-legacy-schema.ts`. Required PostgreSQL shape is: `chat_widgets` UUID PK and UUID `tenant_id`/`organization_id`, text `name`/nullable `greeting_message`, non-null jsonb `config`, non-null boolean `is_active`, timestamptz create/update, nullable text slug/description/brand/welcome/business plus public/legacy-bot fields and integer max; `chat_conversations` UUID PK/scope/widget/contact, visitor name/email/token text, status text, visitor/agent typing booleans and timestamps, create/update timestamps; and `chat_messages` UUID PK, UUID conversation, sender/message text, boolean `is_bot`, and created timestamp. The manifest pins each required nullability/default, the widget/conversation FK identities, `chat_conv_org_idx (organization_id,status,updated_at DESC)`, `chat_msg_conv_idx (conversation_id,created_at,id)`, and every column consumed by the compatibility routes. Documented extra legacy columns are allowed; a missing `visitor_token`, wrong type/nullability, absent required index, or partial three-table install fails closed. If all three tables are absent, migration reconciliation may skip only the legacy-table guard, but public chat remains unavailable until a separately tracked legacy-schema migration installs this fingerprint and a later no-pending-migration run attaches/verifies the guard.
2. `reserved_config` raw-inventories duplicate or case-fold-colliding object members, malformed/non-object/over-bound/non-I-JSON values, every ASCII-case-insensitive `__proto__`/`prototype`/`constructor`, every ASCII-case-insensitive key beginning `noli`, and every ASCII-case-insensitive `allowedOrigins` key at any depth, including array elements. No pre-existing blob is ever accepted as origins, a delete/lifecycle intent, or any security authority, even if its shape is perfect. Apply may strip exact reported reserved/dangerous paths only with `--resolve reserved-config=strip`, preserving only recursively validated null-prototype client config and writing an immutable command/ActionLog digest; legacy `allowedOrigins` is reset to hosted-only until an authorized manager republishes it through the top-level field, and malformed or unapproved rows remain quarantined and block enablement. After that proof, the server initializes exact `config.noliAutomationEpoch=0` and `config.noliPublicPromptEpoch=0` on each legacy widget in the same operation-bound batch; rerun insert-or-verifies and never resets a contract-owned value. Each is a JSON integer in `0..2^63-1`, is never client writable/serializable, and thereafter changes only by its specified increment-one lifecycle or prompt-setting CAS. Every later legitimate delete/lifecycle intent insert-or-verifies a matching server command/ActionLog operation receipt and exact widget-ID locator lifecycle tuple, so config shape alone never authorizes or hides cleanup. The reserved-widget trigger rejects missing/malformed/decremented/skipped epochs, direct serializers, and any client attempt to add/change/remove them.
3. `legacy_work` runs only after the deployment is externally disabled and every pre-contract writer/callback is drained. For each at-most-1,000-message conversation it takes the exact conversation lock, maps every visible row in stable `(created_at,id)` order, creates/verifies the session, and creates a deterministic historical terminal reply-job record for every visitor inbound. Bootstrap never inherits the entity default blindly: a closed/revoked conversation maps to `bot_state='disabled'`; any provable manual-agent/business reply (`sender_type='business'` with `is_bot=false`) or ambiguous legacy handoff/ownership maps fail-closed to `handed_off` with a bounded `legacy_cutover_manual_or_ambiguous` reason; only an open history whose every non-visitor message is provably bot-owned and whose work mapping is complete may become `active`. Conflicting evidence is quarantined, never active. A deterministic old reply row is bound and verified; a `__noli_bot_reply_claim__`/`noli:public-chat:bot-reply:*` sentinel or an inbound without a provable reply is never replayed and becomes sequence-resolved `no_reply` with the allow-listed `legacy_cutover_unanswered` reason before the sentinel is removed. The transaction replaces plaintext with a marker only after the full mapping/job/state set is durable. Over-cap conversations follow the public-revocation rule instead and remain authenticated-paged/read-only with disabled automation. Verify proves zero sentinels, zero eligible unmapped visible rows/inbounds, zero publicly readable over-cap rows, exact bot-state classification, and same-body/idempotent crash resume.
4. `legacy_reference_integrity` performs a deployment-drained, bounded global/bidirectional scalar-ID inventory before any scope can enable. In stable primary-key pages it proves the complete graph: (a) every `chat_conversations.widget_id` resolves to one widget with the same organization+tenant; (b) every chat-claimed proposal/action `payload.conversationId` and every non-null `inbox_conversations.chat_conversation_id` resolves to one conversation with the row's same organization+tenant; (c) every action→proposal→email and discrepancy→proposal/optional-action edge resolves, keeps organization+tenant equal at every scoped hop, and a discrepancy action belongs to that exact proposal; (d) every note resolves to one inbox-conversation parent whose organization+tenant becomes the note's scope; and (e) the inverse pages for every authoritative widget, conversation, action, proposal, email, and inbox conversation find **all** scalar backreferences regardless of the referencing row's claimed scope/status/deleted state. The public-chat deterministic triple must reverse-resolve through the three unique reply-job indexes to one and the same job/scope; mixed or duplicate claims are fatal. Parse failures, missing targets, orphan notes, same-organization/different-tenant edges, and A↔B edges are typed blockers. The pass never uses email, contact, free text, or timestamps. Its canonical environment artifact and each affected scope receipt bind every table's forward and inverse primary-key high-water/count/digest plus the complete graph fingerprint, so no row can fall between scope-local candidate sets. Every authenticated reader, list/count/search/stream/Assistant path and every lifecycle/cleanup join independently requires the validated full chain; a mismatch is hidden and raises integrity telemetry, never a foreign name/transcript/status/payload load.

   Repair is exact and permissioned. A live cross-scope edge requires every affected scope disabled, sorted multi-scope locks, and the actor's applicable settings/engagement or downstream mutation permission in every scope; it may unlink/dismiss the referencing row or dependency-delete an explicitly selected tainted owned chain, but never mutates a foreign target. A missing-target edge requires the row owner's permission plus fresh deployment-drain and global orphan proof. A conversation may be rebound only to an explicitly selected same-scope widget with matching ownership proof; guessed ownership is forbidden. Action/proposal/email/discrepancy reparenting is never a repair: the operator may delete/dismiss only the expected referencing row and its proven same-scope exclusive dependents in discrepancy→action→proposal→email order. An orphan note may be dependency-deleted only under its freshly proven deleted/missing chat-exclusive parent and owner-scope authorization; a note on a mixed rebuilt parent remains with that parent. Every action CASes expected row/target/scope/content paired keyed digests and writes a redacted receipt. Verify requires zero invalid parent edges and zero unvalidated forward **and inverse** downstream backreferences. Tests cover A-conversation→B-widget, B-action/inbox→A-conversation, A-action→B-proposal, A-proposal→B-email, discrepancy→foreign proposal/action, ordinary B action→A chat proposal, same-org/different-tenant, orphan/restrict/cascade note fixtures, missing targets, equal UUIDs, both repair orderings, and all readers/finalizers.
5. `legacy_cs` runs only after reference-integrity zero proof. It inventories random-ID pre-contract proposal actions by exact scope plus parsed `payload.channel='chat'` and the now-validated same-scope conversation ID; contact/email/text matching is forbidden. Apply first inverse-enumerates every discrepancy for the proposal and action. It dependency-deletes an exact same-scope chat-derived discrepancy, then dismisses/marks non-sendable and deletes action, proposal, and synthetic email only when the complete chain is chat-exclusive, scope/parent/content provenance agrees, and fresh inverse probes prove no remaining discrepancy/action/proposal/email reference. A foreign, shared, ordinary-channel, malformed, or conflicting discrepancy/row is a typed blocker for explicit operator resolution, never accepted quarantine; a globally missing expected child is already clean only when inverse proof is also zero. Verify proves zero actionable legacy chat proposal, zero exact conversation/job binding, and zero residual full-chain reference, with crash-resume fixtures for random IDs.
6. `legacy_inbox` runs only after reference-integrity zero proof and inventories validated same-scope `inbox_conversations.chat_conversation_id` bindings plus every forward/inverse note child. A chat-exclusive row may be deleted only after its exact notes are dependency-deleted in bounded primary-key pages and a fresh inverse zero proof succeeds. A mixed email/SMS row must retain its notes, clear the exact chat link, and transactionally rebuild **every** derived preview/channel/direction/status/unread/display/avatar scalar from authoritative non-chat records, persisting and rechecking paired HMAC source/result digests plus key IDs; notes remain reachable only through that verified same-scope parent. If any field or note-parent relationship cannot be rederived exactly, the row remains a typed launch blocker; there is no receipt-only or accepted-quarantine path. Verify requires zero chat-conversation links, zero orphan/foreign note edge, and exact reconstructed scalar digests/key IDs for every mixed row. Inbox list/count/detail/notes/search/summary/status/Assistant readers and note writers use the shared scope/channel/parent guard and cannot consume a linked or unverified-rebuild row.
7. `identity` inventories every legacy conversation `contact_id` created or reused from unverified visitor email and first nulls only that exact scoped conversation link. It tracks field-level provenance for every affected entity/person scalar, including `display_name`, `primary_email`, first/last name, status, and any searchable/exported/AI-consumed identity value. A provably pre-existing independently authoritative contact may be preserved only after each scalar is rederived from pre-chat or authoritative non-chat records; any chat-origin or unproved field is cleared. A chat-created entity/person that remains chat-exclusive is dependency-deleted. If it later gained legitimate history, company, relationship, proposal, or manual edits, that fact does not bless the anonymous name/email: the only launch resolution is to move each independently proven non-chat relationship/history to an operator-selected independently authoritative same-scope target (never email-matched), then delete the chat-created source. If no target exists, the operator must create one through ordinary authenticated contact CRUD and explicitly select it. Whole-record preservation or a one-field edit is forbidden.

   Because old `contact_timeline_events` has no conversation identity, every `event_type='chat'` row on a tainted contact is unverified contamination. Automatic apply never time/email/title-matches, broad-deletes, reclassifies, or accepts it. The stage reports only safe scalar IDs plus paired HMAC content digests/key IDs and blocks until an actor holding both public-chat and existing contact/timeline mutation permissions exact-deletes each expected row or performs the exact merge above; changed/missing rows force re-inventory. There is no `preserve_unverified_mixed`, scalar-acceptance, or visible quarantine waiver. Verify requires zero chat links/events, zero chat-created mixed source records, and zero unproved chat-origin scalars across contact detail/timeline/summary/search/export/AI paths; the reconciled guards prevent recurrence. Tests mix a spoofed chat-created name/email with later legitimate email/SMS/company/history/manual edits and prove none of the original scalars survive implicitly.
8. `verify` is non-mutating and emits one bounded canonical verification artifact that binds all required zero results above to current schema/trigger, locator, runtime generation, deployment-drain, cutover-state, and inventory digests.
9. `prepare` consumes that local verification artifact plus an exact reference to the still-fresh controller-committed deployment-drain typed receipt, repeats the cheap exact checks under the organization lock, stores all launch receipt digests/timestamps, and CASes `disabled -> ready`. It is idempotent only for the exact same operation/generation/digests; a changed row, trigger, deployment, generation, or inventory leaves/demotes the scope disabled and requires a new verify artifact.
10. `enable` takes the organization lock, performs a fresh deployment-provider inventory comparison, and atomically changes only the exact `ready -> enabled` row when every stored receipt still matches, all pre-contract runtime classes remain absent, and no reserved config/claim/unmapped/full-graph invalid or inverse reference/actionable-legacy-CS/legacy-inbox/orphan-note/public-over-cap, unverified mixed-contact timeline, or unproved chat-origin scalar residual exists. An ActionLog acceptance without zero database proof is never sufficient.

The `token-retirement` phase is the mandatory owner for `0.6.0`: with public/agent/scheduler traffic disabled and its own drain receipt, it scans every conversation, converts any remaining plaintext or null legacy token to a fresh non-authenticating marker, creates a fully mapped expired/revoked allocator only when the bounded transcript can be mapped, leaves over-cap rows marker-revoked/read-only, and proves zero plaintext-like/null residuals plus zero query-token clients before bridge removal. It has separate dry-run/apply/verify receipts and can never reuse the `0.5.x` launch receipt.

The `unlink` phase is the only supported Noli unlink/replacement path after bootstrap and participates in the same cross-system cancellation/finalization protocol; it is not a local-only link clear. A CRM-initiated unlink first creates the dual-approved Noli registry revoke/change operation and obtains its signed cancellation request, while a Noli-initiated revoke resumes the already-created operation. CRM persists cancellation `requested`, sets the cutover user-barrier operation `materializing`, closes scope writers, runs the exact quiesce proof, materializes at-most-32-user pages to a stable sealed union, and demotes a ready/enabled row only after no old handler can act; an already-disabled row exact-verifies the same operation. Resumable exact-scope passes then prove every widget private/clean and locator, conversation, sidecar, strict schedule/progress/binding/lease, queue subject, legacy Inbox/CS link, external phase, organization lease, barrier-covered associated-user lease, and organization external grant absent. Generic lease cleanup uses only normal-ended/terminated-runtime contracts; a multi-organization user's unrelated live lease conservatively blocks. Noli organization erasure uses the GDPR authority header with the same bounded barrier protocol. The final zero-state function takes only the bounded Noli/raw-old, tenant, and organization locks, exact-matches the sealed materialization fingerprint plus a fresh stable union/zero proof, writes the durable redacted zero-state-unlink acknowledgment, and in one O(1) transaction deletes the cutover authority and organization link together. That deletion logically deactivates all joined barrier rows; it never reacquires every user fence. Consumed receipt rows survive, and physical barrier rows are subsequently purged in pages of at most 32 under terminal proof. The CLI supplies the stored acknowledgment to Noli; crash/retry uses the exact operation ID/status endpoint. Replacement is a later fresh controller-verified bootstrap, and receipt uniqueness prevents reuse. Clerk/sign-in code never links, unlinks, or replaces.

Launch ordering is mandatory and deliberately uses a maintenance window. Before CRM rollout begins, the independently reviewed Noli `crm_scope_bindings`/reservation dual-approval workflow, attestation and confirmation/status endpoints, cancellation plus CRM-completion-acknowledgment protocol, signing-key configuration, and shared production contract fixture must all be deployed and evidenced; a mock, partial endpoint set, or undeployed branch is not launch authority. Build/verify one immutable CRM compatibility image first; use the Hetzner contract wrapper to enter nginx/controller maintenance, disable old restart/timer paths, and quiesce, drain, and terminate **every** pre-contract app, MCP, widget/settings/Assistant writer, scheduler producer/worker/subscriber, queue worker, GDPR route, cron/timer, and callback. Obtain `PreinstallDrainReceiptV1` stage `migration_authorized`; while its controller maintenance fence is still held, run the compatible image's generated migrations plus the journaled generic-scheduler seed/transport cleanup and fan-out registry preflight/seed/verify, obtain the paired fresh `scheduler_cutover_complete` stage; the earlier one-shot migration step has already inserted/consumed authorization, and the first end-of-migrate guard transaction exact-reads that row while consuming/inserting completion only, whose DDL waits for/therefore exposes any surviving old transaction; then start the complete manifested data-plane fleet on exactly that image with the shared public-chat gate disabled, provision and claim a fresh per-process database identity for every role, and reverify guards/inventory/origin before loosening only the install fence. A paused old transaction/process must be terminated and rolled back before guard installation can complete. From guard installation onward rollback to old code is forbidden. For each scope, complete the dual-approval Noli request, obtain fresh link attestation plus `PublicChatBootstrapDrainReceiptV1`, bootstrap one disabled cutover operation, have the controller verify and atomically accept the separate confirmation receipt, then run locator/cutover dry-runs and resumable batches. Obtain a fresh scoped `PublicChatDeploymentDrainReceiptV1`, have the controller verify and registrar-commit it, and verify legacy schema, triggers, zero reserved/sentinel/unmapped/public-over-cap/unverified-mixed-chat-event residuals, exact remediations, exact locators, and runtime drain. Receipt-bound `prepare` reaches ready; atomic enable requires a live Hetzner controller/fence inventory recheck. A missing/stale/replayed/wrong-audience receipt, pending/cancelled Noli reservation, nonzero eligible gap/mismatch, changed collision set, Noli prerequisite drift, or restarted/unknown legacy process is a no-go. Tests pause an old transaction before migration and prove drain/termination or DDL blocking prevents it from committing across guard installation. This task may implement/test commands against isolated databases but does not call Noli/Railway/Hetzner, apply production migrations, or deploy without explicit approval.

### CustomerPublicChatSession (`customer_public_chat_sessions`)

- `id`: UUID primary key, generated by PostgreSQL.
- `organization_id`: UUID, required.
- `tenant_id`: UUID, required.
- `noli_organization_id`: text storage, required immutable canonical lowercase UUID after admission/bootstrap.
- `widget_id`: UUID, required scalar reference to unmanaged chat widget.
- `conversation_id`: UUID, required scalar reference to unmanaged chat conversation.
- `visitor_token_hash`: text, nullable only for an authenticated bootstrap that is atomically expired and revoked; otherwise format `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>`.
- `token_expires_at`: timestamptz, required. New and bootstrapped sessions use the approved 30-day lifetime.
- `token_revoked_at`: timestamptz, nullable. Closure blocks writes immediately; revocation blocks reads and writes.
- `last_sequence`: integer, required, default `0`.
- `last_message_ordinal`: integer, required, default `0`. Every tracked visible message consumes exactly one monotonically increasing ordinal under this row's lock.
- Reply capacity is an O(1) session invariant: nonnegative `reply_reservation_epoch` and `reserved_reply_slots` default to `0`. Every active processable visitor admission captures the current epoch on its job and increment-one reserves a slot; deterministic publication decrements exactly one only while the captured epoch still matches. First manual takeover and conversation close increment the reservation epoch and set the old epoch's aggregate count to zero in the same session-lock transaction before consuming any agent/close-note slot, so 999-visible+1-reserved and 998+2 can choose the lifecycle winner without a scan. A stale job may record suppression but can neither publish nor decrement a newer epoch. Reopen/new active admissions use the retained higher epoch.
- Processable-service capacity is distinct: nonnegative `outstanding_processable_jobs` defaults to `0` and is check-bounded by `2`. A processable admission increments it with the population/environment counts. Terminalization does not decrement it while holding later job/session locks; the separate environment-first release transaction below decrements it exactly once with the job's immutable release tuple. Terminal-but-unreleased jobs remain conservatively counted, and session deletion requires zero.
- Ordinary-work head: nullable `ordinary_work_head_job_id`, positive `ordinary_work_head_sequence`, and `ordinary_work_due_at` are all-or-none and exact-match the conversation's lowest job whose sequence is unresolved. Admission initializes them for the first processable job; every sequence-resolution/run-after/head deletion transaction point-selects the next job through the unresolved-sequence index and updates/clears the tuple atomically. It is routing/fairness state only and never authorizes a claim; drift fails reconciliation rather than causing a backlog scan.
- `automation_lifecycle_epoch`: bigint, required, default `0`, nonnegative and increment-only on each authoritative open-to-closed conversation transition. Reopen never decrements or resets it; jobs and CS actions capture it to prevent close/reopen ABA.
- `manual_intervention_epoch`: bigint, required, default `0`, monotonically incremented by every accepted authenticated agent reply and captured by each CS-pause proposal/action.
- Conversation lifecycle cleanup is durable and bounded: nullable `lifecycle_cleanup_operation_id`, `lifecycle_cleanup_kind` (`conversation_close | agent_takeover`), positive `lifecycle_cleanup_epoch`, database-time `lifecycle_cleanup_due_at`, bounded validated `lifecycle_cleanup_stage`, and at-most-4-KiB keyset `lifecycle_cleanup_cursor` are all-or-none. The first close/takeover writes them with the incremented applicable epoch in O(1); reopen is rejected while a close marker remains, and later agent replies exact-verify/leave an existing takeover marker rather than replacing it. Only the strict lifecycle worker, a stronger delete marker, or organization erasure may advance/absorb them.
- `bot_state`: text, required, default `active`; `active | handed_off | disabled`. The default is used only for a newly admitted current-contract public session; legacy bootstrap always supplies the explicit fail-closed state mapping above.
- `handoff_reason`: text, nullable, allow-listed machine code.
- `handoff_message_id`: UUID, nullable.
- `handed_off_at`: timestamptz, nullable.
- `created_at`, `updated_at`: timestamptz, required.

Indexes:

- Unique `customer_public_chat_sessions_conversation_key (conversation_id)` for point lookup and one allocator row.
- `customer_public_chat_sessions_scope_conversation_idx (organization_id, tenant_id, conversation_id)` for bounded exact-scope keyset/session validation.
- `customer_public_chat_sessions_ordinary_work_due_idx (organization_id, tenant_id, ordinary_work_due_at, conversation_id) WHERE ordinary_work_head_job_id IS NOT NULL` for keyset scanning only conversations with outstanding ordinary work; dormant/history sessions never consume the sweep page.
- `customer_public_chat_sessions_scope_widget_idx (organization_id, tenant_id, widget_id)` for scoped cleanup and GDPR discovery.
- `customer_public_chat_sessions_lifecycle_due_idx (organization_id, tenant_id, lifecycle_cleanup_due_at, conversation_id) WHERE lifecycle_cleanup_operation_id IS NOT NULL` for bounded close/takeover materialization and missing-strict-row desired discovery.
- `customer_public_chat_sessions_org_created_idx (organization_id, tenant_id, created_at)` for organization new-session admission.

The token hash is not indexed. Tokens have high entropy and are compared only after locator resolution plus the exact scoped conversation lookup. A check requires either a valid hash or both `token_revoked_at` and an already-expired `token_expires_at`. An authenticated first write to a legacy conversation locks it, proves no sentinel/legacy worker, maps all visible rows, and creates the allocator session: it hashes a valid existing plaintext token and replaces the legacy value with a non-secret rollback marker, or creates an immediately expired/revoked null-hash session and marker for a tokenless row. Public callers still receive `404`. The atomic close-note path is included among these authenticated bootstrap writers.

### CustomerPublicChatMessageOrder (`customer_public_chat_message_orders`)

- Identity: `id`, `organization_id`, `tenant_id`, `widget_id`, `conversation_id`, and `message_id` UUIDs, all required scalar values.
- `ordinal`: integer, required and greater than zero.
- Writer proof: required `writer_kind` is exactly `legacy | visitor | bot | agent | close_note | cs_approval`; nullable `writer_operation_id`, `writer_actor_user_id`, and paired `message_body_digest`/`message_body_digest_key_id` are all required for `agent`, `close_note`, and `cs_approval`, while the actor is forbidden for anonymous/worker/legacy rows and may later be operation-redacted without changing the other proof. Agent/close rows exact-match the durable command receipt's request/result/message coordinates; a retry can never allocate a second ordinal or accept edited text under the same operation. The keyed digest follows the shared durable-digest contract, is never exposed, and is deleted with the row during exact organization/conversation cleanup.
- `created_at`: timestamptz, required and set with database time in the same transaction as the visible message.

Indexes:

- Unique `customer_public_chat_message_orders_message_key (message_id)`.
- Unique `customer_public_chat_message_orders_conversation_ordinal_key (conversation_id, ordinal)`.
- `customer_public_chat_message_orders_scope_conversation_idx (organization_id, tenant_id, widget_id, conversation_id, ordinal)`.

All tracked writers—public visitor admission, deterministic worker publication, authenticated agent reply, atomic close note, and Customer Service approval—allocate an ordinal through the exact session row. Existing messages are deterministically mapped only during a fenced public or authenticated legacy bootstrap. Once a session exists, an unmapped visible row is an integrity/reconciliation failure and is never silently ordered by timestamp.

The legacy-message guard is an `AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE` row-level PostgreSQL **constraint trigger**, `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED`, so a legitimate transaction may insert the visible `chat_messages` row before its order row. At deferred execution it first acquires the same domain-separated conversation advisory transaction lock used by bootstrap/writers, then re-reads the exact legacy conversation, session, and order state. It fails closed if scope cannot be resolved and, whenever a sidecar session exists, requires exactly one message-order row matching message ID, conversation, widget, organization, and tenant. The trigger therefore blocks behind an uncommitted bootstrap and observes the committed session before deciding; an old revision cannot slip a missing row through the visibility gap. It also checks the session's immutable Noli organization fence; marker/sentinel sender tricks cannot bypass it. DELETE is not a writer event and remains available to dependency-ordered cleanup. An operation-authorized cleanup never creates/updates a visible message. Tests cover message-before-order and order-before-message success, missing/conflicting order failure at commit, update/reparent attempts, the exact uncommitted-bootstrap/old-writer interleaving, a delayed pre-cutover commit, erasure-fence rejection, and idempotent trigger reconciliation.

### CustomerPublicChatReplyJob (`customer_public_chat_reply_jobs`)

- Identity: `id`, `organization_id`, `tenant_id`, `widget_id`, `conversation_id`, `inbound_message_id`, `reply_message_id` (UUIDs), `noli_organization_id` (immutable canonical lowercase UUID stored as text), and `sequence` (integer), all required.
- Lifecycle fence: immutable nonnegative `widget_automation_epoch`, `widget_public_prompt_epoch`, `scope_public_prompt_policy_epoch`, `conversation_automation_epoch`, and `reply_reservation_epoch` bigints captured under the organization/widget/conversation/session locks at admission or provider grant as applicable. Provider grant, deterministic publication, reconciliation publication, CS proposal/action, approval, and notification grant all require exact equality to current cutover `public_prompt_policy_epoch`, server-owned widget `config.noliAutomationEpoch`/`noliPublicPromptEpoch`, session `automation_lifecycle_epoch`, and applicable reservation epoch plus the frozen prompt digest; a global/widget prompt edit, close/reopen, manual takeover, or deactivate/reactivate cycle can never make an older job current again. Every current-reservation-epoch publish or suppress/cancel terminalization consumes exactly one aggregate reservation; a stale-epoch job records suppression but consumes none.
- Phase fence: `status` text default `queued`, `run_after` timestamptz nullable, `claim_token` UUID nullable, `attempt_count` integer default `0`, `phase_started_at` timestamptz nullable.
- Processable reservation: processable jobs require immutable `processable_population_id`, positive `processable_population_generation`, and positive `processable_reservation_generation`; handed-off `no_reply` jobs require all three null. Nullable `processable_reservation_released_at` and lowercase SHA-256 `processable_reservation_release_digest` are all-or-none, initially null, and immutable once set. Admission atomically increments the exact environment, population-child, and session `outstanding_processable_jobs` counts with this tuple. After terminal/no-more-side-effects commits and every execution-liveness/class/scope/session/job lock from that work is released, a separate transaction takes daemon singleton when applicable → quota-environment counter → exact population child → Noli/tenant/organization → session → job, exact-matches terminal status/sequence resolution/zero live external-dispatch-execution-notification authority, every generation, and three positive current counts, decrement-once releases environment/child/session counts, and writes a domain-separated digest over immutable `{ jobId, populationId, populationGeneration, reservationGeneration, terminalStatus, terminalOutcome, releaseAt, terminalNoAuthorityProofDigest }`. Mutable prior aggregate counts are deliberately excluded. Retry recomputes the digest from retained immutable fields and no-ops even after unrelated admissions/releases; underflow, changed population generation, deleted session, or conflicting second release fails. Direct and sweep handlers, lifecycle/widget cleanup, and organization GDPR may invoke this same exact-ID capability only as a post-lock epilogue; crash before it leaves the global release lane authoritative. Terminal-but-unreleased remains counted and cleanup/GDPR cannot delete the job/session/population child.
- Result: `outcome` text nullable (`reply | handoff | cs_pause | no_reply`), `generated_text` text nullable, `public_reply_text` text nullable, `model` text nullable, `tokens_in`/`tokens_out` integer nullable, `byo_key` boolean nullable. `cs_proposal_id`, `cs_proposal_action_id`, and `cs_inbox_email_id` UUIDs are nullable together, deterministic/job-bound, and required exactly for a persisted `cs_pause` plan.
- Exact side effects: `metering_attempted_at`, `published_at`, immutable `notification_pending_at`, `notification_attempted_at`, `notification_sent_at`, `notification_settled_at`, `notification_cancelled_at`, and `sequence_resolved_at` timestamptz nullable, plus nullable `notification_cancel_reason` from one canonical enum: `manual_agent | proposal_approved | proposal_dismissed | proposal_invalidated | conversation_closed | widget_deactivated | widget_deleted | not_configured | recipient_or_sender_unavailable | user_erasure | organization_erasure`. Pending is required after a paused-CS proposal publishes and is historical; its unresolved state is derived by both settled/cancelled timestamps being null. Cancel time/reason are paired, forbidden after any notification attempt/phase, and mutually exclusive with settlement. Database lane checks bind each reason to its exact lifecycle/proposal/config/user/organization winner; it is not a caller-supplied status. Attempt/sent/settled/cancelled ordering and mutual exclusion are checked. Sequence resolution means the visitor-visible reply/handoff/no-reply outcome is final; it does not make an externally ambiguous or unresolved-notification job GDPR-terminal.
- Notification user subjects: nullable top-level `notification_recipient_user_id`/`notification_recipient_connection_id` are a subject-coordinate pair, with nullable immutable `notification_recipient_redacted_at`; the analogous sender-owner pair/timestamp exists only for a user-owned sender, while an organization-owned allow-listed HTTP ESP has none. Separate nullable recipient/sender lease ID plus positive generation pairs describe **live** authority, not immutable attempt history. The generated checks and guarded transitions recognize exactly four states: (1) a no-attempt pending/cancelled row has no notification attempt tuple, subject pair, lease pair, or redaction timestamp; (2) a live grant has the complete immutable attempt tuple, every applicable unredacted subject pair, the exact distinct-user lease pair set, and `external_phase=notification`; (3) an exactly settled or acknowledged attempt retains its immutable attempt tuple and unredacted subject pairs but has no lease pair or notification phase; and (4) a post-settlement role redaction has that role's subject pair null and its redaction timestamp non-null, independently of the other role. A subject pair is all-or-none; it is non-null only with a null redaction timestamp, and once cleared it can never be restored. A lease pair is all-or-none and may exist only in the live-grant state; settlement and exact lease deletion clear it atomically. One distinct user maps to one deterministic lease even if it fills both roles; same-user erasure redacts both role pairs/timestamps in one transaction, while distinct users may be redacted A-then-B or B-then-A without hiding or invalidating the remaining role. Before redaction the canonical notification JSON contains only HMAC subject/connection proofs, never these raw UUIDs. Transition tests exercise every legal edge and reject a partial subject, partial lease, settled-with-lease, live-without-lease, redacted-with-subject, restoration, or cross-role clear.
- Provider/accounting binding: `provider_started_at` timestamptz nullable; immutable `provider`, `provider_purpose`, and `provider_attempt_id` nullable until provider admission, then required together. Paired `provider_input_digest`/`provider_input_digest_key_id` use the shared `provider-input:v1` HMAC domain over the complete bounded provider bytes/role structure, and bounded `provider_config_identity` (at most 2 KiB canonical JSON with model/config version and no transcript/secret) is written in the same commit. For public CS, bounded immutable `public_prompt_snapshot` canonical jsonb plus paired recomputed `public_prompt_snapshot_digest`/`public_prompt_snapshot_digest_key_id` are additionally required and exact-bind the eligible source IDs/content/config digests described above; every nested source/config digest stores its own key ID, and all are forbidden for standalone attempts. The standalone frozen public-config HMAC likewise stores its digest key ID.

  A metering grant atomically writes immutable `metering_attempt_id`, purpose, paired `metering_request_digest`/`metering_request_digest_key_id`, and at-most-2-KiB canonical `metering_request_identity` containing only schema/version, exact organization/Noli scope digest, provider/model, tokens in/out, BYOK flag, paired allowance-account/meter identity HMAC+key ID, and unit/config version; it stores no key or customer text. A notification grant likewise atomically writes `notification_attempt_id`, purpose, paired `notification_request_digest`/`notification_request_digest_key_id`, nonnegative `notification_alert_settings_epoch` and `notification_routing_epoch`, and bounded canonical `notification_request_identity`. That identity contains only schema/version, scope digest, exact job/proposal/action IDs, the two epochs, template/locale/provider/origin versions, and separate `{digest,digestKeyId}` proofs for recipient user/connection/address, sender user/route/provider/sender/from identity, provider account, canonical operator origin/path, template, subject, and body—never a raw user/connection UUID, address, content, credential, or token. The outer request HMAC covers the complete identity plus fixed send options; it is not a substitute for the domain-separated component proofs. Each digest is recomputed before commit. The immutable attempt/identity/digest/key-ID/epoch group is all-or-none forever; applicable raw subject pairs are required at grant but follow the independently generated post-settlement redaction state machine above, and lease pairs are required only for the live notification phase. The post-commit client receives exactly the frozen payload that produced the immutable group; later allowance/config/recipient/template/origin rotation cannot change an existing attempt.
- External barrier: `external_phase` nullable (`provider | metering | notification`), `external_phase_started_at` timestamptz nullable, and `external_ambiguity_until` timestamptz nullable. The three values are set/cleared together and are never hidden inside metadata.
- External settlement: each phase has immutable `<phase>_settled_at`, bounded allow-listed `<phase>_settlement_outcome`, `<phase>_settlement_source` (`direct_return | authoritative_resolution | acknowledged_no_retry | organization_erasure` where applicable), and optional provider/status receipt ID of at most 256 characters. For `authoritative_resolution`, five additional fields are required together and forbidden for every other source: `<phase>_resolution_receipt` (at most 2 KiB validated canonical jsonb), its `sha256:<hex>` digest, bounded verifier-adapter name/version, and authenticated lookup-response digest. The canonical receipt's kind/purpose/attempt ID must exact-match the immutable phase attempt and its stored provider input/config or metering/notification request digest; its digest is recomputed inside the settlement transaction. Early provider resolution accepts only `ProviderAttemptResolutionReceiptV1` containing schema/provider/account-or-BYOK-key digest/purpose, exact provider attempt ID and request/input digest, terminal `completed | rejected | cancelled | proven_not_received` outcome, provider receipt/status ID, observed-at, verifier adapter/version, and authenticated lookup-response digest. `MeteringAttemptResolutionReceiptV1` and `NotificationAttemptResolutionReceiptV1` carry the corresponding exact request digest plus their nonsecret account/template identity digest and allow-listed terminal outcome; they cannot settle a same-labeled attempt whose billed units, scope, recipient, template, or content/config digest differs. Each allow-listed adapter must obtain that state from a documented authenticated status/cancellation API or verify a provider-signed receipt; an operator assertion, HTTP timeout, local log, or fabricated JSON is never authoritative, and a provider without such API has no early path. At/after the 4,200-second database deadline, provider-slot `acknowledge_no_retry` may instead accept unresolved transport only after exact execution normal-end/termination proof; it atomically writes the source/outcome and phase-specific reconciliation slot while clearing the barrier, never replays, and does not alter the already published/suppressed outcome. Metering/notification authoritative receipts follow the same canonical storage, exact-attempt/request binding, and atomic settlement rule for their supported adapters. No raw provider body/content is stored, and crash/retry insert-or-verifies the complete immutable settlement tuple before considering the phase cleared.
- Dispatch fence: non-null `dispatch_epoch` bigint defaults to `0` and monotonically increments for each direct-nudge binding. Nullable `dispatch_lease_id` UUID, positive `dispatch_generation` equal to the current epoch, `dispatch_no_new_start_at`, `dispatch_retire_after`, and `dispatch_completed_at` timestamptz fields form the live binding. Producer liveness adds nullable `dispatch_runtime_instance_id`, positive `dispatch_runtime_generation`, required `dispatch_runtime_start_attestation_digest`, `dispatch_runtime_started_at`, and `dispatch_runtime_heartbeat_at`, which are all-or-none and exact-match the processor lease while the binding-keyed session lock is held. Async production additionally has a positive never-reused `dispatch_redis_command_generation` and one current two-phase command shape. `binding_pending` is exact `{ clientClaimId, clientClaimIdentityDigest, registeredIdentityVerificationDigest, registeredConnectionStateDigest, redisServerRunId, redisClientId, clientGeneration, commandNonce, purpose='strict_direct_enqueue', bindingChallengeNonce, bindingChallengeAt }` with `databaseTupleDigest`, `currentCommandTupleDigest`, `registeredCommandStateDigest`, `controllerRootBindingAckDigest`, `controllerRootBoundAt`, acknowledged-result fields, and controller-fence fields all null. The registrar-only bind CAS makes it `registered` by filling those five fields all-or-none; only that database shape plus its exact fsynced controller-root commit marker is send-eligible. A normal acknowledged result is reconciled/folded only by the controller route, while ambiguity may add only registrar-authored all-or-none `{ controllerFenceReceiptDigest, controllerFenceTupleDigest, controllerFenceOutcome, controllerFenceVerifiedAt }` with a sufficient outcome; both paths feed the cumulative result chain before the current shape clears.  The row also owns generated `redis_client_handoff_count`, `redis_client_handoff_chain_digest`, and `redis_client_last_handoff_leaf_digest`; genesis is count zero/null leaf, and every normal/fence fold atomically advances the owner chain with the independently advancing root-claim handoff ordinal before clearing the tuple. Local mode requires every current Redis/binding/result/fence field null and does not alter any retained historical handoff chain. Immutable same-generation normal/ambiguous termination receipt fields are `dispatch_last_runtime_ended_generation`, `dispatch_last_runtime_ended_at`, allow-listed `dispatch_last_runtime_end_code` (`verified_success | proven_pre_send | possible_send_client_terminated`), a bounded scope/lease/runtime/client-shutdown digest, and nullable controller `dispatch_runtime_termination_receipt_digest` when adjudicated after crash. A new epoch is forbidden while a current Redis tuple or unproved command remains and otherwise clears the prior receipt/command diagnostics only after their cumulative digest is retained; verified success/pre-send clears the binding/lease after writing its terminal audit, while possible-send retains binding/lease, registered Redis tuple, and its ended receipt until a sufficient exact-tuple client-fence receipt is folded and fresh transport reconciliation completes. Crash/pause leaves current runtime fields and no receipt. The admission transaction creates the exact processor lease and complete binding or neither; every settlement/retirement CAS includes lease ID and generation and atomically deletes that lease, while the persistent epoch prevents a late attempt/proof from clearing or describing a newer generation. The direct queue payload carries this one-time generation and a deterministic transport subject ID derived from the job.
- Execution liveness: non-null `execution_epoch` bigint defaults to `0`. A live claim increments it and stores positive `execution_generation`, `execution_guard_kind` (`direct | strict_sweep`), `execution_guard_lease_id`, positive `execution_guard_generation`, bounded `execution_runtime_instance_id`, positive `execution_runtime_generation`, required `execution_runtime_start_attestation_digest`, and database-time `execution_started_at`, `execution_heartbeat_at`, and `execution_reclaim_after`. A direct invocation creates an exact job-bound processor lease; a strict sweep references and exact-verifies its schedule execution lease/generation/start attestation instead of creating another guard. Each external-phase grant stores the matching `external_execution_generation`. Normal no-more-side-effects completion atomically writes immutable `last_execution_ended_generation`, `last_execution_ended_at`, `last_execution_end_code`, and a bounded digest of the exact guard/runtime, then clears the live execution fields and deletes a direct-owned lease; a sweep-owned lease remains on its schedule until every same-generation job reference clears at the sweep boundary. Crash leaves the live fields. Controller adjudication additionally records the exact `execution_runtime_termination_receipt_digest`. Generation CAS prevents a late direct or sweep handler from acting through a later execution. This guard is independent of the pre-execution direct-dispatch binding.
- Direct transport cleanup: nullable `dispatch_cleanup_progress` and `dispatch_cleanup_proof` jsonb use the shared bounded transport schemas defined for `ScheduledJob`, with `subjectKind='reply_job'`, `subjectId` equal to this job, and generation/epoch equal to its persistent dispatch epoch. They are valid for active ambiguity recovery and deletion/erasure cleanup, not only last-schedule retirement. Any new dispatch epoch invalidates prior proof. This row, not an in-memory/widget-only cursor, owns restart-safe multi-page direct-nudge cleanup until the exact queue absence proof is consumed.
- Reconciliation audit has four immutable nullable slots.
