Outcome uses paired `outcome_reconciliation_action` (`publish_persisted_result | resolve_to_handoff | cancel_pre_provider`), `outcome_reconciled_at`, and `outcome_reconciled_by_user_id`. Provider, metering, and notification each use paired `<phase>_reconciliation_action` (exactly `acknowledge_no_retry`), `<phase>_reconciled_attempt_id`, `<phase>_reconciled_at`, and `<phase>_reconciled_by_user_id`. Each authenticated action requires its whole slot initially empty and CASes the exact expected phase/attempt; a 75-second outcome handoff never consumes the provider barrier slot, and one phase acknowledgment never consumes another. A later operation-bound user erasure may null only each actor while action/attempt/time remain durable.
- Organization-erasure proof: `erasure_operation_id` UUID and `erasure_cancelled_at` timestamptz nullable; both are set together only by the exact operation-bound GDPR transition and are not an authenticated reconciliation action.
- `result_metadata`: bounded jsonb nullable. The zod schema permits only confidence and validated flag reasons; deterministic CS row identities live in their explicit scalar fields. No secret, claimed identity, raw provider response, or unbounded transcript is stored here.
- Diagnostics: `last_error` text nullable, sanitized/truncated machine-safe detail only.
- Audit: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `completed_at` timestamptz.

Statuses are exactly `queued | leased | provider_started | result_ready | metering_started | publish_ready | reconciliation | completed | failed | cancelled`. `completed`, `failed`, and `cancelled` match the existing GDPR terminal-state classifier.

A database/service invariant forbids any terminal status while `external_phase` is non-null, a notification is unresolved (`notification_pending_at` non-null and both `notification_settled_at`/`notification_cancelled_at` null), a notification user lease remains, a dispatch lease remains unresolved, or a live execution-liveness guard remains. Any terminal job with a nonnull processable reservation additionally requires `completed_at`, `sequence_resolved_at`, one exact persisted outcome plus verified publication/handoff/no-reply/suppression proof, and the session-head advancement implied by that outcome in the same terminal CAS; otherwise it remains nonterminal `reconciliation`. After commit it releases later locks and enters the common exact-ID reservation-release epilogue. External phase/type/start/deadline/execution-generation nullability must be all-or-none and each phase must match its immutable attempt/purpose/request-digest binding plus the exact execution that granted it; provider input/config and metering/notification request identity/digest/key-ID pairs are immutable and all-or-none for their attempts. A **live** notification phase additionally requires the exact distinct-user lease set and every then-applicable unredacted indexed subject scalar. An already settled/acknowledged notification attempt requires lease zero and may retain both subject roles, one post-settlement-redacted role, or both post-settlement-redacted roles according to the generated state checks; redaction is forbidden before exact settlement/cancellation and lease zero, and it never alters the immutable request identity/digests. A new phase may be created only when the prior slot is null. Every non-null settlement time requires its source/outcome, exact immutable attempt/request digest, and phase-appropriate receipt tuple; authoritative receipt fields are all-or-none and recompute/exact-match their canonical JSON, while direct/acknowledged/erasure sources forbid them. Clearing an external phase, writing settlement proof, and exact-deleting its notification user leases are one CAS transaction, and no later write may alter that tuple. Live dispatch lease ID/generation/no-new-start/retire-after must be set together, generation must be positive/equal to the persistent epoch, database-time no-new-start must precede retire-after, current producer runtime must exact-match lease provenance, and a retained ended receipt must match the same generation with current runtime cleared. Completion or operation-retirement clears the live dispatch binding and exact processor lease atomically through an ID-plus-generation CAS but retains the epoch/proof history. Live execution fields are all-or-none, generation must equal `execution_epoch`, direct guards require one exact owned processor lease, strict-sweep guards require one exact live schedule binding, and `execution_reclaim_after` is only eligibility for the lock/ended-or-terminated proof above. An execution-ended receipt may match only the immediately preceding generation and is immutable. `sequence_resolved_at` requires one exact persisted outcome and either verified publication, explicit handoff/no-reply, or takeover suppression; it never clears an external barrier or unresolved notification. Each reconciliation slot has all-or-none action/attempt/time/actor requirements as applicable, while operation-bound user erasure may redact only the explicitly nullable actor/notification-subject scalars after their proof gates. Ordinary `cancelled` is pre-provider only; the sole post-provider terminalization is an expired-ambiguity organization-erasure transition that, while holding/proving the execution guard and every notification user lease/session lock, clears the external phase, operation-cancels any unresolved notification only under its no-attempt rule, clears claim/generated result, retains phase/attempt/settlement and execution-end diagnostics plus operation/time proof, and invalidates the claim in the same transaction. This keeps the terminal-state GDPR scanner sound without permitting a paused handler to call after erasure.

Indexes:

- Unique `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_inbound_key (inbound_message_id)`.
- Unique `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_conversation_sequence_key (conversation_id, sequence)`.
- Unique `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_reply_key (reply_message_id)`.
- Unique partial `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_cs_action_key (cs_proposal_action_id) WHERE cs_proposal_action_id IS NOT NULL`.
- Unique partial `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_cs_proposal_key (cs_proposal_id) WHERE cs_proposal_id IS NOT NULL`.
- Unique partial `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_cs_email_key (cs_inbox_email_id) WHERE cs_inbox_email_id IS NOT NULL`.

- `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_scope_status_run_after_idx (organization_id, tenant_id, status, run_after)` for exact-scope sweeps.

- `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_due_notification_idx (organization_id, tenant_id, run_after, id, conversation_id) WHERE notification_pending_at IS NOT NULL AND notification_settled_at IS NULL AND notification_cancelled_at IS NULL AND notification_attempted_at IS NULL AND external_phase IS NULL` for the exact `(runAfter,jobId)` keyset selector; the trailing conversation ID makes the at-most-one-alert-per-conversation page decision covering without inserting a non-cursor key between the cursor columns.
- `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_due_terminalization_idx (organization_id, tenant_id, run_after, id) WHERE sequence_resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND status IN ('leased','provider_started','result_ready','metering_started','publish_ready','reconciliation') AND external_phase IS NULL AND dispatch_lease_id IS NULL AND execution_guard_lease_id IS NULL AND (notification_pending_at IS NULL OR notification_settled_at IS NOT NULL OR notification_cancelled_at IS NOT NULL)` for autonomous barrier-free completion after a final-settlement crash.
- `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_processable_release_due_idx (completed_at, id) INCLUDE (processable_population_id, organization_id, tenant_id, conversation_id) WHERE processable_reservation_generation IS NOT NULL AND processable_reservation_released_at IS NULL AND status IN ('completed','failed','cancelled')` for the fixed environment row's global keyset cursor and environment-first decrement-once recovery; the capability still rechecks every zero-authority predicate and exact population/session generation after locking.
- Unique partial `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_dispatch_lease_key (dispatch_lease_id) WHERE dispatch_lease_id IS NOT NULL` for exact lease binding.
- `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_dispatch_retire_idx (organization_id, tenant_id, dispatch_retire_after, id) WHERE dispatch_lease_id IS NOT NULL` for exact erasure and autonomous stale-dispatch maintenance.
- `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_dispatch_runtime_idx (organization_id, tenant_id, dispatch_runtime_instance_id, dispatch_runtime_generation) WHERE dispatch_runtime_instance_id IS NOT NULL` for exact paused/crashed producer adjudication.
- `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_execution_guard_idx (organization_id, tenant_id, execution_guard_lease_id, execution_generation) WHERE execution_guard_lease_id IS NOT NULL` for liveness proof and operation-bound erasure.
- `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_execution_reclaim_idx (organization_id, tenant_id, execution_reclaim_after, id) WHERE execution_guard_lease_id IS NOT NULL` for bounded autonomous stale-guard recovery independent of erasure.
- `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_notification_recipient_user_idx (notification_recipient_user_id, organization_id, tenant_id, id) WHERE notification_recipient_user_id IS NOT NULL` for exact user-GDPR discovery.
- `customer_public_chat_reply_jobs_notification_sender_user_idx (notification_sender_user_id, organization_id, tenant_id, id) WHERE notification_sender_user_id IS NOT NULL` for a distinct personal sender owner.
- Unique partial indexes on `notification_recipient_user_lease_id` and `notification_sender_user_lease_id` when non-null, with the same-user invariant allowing the exact same job/lease tuple in both role columns but no claim by another job.

Each CS reverse lookup must use its unique partial index, then exact-verify that all three non-null IDs resolve to that same one job and scope before any Inbox payload is selected. A partial or mixed triple is protected integrity-blocked state, never an ordinary row. Generator fingerprints and `EXPLAIN` fixtures prove bounded raw action/proposal/email-ID classification; duplicate or cross-job claims fail at the database boundary.

No ORM relationship or database FK is added to unmanaged chat tables. The global UUID unique keys mirror the unmanaged tables' UUID primary-key identity and deliberately fail closed on any cross-scope reuse; they never replace organization-plus-tenant predicates on a tenant-data read, CAS, conflict verification, or cleanup. Five ordinary scope-owned entities are operational and hard-deleted through exact cleanup without soft-delete columns. The quota-event entity is scope-owned but survives ordinary resource/link cleanup only through its fixed rolling retention window. The global receipt-consumption security ledger has scalar/digest coordinates only, no ORM relationships, and survives scope cleanup under its audit-retention contract.

### CustomerPublicChatQuotaEvent (`customer_public_chat_quota_events`)

This privacy-minimal operational ledger is the authoritative rolling admission budget. It has no CRUD/query-engine route, search/export/response serializer, ORM relationship, or FK to unmanaged chat tables.

- `id`, `organization_id`, `tenant_id`, `widget_id`, `conversation_id`, and `source_id` are required UUID scalars; `noli_organization_id` is the immutable canonical lowercase UUID string. `event_kind` is exactly `session_start | visitor_message | provider_start`. `source_id` is respectively the exact session/conversation, inbound message, or reply-job UUID that won admission.
- `occurred_at` is required database time from the same transaction as the source admission/grant; `retain_until` is required and check-equal to `occurred_at + interval '2 hours'`. There is no update timestamp or mutable payload. Unique `(event_kind, source_id)` makes retries insert-or-verify one exact scope/resource event and makes cross-scope source reuse fatal.
- Exact indexes are `(organization_id, tenant_id, event_kind, occurred_at, id)`, `(organization_id, tenant_id, widget_id, event_kind, occurred_at, id)`, `(organization_id, tenant_id, conversation_id, event_kind, occurred_at, id)`, and `(retain_until, id)`. The first three support the fixed rolling-hour predicates; the last supports bounded expiry.

After discarding candidate reads, the service takes any already-required execution-liveness lock → pager-admission when applicable → fixed quota-environment counter → exact population child → Noli/user/tenant → organization → widget → conversation/session suffix in the universal order, revalidates, counts events with `occurred_at > clock_timestamp()-interval '1 hour'` and inserts the new event in the transaction that creates the session/message or commits the provider-start grant. An exact duplicate verifies the existing source/event and consumes no budget. The session's monotonic `last_sequence` is additionally the 500-message lifetime counter; historical bootstrap initializes it exactly and it never decrements. Deleting a terminal job, conversation, widget, locator, cutover row, or Noli link cannot delete quota events, so replacement resources still consume the local organization window. Ordinary unlink zero proof explicitly excludes unexpired quota events.

Expiry has one autonomous authority independent of tenant strict rows: manifested `crm-public-chat-retention.service` runs the immutable image with `mercato customers public-chat-retention-sweep --daemon --interval-seconds 60 --quota-batch-size 10000 --receipt-batch-size 1000 --terminal-batch-size 1000`. It gets one fresh principal per daemon start; restart demotes/retires the old one, cached-secret restart and timer/cron duplicates are forbidden. It can execute exactly five fixed-search-path functions: quota-event expiry, protected receipt-child expiry, durable event/queue terminal-root/counter plus client-invalidation cleanup, generic-schedule tombstone cleanup, and event-fanout registry-history cleanup. `quota-batch-size` is a per-tick successfully deleted **row** ceiling with a separately generated inspected-row ceiling; receipt and terminal batch sizes are per-tick completed causal-unit ceilings. The terminal ceiling is shared across event/queue terminal, client-invalidation, schedule-tombstone, and registry-history units by a persisted round-robin subcursor, so each continuously eligible kind receives service. None is a transaction-size argument. Its two already-budgeted database connections are fixed lanes: lane A runs quota expiry only; lane B alternates exactly one receipt causal unit then one terminal causal unit while both are eligible, skipping an empty/exhausted side but never taking a second unit from one side while the other remains continuously eligible. Each capability has a distinct transaction advisory lock within the 1,024 reserve, generated metadata-only index/cursor, and commits its cursor after each causal unit; neither lane starts a new unit after tick+50 seconds. One quota transaction may candidate-read at most 16 keyset rows, then lock the one protected environment counter before their at-most-16 sorted scope-population children, revalidate the candidate quota rows, delete them, and decrement child plus environment live-row counts; receipt and terminal transactions change at most one causal unit; an invalidation unit is a keyset of at most 16 rows plus its one fixed environment counter, while every other terminal unit is one causal root/tombstone/version. The quota exception has one environment counter, at most 16 population children, 16 quota rows, and the generated relation/advisory set in exactly that lock order; a receipt or terminal unit has at most one actor, tenant, organization, schedule/source, and root plus 16 counter-generation coordinates. Every transaction remains at most 64 total relation/row/transaction-advisory lock entries; a larger dependency set is persisted as child progress and handled later. Quota expiry requires database `retain_until`, fixed diagnostic, and resumes lowest key. Its lane advisory lock is only replica ownership and never substitutes for or reorders the universal environment→population→quota-row hierarchy. Receipt expiry uses `receipt_retention_window` and the fixed actor/schedule/source/receipt/root order. Event/queue terminal cleanup uses `terminal_retention_window`, processes its persisted terminal-versus-invalidation subcursor, and for terminal roots proceeds effect/child → execution → outbox → root → zero-reference dynamic counter, and only deletes 30-day terminal rows after exact transport/reference/key/dependency zero; nonterminal/leased/effect-started/ambiguous never qualify. Its invalidation sublane uses the protected `(expires_at,id)` cursor and deletes at most 16 expired rows plus exact-decrements the fixed live-row/byte counter in one unit; lock blockers advance inspection but never counterfeit deletion. Schedule-tombstone cleanup uses the fixed `generic_schedule_storage` cursor and deletes one soft-deleted non-strict schedule only after its active/waiting pointers, source/outbox/execution/effect/root, legacy transport, and Redis identities are exactly terminal/absent; the same transaction decrements its protected stored-row/byte charge. It advances inspection cursors past lock blockers, wraps epochs, atomically decrements the applicable counters, and needs no new admission. Direct DML is revoked; forged GUC/cross-function calls fail.

The strict-scope population constant is `P=40` per environment and the per-scope rolling maximum is exactly `R=100 session_start + 600 visitor_message + 300 provider_start = 1,000` quota rows/hour. A strict population slot is not reusable while that scope has any live quota row, even when its transport/lifecycle work is otherwise retired, so enable/burst/disable churn cannot exceed the population-derived arrival bound `P×R/60 = 666.67 rows/minute`. The fixed protected `public_chat_quota_environment` counter hard-limits live rows to `Q=P×3×R=120,000`: two nonexpired hourly cohorts plus one just-eligible cohort awaiting its bounded sweep. Every new event charges it in the same source transaction; quota expiry or exact GDPR decrements it in the same delete transaction; saturation rejects the new source+event atomically while cleanup/GDPR remain legal. Seed/readiness exact-count the ledger and reject counter/cap drift. On the qualified production PostgreSQL profile under concurrent maximum admission, lane A must sustain at least 10,000 eligible unlocked deletes end-to-end per healthy tick in at most 625 short transactions, with a hard `<=75ms` wall-clock bound per transaction including lock wait, statements, and commit, no transaction exceeding the generated 64-lock census, and the complete 10,000-delete batch finishing before the 50-second no-new-unit boundary; therefore the maximal synchronized `P×R=40,000` cohort clears in four ticks and, including phase to the first tick, in under five minutes. A measured lower floor, counter saturation/drift, no cursor progress, or oldest quota row eligible for five minutes fails quota-producing readiness/admission but never cleanup. Lane B must sustain its manifested 1,000 receipt plus 1,000 combined terminal causal-unit ceilings per healthy tick on the same profile. Receipt overload has deadline `2 + ceil(receipt eligible count / 1000)` minutes. The persisted terminal round-robin has exactly four kinds—event/queue terminal, client invalidation, schedule tombstone, and registry history—so every continuously eligible kind receives at least 250 completed units per healthy tick. Event/queue, schedule, and registry each independently have deadline `2 + ceil(that kind's eligible count / 250)` minutes; the qualified invalidation lane must delete 16 eligible unlocked rows per unit and has deadline `2 + ceil(eligible invalidation rows / 4000)` minutes, measured from its oldest eligible row. No aggregate `/1000` calculation may hide a skewed kind. Missing progress or exceeding any applicable deadline fails the dependent readiness/key-rotation/storage gate. Controller restarts the daemon even with zero traffic. Organization GDPR retains separate exact-scope capabilities. Tests race all five capabilities with grants/claims, forge lanes, synchronize the 40,000-row quota cohort, retain a slot through quota-only residue, cover `P-1/P/P+1` and `Q-1/Q/Q+1`, alternate continuously eligible receipt/terminal kinds, sustain each skewed single-kind and four-kind terminal backlog through wrap, cover 1,000 locked heads, churn/purge schedule tombstones, crash after every unit/cursor commit and wrap, full capacity/zero traffic, dynamic-counter retirement, measured service floors, the exact 64-entry transaction census, 30-day soak, and one bounded principal.

The quota guard has one explicit historical-binding GDPR rule. Ordinary rows retain their immutable admission-time Noli ID across permitted zero-state unlink/rebind so the local rolling budget cannot reset. During organization erasure, however, a bounded preflight under the **current** exact deleting fence/operation/Noli binding derives from the OLD rows plus current scope authority the complete sorted affected population-child set `{ childId, childGeneration, historicalNoliId }` for that exact local organization+tenant, stores its at-most-four count/digest and durable quota-lane cursor on the operation proof, and rejects drift or a fifth child. The quota-only delete lane processes at most 16 rows per short transaction: fixed environment counter → complete sorted affected child rows → current plus sorted historical Noli fences → tenant/organization → quota rows; it revalidates each OLD row's exact local scope and child ID/generation, deletes regardless of historical Noli coordinate, decrements the matching child and environment counts atomically, and advances the operation cursor/count digest. It cannot select another local organization/tenant or authorize any non-quota table. The final purge never bulk-deletes quota: it locks the same bounded set, proves zero matching quota rows and exact zero live-quota counts, handles the current strict child separately, and generation-deletes every child only when `strict_required=false`, outstanding-processable count zero, and registration/binding zero. Thus A-origin events cannot strand a later B-bound erasure, while a B fence cannot delete A's different local scope or race an A-keyed child mutation. Tests create mixed historical-A/current-B rows through a completed unlink/rebind, crash every 16-row cursor/count decrement, race an old-A population writer under its fence, erase B, finalize the bounded child set, and include same-tenant/equal-UUID cross-local negatives.

Processable reply admission is additionally service-shaped, not merely quota-shaped. The fixed environment/population counters enforce hard unreleased processable-reservation maxima `B_environment=160`, `B_tenant=16`, `B_scope=4`, and `B_conversation=2`; the environment counter also enforces `0<=live_scope_target_bindings<=4`. A job is counted from its accepting transaction through provider/transport ambiguity and any terminal-but-unreleased crash residue until the separate exact release CAS writes its immutable digest and decrements every counter. The environment pager-admission lock serializes the environment and at-most-four tenant population-child sum; the child and session `outstanding_processable_jobs` fields protect the scope/conversation counts in the universal order. Exact retries and handed-off `no_reply` messages consume no processable slot. At any boundary, an otherwise active visitor message returns nondisclosing `429 public_chat_busy` with bounded database-time `Retry-After` **before** transcript, job, quota-event, reservation, or transport mutation; cleanup, settlement, lifecycle, and GDPR remain legal at every cap. The independent strict reconciler—not a pager-selected scope and not a new process—runs one global processable-release slice before its scope duties on every loop and at least once per healthy minute. Its singleton lease owns a slice of at most 25 independent units/5 seconds without holding the hot environment row across the slice. For each unit it candidate-reads the global partial index strictly after `(completed_at,id)`, then one short transaction takes environment→child→scope/session/job and commits either release+cursor or blocker/CAS-loss-only cursor advancement; indexed EOF increments epoch/wrap in its own short CAS and returns to the minimum. No transaction spans two candidates or the five-second slice, and no unit enters with a held scope-target/execution lock. It completes at least 25 eligible unlocked releases per healthy minute, so all 160 drain within seven healthy minutes; with `I_release` the complete indexed population including blockers, oldest eligibility has deadline `2+ceil(I_release/25)` minutes. Reconciliation exact-counts unreleased job tuples against environment/tenant/scope/session counters and validates cursor/index state. Drift, cursor stall, or oldest-deadline breach fails admission/readiness instead of guessed repair. Tests hold/corrupt the earliest 25 while later rows release across wrap, crash before/after terminal/release/cursor CAS, race direct/GDPR exact-ID epilogues with the global lane, race `B-1/B/B+1` admission with release, change unrelated counts before receipt replay, retain an outstanding-only child/session, and prove no retiring/quota-only scope can hide release work.

The service proof deliberately ignores direct nudges. The pager may create a scope target only while the protected live-binding count is below four; a successful selection increments it in the same transaction and exact target settlement/retirement decrements it once. At four, that fire records a capacity wait and neither inspects nor advances the scope cursor. Four non-borrowable sweep slots with a 150-second hard ceiling provide 96 starts/hour of capacity against at most 60 new selections/hour. After a healthy transport/runtime recovery, all at-most-four inherited bindings start within one minute and finish by 3.5 minutes; thereafter one-per-minute selection has service slack. A just-missed scope among at most 40 therefore reaches target-handler start within a conservative 45 healthy minutes, and four preexisting ordinary jobs in one scope each receive the first fairness-cycle start within a conservative 180 healthy minutes. The whole 160-job environment clears within that same four-pass bound after admission closes; the `>=60 starts/hour` drain observation applies only while work is distributed across all 40 continuously due scopes, not to a sparse single-scope backlog. The direct slot only improves these bounds. Capacity-gate waits are included in healthy time; a live pause, external ambiguity, unreadable transport, or missed pager tick is an explicit degraded interval and blocks that scope's additional admission at four rather than hiding work. Virtual-database-time tests sustain the full legal offered 600-message/300-provider-rate traffic for multiple windows, prove atomic backpressure at every `B-1/B/B+1` and live-binding `3/4/5` boundary, Redis loss/direct flood/maintenance-heavy sweeps, inherited four-binding recovery, finite DB/Redis state, qualified distributed 60/hour drain, the 45-minute target-start bound, and the 180-minute fourth-preexisting-job bound.

### ScheduledJob additive dispatch binding

The existing scheduler entity gains five additive groups:

- Generic durable materialization: nullable positive bigint `schedule_revision`, positive bigint `generic_schedule_mutation_generation`, UUID `generic_schedule_incarnation_id`, bounded ASCII `generic_target_entry_key`, positive bigint `generic_target_entry_version`, lowercase `sha256:<64-hex>` `generic_target_registry_digest`, and nonnegative bigint `generic_projected_retained_rows_30d`/`generic_projected_retained_bytes_30d` are server-owned. After the drained seed/guard boundary, every `strict_owner IS NULL` row—including disabled/deleted tombstones—requires all eight identity/digest/projection coordinates; every strict row requires all eight null. Enabled/nondeleted generic rows require positive exact projection values, while disabled/deleted tombstones retain identity/digest but require both projections zero. A new generic creation receives a fresh database-generated never-reused incarnation, revision `1`, mutation generation `1`, and a server-derived immutable target-entry key/version; request bodies cannot select owner/source/entry identity. Revision increments exactly once on every execution-affecting target, payload, scope, feature, cadence, timezone, enable/disable, delete, restore, or accepted registry entry key/version/digest mutation. Mutation generation increments exactly once on every accepted generic schedule mutation, including presentation-only name/description edits and guarded undo/redo, and never rewinds or reuses a value. Nullable `generic_materialize_after`, `generic_last_materialized_for`, `generic_last_materialization_outbox_id`, UUID `generic_waiting_recurring_outbox_id`, UUID `generic_active_execution_id`, and bounded `generic_materialization_error_code` are also server-owned; an enabled/nondeleted generic row requires `generic_materialize_after`, while a strict or disabled/deleted row has no generic due authority or waiting pointer. The waiting pointer is nullable current-incarnation/revision recurring authority. The active pointer is a nullable **incarnation-wide, cross-revision** barrier shared by recurring and manual fires; disabled/deleted tombstones retain it until the exact old execution settles or terminal-cancels. At most one of each pointer may exist, only exact materialize/claim/mutation-cancel/settle CAS may set/clear them, and queue cleanup may not delete a pointed row. `generic_last_materialization_outbox_id` is non-owning diagnostic history that may dangle after claimed history expires and is never dereferenced as live authority. The exact due selector is `(generic_materialize_after,id) WHERE strict_owner IS NULL AND is_enabled AND deleted_at IS NULL`; a second covering projection index contains `(generic_projected_retained_rows_30d,generic_projected_retained_bytes_30d,id)` under the same predicate. In the ordinary success case `generic_materialize_after=next_run_at`; a typed pre-materialization blocker leaves `next_run_at` unchanged and moves only `generic_materialize_after` to a bounded database-time retry so a bad early row cannot starve later due rows. A successful fire transaction stores the exact due time/outbox ID, clears the error, and advances both due fields to the first cadence strictly after its captured database time. Direct DML, incarnation/entry-key/version/digest/projection change outside its exact capability, projection mismatch, revision or mutation-generation reuse/decrement/skip, cursor regression, target/scope change without revision, partial due state, or unauthorized live-pointer transition fails the generated guard. Production generic schedules use only this database cursor and the queue-durability outbox contract below; they never install a BullMQ repeatable or Job Scheduler. Authenticated manual trigger is the same durable path with a required authenticated request-envelope UUID idempotency key and does not alter the recurring cursor. Strict-owner rows use only the separate authority/bindings below.
- Generic stored-state bound: every non-strict `scheduled_jobs` row—including enabled, disabled, and soft-deleted rows—precharges one generated conservative **maximum lifecycle encoded charge** covering the largest allowed create/update/disable/delete/restore/tombstone shape for its registry entry. Nullable bigint `generic_storage_precharge_bytes` is server-owned, must be `1..65536` for every seeded generic row and null for every strict row, and retains that identical value until physical deletion; it is nullable only at generated DDL time for the drained seed. Generation-fenced `generic_schedule_storage` counters form fixed environment → system-or-tenant → declared-scope hierarchy with hard stored maxima: organization 2,000 rows/128 MiB, tenant aggregate 4,000/256 MiB, system 2,000/128 MiB, and environment 20,000/1 GiB. The environment row plus at most one tenant and one declared-scope child per live scope are charged to the fixed `queue_other_critical` infrastructure allow-list; their own generated maximum is 40,001 rows and they cannot borrow causal capacity. These same lifecycle-owned storage rows carry the protected materializer inspection/service cursor fields: first create, seed, or scope-move exact-creates the destination hierarchy and its generation before charging/inserting the schedule; disable/enable reuses it; the last physical schedule purge may generation-CAS delete an empty child only after zero schedule/root/descendant reference; and recreation receives a newer parent-allocated generation. No separate materializer-cursor row exists. Create—including disabled create—locks the complete hierarchy and rejects before inserting unless the full fixed lifecycle charge fits every cap. Same-scope update, disable, delete, restore, settlement, and cleanup never seek or change storage capacity and therefore remain legal at saturation; a target-entry change is accepted only when the original fixed charge already covers the new entry, otherwise it is a create-new-schedule migration. A scope move atomically transfers the unchanged precharge under the sorted OLD+NEW hierarchy described below and deletes an emptied OLD cursor child only after the same zero-reference CAS. Soft delete retains its charge through a fixed 30-database-day restore horizon and until the autonomous exact-zero purge below; restore is legal only before purge, while operation-GDPR explicitly and irreversibly waives restore and may purge earlier after its stronger proof. The scheduler migration adds `generic_storage_precharge_bytes bigint NULL`, its generic-positive/strict-null check, `(deleted_at,id) WHERE strict_owner IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NOT NULL`, and covering stored-scope indexes that include the charge; seed/readiness exact-count every generic row/precharge and counter generation, fail uncharged/drifted state, and reject a legacy population above a cap. A later same-scope counter recreation receives a newer generation, so delayed create/move/purge/materializer CAS cannot ABA the stored-state charge or cursor.
- Strict authority: nullable `strict_owner` is accompanied by server-owned `strict_role` exactly `pager | scope`. The one pager row has owner `customers.public-chat-recovery-pager.v1`, deterministic environment pager ID/name, `scope_type='system'`, and null organization/tenant/Noli/lifecycle/retirement/per-scope fairness/population fields. It alone owns paired `strict_next_execution_transport_id`/`strict_next_execution_scheduled_for`, which store the exact public BullMQ job ID/time returned by canonical `upsertJobScheduler` and advance only through exact-reloaded current/successor Jobs—never parsed private IDs. Pager-only state is paired `strict_pager_cursor_tenant_id`/`strict_pager_cursor_organization_id`, nonnegative `strict_pager_epoch`, and canonical `strict_pager_last_tick_at`; every inspected scope advances it and EOF alone wraps/increments the epoch. A scope row has owner `customers.public-chat-recovery-scope.v1`, exact non-null local organization/tenant/canonical lowercase Noli coordinates, population-child ID/generation, `strict_lifecycle` (`active | retiring`), nullable `strict_last_pager_visit_at`, and null pager/next-execution fields. Its retirement fields are all-or-none: `strict_retire_operation_id`, `strict_retire_kind` (`widget_delete | organization_erasure`), and `strict_retire_started_at`. Restart-safe scope fairness remains scalar/server-owned: paired reply cursor/epoch; lifecycle cursor triple/epoch; and paired cursor/epoch for `notification | execution_guard | direct_cleanup | terminalization`. Only its bound target sweep advances those coordinates. The lifecycle selector and bounded verification rules remain as defined below. Generated partial indexes are unique singleton `(strict_owner) WHERE strict_role='pager'`, unique scope `(strict_owner,tenant_id,organization_id) WHERE strict_role='scope'`, and pager keyset `(tenant_id,organization_id,id) WHERE strict_role='scope'`; the scope row exact-matches its generation-fenced population child. Generic CRUD, disable/delete, manual trigger, undo, hooks, and best-effort sync reject both strict roles. Only strict reconciliation or matching operation finalization may create/repair/retire/remove a scope, and only environment maintenance may remove the pager.
- Dispatch binding: non-null `strict_dispatch_epoch` bigint defaults to `0`, increments for every live binding, and never clears. Common bounded execution key, positive generation equal to epoch, no-new-start/retire/reclaim/maintenance/scan times, enqueue time, runtime role/instance/generation/start-attestation/start/heartbeat, same-generation normal-ended receipt, controller termination receipt, and producer-phase strict Redis command generation/current full run-ID+client+nonce+purpose tuple/acknowledged-result-or-signed-fence-receipt chain are all-or-none by phase. Pager rows alone may use `pager_install | pager_execution_claimed`; their binding has null processor lease and null Noli/organization/tenant/target fields, is protected by the environment pager session lock/runtime proof, and cannot become an organization GDPR subject. Scope rows alone may use `scope_target_granted | scope_target_enqueued | scope_target_active`; they require exact deterministic target ID, population/scope generation, Noli/organization/tenant, and one matching `gdpr_local_write_leases` processor lease with identical current-owner provenance. `scope_target_granted` is the committed pre-enqueue phase and requires null `enqueue_at`; enqueued/active require it. A pager execution that selects a scope creates the `scope_target_granted` binding/producer lease and increment-one charges the fixed environment live-target count in the same cursor-advance transaction before target enqueue; retry exact-verifies that charge and never increments twice. The pager binding never substitutes for it. Phase/check constraints require install versus execution reclaim horizons, scan-after not earlier than maintenance, and 300-second/latest-heartbeat scope-target reclaim beyond the 150-second sweep ceiling. Every pager install/fire producer and scope-target producer holds its binding-keyed PostgreSQL session lock from before final database grant through actual Redis/local command and success, proven-pre-send, or ended-ambiguous receipt. Target claim takes the binding-keyed scope lock and atomically transfers ownership from producer to target: it accepts exact `scope_target_granted | scope_target_enqueued`, revalidates the deterministic transport ID/envelope/population and producer normal-ended, or same-generation ended-ambiguous plus sufficient exact-tuple `RedisClientFenceReceiptV1` proof; runtime termination without that connection fence is insufficient, deletes the exact producer lease, inserts the new target-runtime lease with a higher never-reused lease generation, retains an immutable producer-handoff proof digest, replaces the binding's current-owner runtime/start/heartbeat/lease provenance, sets `enqueue_at` if the granted→active path lacked it, and CASes active. Retry exact-verifies the completed handoff; no partial lease/runtime replacement is legal. `scope_target_active` then heartbeats at least every 15 seconds/before each job claim and holds the scope lock through no-more-side-effects. Unique partial indexes cover role+execution key, scope lease/current-owner generation, target ID, granted/enqueued producer handoff, live strict Redis command/fence recovery, and maintenance selectors. Clearing retains epoch plus adjudicated proof; a scope cannot start a new generation/delete while same-generation reply-job guard references exist, while global pager history is independently retained.
- Bounded transport cleanup: nullable `strict_transport_progress` and `strict_transport_proof` jsonb columns use the same zod schemas as reply-job cleanup, each capped at 4 KiB. Progress is exactly `{ version: 1, operationId, subjectKind, subjectId, leaseId, generation, retirementEpoch, inventoryKind, state, pass, cursor, lastStableKey, examined, removed, updatedAt }`; proof replaces paging fields with `{ completedPass, inventories, provedAt, digest }`. `subjectKind` is `strict_pager | strict_scope | reply_job`. Pager progress may exist only for environment maintenance/active global ambiguity and never accepts a widget/organization operation. Scope progress binds the exact scope registration/population generation and matching lifecycle operation when retiring; reply-job progress owns direct-nudge ambiguity. The active-operation UUIDv5 name remains `noli:public-chat-active-transport:v1:<subjectKind>:<subjectId>:<retirementEpoch>`. Lease/generation nullability follows the role checks above. Any residue resets the pass, any incremented epoch invalidates proof, and only a bounded page-zero-to-EOF zero pass writes proof. Organization/widget cleanup may use only `strict_scope | reply_job`; encountering `strict_pager` is a hard matcher rejection, not authority to remove it.

Global pager and scoped target reconciliation settle only their own bindings. Pager install/fire uses the system binding/runtime proof and no fictitious organization processor lease. One verified pager fire advances its cursor and creates exactly one scope target binding plus its processor lease and one environment live-target charge in the same short transaction; retry resumes that frozen selection and cannot select or charge a second. A scope pre-send rejection, target acknowledgment, or post-absence retirement first requires its strict Redis command chain fully proved—an ambiguous command needs the sufficient exact-tuple fence receipt and fresh landed-target or absence reconciliation—then commits an immutable ID+generation-matched no-more-side-effects/no-more-send proof under its scope binding/session lock and releases that lock. A separate idempotent settlement transaction then takes the environment counter before the population child and scope binding, revalidates that proof, clears only its own binding, deletes exactly its one matching `gdpr_local_write_leases` row, and decrement-one releases the exact environment live-target charge atomically; zero/multiple/mismatched deletion or count underflow rolls back. Enqueue success is not target completion, and the scope binding/charge remains until the target handler's no-more-side-effects boundary. Timeout, disconnect, crash, or possible-send remains ambiguous; generation CAS prevents a late writer clearing/replacing newer state. A retiring scope accepts no new target and remains durable through transport/reference cleanup; only its final local zero-proof transaction deletes it. The global pager survives every organization retirement and is removed only by environment maintenance. These columns/checks/indexes are generator-owned by the narrow scheduler migration and all snapshots.

- Scope-parent binding: every selected scope stores immutable `dispatch_parent_pager_schedule_id`, `dispatch_parent_pager_transport_id`, bounded `dispatch_parent_pager_execution_key`, exact selected target ID/dispatch generation, and nullable adjudicated result digest. The parent coordinates are all-or-none with either a live scope `dispatch_execution_key` or a settled-selection tombstone. A unique partial `(dispatch_parent_pager_schedule_id,dispatch_parent_pager_execution_key) WHERE strict_role='scope' AND dispatch_parent_pager_execution_key IS NOT NULL` covers both live and settled selections, so a stalled/retried pager execution point-loads the one frozen scope even after fast target settlement and cannot scan/select/charge another. The bound target payload exact-matches both parent key and scope key; they are distinct typed coordinates and neither may be reconstructed from the other. The selection transaction writes parent tuple, selected target/generation, scope binding/lease, target ID, and pager cursor atomically. Scope settlement clears the live binding/charge but retains the parent tuple, selected target/generation, and required domain-separated result digest as the tombstone. It may clear that tombstone only after the pager execution has immutable no-redelivery end proof; conversely pager-end cleanup retains it while the scope binding is live. Scope-row finalization is forbidden while the tuple remains. A conflicting reuse, second scope for one parent execution, target/generation mismatch, premature tombstone clear, or parent-key rewrite fails guards. Tests settle pre-send and fast target completion before pager end, crash the pager before its own end, retry the same parent key, then end/clear in both orders and prove one selection/charge.

## API Contracts

All bodies and query/path values use zod validators in `apps/mercato/src/modules/customers/data/validators.ts`. Every token-bearing or session-dependent public response—including start/duplicate acceptance, append, poll, typing, errors, and preflights with session context—uses `Cache-Control: no-store` and minimal errors.

### Start a conversation

- `POST /api/chat/public`
- Metadata remains anonymous with the existing rate limit.
- Preferred request:

```json
{
  "widgetId": "uuid",
  "conversationId": "widget-bound deterministic uuid",
  "messageId": "client-generated uuid",
  "visitorToken": "43-character base64url secret",
  "visitorName": "optional bounded text",
  "visitorEmail": "optional bounded normalized email",
  "message": "bounded non-empty text"
}
```

- Preferred `conversationId` is not arbitrary. It must equal `UUIDv5(namespace=widgetId, name="noli-public-chat-conversation-v1:" + lowercase(messageId))`, where `widgetId` is the immutable server-assigned widget UUID and `messageId` is the random first-message UUID. The route recomputes and rejects a mismatch with the same invalid-request `400` before locator insertion or transcript write. Widget IDs are generated only by the server, never caller-selected, and a deleted widget ID is never intentionally reissued; conversation hard deletion exists only inside that widget's operation-bound hard deletion or organization erasure, never as a standalone while its widget remains reusable. The omission bridge generates `messageId` first and derives `conversationId` by the same formula. Thus a capability deleted with its widget cannot be recreated under another widget even by a caller who knows the old conversation ID, token, message ID, and victim origin; legacy non-derived conversation IDs remain readable only through their existing locator until cleanup and are never accepted for a new preferred start.
- In release `0.5.x`, all three preferred retry fields (`conversationId`, `messageId`, `visitorToken`) may be omitted together and are server-generated; a partial trio is invalid `400`. New widget code always supplies the complete trio so a lost response can be retried exactly. Omission support is marked deprecated in OpenAPI and is removed in `0.6.0`.
- Response `201` for new acceptance or `200` for an exact duplicate: `{ ok: true, data: { conversationId, messageId, id: messageId, visitorToken, greeting } }`. `messageId` and `id` are additive start-response fields, not mislabeled legacy aliases.
- For a new conversation, the raw token is returned once; only its digest plus a different non-secret legacy rollback marker are persisted. The separate legacy bridge may verify pre-existing plaintext and replaces it only when bootstrap succeeds. Name/email remain unverified metadata and `contact_id` remains null.
- Temporal-capability regressions delete a victim widget and separately erase its organization, then let an attacker configure the victim origin and submit the exact old conversation/token/message tuple under an attacker widget. Start must fail the widget-bound-ID check and stale append/poll/typing remain `404`; no future visitor text reaches the attacker scope.

### Append a visitor message

- `POST /api/chat/public`
- Request: `{ conversationId, messageId, visitorToken, message }`.
- Compatibility: in `0.5.x`, `messageId` may be omitted and is server-generated, but that request cannot promise network-retry idempotency. It becomes required in `0.6.0` and the omission is OpenAPI-deprecated now.
- Response `201` for new acceptance or `200` for exact duplicate acceptance: `{ ok: true, data: { messageId, id: messageId } }`. The legacy `id` field remains through `0.5.x`.
- Missing/wrong token, tokenless legacy row, and wrong scope all return the same `404`.
- Conflicting message-ID reuse returns minimal `409`.

### Poll transcript

- `GET /api/chat/public?conversationId=<uuid>&after=<opaque-cursor>&limit=<1..100>`.
- Preferred token transport: `X-Noli-Chat-Token` request header. `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` includes it.
- Query-string `visitorToken` remains an OpenAPI-deprecated `0.5.x` bridge for cached widget scripts and is removed in `0.6.0`. If header and query values are both present they must match exactly or the request returns nondisclosing `404`. `RELEASE_NOTES.md` documents the header migration, hosted-only default, origin configuration, and removal target.
- Header-token clients use keyset pagination with at most 100 messages per request. For sidecar-backed sessions, the opaque base64url cursor encodes version plus exact conversation ID plus last message ordinal; zod validates it and the service rejects it unless the embedded conversation matches the already-authorized conversation. Cursor tampering can only move within that possessed transcript and cannot alter writes or scope. Offset pagination is forbidden.
- For header-token clients, omitted `after` returns the first page in ascending causal display order. `nextCursor` is the retained last-observed cursor, not a continuation-only sentinel: a nonempty page returns the cursor for its last row, an empty page echoes the validated request cursor, and only an empty transcript with no prior cursor returns null. Additive `hasMore` tells the client whether to drain another page. This lets an idle poll retain its position and later observe newly appended messages.
- A query-token request with no `after` is identified as the bounded cached-`0.5.x` legacy poll mode and returns the complete ascending visible transcript so the old length-based widget continues to work. It is legal only for a transcript of at most 1,000 visible messages and never truncates. Controlled rollout audits **every** legacy conversation, not only open ones: before enablement, any over-cap conversation that still has a plaintext public token is closed if necessary and has that token replaced under the exact conversation lock with a fresh non-authenticating `noli-sidecar-v1:` over-cap-revocation marker, without creating a session or pretending to map only part of the transcript. Public lookup of that marker returns the same `404` as a revoked token. The scope is read-only for public/agent writes until separately archived/remediated, while authenticated paged possession-free readers remain available. Zero publicly readable over-cap conversations is a launch receipt gate; closing alone is not remediation. Header-token requests never use this mode. The full-transcript bridge is removed with query-token support in `0.6.0`.
- A token-bearing legacy conversation without sidecars may use stable `(created_at, id)` keyset ordering only during the one-release read bridge. Its first successful append atomically maps every existing visible row before admitting the new message. During `0.5.x`, after possession is proved, a sidecar-backed conversation also accepts an exact legacy-cursor version retained by a client across that bootstrap: the service resolves its scoped last message ID through the message-order row, rejects an absent/mismatched/unmapped row, and translates it to the ordinal boundary. Every response thereafter emits only the ordinal cursor. New/sidecar-backed sessions never otherwise fall back to timestamp/UUID order.
- Response preserves the safe legacy names: `{ ok: true, data: { messages: [{ id, sender_type, message, created_at, is_bot }], agent_typing, agent_typing_at, status, nextCursor, hasMore } }`. `status`, `nextCursor`, and `hasMore` are additive. It exposes no contact identity, raw/token hash, job, claim, proposal, model metadata, or internal error data.
- Every transcript response uses `Cache-Control: no-store`.

### Set visitor/agent typing

- `POST /api/chat/typing`.
- Visitor request: `{ conversationId, isTyping, sender: "visitor" }` plus `X-Noli-Chat-Token`.
- Visitor typing is header-only; there is no query-token bridge on this mutation. It resolves the conversation locator first, then under the global lock order requires exact possession, active widget, open conversation, active session, and an unexpired/unrevoked token before an exact organization/tenant/conversation update. A reserved rollback-marker value is never accepted as a legacy raw token. Lifecycle, token, locator, or scope failure returns the same `404` and performs no mutation.
- Any non-visitor sender requires authenticated cookies and exact auth organization/tenant scope. Anonymous callers cannot set agent typing state.
- Missing/wrong possession returns `404`; invalid body returns `400`.

### Close, deactivate, and delete

- Public message admission requires an active widget, an open conversation, an unexpired and unrevoked session token, and exact organization/tenant scope. The worker rechecks widget/conversation/session state under the global lock order before entering any external phase.
- A `handed_off` session still accepts possessed visitor messages for the human transcript, but each admission atomically creates an already sequence-resolved `no_reply` job with no dispatch lease/provider/queue call; automation never resumes implicitly. A `disabled` session rejects admission. Tests cover post-takeover visitor messages, close, widget deletion, and GDPR cleanup without stranded queued work.
- Closing a conversation rejects new visitor writes but retains possession-based reads for the token lifetime. Revocation or expiry rejects both reads and writes with the same nondisclosing `404` used for wrong scope/token.
- Agent replies to an already-closed conversation are rejected. Closing with the optional bounded note uses one O(1) server transaction: bootstrap/map a legacy allocator when needed; increment the conversation and reply-reservation epochs and zero superseded reservations; if supplied and fewer than 1,000 rows are already visible, allocate/insert-or-verify the final agent note plus message-order receipt; then set status `closed`, install the close cleanup marker, and ensure strict authority. At 999 visible plus stale reservations the close note can win and consume ordinal 1,000; at 1,000 visible an attempted note returns `409` without closing, while a no-note close remains legal. A close marker is stronger than a pending takeover marker and atomically replaces its operation/kind/epoch, resets the inner cursor, and requires a full rescan; crash at any old cursor boundary cannot clear the newer close. The chat UI sends that one request instead of closing first and issuing a second `/chat/messages` write.
- Conversation close and ordinary widget deactivation are O(1) logical lifecycle winners under the global lock order, never lifetime-row updates. The first open-to-closed transaction increments `session.automation_lifecycle_epoch` exactly once, commits closed state plus its operation-bound session cleanup marker, and creates/exact-verifies strict recovery authority; the active-to-inactive widget transaction increment-one CASes server-owned `config.noliAutomationEpoch`, commits inactive state plus reserved `config.noliLifecycleIntent={ operationId, kind:'deactivate', automationEpoch, requestedAt, dueAt, scanAfter, stage:'jobs', cursor:null }`, exact-mirrors operation/due/scan coordinates on the active widget-ID locator, and likewise ensures strict authority. Times are database time; `scanAfter` initially equals `dueAt` and only the strict lifecycle worker may advance it with bounded backoff after a blocked/CAS-lost inspection. Those state/epoch changes immediately make every admission, proposal approval, notification grant, provider/publication CAS, and reader/writer lifecycle check lose without scanning a job/session/action. Reopen/reactivate is `409 lifecycle_cleanup_pending` until its exact marker reaches a zero-residual pass; widget DELETE or organization erasure may atomically absorb/supersede the older marker, replace the locator tuple, and rescan from the start. Repeating the same close/deactivate operation exact-verifies rather than incrementing again.
- The strict lifecycle worker materializes the winner in bounded batches: it makes deterministic CS actions non-sendable, locally cancels only unattempted/unopened pending notifications with the allow-listed lifecycle reason, and cancels/resolves only queued or pre-provider leased jobs whose direct dispatch/execution binding is verified complete or exactly retired after transport absence proof. Effects are kind-specific: `conversation_close` leaves `visitor_token_hash`/expiry/revocation unchanged so possession reads remain available through their documented lifetime, while closed status/epoch blocks writes and automation; widget deactivation/delete disables and revokes each affected session when its conversation batch is reached. It advances the session/config marker after each at-most-25-job or five-conversation/10,000-row transaction and clears it only after a full zero-residual rescan. Work already at `provider_started`, `result_ready`, metering, notification, or publication cannot be cancelled: it preserves the provider result/usage and completes each already-started external phase exactly once, but every later grant/publication CAS requires captured epochs and suppresses stale bot/holding/proposal output. The job records `no_reply` (or an already-established handoff), resolves its sequence, and stays `reconciliation` while any external ambiguity remains. When a lifecycle batch terminalizes a job, it commits and releases every execution/scope/session/job lock before invoking the common environment-first exact-ID reservation release; widget/session/job deletion and finalization require the release tuple and zero session outstanding count, while a crash is recovered by the global lane even though the scope is retiring. Crash after the O(1) lifecycle commit but before the first batch is safe because the logical fence is already authoritative; high-cardinality and possessed-read-before/after-close-batch fixtures prove bounded locks/transactions, retained close reads, and eventual materialization.
- Close/deactivate tests pause queued and provider-started work at pre-provider claim, direct-dispatch ambiguity, provider call, result persistence, metering/notification call, and publication CAS, then exercise close→reopen and deactivate→reactivate before resumption. Each interleaving proves either lifecycle wins with no late visible/downstream write or already-committed publication wins before the epoch bump, with one meter at most, exact sequence resolution, and no stranded terminal job.
- Widget DELETE requires both `customers.settings.manage` and `customers.engagement.manage`. Its first exact scoped transaction is also O(1): under the global lock order it increment-one CASes `config.noliAutomationEpoch` exactly once for this delete operation, sets `is_active=false`, atomically absorbs any older deactivation marker, writes reserved validated `config.noliDeleteIntent = { operationId, requestedAt, scanAfter, noliOrganizationId, phase: "requested", cleanupStage: "jobs", cleanupCursor: null }`, exact-mirrors operation/database-time scan coordinates on the active widget-ID locator, insert-or-verifies the matching server command/ActionLog receipt, and creates/verifies active strict recovery authority. It does **not** scan or update sessions, jobs, actions, messages, or notifications. The outer CommandBus logger deduplicates this already-committed logical record; config shape without the transactional receipt is never authority, and a crash cannot leave a legitimate untrusted intent. Later bounded job/session batches apply the safe cancellation rules above. A live/ambiguous dispatch or execution binding remains pending until verified complete or exact proof-bound retirement; no cancellation path can make a terminal job while a delayed enqueue or external call is possible. Ordinary PUT deactivation writes only its distinct lifecycle marker, never delete intent. An unlinked widget can never have new public state; it is either synchronously hard-deleted in this first transaction only after an O(1)/bounded-index exact zero-legacy-state proof or returns `409` without an intent, because no safe immutable Noli schedule authority can be invented. A linked zero-session widget may be synchronously removed only when an exact **scheduler-desiring** source outside this widget's deletion set keeps the shared strict row desired-active. Scheduler-desiring has exactly five sources: (a) a scheduler-eligible session whose immutable Noli scope matches, `bot_state='active'`, token is unrevoked/unexpired by database time, widget is active with no delete intent, conversation is open, and cutover is enabled; (b) any nonterminal reply job, regardless of current lifecycle, until all barriers settle; (c) any pending conversation-close, agent-takeover, or widget-deactivation lifecycle cleanup marker; (d) another `requested`/`cleaning` widget-delete intent; or (e) an incomplete organization-erasure receipt. A cutover row alone, handed-off/disabled/revoked/expired/closed session without a cleanup marker, inactive/private clean widget, terminal job, legacy transcript/history, quota event, or contact/inbox/timeline residue is not scheduler-desiring. If no outside source remains, the widget and intent remain durable and enter the ordinary `retiring` transport-proof protocol even when no session/job has ever existed; an active strict row is never orphaned or deleted without proof.
- `noliDeleteIntent` is server-owned and immutable outside the exact operation-bound finalizer. Every settings update, activation/deactivation command, undo/redo, slug/origin change, and Assistant mutation locks and re-reads the widget; if a delete intent exists it returns `409` and cannot rebuild, clear, replace, or overwrite the reserved key. The settings serializer preserves all bounded client-owned non-reserved config plus every server-owned reserved key and rejects every client-supplied reserved key. Only a matching operation-bound finalizer may remove the widget (there is no "cancel delete" path in this release). Delayed settings-write-versus-DELETE tests prove the marker cannot be lost.
- Widget create, public activation, Noli-link establishment, and locator publication also take the organization lock and read the strict row. While it is `retiring`, they fail safely or keep the new widget private/locatorless until retirement completes; this release has no abort-retirement/reactivate shortcut. A pause after the retiring commit followed by create/activate/link cannot wedge the old finalizer or attach new work to the retiring row.
- Provider, persisted-result, metering, notification, publication, reconciliation, and unresolved dispatch phases remain fenced until exact resolution. A finalizer may select an inactive widget only when its exact reserved config intent exists and validates; `is_active=false` alone is never sufficient.
- Zero nonterminal database jobs is necessary but not sufficient for hard deletion. While terminal job rows still exist, the finalizer captures their exact queue subject identities, traverses each shared queue state in bounded restart-safe pages, removes and proves absence of matching direct nudges from waiting, delayed, prioritized, paused, waiting-children, completed, and failed states in both strategies, and treats any active invocation as a barrier until it reaches its database-terminal/no-more-side-effects point and exits. The durable cleanup cursor records queue/state/page proof and a final complete zero-match pass; no `0..-1` inventory is allowed. Local cleanup uses the common queue advisory lock. An unreadable inventory, unacknowledged removal, residual item, or active worker returns pending/reconciliation rather than deleting the authoritative job row. A delayed handler that finds a terminal/missing exact job is a strict no-op.
- Cleanup is bounded and resumable, not one unbounded transaction. Before destructive cleanup, the strict lifecycle loop services pending conversation-close, agent-takeover, and widget-deactivation markers in operation/UUID order: each pass handles at most 25 jobs or five conversations/10,000 rows, applies only exact older-epoch session/action/notification/job transitions, persists the marker cursor, and clears the marker after a zero-residual rescan without deleting transcript/business rows. Close and takeover markers are point-scoped to one conversation but still keyset their jobs/actions; close is the stronger marker, while takeover exact-materializes `manual_agent` suppression without revoking possession. A deactivation marker keysets conversations and their jobs. Marker work participates in the fixed maintenance fairness cycle, so high-cardinality lifecycle materialization cannot starve ordinary/provider/transport work or require a browser retry.
- While the strict schedule remains active, DELETE and organization sweeps advance only the matching server-owned intent through keyset stages (`reference_integrity` → `jobs` → `legacy_cs` → `legacy_inbox` → `conversations` → `ready_to_retire`) with a validated `{ stage, lastScalarId, conversationId?, dependency?, childCursor?, transportProgressRef? }` cursor. Each invocation handles at most 25 jobs or five ordinary conversations and at most 10,000 affected rows/240 seconds. The reference stage validates the complete widget/conversation, reply-job↔action→proposal→email, discrepancy→proposal/action, inbox-conversation, and note→inbox-parent graph in forward and inverse primary-key pages regardless of a referencing row's claimed scope/status/deleted state; any foreign/orphan/mixed-job edge becomes a typed multi-scope/orphan blocker before a parent can disappear. A job batch captures exact IDs, materializes non-sendable CS/cancel-safe notification/job state, proves/removes its direct nudge from every queue state, inverse-enumerates and deletes only exact same-scope chat-derived discrepancies, then in one scoped transaction deletes the deterministic action/proposal/synthetic-email rows only after fresh zero-inverse probes and finally deletes the terminal job/advances the cursor. The `legacy_cs` stage selects random-ID pre-contract actions only after full reference-integrity proof, by exact organization+tenant, parsed `payload.channel='chat'`, and the validated same-scope conversation ID. It proves the complete discrepancy/action/proposal/email chain is chat-exclusive before dependency-order deletion; missing expected children are already clean only with inverse zero proof, while shared, foreign, ordinary-channel, malformed, or conflicting identities become typed blockers and are never matched by contact/email. The `legacy_inbox` stage walks the same validated conversation set and resolves/unlinks each exact binding before any conversation can disappear; it keyset-deletes notes only with a chat-exclusive parent, while a mixed parent retains its notes and clears its chat link only while rebuilding every derived scalar from authoritative non-chat sources and exact-verifying paired source/result HMACs and key IDs. Unreconstructable contamination or an orphan/foreign note blocks without advancing. Conversation cleanup then selects one exact same-scope inactive conversation in the intent, revokes/disables its session, and deletes message-order/message children in bounded keyset sub-batches (`dependency` plus `childCursor`); it retains the session, conversation locator, and conversation until zero children and zero full-graph forward/inverse references are freshly re-proved, then removes those parents and advances `lastScalarId`. A single >10,000-row legacy conversation or note/discrepancy set therefore progresses without an oversized transaction. Crash before commit repeats safely; crash after commit resumes after the durable outer/inner cursor. Stage-end zero-residual proof restarts that stage from null on any unexpected residual instead of skipping it.
- After tenant batches leave only the widget, its active widget/slug locators, delete intent, and DB-only scope registration, the finalizer re-derives the exact strict-authority provider result while excluding this deletion set. If another scheduler-desiring source remains, one small transaction deletes the widget-ID locator, retires the slug locator, removes this widget/intent, and preserves the active scope registration. Retained cutover-only or private/historical rows never choose this branch. If no scheduler-desiring source remains, one transaction CASes the intent to `phase: "retiring"`/`cleanupStage: "transport"` and the scope registration to `strict_lifecycle="retiring"` with the same operation/Noli identity. From that commit, no reconciler/producer may create new scoped target or direct transport. The durable scheduler-owned retirement loop settles/proves only this scope's target/direct bindings and explicitly inventoried legacy per-scope transports, treats active invocations as barriers, and retries without traffic; it neither removes nor interprets the environment-global pager. After exact scoped absence, the registered customers finalizer uses one final small transaction to re-lock/revalidate intent, registration, operation, zero residual tenant state and proof, then deletes the widget-ID locator, retires the slug locator, deletes the widget, clears `strict_required`, and deletes the DB scope registration together. Quota residue may retain only the population child. A bare registration deletion before scoped transport proof is forbidden.
- If every database and transport condition is proved, the request performs exact cleanup and returns `200 { ok: true, data: { status: "deleted", widgetId } }`. If ordinary in-flight work or queue/schedule cleanup remains, it returns additive `202 { ok: true, data: { status: "deactivating", widgetId, pendingJobs, retryAfterSeconds: 5 } }`. If adjudication is required, it returns `409 { ok: false, error: "Reconciliation required", data: { status: "blocked", widgetId, blockers: [{ id, kind, subjectId, safeCode }], nextCursor } }` only to a caller holding both delete features. The bounded kinds are `job_phase | legacy_cs | legacy_inbox | transport | integrity`; blocker IDs are domain-separated deterministic UUIDv5 over operation/kind/exact scalar subject and never contain PII.
- Worker completion performs only a local database finalization attempt, and the pager-selected organization sweep retries finalization only for config-delete-marked widgets; neither emits a follow-on transport nudge. Cleanup does not depend on a browser retry and never converts ordinary disablement into deletion. Repeated DELETE is safe while the widget exists; a fully removed widget returns the normal nondisclosing `404`.
- Each cleanup batch runs only after the relevant jobs are terminal and its exact transport and complete bidirectional-reference proofs succeed. It uses job-bound scalar IDs and the unique reverse indexes to identify one exact Customer Service action/proposal/synthetic `inbox_emails` triple; it deletes exact same-scope chat-derived discrepancies first, then action, proposal, and email, with a fresh inverse-zero proof before each parent delete and only then deletes the job. A globally absent expected child is already clean only when no inverse row claims it; a present wrong-scope/content/parent or ordinary discrepancy blocks rather than falling back to claimed email/contact or broad channel deletion. Historical public-chat `contact_id` values are never used as trusted cleanup scope. The bounded `legacy_cs` rules above cover random pre-contract IDs. The bounded `legacy_inbox` stage validates each row/conversation and note/parent scope in both directions. It deletes an inbox conversation only when provenance proves it is chat-exclusive (`contact_id`/avatar identity null, chat-only source/channel, no non-chat proposal/action or authoritative email/SMS history, and one exact chat binding) and only after bounded dependency deletion plus inverse-zero proof of its notes. Otherwise it retains notes, clears only the chat linkage, and transactionally rebuilds every preview/channel/direction/status/unread/display/avatar scalar from authoritative non-chat records, exact-verifying paired source/result HMACs and key IDs; insufficient/conflicting provenance or an orphan/foreign note returns a typed reconciliation blocker and preserves the mixed row without making it readable through a chat path. Organization-wide GDPR may delete the whole exact-organization graph under its separate proof, but widget cleanup never deletes another channel's state or leaves note/discrepancy PII orphaned.

### Reconciliation operator contract

- `GET /api/chat/reconciliation?jobId=<uuid>` or `?widgetId=<uuid>&after=<cursor>` and `POST /api/chat/reconciliation` require `customers.engagement.manage`, exact organization/tenant scope, and a local authenticated user ID. Widget/blocker access additionally requires `customers.settings.manage`, matching widget DELETE. They expose only bounded machine status, phase timestamps, ambiguity deadline, outcome availability, typed blocker identities/safe codes, and allow-listed resolution options—never transcript/provider secrets. A widget query returns at most 100 blockers with a scope-bound keyset cursor.
- Job POST accepts exactly one action and reconciliation slot: outcome-slot `publish_persisted_result` only when a byte-bounded exact result already exists; outcome-slot `resolve_to_handoff` for stale/ambiguous **provider** work at/after the 75-second visitor threshold without replay; outcome-slot `cancel_pre_provider` only for `queued`/`leased` with settled dispatch and execution guard; typed outcome-slot `resolve_binding_integrity_to_handoff` only for the immutable stored-versus-current Noli mismatch tuple; or provider/metering/notification-slot `acknowledge_no_retry` for that exact ambiguous attempt after its database-time deadline or authoritative phase receipt. A provider acknowledgment CASes `provider_attempt_id`, requires database time at/after `external_ambiguity_until` unless a valid `ProviderAttemptResolutionReceiptV1` proves earlier terminal state, and in either case requires matching execution normal-end or `RuntimeTerminationReceiptV1`; the outcome handoff slot remains independent. An acknowledgment request supplies and CAS-matches `slot` plus `expectedAttemptId`; one phase cannot consume another's audit. `publish_persisted_result` invokes the same global-lock publication transaction as the ordinary worker: matching enabled generation, active widget, open conversation, active session, captured widget/conversation lifecycle epochs, exact scope, sequence ownership, and visible-capacity reservation are rechecked before deterministic bot/holding/CS publication. `resolve_to_handoff` uses that same lifecycle gate for any visible handoff. `resolve_binding_integrity_to_handoff` additionally requires exact recomputation of the persisted mismatch, zero provider/external/result/notification/dispatch/execution authority, and no possible delayed writer; under the same lifecycle/sequence/capacity locks it writes deterministic handoff or lifecycle-appropriate `no_reply`, resolves and advances the sequence, records the action receipt, terminalizes with `completed_at`, then releases all later locks before the common processable-reservation epilogue. Changed/relinked binding, missing tuple, any I/O attempt/result, or stale action fails without mutation. If close, deactivation, deletion, agent takeover, retirement, or erasure won, either outcome action durably suppresses publication to the appropriate explicit `no_reply`/already-established handoff and resolves sequence only under ordinary capacity/state rules; it never appends into lost lifecycle state. An acknowledgment clears only its matched external barrier, preserves the already published/suppressed outcome and diagnostics, sets terminalization due when no other barrier remains, and never converts a published outcome into another handoff. No action clears a still-unsettled phase early without the exact authoritative receipt and execution-liveness proof above. Generated action enums, request schemas, writer guards, the mismatch partial index, and exact replay tests include this binding-integrity slot; fixtures cover absent/changed/relinked current bindings, lifecycle loss, crash before/after terminal/release, and later sequence progress.
- Blocker POST binds one deterministic blocker ID and an allow-listed action. `legacy_inbox` permits only the attested exact unlink plus complete non-chat scalar rebuild; `legacy_cs` permits exact dismissal/inactivation and removal of only the chat-conversation binding while retaining a non-actionable conflicting row; an exact missing expected child is automatically already-clean and needs no action. `foreign_reference` requires both live scopes disabled, permissions in both, sorted dual-scope locks, and may mutate only the referencing row; `orphan_reference` requires owner permission plus fresh deployment-drain/global absence proof. `invalid_conversation_parent` may exact-delete the declared-scope tainted conversation or rebind it to an explicitly selected same-scope widget, never mutate a foreign widget. `transport` permits retrying proof but never attested deletion; unknown `integrity` remains blocked unless a separately typed exact repair is available. Each action re-derives the blocker and forward/inverse references under locks, is idempotent, and writes immutable redacted command/ActionLog proof in the same transaction. Direct SQL, email/contact inference, and arbitrary JSON patches are forbidden.
- Every transition is CAS-bound to job/blocker/operation/scope/status and exact reconciliation slot/attempt as applicable, sets only that immutable scalar audit tuple once, and writes its deterministic slot-specific redacted ActionLog record. Tests cover stale-result acceptance, provider handoff, publish/handoff reconciliation racing close/deactivate/delete/agent takeover/erasure, one job requiring metering acknowledgment followed later by notification acknowledgment, illegal early/wrong-slot cancellation, every legacy blocker action through final deletion, actor/scope mismatch, duplicate same-slot action, distinct two-slot dedupe, crash around transactional audit, late-worker CAS loss, and subsequent autonomous finalization.
- `failed` is legal only for a proven irrecoverable local integrity error that atomically disables the session and cancels later pre-provider jobs only after each dispatch binding is settled/retired; for every processable job the same CAS records an explicit handoff/no-reply/suppression outcome and proof, resolves the sequence and session head, and sets `completed_at`, or the row stays nonterminal `reconciliation`.
