After releasing locks it uses the common reservation-release epilogue. It can never let a later reply bypass an unanswered earlier message. Normal provider/config/allowance failures publish a deterministic handoff and complete. Ordinary `cancelled` is reserved for deactivation/deletion before provider start; the separately proved organization-erasure exception is defined above. Ambiguous or conflicting state remains nonterminal `reconciliation` until the operator contract resolves it or the exact GDPR-operation rule applies.
- The operator route is the supported phase/blocker reconciliation procedure; the cutover CLI owns launch, and no direct SQL runbook may mutate either contract.

### Internal Noli link cancellation and acknowledgment

- CRM exposes exactly one push/status authority through the private control service; there is no implicit polling worker. `POST /api/internal/noli/public-chat-link-cancellation` requires edge plus end-to-end CRM↔Noli fleet mTLS/service authentication before reading the bounded `{ cancellation: NoliOrganizationLinkCancellationV1 }` body. The control process does **not** turn an application verification into database authority. It forwards the exact duplicate-key-checked raw artifact bytes and digest over its root-owned socket capability to the controller's kind-specific `/v1/noli-artifact/verify-link-cancellation` endpoint. A disjoint controller verifier independently JCS/schema/signature/audience/key/freshness-verifies the complete artifact and exact environment/service, reservation/attestation/registry, Noli/local organization+tenant, operation, and reason. Only its `crm_noli_artifact_controller` database principal may execute fixed-search-path `public_chat_accept_link_cancellation_v1`; control/app/MCP/workers cannot. Invalid network/artifact authentication is `401`; unknown scope/reservation is nondisclosing `404`; a valid conflicting digest/operation is `409` and never changes state.
- In one controller-owned function transaction under the global locks, the already cryptographically verified typed artifact insert-or-verifies exactly one durable ledger lane by digest/nonce/reservation/operation. If attestation was never consumed, it writes `noli_link_cancellation_tombstone` as the mutually exclusive winner and atomically invokes the never-consumed finalizer/pending outbound-ack creation. If attestation consumption won, it writes `noli_link_cancellation_request` (coexisting with and exact-referencing that attestation), then writes/exact-verifies the cutover cancellation pair/ActionLog and `none -> requested` fence. No runtime may submit derived claims or skip the raw artifact. Registry change/revoke starts or resumes the control-runtime quiesce/unlink coordinator; `organization_erasure` starts or resumes its exact CRM GDPR operation. Every internally terminal result, including `never_consumed`, remains externally `202 { status:'quiescing', operationId, retryAfterSeconds:5 }` until separate controller acknowledgment signing and signed-artifact CAS commit. Only then does POST/GET return `200` with the stored terminal status, acknowledgment digest, and exact artifact. Other incomplete work returns `202 { status:'cancellation_requested'|'quiescing', operationId, retryAfterSeconds:5 }`. The handler never waits on provider/transport I/O and never fabricates completion.
- `GET /api/internal/noli/public-chat-link-cancellation/[reservationId]?operationId=<uuid>` uses the same fleet authentication and returns only the exact bounded state `never_consumed | cancellation_requested | quiescing | zero_state_complete | gdpr_complete | blocked`, safe blocker code/retry interval, and terminal acknowledgment digest/artifact when present. The terminal `CrmPublicChatLinkCancellationAcknowledgmentV1` is durable JCS signed output with exact audience `noli-public-chat-link-cancellation-ack-v1`, environment/service, reservation/attestation/registry, Noli/local scope, cancellation operation/reason, result, completion receipt digest/time, issuer/key ID, nonce, and signature; no PII or transcript/config is included. Noli verifies this exact artifact before finalizing a revoke/change/erasure.
- CRM containers do not sign that artifact, and caller-supplied claims are never signing authority. After the control-runtime terminal finalizer persists canonical base claims/digest and one random signing request ID, only a verified current `CRM_RUNTIME_ROLE=control` process may send `{ signingRequestId, baseClaimsDigest }` to controller-only `POST /v1/public-chat/cancellation-ack-sign`; app/MCP/worker/scheduler roles have no socket capability or acknowledgment-ledger read. Control cannot submit payload bytes, result, scope, reservation, operation, nonce, issuer, or key choice. The controller authenticates that exact live role, then uses its separate least-privilege database principal to load the immutable pending row through security-barrier view `public_chat_ack_signing_candidates_v1`. The view exposes only bounded canonical base claims and terminal proof tuple, selectable only by the controller role. The controller independently reparses/recanonicalizes stored claims, recomputes their digest, verifies schema/audience/environment/request ID, and validates result-specific terminal evidence: exact tombstone or consumed cancellation-request row and database-guarded never-consumed, zero-state-unlink, or GDPR-completion proof. Controller policy selects issuer/active acknowledgment key ID and one nonce, constructs exactly `{ baseClaims fields, issuer, signingKeyId, nonce }`, computes its JCS digest, and signs those bytes (only `signature` absent) with the distinct CRM-ack key. An absent/changed/nonterminal/unverifiable row, stale proof, database/view outage, caller mismatch, or key-policy mismatch fails closed without a signature.

  The controller durably insert-or-verifies `(requestId,baseClaimsDigest,finalUnsignedDigest,keyId,nonce,signature)` in its own root-protected store, then **itself** calls the only acknowledged-signature persistence capability: fixed-search-path guard-owner `public_chat_ack_commit_signed_v1`. The controller database principal has `EXECUTE` on only this function in addition to candidate-view `SELECT`; app/MCP/worker/scheduler roles have neither. The function locks the pending row, re-runs the same fresh source-evidence/no-recreated-authority checks, recomputes and exact-matches base/final projections, request ID, issuer/key ID/nonce and artifact bytes against the pending tuple, and may update only the signed columns by one pending→signed CAS. It trusts the authenticated controller capability for the signature but never caller-supplied terminal facts; PostgreSQL is not asked to improvise an Ed25519 verifier. A conflict or changed terminal source rolls back and the controller stores no false committed status. Only after that database CAS may the socket return success; lost response recovers through controller `GET /v1/public-chat/cancellation-ack-sign/[requestId]`, which rechecks the root-store/database tuple. The app only polls the CRM signed row and cannot persist returned bytes. The endpoint is not a generic signing oracle and cannot sign provider/transcript/config bytes or a different acknowledgment supplied by a fully authenticated malicious app. Noli verifies the final object's JCS bytes with only `signature` removed. Changed request/claims-digest reuse or key/issuer/nonce substitution fails; old-key recovery returns the original stored signature, and Noli's ack-key ring retains that key until every signed operation is consumed. Tests authenticate hostile app/MCP/worker roles and attempt forged direct/CAS writes, request another scope/result/payload, mutate/withhold the pending row, break the view/DB, race terminal deletion/recreation, and lose responses before/after root-store and database commits; only the independently proven controller candidate can ever become signed.
- POST loss, duplicate delivery, POST-versus-GET races, control/controller restart, and response loss before/after controller artifact verification/database commit are safe by the reservation/operation/digest claims; a changed signed artifact cannot take over. Noli delivers POST and polls this control-service GET until a terminal acknowledgment—CRM does not call a hidden paid/external worker. Cross-repository fixtures share canonical signed bytes and test hostile runtime bypass, never-consumed, pending/confirmed, cancellation-before-confirmation, response loss at each local/controller commit, blocked ambiguity, zero-state unlink, GDPR completion, key rotation, and Noli refusal to finalize on timeout/unknown/mismatched acknowledgment.

### Worker payload

- Queue: `customers-public-chat-replies`.
- Exact job nudge: `{ mode: "job", jobId, organizationId, tenantId, conversationId, dispatchGeneration, transportSubjectId }`, where generation equals the reply row's persistent dispatch epoch and `transportSubjectId` is the domain-separated deterministic queue job ID.
- Bound sweep nudge: `{ mode: "sweep", pagerScheduleId, pagerExecutionKey, scopeRegistrationId, populationGeneration, organizationId, tenantId, dispatchGeneration, executionKey, transportSubjectId, _idempotencyKey? }`. The target subject is UUIDv5-derived from the frozen pager-execution/scope-registration/scope-dispatch identity and is stored in the live scope binding before enqueue.
- The public target-worker normalizer accepts exactly three transport shapes: the bound direct job nudge; the owner-exclusive pager worker's complete flat bound sweep with optional `_idempotencyKey`; and the local pager adapter wrapper whose inner payload contains that same bound sweep and whose outer environment/pager/current-execution identity exactly matches it. The global Job Scheduler's static owner envelope is accepted only by the separate `customers-public-chat-sweeps` worker and can never enter this normalizer. Direct nudges validate against their reply row; sweeps validate pager execution, population/scope generation, Noli/local scope, dispatch generation/key, and deterministic subject against the exact scope registration before discovery/claim/effect. A stale generation, freed population child, forged scope, or global envelope on the target queue is a transport no-op plus reconciliation signal, never fallback authorization.
- For the local wrapper, outer pager/environment/execution and inner pager fields must match exactly, while the inner organization/tenant must come only from the frozen scope selection. Every UUID/date/mode is validated and unknown keys outside the documented shape are rejected. Async and local shapes normalize to the same internal scope-sweep command before any tenant query.
- Worker metadata declares exact organization subject extraction for the target queue, the exact `userSubjects: "dedicated-notification-leases"` sentinel meaning **zero payload-derived user subjects**, and durable-job self-fencing. Generator/CLI preserves that sentinel and forbids mixing heuristic-lease handlers. Payload validation and exact database authorization happen before any side effect. `JobContext` additively exposes `{ transportJobId, schedulerKey?, scheduledFor?, nextRepeatableJobId?, nextScheduledFor? }`; async mode maps public BullMQ fields without parsing job-ID strings. For the global pager execution, the wrapper boundedly reloads current/successor public Jobs after scheduler advancement, exact-verifies current ID/repeat key/environment pager identity, successor ID/same key, and positive integer-minute cadence alignment, then uses only those public identities. Local mode supplies exact current/next pager due identities under the same rule. Undefined/mismatched successor identity fails before scope selection.

The strict wrapper recognizes the static **global pager** envelope before generic lease logic and serializes it with the environment pager claim/session lock. In one short transaction it exact-compares the persisted current/next public ID/time pair. A current execution CAS-advances to the verified successor; an immediately preceding paused execution may be skipped only from point-read predecessor→current→successor continuity and is then a fenced no-op, while a later pointer makes a resumed handler stale. For the authorized current execution, it first locks/reloads the fixed quota-environment counter. At `live_scope_target_bindings=4`, it records bounded capacity-wait telemetry and settles this pager fire without inspecting or advancing the scope cursor. Below four, the selector starts strictly after the persisted `(tenantId,organizationId)` cursor, visits at most one registered scope, and advances the cursor for every inspected tuple—including retiring, already-bound, contended, malformed, or CAS-lost state. When the cursor is at the last tuple, the same fire proves indexed EOF, increments the epoch, wraps, and visits the first tuple in the same transaction; only a truly empty population yields no visit. After taking that candidate's population/Noli/tenant/organization locks and re-reading desired precedence/lifecycle/binding, one fresh desired-active, non-retiring unbound scope is frozen atomically with cursor advance, visit time, increment-one environment live-target charge, new `scope_target_granted` dispatch generation/producer lease, and deterministic target UUIDv5 name `noli:public-chat-recovery-sweep:v2:<pagerExecutionKey>:<scopeRegistrationId>:<scopeDispatchGeneration>`. Commit loss leaves neither cursor-only acceptance nor an unbound/uncharged target. Retry of the same pager execution resumes only its frozen scope/target and cannot select or charge a second. Enqueue possible-send belongs to the scope binding; the short pager execution then settles independently. SIGKILL leaves exact pager current/next identity and, if selected, one exact charged scope binding—never a random unowned lease.
- Public chat uses additive strict APIs. Any transaction creating its first scheduler-desiring source calls database-only `ensureStrictScopeRegistrationTx(trx, registration)`, which takes/reserves the population child, enforces `P=40/T=4`, and creates/verifies the deterministic DB scope row in the same commit. An active scope preserves pager/fairness coordinates; transport never runs in that transaction. `ensureGlobalPublicChatPager` is environment reconciliation only and cannot be called from admission or an organization transaction.

Quota-only or outstanding-processable-only children with `strict_required=false` are reconciled as capacity inventory only and are never returned to the pager target-candidate view or used to recreate a scope registration. Lifecycle precedence remains erasure → widget delete → close/takeover/deactivation → ordinary eligible state → absence, with exact zero-schedule proof rechecked under locks. Each desired/retiring scope must have one population child and DB registration; a missing row is repaired inside its retained slot. The global pager visits at most one scope each minute rather than promising a per-scope one-minute wake. With at most 40 counted scopes, same-fire EOF wrap, and cursor advance on every inspection, a continuously desired unbound scope just missed by the cursor is selected/enqueued within 40 cursor-visiting healthy minutes. The at-most-four inherited bindings after a healthy recovery start within one minute and finish under the 150-second ceiling by 3.5 minutes; subsequent one-per-minute arrivals have strict service slack. Including that capacity-gate catch-up and target admission, the conservative saturated healthy target-start bound is **45 minutes**, measured from committed desired state or release of a transient row lock to handler start. A retiring scope is never re-enabled/selected; it settles only its exact target binding, legacy scoped transport, active invocations, and finalizer. It cannot remove or mutate the global pager. If a desired/retiring row is missing, the generation-fenced population child preserves its slot and authorizes bounded repair only after fresh source/lifecycle proof. Finalization deletes the scope row and clears `strict_required` only with exact zero proof; quota residue retains the population child. Transient failure degrades only the affected public-chat readiness plus the global bound monitor, never rolls back to old code. ### Widget script and hosted page

- `GET /api/chat/widget/[widgetId]` validates the UUID, resolves the domain-separated `widget_id` locator, loads by the returned organization+tenant+widget coordinates, and revalidates the immutable Noli link, locator target, `is_active`, and public cutover state. It never performs an unscoped `chat_widgets.where(id)` fallback. Missing/quarantined/unlinked/stale/mismatched/disabled state returns one uniform `404` with `no-store`. A successful script serializes server values with `JSON.stringify`, validates colors/position, and renders tenant text only through `textContent`.
- Visitor widget POSTs include client-generated message IDs/token and typing/poll requests use the token header. Authenticated widget **creation** separately requires the durable client-generated command `requestId` described above while continuing to forbid a caller-selected widget ID.
- `GET /api/chat/page/[slug]` canonicalizes and resolves exactly one domain-separated `widget_slug` locator, then loads one widget using the returned organization, tenant, and widget predicates and revalidates the normalized slug, `is_active=true`, and `public_page_enabled=true`. It never globally scans tenant `chat_widgets`; missing/quarantined/stale/mismatched locator or lifecycle returns the same `404`.
- Widget create/update validates and bounds all fields and enforces global slug uniqueness. Existing duplicate slugs remain unavailable until an operator resolves them; no cross-tenant fallback is allowed.
- New/update slug admission takes a transaction-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock derived from the normalized slug, checks globally under that lock, and commits the widget mutation before release. Explicit update collisions return `409`; generated create slugs retry a bounded random suffix under its own lock. Concurrent create/update and existing-collision tests are mandatory.
- Authenticated POST/PUT accepts top-level `allowedOrigins: string[]` as the sole writable security field and maps it to persisted `config.allowedOrigins`. The existing client-owned `config` contract remains a bounded plain-JSON object through `0.5.x` (16 KiB serialized, depth/key/count/string bounds): all previously stored non-reserved keys round-trip and replacement retains the old client-owned replacement semantics, while the service reattaches server-owned reserved keys. The bounded raw-JSON reader rejects duplicate and ASCII-case-fold-colliding object keys before parsing. Every HTTP/Assistant/import value is then recursively rebuilt into null-prototype plain objects and arrays from I-JSON primitives only; accessors, symbols, non-finite numbers, non-plain prototypes, and ASCII-case-insensitive `__proto__`, `prototype`, or `constructor` keys at **any** depth (including inside array elements) are rejected. Client `config` likewise rejects every ASCII-case-insensitive key beginning `noli` and every ASCII-case-insensitive `allowedOrigins` at any depth. Exact server-owned top-level config keys are `noliAutomationEpoch`, `noliPublicPromptEpoch`, `noliLifecycleIntent`, `noliDeleteIntent`, and normalized `allowedOrigins`; none is sourced from or returned inside the authenticated client-config projection. Code never uses a generic deep merge, object spread, or `Object.assign` from client/stored config into an authority/config object; replacement starts from validated client data and reattaches the locked server values. Public rendering consumes only registered typed presentation keys—`primaryColor` under the exact color grammar and `position` in `bottom-left | bottom-right`—and never spreads arbitrary config. Adding a consumed key requires registry, validator, cutover inventory, and adversarial tests. A new linked/current-contract widget receives server-owned `config.noliAutomationEpoch=0` and `config.noliPublicPromptEpoch=0`; an unlinked private widget has no reserved authority and the later operator cutover initializes both. Updates preserve all server values except their specified locked mutation, activation requires valid epochs, and create never accepts a caller-selected widget ID, preventing deleted-ID/epoch reuse. On create, omission means `[]`/hosted-only; on update, omission leaves origins unchanged and an explicit empty array selects hosted-only. Authenticated list/read adds top-level normalized `allowedOrigins`; public widget/script/page responses never expose the administrative allow-list, either epoch, or delete intent. Invalid origins return field-level `400` and never partially update. Cutover uses the complete raw inventory above; a dangerous/duplicate/non-I-JSON legacy value quarantines public activation, while a private audited repair may reconstruct only safe client keys and drop the unsafe entries. Route and Assistant tests cover nested/conflicting/mixed-case origins, every root/nested/mixed-case pollution/reserved key, `constructor.prototype`, duplicate/case-colliding raw keys, arbitrary inert `html`/`script`/`apiBase`/`origin`/`visitorToken`/lifecycle-looking keys, unchanged safe old-client round trips, `Object.assign`/common merge variants, authority omission/overwrite, delayed old-client write versus delete/lifecycle CAS, global prototype integrity across a following request, and typed presentation rendering only.
- `APP_URL` is the sole production authority for both the canonical hosted origin and authenticated operator-alert origin. Startup/config validation parses it with `URL`, requires HTTPS, no credentials/query/fragment, and path exactly `/`, lowercases/punycodes the hostname, removes the default port, rejects IP literals/loopback/private names outside explicit test mode, and serializes one normalized origin with no trailing path. Production has no fallback: `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, `VERCEL_URL`, `Host`, `Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-Host`, request-derived host, routing rows, tenant input, and localhost defaults are never trusted. Development/test uses a separately explicit loopback mode that cannot pass production readiness. The normalized origin/fixed operator path/version digest is in the checked-in role manifest, controller deployment receipt, and every runtime start attestation; all app, MCP, worker, scheduler, and reconciler replicas must exact-match it before enablement or grant.
- Every actual public API request enforces the exact request origin against the configured list or canonical application origin. A missing `Origin` is treated as a canonical-hosted/non-browser request only when canonical `APP_URL` validation succeeded; `Origin: null` is always rejected. `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` may strengthen but never replace this rule. Non-browser origin forgery is contained by database admission/provider budgets.
- Every CORS-path response includes `Vary: Origin`. Because OPTIONS has no widget/conversation body, it may echo only a syntactically valid normalized non-null origin to permit the actual request; the actual request always performs widget authorization again. Once the actual request resolves a real widget and authorizes its normalized origin, **every** minimal application response for that request—`2xx`, possession/lifecycle `404`, conflict `409`, rate-limit `429`, and bounded `5xx/503`—echoes that origin in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so the embedded widget can observe status and safely clear stale possession or render retry/handoff state. Only widget/origin-authorization failures omit ACAO and remain an opaque browser CORS failure; no response exposes the allow-list or distinguishes missing from unauthorized widget scope. Tests cover cross-origin readable possession/lifecycle/rate-limit/unavailable responses after origin authorization, opaque wrong-origin/nonexistent-widget failures, absent/null/spoofed origins, default-port normalization, and untrusted forwarded-host headers.
- All modified routes continue to export `openApi`.

### Authenticated chat authorization

- Conversation lists and transcript reads require `customers.engagement.view` plus exact organization and tenant scope.
- Agent replies, agent typing, and conversation status changes require `customers.engagement.manage` plus exact organization and tenant scope.
- Every Customer Service proposal/action/synthetic-email list, count, detail, preview, stream/subscription, export, queue UI, and Assistant reader uses one shared channel-aware query/authorization service **before any payload, held draft, generated text, or transcript-derived summary is loaded**. Its database predicate is exact organization+tenant plus the explicit validated channel/job binding; malformed or missing channel is hidden/fail-closed. Chat-channel rows require the intentionally retained Customer Service/email base permission **and** `customers.engagement.view`; mixed email/SMS/chat pages filter unauthorized chat rows in the scoped query rather than fetching then redacting, and cursor/count semantics are computed over only authorized rows. Email/SMS reads retain existing permissions.
- Customer Service draft approve/dismiss adds mutation authorization on top of that read gate. A chat-channel action requires `customers.engagement.manage` plus `customers.engagement.view` and the existing Customer Service/email base permission; absence of any denies before action/payload load. HTTP approve/dismiss routes, queue UI, worker/subscription consumers, and `customer_service_approve_draft`/dismiss Assistant tools call the same channel-aware service implementing the deterministic chat approval contract. Email/SMS actions retain their existing permission and send paths; a chat action can never fall through to `sendReply` email using visitor `to` metadata. Cross-feature/cross-tenant tests cover list/detail/count/stream/Assistant and mutation callers, including an email-only reviewer on a mixed page who cannot infer a chat row from payload, count, cursor, event, or timing.
- Every authenticated full widget GET/list/count/config/embed/deletion-status reader, `manage_chat_widget` Assistant read, creation, settings change, and ordinary activation/deactivation requires `customers.settings.manage` plus exact organization and tenant scope **before any widget row or count is loaded**. An engagement-only chat viewer gets widget ID/name only through the already-authorized minimal conversation projection and cannot call the administrative widget projection. Widget DELETE additionally requires `customers.engagement.manage`. The route/service, not hidden UI, enforces this split; negative GET/list/count/Assistant tests prove a non-settings actor cannot infer config, origins, prompt/knowledge fields, embed code, deletion state, row existence, or count/timing across its exact scope.
- Authenticated widget POST requires top-level UUID `requestId`; agent-message POST requires UUID `requestId` and UUID `messageId`; conversation close requires UUID `requestId` and requires UUID `noteMessageId` iff a bounded note is supplied. These fields are additive to the request schemas but mandatory for the corrected mutation paths. The shared command-receipt service runs after authorization and before any allocation, returns the original allow-listed result on an exact committed retry, and rejects changed reuse as specified above. Both browser pages and Assistant persist/reuse the same IDs across network ambiguity.
- `/backend/chat` keeps `customers.engagement.view` as its base page requirement and conditionally hides/disables engagement mutations without `engagement.manage`; it does not request the full widget administrative endpoint, and widget controls/data are absent without `settings.manage`. `/backend/customer-service` keeps its broader existing email base access; its widget panel and all backing administrative widget queries are feature-gated by `customers.settings.manage`, while chat review rows independently require `engagement.view`. APIs remain authoritative. Authentication without the operation's exact feature set never grants access, and omission of tenant scope is an error rather than an organization-wide fallback.
- The authenticated widget route preserves its `0.5.x` wire contract while becoming explicit. `PUT` and `DELETE` continue to accept `?id=<uuid>`; `PUT` additively accepts a body `id` only when the query ID is absent, and rejects mismatched dual IDs. POST/PUT continue to accept the documented camelCase fields (`name`, `greetingMessage`, `config`, `isActive`, `slug`, `description`, `brandColor`, `welcomeMessage`, `businessName`, `publicPageEnabled`) and ignore deprecated legacy `bot_*` writes exactly as the current route does. One shared color validator accepts only `#RGB`, `#RGBA`, `#RRGGBB`, or `#RRGGBBAA`, normalizes hex case to one canonical form on create/update/backfill, and makes serve-time legacy/malformed values fall back to the fixed safe default before any CSS/custom-property context; length or HTML/JavaScript escaping alone is never treated as CSS safety. GET/POST/PUT response data allow-lists the existing safe top-level keys `id`, `tenant_id`, `organization_id`, `name`, `greeting_message`, client-owned `config`, `is_active`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, read-only `bot_enabled`, `bot_knowledge_base`, `bot_personality`, `bot_instructions`, `bot_guardrails`, `bot_handoff_message`, `bot_max_responses`, `slug`, `description`, `brand_color`, `welcome_message`, `business_name`, and `public_page_enabled`; list additionally retains `embedCode` and `conversation_count`, and additively returns normalized `allowedOrigins` plus a safe deletion-status code. It never spreads the database row, token, Noli binding, delete operation ID/cursor, or reserved config. Unchanged old page/Assistant request and response fixtures plus CSS-breakout payloads in both widget script and hosted-page rendering run alongside the corrected Assistant payload/result handling.
- The conversation list keeps its current response envelope and allow-lists the fields consumed by the page: IDs, unverified visitor name/email, legacy contact ID, status, timestamps/typing state, widget name, last visible message metadata, and visible-message count. It excludes token, sidecar, claim, internal error, and model fields.
- For a sidecar-backed conversation, every authenticated list/detail/preview/count/summary/action reader joins the exact scoped message-order rows: preview is the highest ordinal, count includes only mapped visible rows, and transcript order is ascending ordinal. A visible unmapped row is a reconciliation error, never silently included or timestamp-sorted. Only a legacy conversation with no session may use the bounded `(created_at, id)` compatibility ordering until bootstrap. Equal-timestamp and concurrent agent/provider tests prove all readers agree with causal visible order.
- Authenticated detail keeps `{ ok, data: { conversation, messages, nextCursor, hasMore? } }`, where only `hasMore` is additive. Through `0.5.x`, the exact safe conversation keys are `id`, `organization_id`, `tenant_id`, `widget_id`, `contact_id`, `visitor_name`, `visitor_email`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `visitor_typing`, `visitor_typing_at`, `agent_typing`, `agent_typing_at`, and deprecated `visitor_token: null`. The exact safe message keys are `id`, `conversation_id`, `sender_type`, `message`, `created_at`, and `is_bot`. Organization/tenant/conversation IDs are retained safe scope/relationship fields, not sidecar exposure. The raw secret is removed immediately; only the null token key is removed in `0.6.0`. Any later removal/rename of the other legacy keys requires its own compatibility release.
- Authenticated detail has two additive `0.5.x` modes. With no `after`/`limit`, it preserves the old client contract and returns the complete ascending transcript only when the exact visible count is at most 1,000; `nextCursor` is the last applicable cursor (or null) and the old page may ignore it. If the count exceeds 1,000 it returns an explicit non-partial `409 { ok: false, error: "paged_transcript_required" }`; it never silently truncates or allocates an oversized response. With an `after` cursor and optional `limit<=100`, it uses retained-cursor/`hasMore` keyset semantics so the updated UI can drain every sidecar or legacy page; legacy rows use the scoped `(created_at,id)` cursor until full bootstrap. Header/query/body scope cannot override authenticated organization/tenant. In `0.6.0`, the UI may switch the default to paged only after old-client compatibility is explicitly retired. Tests run the unchanged replace-state client and new drain loop against 0, 1, 100, 101, 1,000, and >1,000/equal-timestamp transcripts, proving the old mode returns a full response or explicit error and the paged mode never truncates, duplicates, or skips.

### Cache contract

- Every token/session/transcript/typing response and every authenticated chat/widget API response uses `Cache-Control: no-store`; failures do too. No cache key contains a visitor token.
- Every widget-script response uses `Cache-Control: no-store`; browsers/CDNs may not reuse a previously authorized tenant-branded script after cancellation or organization erasure. An ETag may remain telemetry-only but `304` is forbidden because every request must execute the live scope/cancellation/erasure gate and return a complete gated response. The script contains no administrative origin list, visitor identity, token, transcript, tenant secret, or administrative security state.
- The hosted page, including its `404`/disabled/collision result, always uses `Cache-Control: no-store`. It must revalidate current lifecycle and locator state rather than serve an activation decision from a shared cache.

### Request ingestion and edge isolation

- Every touched JSON mutation uses one shared pre-parse streaming reader; direct `req.json()`, `request.json()`, and read-all-then-validate helpers are forbidden. Authentication, exact route authorization, origin/rate-limit checks, and cheap scope resolution run before reading a body wherever they do not depend on it. The reader accepts only `application/json` with optional UTF-8 charset, rejects every `Content-Encoding`, rejects a declared `Content-Length` above the route cap before allocation, and counts a missing/lying/chunked body through `cap+1` under one five-second AbortSignal before parsing. Overflow returns minimal `413`; unsupported media/encoding returns `415`; timeout/malformed/duplicate-key/non-I-JSON input returns minimal `400`. It cancels and drains the stream, retains at most the cap, decodes UTF-8 strictly, rejects duplicate members before object construction, then applies the route's depth/key/count/string zod contract. Unknown arrays/objects cannot force unbounded allocation before validation.
- Exact decoded request caps are: public start/append/poll `32 KiB`; visitor typing `2 KiB`; authenticated agent reply/close/status `32 KiB`; widget create/update/delete/reconciliation and Customer Service settings/scenario/approve/dismiss mutations `64 KiB`; personal-KB selected IDs `8 KiB`; internal Noli cancellation/status/acknowledgment, GDPR, and controller reconciliation commands `32 KiB`. The separate streamed knowledge upload remains `6 MiB` multipart/`5 MiB` file as specified above and accepts no JSON fallback. Any newly touched mutation must enter this checked-in route-cap registry before launch; a default global 20 MiB body allowance is not authority.
- Production nginx defines matching exact-location limits as defense in depth and permits only ports 80/443 on the host. The app and MCP services use Docker-network `expose` only; app port 3000, worker debug ports, PostgreSQL, and Redis have no host `ports` binding. Port 80 drops all query arguments on its fixed canonical HTTPS redirect and never proxies a sensitive request. Controller/readiness socket and host-network inventories prove there is no non-loopback/direct app path that bypasses nginx, and the firewall admits only the intended ingress/controller management paths.
- Tests send over-limit declared, missing-length, lying-length, chunked, compressed, slow, malformed, duplicate-member, huge unknown-string, deep-object, and huge-array bodies through nginx and attempt direct host `:3000`; each produces the exact bounded failure with zero route write, queue enqueue, provider call, credential load, or excessive retained memory. A concurrency soak mixes those attacks with healthy capped public and authenticated requests and proves bounded latency/memory and healthy settlement capacity.

### Logging and telemetry contract

- Raw visitor tokens from body, header, or deprecated query transport; token digests/markers; visitor name/email; message/transcript text; provider prompts/results; and raw external errors are secret/PII and never enter application errors, queue/scheduler receipts, metrics labels, traces, audit logs, or structured request logs. Observable records contain only bounded machine codes, phases, counts/durations, and the minimum safe scoped IDs needed for operator correlation.
- The application request logger sanitizes the URL before any log/error/trace capture and replaces `visitorToken` plus token-like header/body fields with a fixed redaction marker. Error serializers and provider/queue wrappers allow-list fields rather than spreading request, payload, SDK error, or response objects. Queue payloads remain content-free and receipts never echo arbitrary payload data.
- Tests install capture loggers/tracers, exercise success plus validation/provider/queue failures through body/header/query token paths, and assert sentinel tokens, PII, transcript, prompts, provider bodies, and complete unsanitized URLs are absent. Forbidden-pattern checks cover direct request/error logging in the touched routes.
- The `0.5.x` query-token bridge is permitted only behind exact edge proof; raw-query logging is a launch blocker, not a documented residual. Both nginx server blocks and every controller/container log sink use a dedicated allow-list `log_format` containing only normalized method, `$uri` (never `$request`, `$request_uri`, or `$args`), status, bounded bytes, duration, and a safe correlation ID; they never log headers, bodies, upstream full URLs, redirects, or raw error objects. Plain HTTP never redirects a token-bearing request by replaying its query: the legacy route is HTTPS-only, and port 80 redirects only the canonical path with all arguments dropped or returns a fixed error. Application/APM/tracing instrumentation sanitizes the URL before span naming/error capture and has query capture disabled. A launch probe sends unique sentinel tokens through body/header/query success and failure paths, then inventories nginx stdout, Docker/container logs, journald/controller logs, application logs, traces, and APM export and proves zero sentinel/full-query occurrences. The cutover also inventories every preexisting query-bearing log store, applies a documented access-restricted secure expiration/deletion plan, and rotates/revokes any token proven exposed before enablement. Browser-history exposure remains an explicit compatibility risk, so new widget code never uses query transport and `0.6.0` removal remains mandatory.

### Provider admission budgets and bounds

- Paid-provider admission is serialized in PostgreSQL with its already-held execution-liveness lock as the earliest class, then after candidate reads the fixed quota-environment counter → exact population child → Noli/tenant → organization → widget → conversation/session/job suffix. It revalidates all coordinates, counts exact retained `provider_start` quota events against database `clock_timestamp()`, and persists its own event plus `provider_started` transition and child/environment count increment in the same transaction. “Organization→widget” describes only that suffix and never permits a later environment-counter acquisition.
- Approved launch defaults are 60 provider starts per widget per rolling hour and 300 per organization/tenant per rolling hour. They are conservative fixed limits and not a substitute for the origin policy.
- Failure to acquire/read the budget or resolve exact scope fails closed to a local handoff without a provider call. The existing process-local per-IP limiter remains defense in depth only; it is not a distributed spend boundary.
- Anonymous storage admission is independently serialized and bounded in PostgreSQL before insert: at most 20 new sessions per widget and 100 per organization/tenant per rolling hour; at most 120 accepted visitor messages per widget, 600 per organization/tenant, and 30 per conversation per rolling hour; at most 500 accepted visitor messages over one conversation's lifetime; and at most 1,000 total visible messages from all writers per conversation. Rolling counts use the retained quota-event ledger, not cleanup-eligible session/job rows; lifetime count uses monotonic session `last_sequence`. Under the session lock the O(1) equation is exactly `last_message_ordinal + reserved_reply_slots + new_visible_rows + new_reply_reservations <= 1000`; no backlog scan participates. An active-session visitor admission consumes one visible ordinal and one potential-reply reservation; handed-off/no-reply admission consumes only its visible ordinal. Bot/holding/handoff publication converts its own current-epoch reservation into one visible ordinal atomically. Every same-epoch suppress/cancel/terminal no-publication path—including deactivation cleanup—decrements exactly one reservation, while stale-epoch work consumes none; close/takeover rotate the epoch and zero the superseded aggregate once. Agent reply/close-note writers consume capacity only after their lifecycle CAS releases or preserves reservations as specified. A duplicate retry consumes nothing. Counts use exact scope, advisory locks in organization-then-widget-then-conversation order, and `clock_timestamp()`; the event insert and source write are atomic. Reconciliation verifies aggregate slots equal the bounded count of current-epoch unresolved reserving jobs, and drift is a blocker rather than a guessed repair. Tests cover deactivate→bounded cleanup→reactivate, suppression crashes, current/stale epochs, and 999/1,000 edges. A count/read failure rejects admission without writing or enqueueing.
- An exhausted rolling admission budget returns minimal `429` with a bounded `Retry-After`; a budget database error returns minimal `503`. Neither response writes a message/session/job nor reveals which organization/widget/conversation limit fired. Concurrency tests distribute callers across many synthetic IPs and prove the database limit, not the process-local limiter, is authoritative.
- Exact zod bounds are: widget/name/business name 100 characters, visitor name 100, normalized email 254, greeting/welcome/description 500, visitor or agent message 1–4,000, 25 origins of at most 2,048 each, CS public/held draft 4,000, sanitized error 500, and serialized result metadata 16 KiB. Provider context contains at most the latest 40 messages from the causal job-sequence snapshot and 16,000 total characters; output is capped at 1,024 tokens and persisted public text at 4,000 characters.
- A sweep performs a nonlocking exact-scope discovery of at most one lowest unresolved due job per conversation, ordered by due time, sequence, and ID, and limits that fair set to 25 conversations. It then acquires the full global lock order and claims exactly one candidate just in time; a changed/busy candidate is skipped without first locking a job row or preclaiming a batch. It processes at most one job per selected conversation and emits no yield/re-enqueue transport. Provider timeout is 45 seconds, the pre-provider lease is 60 seconds, and stale `provider_started` recovery begins only after 75 seconds without replay.

## Internationalization (i18n)

Both existing widget-management surfaces gain an allowed-origins field and hosted-only status text. New strings use `useT()` and are added to all four customers locale files (`en`, `de`, `es`, and `pl`) with English fallback text. API validation errors remain machine-oriented and minimal. An operator reconciliation UI is still outside this patch; if added later, it must follow the same locale contract.

## UI/UX

The embedded/hosted visual widget contract remains unchanged except for accessible error/status feedback. The authenticated widget-management forms add one security field:

- `Allowed website origins` is a newline-delimited input normalized to chips/rows on blur, with an example such as `https://www.example.com`, a 25-origin counter, inline validation, and clear text that an empty list permits only the Noli-hosted page;
- create, edit, and list responses expose `allowedOrigins` only to authenticated settings managers; the copy-embed control is disabled and explains why while the widget is hosted-only;
- both `/backend/chat` and `/backend/customer-service` use the same parser/labels and render hosted-only versus configured-domain status without color as the sole indicator;
- both widget pages branch on DELETE results: `200` removes the row, `202` announces deactivation/pending work and refreshes status, and `409` announces reconciliation required without claiming deletion. The Assistant `manage_chat_widget` consumer uses the exact create/edit/toggle payloads and the same `200`/`202`/`409` result handling;
- page-level access stays compatible: chat requires engagement view, Customer Service retains its broader email access, and widget/settings controls are rendered only with settings permission while transcript mutations require engagement-manage;
- errors use `role="alert"`/`aria-live`, every input has a label and description, controls retain visible focus, interactive targets are at least 44px, and the existing responsive layout has no new horizontal scrolling.

Implementation follows the repository UI conventions rather than introducing parallel primitives: use `Button`/`IconButton` and `ConfirmDialog` from `@open-mercato/ui`, use the shared `apiCall`/`apiCallOrThrow` client, and route destructive/in-flight mutations through `useGuardedMutation`/`runMutation` with the operation's retry context. Forms support Cmd/Ctrl+Enter where submit is already conventional and Escape only where it safely closes a dialog without discarding an active mutation. Destructive controls retain focus or restore it to the invoking row after dialog closure; pending controls expose an accessible busy state.

Playwright/browser proof queries controls by role, label, and description rather than CSS implementation details. It verifies live-region announcements for `202`/`409`/origin errors, focus restoration, keyboard submission/cancellation, 44px targets, permission-hidden controls, hosted-only copy-disable explanation, and no horizontal overflow at 320px plus the existing desktop breakpoints. The same English source strings exist in `en`, `de`, `es`, and `pl` via `useT()`; no security state is conveyed by color alone.

Visitor-facing security changes are behavioral:

- a message remains optimistic in the widget while POST is pending;
- client IDs/token survive response loss in session storage;
- a `404` possession failure clears the stale local session instead of retrying tokenless;
- provider ambiguity produces the configured human-handoff text rather than duplicate or indefinite silence;
- a disabled or collision-ambiguous hosted page renders the existing not-found experience.
- an origin denial renders/announces a generic unavailable state without disclosing the allow-list.

Tenant-provided strings always enter the DOM through `textContent`. Static trusted SVG/markup may remain in `innerHTML` only when it contains no tenant/user data.

Server generation uses context-specific encoders rather than a generic replacement: HTML text nodes escape `&`, `<`, and `>`; quoted attributes also escape both quote forms; URLs are constructed with `URL` and then attribute-escaped; JavaScript string data is serialized with `JSON.stringify` and escapes `<`, U+2028, and U+2029 before entering an inline script. Hosted-page tenant values are assigned with `textContent` or safe attributes after parsing inert data. Regression payloads include `</script>`, both quotes, ampersands, markup, and U+2028/U+2029 in every widget and hosted-page field.

## Configuration

- Production requires `QUEUE_STRATEGY=async`, a valid queue Redis URL, discovered workers enabled, the combined generic DB-time materializer/C1 worker, owner-exclusive global pager worker, durable outbox dispatcher, and autonomous strict reconciler running, plus BullMQ `>=5.66.5 <6` with the tested strict Job Scheduler/current-job reload/next-ID capabilities. The literal strategy value is `async`; `redis` is invalid for the current factory. Wrong version, missing capabilities, missing generic materializer/outbox readiness, residual generic recurring Redis state, an incomplete startup reconciliation pass, or an unproved canonical strict recovery schedule fails readiness.
- Production requires a valid canonical HTTPS `APP_URL`; invalid/missing configuration fails closed for public chat and is reported by startup/config checks.
- Visitor tokens remain random client/server secrets and are not derived from a deployment secret. This contract does add explicit control-plane signing configuration: the Hetzner/CI controller owns environment-specific runtime-receipt secret `CRM_PUBLIC_CHAT_CONTROLLER_ED25519_PRIVATE_KEY` and a distinct least-privilege acknowledgment secret `CRM_PUBLIC_CHAT_ACK_ED25519_PRIVATE_KEY`, each with its own key ID; the Noli control plane owns separate `NOLI_CRM_LINK_ATTESTATION_ED25519_PRIVATE_KEY` and key ID. No CRM data-plane or migration container receives a signing private key or signed-artifact verification key. The isolated controller alone requires bounded `CRM_PUBLIC_CHAT_CONTROLLER_PUBLIC_KEYS_JSON` and `NOLI_CRM_LINK_ATTESTATION_PUBLIC_KEYS_JSON` plus exact environment/issuer/audience configuration, and exposes only typed committed receipt status/digests to runtimes. Noli receives the allow-listed `CRM_PUBLIC_CHAT_ACK_PUBLIC_KEYS_JSON` for completion verification; the controller acknowledgment endpoint cannot use the runtime key or another audience. The existing CRM↔Noli internal service credential authenticates registry requests/attestation retrieval but is not signing or mapping authority. Startup fails public-chat readiness on missing/malformed/duplicate/revoked key IDs or cross-environment issuer configuration. Provisioning, overlap rotation, retention until all durable receipts are consumed, revocation, and secret-log/redaction evidence are launch checklist items.
- CRM roles that compute low-entropy durable equality proofs also require the validated HMAC keyring `CRM_PUBLIC_CHAT_DIGEST_KEYS_JSON` and `CRM_PUBLIC_CHAT_DIGEST_ACTIVE_KEY_ID` defined by the durable digest contract. This is not a signing/mapping/token secret and is never accepted by the controller/Noli or exposed to clients. Startup/readiness fails on a missing active ID, malformed/duplicate key, active ID absent from the map, or any referenced retained-row key ID absent from the deployed role set; overlap rotation uses maintenance-demote and cannot silently reset permanent slug budgets, which use rotation-independent SHA-256 coordinates.
- An unlinked widget organization is rejected before public admission. For an already-linked accepted job, missing platform credentials, blocked allowance, or unavailable/ambiguous allowance resolution produces local handoff without a provider call.

### Production service and queue topology

The checked-in Hetzner role manifest replaces the current app+MCP-only Compose shape with a fully digest-locked image graph and these explicit runtime roles; hidden app auto-spawn, `queue worker --all`, local/file queue fallback, and an unmanifested replica are forbidden:

Every production container reference is an allow-listed immutable `repository@sha256:<digest>` in that manifest: every final app image and Dockerfile `FROM` stage/base provenance, nginx, certbot/certificate helper, PostgreSQL, Redis, controller/Docker helper, migration one-shots and the retention service, and every sidecar. There is no production-host build. A reviewed CI/buildx pipeline first parses every Dockerfile and its resolved build arguments against the checked-in base-image allow-list, builds each platform once with network/material provenance constrained to those bases, pushes to the authenticated immutable registry, records the returned manifest-list digest plus each platform image/config/layer digest, SBOM, source commit, builder identity, and signed provenance, and emits a reviewable manifest update. Only after that update is approved and installed may the controller pull or start anything. Before pull/start, the controller statically parses the rendered Compose configuration, rejects tag-only/implicit-`latest`/unresolved-ARG references and unmanifested services, verifies registry signature/provenance and the selected platform digest, and requires the running container's `RepoDigests`, image ID, and app build provenance to exact-match. The host wrapper never rebuilds or retags. Preinstall/deployment/runtime receipts bind the complete image-graph and provenance digest, not merely the app image observed at signing time. Digest rotation is a reviewed manifest change and compatible maintenance rollout; a registry tag moving cannot authorize new bytes.

The generator also emits a canonical enabled-worker/producer manifest from the exact `apps/mercato/src/modules.ts` graph and resolved module registry. Every producer-to-queue-to-handler edge binds module, worker and handler IDs, queue, handler-source digest, versioned payload schema and digest, maximum encoded bytes/depth/string/array/object cardinality, authoritative durable source, deterministic job-ID rule, attempts/backoff/timeout/`lockDuration`/renewal/`maxStalledCount`, completed/failed retention, GDPR organization/user subject schema and maximums, effect class, trust group, role, Redis ACL, per-queue backlog/claim cap, group side-effect cap, pool/lock cap, and shutdown rule. It additionally binds the exact destination-window ID/generation/family and one-row/maximum-encoded-byte transport charge; retained-envelope canonicalizer ID/version/digest; status adapter ID/version and complete allowed BullMQ state map; nonbuffering/nonretrying exact-remove adapter ID/version/options; Redis identity-preflight and client-fence policy/version; and an explicit `parent/dependency/FlowProducer=false` contract. Enqueue and claim both schema-check the same immutable envelope; mismatch is terminally quarantined with no handler/effect. Every reachable `createQueue`/events/scheduler producer binds to one registered consumer and a database-backed source/outbox/reconciler, or is explicitly launch-disabled with proof that no enabled producer can address it; an acknowledged Redis write alone is never durable authority. Externally accepted payment/webhook work commits a bounded inbound receipt plus outbox before `202`, and workflow/search/email/notification producers commit their owning transition plus exact-ID outbox atomically. Redis ACK/AOF loss, enqueue response loss, and stale/orphan Redis jobs reconcile from that source without blind replay. Disabled-module worker source alone is not enabled authority.

The source audit has 12 current queues: the 11 enabled non-public descriptors (`events`, `notifications`, `messages-email`, `fulltext-indexing`, `vector-indexing`, `workflow-activities`, both customer-account cleanup queues, and the three payment queues) plus `scheduler-execution`. The launch topology replaces the union-privileged `events` queue with five trust-group queues (`events-delivery`, `events-search`, `events-workflow`, `events-account-cleanup`, and `events-payment`) and adds the public-chat target plus owner-exclusive `customers-public-chat-sweeps`, for exactly 18 launch queues. Each frozen durable subscriber is bound to one group queue and is consumed only by that group's role; no event runtime mounts another group's database grants or secrets. `--all`, any unreviewed descriptor/env/CLI concurrency drift, a second handler for a queue, unknown producer/worker, missing wildcard subscriber, unmanifested module switch, or inventory digest drift fails generation and readiness. Source metadata remains fingerprinted input, but the checked-in manifest is authoritative and may explicitly lower a descriptor default (including scheduler execution to one and each grouped queue to one); the runner ignores no value silently and fails unless effective queue/global/retry/stall/retention limits equal that manifest, regardless of legacy env or CLI input.

Every service also has a generated role-scoped DI/startup manifest. A process boots only its named handlers, clients, subscribers, producers, and startup hooks; the current full-request-container behavior is forbidden for production workers. The supervised generic database-time materializer and generic schedule mutation hooks exist only in the manifested generic scheduler process; legacy Redis recurring cold-sync is disabled. Public-chat strict reconciliation exists only in the independent strict authority reconciler. Startup traces every registered hook plus database/Redis/provider client to its role; an extra registrar, legacy scheduler sync, global subscriber, credential, or client fails readiness. Every accepted ordinary durable-queue source freezes the exact producer edge, handler ID/version/digest, payload/result schema versions/digests, effect policy and reconciler version/digest, and target/config/credential-version digests used by claim and reconciliation. A compatible rollout may mark an implementation non-current but must retain it in the role image and registry while any indexed source, outbox, execution, effect, grant, ambiguity, or inline reconciliation tuple references it; a generated zero-reference query and handler-body/schema fingerprint gate removal. One rollout fixture accepts payment, email, workflow, search, and nested-queue v1 work, makes v2 current, restarts the complete fleet, and proves v1 can claim/resume/status-reconcile/no-retry-settle while no new v1 source is accepted. An ordinary queue job acquires exactly one group permit and holds it through its one bounded handler unit. A durable event envelope acquires **no outer group permit**: it merely finds the next stored execution, then each one-at-a-time subscriber materialization/effect unit acquires and releases exactly one group permit before the next is considered. There is no nested acquisition or permit transfer. After its applicable permit succeeds, each ordinary job or event unit creates a fresh child DI scope and `orm.em.fork({ clear: true, freshEventManager: true })`, resolves all dependencies from that child, uses a separate registered session-lock connection, and disposes/clears/closes the child and entity manager in `finally`. No request container, identity map, transaction, unit of work, mutable singleton handler state, or permit is shared across jobs/units. Concurrent rollback, same-ID/cross-tenant, and C1 workflow/account event-child fixtures prove isolation and progress.

The process-wide permit is a nonblocking handler-entry preflight before child-scope creation, GDPR lease, database transaction, credential load, or external call. If unavailable, the version-pinned BullMQ adapter immediately calls `job.moveToDelayed(databaseNow + boundedJitter(5..15s), jobContext.lockToken)` and throws the library's exact `DelayedError`, so a claimed job carries no side-effect authority and never waits behind a 240-second handler. Each subscriber/child effect independently acquires the same group permit; an outer event job never hides unbounded inner concurrency or uses `Promise.all` for effectful children. A no-new-child deadline leaves enough of the 240-second process bound for settlement; after each committed child the envelope yields/requeues remaining rows rather than starting late. Every external client receives the effect grant's hard `AbortSignal`/deadline; raw `Promise.race` timeouts and operations continuing after permit/lock release are forbidden, and an abort-ignoring client is terminated before the attempt becomes safely retryable or remains `ambiguous`. Drain first pauses every queue in the group, relocates every no-permit active job through that tested transition, proves zero claimed waiters, and then waits for at most the manifested global-cap handlers through their 300-second settlement grace before signing drain evidence; missing token/API/abort support fails readiness.

The same generated manifest contains a global scheduler-target-registry digest plus exact immutable entries. Each entry has canonical ASCII key `generic:<ownerModule>:<scheduleTypeId>:v<positiveVersion>:<commandKind>` and an entry digest over exactly that key/version, one queue or command target, payload schema/digest, capability, feature/scope rules, misfire policy, handler ID, and complete per-fire row/byte bound. `generic_target_registry_digest` stores this **entry** digest, not the global registry digest; an unrelated entry change therefore does not invalidate a row. Materialization, manual trigger, claim, and fire-frozen envelopes require stored entry key/version/digest = deployed entry key/version/digest and independently rederive the server-owned target/source projection, so a changed fingerprint, arbitrary queue, or substitution with another otherwise allowed queue fails before authority. Module registration receives a manifest-derived module capability that maps to exactly one entry and server-writes `source_type`/`source_module`; operator/UI/CLI input may select only an allow-listed template ID that the server maps to one entry. Request bodies cannot supply trusted owner, source module, entry key/version, target queue/command, or capability. Those legacy columns become revision-guarded server-owned projections. Preinstall/startup maps every persisted legacy row from its complete target/payload/cadence/scope tuple to exactly one entry; zero/multiple matches or a caller-claimed source that disagrees with the matched entry blocks seed/readiness. A reviewed affected-entry change is never implicitly accepted on deploy: under maintenance drain, `scheduler reconcile-target-registry` takes the projection lock and row lock, exact-validates the old/new entry pair, increments revision, writes the new server-owned key/version/entry digest/projections, and applies the database-time mutation/cursor rules below. The seed and readiness receipt separately bind the global registry digest. Every deployed entry key/version/digest and its exact queue handler, payload/result schema, effect reconciler, legacy cutover verifier, and command implementation remains addressable and fingerprint-valid while any schedule revision, source, outbox, execution, effect, grant, reconciliation tuple, or retained ambiguity references it. Generated reference indexes and a zero-reference readiness query block image/manifest removal; a rollout may make a version non-current but cannot delete its code/schema/capability until terminal retention and all reference counters independently reach zero. An upgrade fixture moves current schedules from v1 to v2 while one v1 transport/effect remains ambiguous, restarts every role, and proves v1 can still reconcile/settle while no new v1 source can be admitted. Both `customers-public-chat-sweeps` and `customers-public-chat-replies` are reserved exclusively to the strict public-chat authority and cannot be selected by generic schedules, commands, operators, or CLI input; the first accepts only the static owner envelope and the second only an exact direct-job or bound target-sweep envelope. The two customer-account cleanup and payment-status queues remain enabled only when their persisted schedule/operator producer is present and exact; otherwise both producer and worker entry are explicitly disabled. Unknown dynamic target, malformed payload, stale owner, ambiguous legacy mapping, missing retained version implementation, or producer-without-consumer blocks readiness.

Generic recurrence is admitted only when retained demand is statically feasible. The target manifest gives an exact conservative row/encoded-byte bound for a complete fire through maximum causal depth, including root/component reservations, source, execution, effects, future receipts, and nested outboxes; unknown/unbounded fan-out is disabled. The cadence validator rejects nonpositive intervals and cron/timezone expressions without a positive conservative DST-safe minimum. Each enabled schedule stores checked `maxFires30d = ceil(30 days / minimumNominalSeparation) + 1` products without credit for polling or coalescing. Create/update/re-enable/restore/accepted-registry-change authorizes and takes applicable lifecycle fences, the environment projection lock, complete generic-storage counter hierarchy, then schedule/insertion fence, and recomputes fixed stored-state precharge plus declared-scope, tenant-aggregate when present, system, and environment recurrence projections through covering indexes. A scope move takes environment first, then the sorted union of OLD+NEW system/tenant storage counters, then the sorted union of OLD+NEW declared-scope counters before reloading the row; it proves destination caps and atomically decrement/increments the identical row/byte charge, never a partial transfer. Projection limits reserve causal counter and retained-revision overlap headroom: organization 1,000 schedules/90,000 rows/180 MiB; tenant aggregate 2,000/180,000/360 MiB; system 1,000/90,000/180 MiB; environment 10,000/900,000/1,792 MiB. These enabled-only projection limits are separate from and no larger than the all-row generic stored-state limits above. Environment projected rows/bytes are exactly `queue_generic_recurring`; separate `queue_other` owns manual/ordinary causal work, while the fixed critical infrastructure charge accounts only the generic-storage counter rows themselves. Direct DML cannot bypass either bound. Seed/readiness rederive stored precharge plus per-fire/cadence values and exact-match all applicable aggregates in the registry/seed receipt. Exceeding any stored-state, product, or organization/tenant/system/environment projection bound blocks mutation/seed/readiness; retained revisions can still fill the larger actual causal capacity ceilings, so every fire reservation independently checks the same hierarchy.

Legacy scheduler cutover ambiguity is registry-bound evidence, never an operator assertion or an age/state guess. Each target entry either pins one `legacyCutoverVerifierId` plus source digest and exact evidence schema, or declares itself non-adjudicable. The root-controller journal may append a bounded `LegacyGenericScheduleAdjudicationV1` entry containing exactly environment/fence/journal generation, schedule ID or explicit orphan marker, legacy definition and child/manual-job IDs plus frozen state digest, matched target entry key/version/digest and payload digest, verifier/build digests, outcome `proved_no_effect | proved_settled`, minimal allow-listed evidence coordinates/digest, database check time, 128-bit nonce, and two distinct operator approval digests. The target-specific verifier—not an approval—must prove from authoritative durable target/command state and exact transport identity either that no effect could have begun or that the one effect settled; dual approval only authorizes accepting that proof. The controller executes the pinned verifier through an exact peer-authenticated helper under the live fence, independently schema/digest-checks its result, enforces unique `(environment,fence,legacyChildOrManualJobId)` and nonce, fsyncs the append, and binds its Merkle root into the terminal preinstall artifact. Cross-target evidence, absence of a provider response, Redis absence, elapsed time, logs alone, or an operator waiver never proves either outcome. `proved_no_effect` may preserve/adopt one recurring nominal occurrence; `proved_settled` skips it and uses the first cadence after the drain boundary. A legacy one-off manual job is never cadence authority: it must normally drain to exact settled state before inventory, or use this verifier; a known accepted request lost by pre-contract Redis loss remains launch-blocked until a source-specific verifier proves settled or a separately approved remediation reissues it through the new durable idempotent path. An entry with no verifier, unbounded/secret evidence, or irreconcilable ambiguity requires the schedule/producer to remain launch-disabled under a separately reviewed remediation—there is no generic override. Tests cross schedule/target/fence, replay nonce/evidence, crash before/after verifier+journal CAS, target success before legacy worker bookkeeping, legacy manual accepted immediately before fence, failed retry/active crash/known Redis loss, and missing-verifier no-go.

Generic recurring schedules have a database-authoritative fire contract, not a BullMQ-timing exemption. The same manifested generic scheduler process runs `mercato scheduler serve --worker-concurrency=1 --materialize-interval-seconds=5 --materialize-batch-size=100`: its supervised materializer uses one already-budgeted ordinary database slot, no additional Redis client, and no provider/target credential. Each tick captures database `clock_timestamp()`, inspects at most 100 due non-strict candidates, processes at most 100 successfully locked rows, and spends no more than four seconds before yielding. There is no fixed 100-ID snapshot and no pre-lock authority. The fixed-environment and applicable system-or-tenant and declared-scope `generic_schedule_storage` hierarchy rows carry protected materializer inspection epochs/cursors plus service-fairness coordinates; they are created/exact-verified and charged atomically with the first stored schedule by create/seed/scope-move and are never schedule authority. They remain while any enabled, disabled, or tombstoned schedule or descendant reference exists; the last schedule purge may delete an empty child only through its parent-generation zero-reference CAS, and a recreated logical scope gets a new generation. No independent materializer metadata population exists. A security-barrier candidate view uses the persistent coordinates plus `(scope_type,tenant_id,organization_id,generic_materialize_after,id)` to expose the next due schedule **after** each scope's last inspected due/ID, wrapping only after an indexed EOF proof. System is a separate bounded lane; when due, one system candidate is considered before the selector rotates least-recently-inspected tenant → least-recently-inspected child scope → next due/ID. Thus one tenant with 2,000 organization scopes cannot manufacture 2,000 peer fair keys ahead of another tenant, and one locked earliest row cannot conceal a later row in the same scope. For each attempt, one short transaction takes the candidate's lifecycle fences, tries the deterministic environment materializer advisory transaction lock, locks the applicable environment→tenant→scope storage/cursor rows, and then tries the exact schedule row with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; every field is discarded and re-read after the lock. Success, stale/missing row, schedule-row lock miss, or a typed revalidation deferral advances the applicable protected inspection cursor/epoch by same-snapshot generation CAS before commit; a locked tenant/scope metadata row instead advances the nearest available parent inspection coordinate so another tenant/scope remains selectable. A failed environment lock makes no change. Service-fairness coordinates advance only for a successfully handled fire or typed deferral as below, so inspection never falsely claims service. Releasing each transaction releases the environment lock; overlapping replicas therefore serialize each durable inspection unit without inverting scope locks or pretending a transaction lock fences a whole tick. Every statement and lock wait is capped by the smaller of a reviewed short limit and the tick's remaining database-time budget. No timeout, cancellation, database error, failed try-lock, or stale cursor generation is interpreted as absence or permission to advance a cadence cursor. Crash/restart retains the last committed inspection position; seed/create/enable/move/last-purge churn and same-scope/same-tenant fixtures with 100 locked earlier rows prove a later due row and a later child scope are inspected within the next complete bounded cursor pass without orphan/leaked cursor rows or ABA.

For each acquired candidate, the transaction exact-revalidates enabled/nondeleted state, scope, `generic_schedule_incarnation_id`, `schedule_revision`, stored=current target entry key/version/digest, cadence/timezone, target capability/payload-schema and canonical payload digests, feature binding, exact stored=rederived retained-demand projection, due time, and hierarchical capacity coordinates, then follows the fixed source/counter order. It advances both the locked tenant-domain and declared-scope **service** fairness coordinates for every successfully handled fire or typed deferral so one bad scope or many-organization tenant cannot remain first; system advances only its separate lane coordinate. The inspection coordinates above advance independently even on a schedule-row lock miss and therefore prevent head-of-line replay without advancing cadence or claiming service. Counter acquisition is nonblocking: an unavailable counter produces `capacity_contended`, while an acquired counter with insufficient family/class/scope capacity produces `capacity_exhausted`; both insert no source/reservation, leave `next_run_at`, last-materialized coordinates, and pointers unchanged, and move only error plus `generic_materialize_after` to a bounded database-time fair retry. All generic schedule due/cursor/envelope times are canonical UTC millisecond instants: PostgreSQL values equal `date_trunc('milliseconds', value)`, wire values are exactly `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, and ID material is the signed 64-bit Unix epoch-millisecond ASCII decimal with no leading zero or plus sign. The shared calculator/validator is used by PostgreSQL seed fixtures and TypeScript; alternate fractional precision, offset spelling, or a sub-millisecond value fails before mutation.

Before a new reservation, the transaction treats only `generic_waiting_recurring_outbox_id` as live waiting authority. When non-null it locks that exact same-incarnation/revision source, reservation, then execution coordinate and proves no execution claim exists; missing, mismatched, or claimed pointed state is corruption, not absence. It inserts no reservation/outbox, leaves `next_run_at` at the first **uncovered/not-yet-materialized** nominal instant after the pointed envelope's immutable `coalescedThroughFloor`, records `outstanding_fire`, and moves only `generic_materialize_after` to a bounded database-time retry. When the waiting pointer is null, it locks the deterministic new source identity, may reserve the complete causal bound from `queue_generic_recurring`, insert-or-exact-verify exactly one immutable recurring `queue_job_outbox`, and set the waiting pointer to that fire ID. An existing active pointer does not prevent this one waiting successor; it prevents the successor's execution claim below. Its transport/outbox ID is UUIDv5 with RFC URL namespace `6ba7b811-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8` and exact canonical name `noli:generic-schedule-fire:v1:<scheduleId>:<scheduleIncarnationId>:<scheduleRevision>:<dueEpochMs>`; every writer/dispatcher/worker independently re-derives it. Its discriminated transport envelope is exactly `{ fireKind: "recurring", scheduleId, scheduleIncarnationId, scheduleRevision, dueAt, coalescedThroughFloor, scope, targetEntryKey, targetEntryVersion, targetRegistryDigest, targetPayloadDigest }`, where `coalescedThroughFloor` is the last nominal cadence instant less than or equal to the fire-creation transaction's captured database time, calculated under the frozen cadence/timezone and normalized to the same millisecond form. Fire creation advances `next_run_at`/`generic_materialize_after` only to the first nominal cadence after that floor and stores the ID as both waiting pointer and latest diagnostic materialization. The immutable outbox is therefore a lower-bound transport claim, not the final effect coverage; first execution claim below atomically freezes the final `coalescedThrough` and advances the still-current schedule cursor through all additional pre-claim time. Commit loss leaves either the old due cursor with no accepted fire or the advanced cursor plus exact durable outbox, never a lost accepted occurrence.

Every generic schedule mutation uses one guarded service, takes the fixed environment then sorted OLD+NEW tenant/system and declared-scope generic-storage counters before locking/reloading `scheduled_jobs` (or its deterministic insertion fence), and captures `clock_timestamp()` in the same transaction; application wall time and a caller-supplied next run are never authority. Enabled create assigns a fresh incarnation/revision/mutation generation, server-derived target entry key/version/digest and projection, fixed maximum-lifecycle storage charge, null latest-fire chain, and both due fields at the first cadence strictly after database now; disabled create assigns the same identity/entry/digest/precharge with zero causal projection and null chain/due fields. Every revision-changing mutation atomically terminal-cancels any exact unclaimed pointed recurring source through the queue capability, releases its unused reservation, clears last-materialized/latest-outbox/waiting/error coordinates for the new revision, and leaves old ledgers independently cleanup-addressable; indexed old-revision unpointed manual/remediation sources are retired by the bounded stale-source lane below. A dispatched stale Redis copy cannot effect and, when visible, uses the unclaimed-terminal detach lane before releasing its slot. The mutation deliberately **retains** `generic_active_execution_id` across revision/disable/delete until that exact old execution settles or terminal-cancels, so a new revision may materialize at most one waiting fire but cannot claim/effect it while old authority can resume. It can never carry a waiting-fire pointer across definitions. An enabled execution-affecting owner/source/entry/target/payload/scope/feature/cadence/timezone or accepted registry change increments revision and recomputes both due fields as the first **new** cadence strictly after database now, with no old-definition catch-up; a scope change performs the atomic precharge transfer above. Disable or unregister/delete increments revision, sets `is_enabled=false`, clears both due fields and the waiting pointer through that atomic cancellation, and retains a precharged soft tombstone with incarnation, revision, target entry key/version/digest, any cross-revision active pointer, and the minimum audit coordinates until every old outbox/execution/effect and Redis subject is terminal/absent. Re-enable/restore before physical purge increments revision and schedules the first cadence strictly after its transaction's database time; disabled time is intentionally not coalesced.
