A same-scope name/description edit increments mutation generation exactly once but changes no revision or storage charge and must remain within the precharged schema maximum. Physical tombstone purge is an autonomous terminal-lane causal unit: it advances the protected storage cursor past blockers, takes the storage hierarchy then schedule row, requires either database time at/after `deleted_at + interval '30 days'` or exact irreversible operation-GDPR authority, exact durable/transport/legacy zero proof, and a second indexed reference-zero check; it then physically deletes one row, decrement-one releases its fixed stored row/byte precharge, and deletes a now-empty generation-fenced storage child only under its parent CAS. At most 1,000 combined terminal units run per tick with the persisted event/queue-versus-schedule round robin; oldest-eligible tombstone age is included in the lane's computed drain/readiness deadline. A later same-ID creation receives a new incarnation, so revision reset cannot ABA-match an old fire. An already committed effect grant may settle after a later disable/revision, but no grant may start afterward: mutation and worker target-grant transactions take the same row lock, and the worker reloads and exact-matches enabled/nondeleted/incarnation/revision/entry-key/version/registry/payload digest in the **same transaction** that inserts a nested target outbox or commits a command effect grant. Whichever row-lock transaction wins defines the boundary; stale work terminal-cancels without effect.

Every scheduler create/update/delete/restore undo or redo is part of that same guarded service, not a raw ActionLog snapshot replay. The guarded original command audit freezes schedule ID/incarnation, before/after revision and mutation generation, scope, entry key/version/digests, payload/cadence digest, expected deleted/enabled state, and canonical before/after digests over **every** mutable logical field including name and description. Both undo and redo HTTP requests require a canonical UUIDv7 `Idempotency-Key`; `AuditLogsActions.tsx` generates and durably retains the key per original-log/action before first send and reuses it after timeout/reload until a terminal response. The route first derives and point-loads a deterministic protected correctness-receipt ActionLog result row under RFC URL namespace `6ba7b811-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8`: exact UTF-8 name `noli:generic-schedule-undo:v1:<originalActionLogId>:<requestId>` or `noli:generic-schedule-redo:v1:<originalActionLogId>:<requestId>`. An existing row exact-verifies action/original-log/actor/scope/request digest, expected and result mutation generations/state digests, and bounded semantic result, then replays without mutation even though the original log is already `undone|redone`; changed reuse returns minimal conflict. When absent, the UUIDv7 must pass the database-time future-five-minute/old-24-hour gate. The result row contains no target payload or copied schedule snapshot. Its protected metadata uses receipt kind `generic_scheduler_undo_result` or `generic_scheduler_redo_result`, `acceptedAt` at the transaction's canonical database millisecond, and `retainUntil` exactly 30 database-time days later. The same accepting transaction creates one deterministic one-component `queue_other_general` capacity root and transfers its pre-reserved row/byte charge into an indexed `receipt_component`; the result receipt, component/root transfer, exact schedule mutation, and original-log CAS either all commit or none do. Existing component indexes `(environment_id,organization_id,tenant_id,retain_until,receipt_record_id)` and nullable-actor discovery own replay, GDPR, and cleanup—there is no ActionLog scan or uncharged result row. The existing receipt-retention lane locks the schedule/original log/result receipt/component/root in global order, advances past blockers, and at `retainUntil` exact-deletes only the result receipt/component and releases its physical charge while retaining the original ordinary audit row; pre-horizon organization GDPR uses its exact dependency-zero lane, and user erasure may null only the result actor. After cleanup, the absent UUIDv7 is older than the 24-hour acceptance window and yields explicit expired request, never a replacement key. A first undo locks the storage hierarchy, schedule, and original log, requires the repository's exact original state `done` plus its live undo authorization, and exact-matches current after-generation/after-digest. Its one transaction derives fresh database-time due fields and server-owned projections/pointers, performs any revision, waiting-source cancellation, or scope-precharge transfer, increments mutation generation, insert-or-verifies the deterministic undo result row, and CASes the original ActionLog `done -> undone` with immutable undo-result generation/digest. A first redo requires original state `undone` and exact current undo-result generation/digest, runs the same service, increments mutation generation, insert-or-verifies its deterministic redo result row, and CASes the original `undone -> redone` with immutable redo-result generation/digest. `redone` is terminal for that original log, so another reversal requires a new schedule command. The scheduler-specialized command bus, ActionLog service, and undo/redo routes pass one forked entity manager so schedule/counter/source mutation, result-root/component transfer, original ActionLog CAS, and result receipt commit or roll back together; the current post-handler `markUndone`/post-redo `markRedone` split is forbidden. A crash before commit changes neither, and an exact response-loss retry point-loads the result row without needing a now-cleared undo token or rerunning mutation. Neither path writes owner/source/due/pointer/storage fields copied from audit JSON. Create undo may soft-delete only the exact created incarnation; delete undo may restore only the exact still-retained deletion incarnation/revision before purge. A purged/recreated same ID, any intervening edit or ABA back to identical presentation bytes, changed registry entry, stale command state, or mismatched counter returns conflict/expired with zero mutation. Fixtures cover lost undo and redo responses, retained lookup after token clear, changed request reuse, UUIDv7 and exact 30-day retention boundaries, actor/organization GDPR, receipt-lane blockers/wrap/capacity release, create/update/scope-move/delete undo/redo across purge/recreate, A->B->C and A->B->A presentation ABA, competing edits, waiting/active work, and every old/new counter lock interleaving.

The launch registry pins `misfirePolicy="coalesce_one"` for every enabled generic recurring schedule, matching the current transport's at-most-one recovery effect rather than silently replaying an outage. For one continuously enabled, unchanged incarnation/revision, a waiting fire may exist behind an active execution or Redis/dispatcher outage, but its first claim freezes one final `coalescedThrough` covering every nominal instant from `dueAt` through the claim transaction's captured database time and advances the schedule cursor past that complete interval before any effect grant. No second fire for that interval can materialize while the waiting pointer exists. A later waiting successor covers only nominal instants strictly after the prior fire's claim-time boundary; a revision/lifecycle change instead stale-cancels the old source and begins a separately versioned contract. A target that requires every missed tick is launch-disabled until a separately reviewed bounded policy and idempotent handler are manifested. A typed pre-materialization blocker inserts no outbox and advances only `generic_materialize_after` to bounded database-time retry; revision or row change loses the CAS, and 100 permanently bad early rows cannot pin later work.

Authenticated manual trigger reuses the existing protected `ActionLog` command-receipt storage rather than introducing an undeclared table. Its deterministic receipt primary key is UUIDv5 under the same RFC URL namespace with exact name `noli:generic-schedule-manual-request:v1:<scheduleId>:<serverCommandRequestId>`; excluding incarnation/revision burns the pair across mutation/reincarnation while the receipt is retained, and after cleanup the UUIDv7 age gate prevents its reacceptance. The route first derives and point-loads that ID. An existing receipt exact-verifies command, actor-or-redacted-actor rule, scope, keyed request digest, and immutable bounded result and may replay through `retainUntil`; mismatch returns minimal conflict. If absent, the canonical lowercase UUIDv7 `serverCommandRequestId` must be within the future-five-minute/old-24-hour database-time window before the new-request path. On first use, one transaction takes the actor/scope fences and fixed scheduler lock order, reauthorizes the active membership and `scheduler.jobs.trigger`, proves actor/scope/day plus outstanding limits, reserves the complete causal bound from `queue_other_manual`, and inserts-or-exact-verifies the receipt and `queue_job_outbox`; no accepted receipt, reservation, or fire can commit alone. The receipt freezes `fireKind="manual"`, schedule ID/incarnation/revision, target entry key/version plus registry/payload digests, scope, one canonical database `requestedAt`, deterministic outbox ID, and accepted semantic result, with no schedule payload or customer text. The outbox UUIDv5 name is `noli:generic-schedule-manual:v1:<scheduleId>:<scheduleIncarnationId>:<scheduleRevision>:<serverCommandRequestId>` under the same namespace, and its exact envelope is `{ fireKind: "manual", scheduleId, scheduleIncarnationId, scheduleRevision, serverCommandRequestId, requestedAt, scope, targetEntryKey, targetEntryVersion, targetRegistryDigest, targetPayloadDigest }`; it contains no actor, `dueAt`, or `coalescedThrough` and never changes the recurring cursor. Response loss, process restart, or crash at every receipt/reservation/outbox boundary exact-replays the retained receipt and cannot create another fire. User erasure may operation-redact actor coordinates under the fence. Pre-horizon organization erasure removes the receipt only through dependency-ordered cleanup; at `retainUntil`, the indexed expired-receipt lane either cancels an unclaimed source or preserves independently frozen claimed/granted authority as defined above, then deletes the receipt component. `POST /api/scheduler/trigger` therefore requires the UUIDv7 `Idempotency-Key` header outside target JSON; missing/malformed/stale input returns `400` before mutation. The authenticated UI/CLI generates and durably retains that key before its first attempt and reuses it after timeout/reload/restart until terminal response; if the 30-day replay horizon expires first, it surfaces an explicit expired request and never silently substitutes another key. The route copies the key into required `CommandRuntimeContext.requestId`; the command bus refuses a manual invocation without an equally stable authenticated envelope key. OpenAPI, client helpers, framework fixtures, receipt cleanup, and post-expiry tests pin the transport so a per-attempt server-generated ID is forbidden.

The durable outbox dispatcher alone writes the exact `scheduler-execution` Redis job and re-derives its fire ID from `fireKind`. The worker re-derives deterministic execution ID as UUIDv5 under RFC URL namespace `6ba7b811-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8` and exact name `noli:generic-schedule-execution:v1:<fireId>`. A Redis transport claim alone is not a durable execution claim. Under reviewed short lock/statement deadlines, the C1 worker may decode the immutable Redis envelope and point-read source, execution, and for a manual fire the receipt actor UUID only as **nonlocking, non-authoritative candidates**; it obtains no payload, permission, claim, or effect from those reads. An exact immutable terminal execution may ACK/no-op without locks. Every other path then takes the fixed lock order below and re-reads all authority. Branch order after that re-read is exact. First, an existing nonterminal execution whose ID is the schedule's active pointer resumes its stored phase; if it already has a committed effect grant, even an old revision may only finish settlement under that frozen grant. An existing nonterminal execution with a different active pointer delays without a new claim or grant. Second, when no execution exists, the worker evaluates source currency **before** any different-active gate: a terminal, missing-schedule, deleted, reincarnated, revised, scope/entry/digest-mismatched, or otherwise stale source uses the detached terminal-cancel capability to settle only that immutable source/reservation and can never touch the current waiting/active pointers, even if another execution is active. Third, only a current source may attempt first claim. A recurring source must exact-match incarnation/revision/scope/target entry/digests and the waiting pointer. If the active pointer is null, that same transaction captures canonical database time, calculates `finalCoalescedThrough=max(coalescedThroughFloor,lastNominalCadenceAtOrBefore(claimedAt))` under the frozen cadence/timezone, requires `next_run_at` still equal the first nominal instant after the floor, advances both due fields to the first nominal instant after the final boundary, stores the final boundary on the execution, insert-or-exact-verifies execution, CAS-clears waiting, and sets active; it never mutates the transported outbox. A different active pointer delays without extending coverage. A manual source instead exact-verifies its deterministic protected ActionLog receipt, outbox, manual-class reservation, current schedule identity/entry/digests, and null active pointer; it never reads or changes the recurring waiting pointer, then inserts execution and sets the shared active pointer. Missing/mismatched required current pointer or cursor is corruption rather than absence. Commit permits the materializer to create one successor covering only time strictly after the frozen final boundary; no later recurring or manual fire can claim while a different active execution remains. Crash after claim is retry-idempotent because the same execution and final coverage resume; duplicate after terminal ACKs without pointer mutation. Lock contention/timeout grants no claim/effect and takes the typed delayed transition; timeout/cancellation is never absence. While holding the same authority in a later grant transaction, a current queue target inserts the deterministic nested `queue_job_outbox` atomically with settlement of the schedule child, while an allow-listed command target uses the generic effect/grant ledger and current scope/feature/permission reauthorization. The no-more-effects settlement or stale-before-grant cancellation transaction marks that exact execution terminal and CAS-clears `generic_active_execution_id` by execution ID even when its schedule revision is now old; it cannot clear a different/newer active pointer. It never calls `createQueue`/Redis directly or executes an unregistered command. Legacy generic repeatables/Job Schedulers are drained, boundedly removed, and proved zero before readiness. The combined service stays within the already declared generic-scheduler 6 short plus one session-lock connections, three Redis clients, C1 effect cap, and 16 session-lock maximum, so the 18/113/49/672 budgets do not change.

All generic-scheduler write lanes share one lock hierarchy; a candidate read is never authority. The hierarchy is: (1) applicable sorted Noli/local-user GDPR fences plus tenant/organization lifecycle/authorization locks; (2) the environment projection/materializer advisory lock when required; (3) the fixed environment→tenant/system→declared-scope `generic_schedule_storage` rows, including their materializer cursor fields, for selection or any schedule create/update/move/delete/purge; (4) `scheduled_jobs`, or deterministic schedule-ID advisory fence when absent; (5) deterministic source identity, then the outbox-ID session advisory lock when transport/cancel/detach is involved, then source outbox; (6) deterministic receipt-ID advisory lock then protected ActionLog receipt; (7) the `scheduler_release_window` counter for a scheduler transport path, then ordinary causal-capacity family/class/scope/actor counters and reservation; (8) execution; and (9) effect. The storage/cursor rows are different physical rows from ordinary causal and release-window counters, so inspection/storage-before-schedule cannot invert source/capacity order. A scheduler dispatcher/detacher therefore locks/reloads the schedule before acquiring the outbox-ID session lock and acquires/rechecks the release-window counter only **after** that session lock; after the final database CAS commits it may retain only the session lock across Redis I/O and outcome CAS. A detach final transaction already holding that session lock follows outbox→release-window order, and no dispatcher/grant/null-slot path may take the release-window counter first. No scheduler path acquires a schedule/storage/fence lock while already holding an outbox lock. If a scope cursor is locked, the already-held parent cursor advances lexicographically past that exact child; if the tenant cursor is locked, the environment cursor advances past that tenant; if the required parent is unavailable, the transaction makes no durable claim and only the tick-local tuple advances. New source materialization takes source identity before causal-capacity counters and inserts only afterward. Mutation, cancel, manual accept, dispatcher grant, detach, claim, receipt cleanup/redaction, grant, settlement, and cleanup never acquire an earlier class later. All state is discarded/re-read after wait; try-lock failure produces only typed deferral. Guards/functions fingerprint this order. For `outstanding_fire`, retained `next_run_at` is the first uncovered nominal instant after immutable `coalescedThroughFloor`; first claim alone advances through final coverage. Paused materialize/mutate, mutation-versus-dispatch/detach, storage-cap/purge, cursor-row blockers/wrap, dispatcher/outbox/release-counter ordering, claim/revision, disable/grant, settlement/disable, receipt cleanup/claim, and cleanup/claim prove bounded retry without deadlock, double charge, or unauthorized advance.

Manual acceptance and execution additionally close the user-erasure race without putting an actor in Redis. On first acceptance, the authenticated actor UUID is a non-authoritative candidate until the transaction takes that user's shared GDPR fence before the schedule/source locks, re-reads the active user, membership, tenant/organization, and `scheduler.jobs.trigger` permission, and creates the receipt/reservation/outbox. If erasure or revocation won, it rejects without durable work; if acceptance won, the indexed receipt reservation makes the actor discoverable to the erasure sweep. On **first claim**, the worker candidate-reads the receipt actor UUID, takes the shared user fence and generated generic user execution lease, re-reads the exact receipt/user/membership/permission, and atomically freezes actor/scope/request/permission coordinates as an indexed execution subject while claiming. Once that execution exists, every resume/grant derives the actor candidate from the immutable execution—not Redis and not a possibly expired receipt—takes the same fence/lease, and reauthorizes the current user/membership/permission before effect grant. It holds the fence/lease through the grant/no-more-effects boundary. Receipt cleanup and first claim serialize; cleanup cancels an unclaimed authenticated-manual source, but it may delete the receipt component after a claim because the execution is independently authoritative. A null-redacted execution actor, inactive user, lost permission, or erasure-won fence detached-cancels before grant; an already committed grant remains an erasure barrier until exact settlement, after which actor redaction may proceed. The generic lease wrapper has a manifested manual-fire resolver for this database coordinate and never recursively interprets payload UUIDs. Tests pause acceptance and worker before the fence, after the candidate read, after receipt commit, after first claim, beyond 30 days before grant, and after grant while racing receipt cleanup, permission revocation, and user erasure, proving no post-erasure receipt/effect and no actor leakage to Redis.

A `fireKind='legacy_manual_remediation'` execution is a third, disjoint worker branch. It exact-verifies the immutable source/reservation copy of controller journal/adjudication authority and current scope/schedule/entry under lifecycle fences, never loads or invents an actor, never takes `scheduler.jobs.trigger`, and never enters the null-actor or receipt-expiry cancellation rules for authenticated manual fires. First claim uses the same shared active pointer; grant is limited to the frozen target-specific remediation capability and all later revision/lifecycle rules. Its causal source remains claimable after the 30-day ActionLog receipt component is deleted; only exact settlement, stale revision/lifecycle cancellation, or operation-GDPR proof can terminalize it. Thus a long outage cannot lose the replacement after legacy Redis and bootstrap creation authority are gone. Cross-kind receipt/source/envelope/execution substitution is corruption and no-op/quarantine, not fallback.

Launch generic schedule definitions use exactly three generated shapes matching the repository contract: `system` requires organization/tenant null and an allow-listed module capability; `tenant` requires organization null plus one active tenant; `organization` requires both IDs and exact active organization→tenant membership. Scope kind+IDs are immutable execution coordinates and define lifecycle/GDPR locks, `scopeDigest`, capacity/fairness counters, and subject discovery. Account-cleanup/payment-status and any other system producer must map to an exact system entry or remain disabled. No shape may persist a user subject in `target_payload`, legacy columns, or derived target/lease paths. In particular, the repository's existing nullable `scheduled_jobs.created_by_user_id` and `updated_by_user_id` are bootstrap-nulled for every generic or strict row under the drained seed, remain null under the complete OLD→NEW guard, and are no longer written by scheduler create/update/delete/undo/CLI/API/UI paths. The authenticated actor exists only in the ordinary encrypted/redacted ActionLog command audit or the separately protected manual receipt and is never schedule authority. A target's generated organization/tenant subject is either absent or exact-equal to the declared scope: system cannot carry either, tenant cannot hide an organization, and organization must match both. Every entry declares `persistentUserSubjects='forbidden'`. The generated target schema is resolved by server-owned entry key/version before every create, update, restore, import, UI/CLI submit, manual trigger, remediation, seed, materialization, and readiness path; it rejects undeclared keys, arbitrary `z.record` fallbacks, UUID-looking hidden users, ambiguous subject projections, and client-selected owner/source/entry/capability coordinates before persistence. Authenticated manual actor is separately indexed authorization, never target data; public manual API accepts tenant or organization scope under matching membership, while system recurrence is module-capability-only. Legacy hidden/mixed/user subject rows remain disabled until target-specific redesign; Redis scanning is not database discovery. Future user-subject recurrence requires an indexed projection entity plus erasure revision/disable/cancel. Fixtures cover all three shapes, inactive/mismatched parents, system account/payment, hidden org/user UUIDs at every acceptance surface, bootstrap-null/repeated mutation of both legacy actor columns, actor separation, GDPR, and both manual/remediation paths.

#### Durable event subscriber lane

The enabled-worker manifest includes a second generated/fingerprinted subscriber-mode registry. The current audit finds exactly 36 enabled subscribers: 27 persistent subscribers that must become durable and nine non-durable subscribers that must be classified explicitly. Every subscriber has one unique ID, normalized event pattern, retained handler version and digest, exact mode (`sync_transactional | local_after_commit | durable`), priority, wildcard semantics, scope/subject schema, effect classification, trust group/queue, and failure policy. `sync_transactional` is bounded deterministic database-only work in the caller transaction; `local_after_commit` is non-authoritative best-effort in-memory cache/telemetry whose loss cannot affect correctness. External, file, provider, queue, credential-bearing, or correctness-required work is always durable. Bootstrap registers only `local_after_commit` handlers in the in-memory bus and only `sync_transactional` handlers in the transaction store; group event workers select only their frozen `durable` executions. One shared matcher/order implementation handles exact and wildcard patterns in every lane and sorts by priority then subscriber ID. A subscriber can never occupy two lanes. Duplicate/missing IDs, forbidden imports/capabilities in a non-durable lane, `persistent:true` without a durable plan, a durable subscriber reached in-process, a local/sync subscriber reached by a worker, or differences in wildcard/priority/context semantics fail generation/readiness. In particular the enabled `workflows:event-trigger` wildcard and every persistent webhook/notification/pipeline subscriber have golden lane fixtures, including transaction retry/rollback and after-commit crash behavior.

Authentication and credential material is not event data. Password-reset, magic-link, invitation, verification, session, API-key, bearer, cookie, HMAC, and provider secrets—or email/content fields coupled to those secrets—are statically denied by event schemas, serializer, logs, outbox, Redis, workflow context, and SSE. The existing password-reset and magic-link emitters are launch-blocked until raw token events are removed, credential delivery uses a dedicated exact-recipient non-bus lane, all portal/staff broadcast annotations on auth events are removed, and any already-issued outstanding token class is expired/rotated under a separately approved production remediation. Generator fixtures fail if a secret-shaped field or credential event can match the workflow wildcard. Cross-user reset/magic requests prove that no other session, subscriber, log, workflow, Redis value, or persisted event can observe the token.

Because the vulnerable emitters predate this branch, launch also requires a separately approved incident-remediation inventory rather than assuming token expiry removed historical copies. After rotating/expiring the affected token classes first, it inventories and targeted-purges or irreversibly redacts workflow definitions/instances/context/audit, event/queue ledgers and Redis/AOF/backups, webhook deliveries, SSE/application logs, traces, error stores, and any downstream replica; only nonreversible keyed audit digests may remain. Externally delivered webhook/email content is recorded as potentially non-retractable exposure and drives credential/user notification assessment. Evidence states what was searched, retained, deleted, or impossible to retract and never claims absence of access/exploitation without logs. This spec task performs no production query, purge, rotation, notification, or deploy.

PostgreSQL `NOTIFY` is an untrusted ID-only wakeup, never payload authority. A source transaction writes a protected, schema-declared `client_event_invalidations` row containing only bounded tenant/organization/user audience coordinates, event/entity IDs, source generation, and expiry; a trusted trigger emits only its opaque row ID after commit. The web-only bridge owns one manifested LISTEN connection, narrow-loads the committed row through a definer that reauthorizes the current connection/session generation, and sends SSE containing only bounded event/entity IDs so the client refetches through ordinary authorization. Raw JSON/content/actions/addresses/tokens never enter `NOTIFY` or SSE; forged, missing, rolled-back, expired, or cross-scope IDs are no-ops. Staff/portal SSE connections have a short database-time authorization lease and are rechecked before each send; session revocation, membership/feature/selected-organization change, deletion, or lease expiry closes the stream. Invalidations expire within 15 minutes, deduplicate on exact audience/entity/generation, and each has a generated complete encoded maximum of 1 KiB. One fixed `client_event_invalidation_environment` counter in `event_fanout_registry_counters` serializes admission and hard-limits live invalidations to 100,000 rows/100 MiB: the source transaction locks it, rejects/omits before insert unless both charges fit, and increments it atomically with the row, so concurrent writers cannot overshoot. The retention daemon's event/queue cleanup function owns a protected `(expires_at,id)` cursor/epoch and persisted invalidation subcursor; one terminal causal unit keyset-deletes at most 16 expired rows and exact-decrements the fixed row/byte counter, with at least 250 units/4,000 eligible unlocked rows per healthy tick and the explicit deadline above. Exact user/organization erasure deletes or subject-redacts its rows after streams close and decrements the same counter in the causal transaction. Seed/readiness exact-count rows and encoded bytes, reconcile the fixed counter/generation/cursor, and fail emission readiness on drift or deadline breach; no runtime has broad cleanup DML. At the ceiling the non-authoritative invalidation is omitted with bounded telemetry while the committed domain mutation and authenticated refetch remain authoritative. Crash/pause, `99,999/100,000/100,001`, concurrent admission, 16-row batches, cursor wrap/blockers, counter drift, backlog, and erasure races prove bounded retention and no post-revocation send.

Persistent emission no longer means “run locally and also enqueue.” In the same transaction as its authoritative mutation, the fixed emitter capability derives the event name, scope, source generation, and exact subscriber matches from `session_user`, locked source rows, and the controller-installed subscriber-manifest digest; the caller cannot supply or widen those fields. For one logical event ID it writes exactly one bounded immutable `event_outbox` row per matched trust group, unique on `(event_id,trust_group)`, with that group's queue, deterministic transport-outbox ID, and frozen sorted execution-set digest. The same transaction consumes the pre-reserved transport component and inserts/exact-verifies the peer `queue_job_outbox` with that actual BullMQ ID and immutable `{ eventId, trustGroup, executionSetDigest }` envelope; `event_outbox` owns no independent enqueue phase, attempt, ambiguity, producer runtime, or Redis absence state. A response loss for one group's generic transport cannot mark or suppress another. It also writes one immutable execution row for every matched durable subscriber. Each execution freezes event/schema and handler ID/version/digest, subscriber-manifest/effect-policy digest, trust group and queue, tenant/organization/user coordinates, minimized payload/input digest, source operation/runtime generation, priority, and database time. Rollout retains every referenced handler version until its pending/leased/effect-started/ambiguous executions settle, or readiness blocks the rollout; adding, removing, reprioritizing, or changing a subscriber never retroactively changes an existing event.

A generated events migration adds exactly six protected tables: `event_outbox` unique on `(event_id,trust_group)` and scalar-unique on its deterministic `transport_outbox_id`, `event_subscriber_executions` unique on `(event_id,subscriber_id)` and exact-matched to its group row/execution-set digest, `event_subscriber_effects` unique on `(event_id,subscriber_id,target_kind,target_digest)`, `client_event_invalidations`, `event_fanout_registry_versions`, and `event_fanout_registry_counters`. The version table stores only bounded typed environment/scope/registry/target coordinates, immutable target/config/credential-version digests, positive `created_epoch`, nullable greater `retired_epoch`, and at most 2-KiB canonical metadata with no secret/content; generated serialization rejects any complete encoded version row above the separately charged 4-KiB maximum. Unique `(environment_id,registry_kind,registry_id,target_digest,created_epoch)`, current-member, frozen-epoch membership, and zero-reference cleanup indexes are generated. The counter table uses fixed environment plus generation-fenced system/tenant/declared-scope rows with current/history rows+bytes, next epoch/generation, cleanup cursor/epoch, and oldest-eligible coordinates. App/control/MCP/worker/scheduler roles have no direct DML or broad payload `SELECT`. The emitter has only the fixed cross-table source+transport insert lane. The durable outbox dispatcher sees only the generic `queue_job_outbox` security-barrier candidate view and performs its exact enqueue/ambiguity/detach protocol with the deterministic group ID; there is no second event transport CAS. A group worker exact-verifies the claimed generic transport envelope against its immutable event group row before it can claim/read one assigned execution, page/materialize historical-epoch targets, grant one child effect, or terminal-CAS that row; it cannot change payload/handler/group/registry epoch, claim cross-scope work, rewind `effect_started`/`ambiguous`, reset another subscriber, or enumerate unrelated rows. ACL/default-ACL/trigger/body fingerprints are readiness gates, and hostile runtime tests cover direct insert/update/delete, overread, transport-peer substitution, cross-group claim, handler/group/epoch substitution, and state rewind.

Durable fan-out is explicit rather than hidden inside one subscriber call. Every generated fan-out source adapter must map its current webhook/subscription/recipient/strategy registry into `event_fanout_registry_versions`; no mutable source row is later treated as historical authority. Under the source's typed scope lock and counter hierarchy, add/replace/remove increments the protected registry epoch and atomically inserts a new version or sets exactly one current row's `retired_epoch`; each admitted execution freezes registry kind/ID/epoch and later selects exactly `created_epoch <= frozen_epoch AND (retired_epoch IS NULL OR frozen_epoch < retired_epoch)`. Legacy current members are seeded only by the fenced `mercato events reconcile-fanout-registry --phase preflight|seed|verify --batch-size=100` cutover while all legacy registry writers, emitters, and event workers remain drained. `preflight` uses every generated adapter to keyset-read the complete legacy population without mutation, derive the exact typed scope/target/resolver digest and 4-KiB charge for each current member **plus** the complete sorted fixed/dynamic counter-row plan and encoded charge. For each absent logical child it freezes the parent's generation/allocator high-water and assigns the next consecutive child generation in sorted-key order; existing children must exact-match. It aggregates version and counter rows/bytes together against every environment/system/tenant/declared-scope cap and fsyncs the count/high-water/Merkle digest into the controller journal; an unknown/duplicate/unbounded member or cap excess aborts with zero version/counter mutation. `seed` resumes that manifested keyset in transactions of at most 100, locks the complete generated counter hierarchy before legacy source/member rows, creates or exact-verifies only the journal-manifested generation-fenced counter children at their assigned generations, rejects allocator/parent drift, charges them plus each version, insert-or-verifies each epoch-one version atomically, and advances a fenced journal cursor/digest only after commit. `verify` performs two stable full adapter rescans around an indexed version/counter reconciliation, requires identical source and seeded counts/high-waters/digests with no extra/unversioned current member, then records the terminal registry-seed digest in the root journal's `registry_verified` leaf and required `event_fanout_registry_seed_digest` of the preinstall completion receipt. Crash/retry repeats exact rows and charges; changed source state invalidates the preflight rather than being silently folded in. The complete mutation guards and adapters replace the bootstrap seed grant before emission enablement; the one-shot seed authority is revoked. An unknown source, target lacking a complete immutable resolver version/digest, mutation path that bypasses this adapter, stale journal/fence, or residual bootstrap grant blocks launch.

Registry history is physically bounded independently of causal ledgers. Every version row has a generated encoded maximum of 4 KiB; hard stored maxima are organization 50,000 rows/100 MiB, tenant aggregate 100,000/200 MiB, system 50,000/100 MiB, and environment 500,000/1 GiB, including counter rows. Add/replace rejects before mutation at any cap; retirement, event settlement, cleanup, and GDPR remain legal. Exact `(environment_id,organization_id,tenant_id,id)` and nullable-user `(environment_id,subject_user_id,id)` indexes make every version a declared subject. Under the organization/user GDPR fence, the source adapter first retires every current matching version and blocks any new matching add. The operation-bound history lane may delete/redact a retired version before ordinary retention only after every referencing execution has completed its stable membership materialization and no nonterminal/leased/effect-started/ambiguous authority can still need that target resolver; already-terminal executions/effects retain only non-PII target/result digests and never dereference the version. Organization erasure deletes the exact scoped row and releases its exact version/counter charge in the same transaction. User erasure null-redacts only the user/recipient identity coordinates plus any user-derived resolver metadata while preserving an irreversible non-owning digest **and the full conservative row/byte charge** until later physical deletion; redaction cannot create capacity. Final subject zero proof includes current/history versions and counter descendants. The retention daemon's combined terminal lane round-robins event/queue terminal, client-invalidation, schedule-tombstone, and registry-history units. One ordinary history unit keysets the protected cursor past blockers and deletes one retired target version only after indexed proof that no nonterminal/retained event execution/effect freezes an epoch in its membership interval and no current source references the target version; the same transaction decrements the exact counter generation/charge. After a version/GDPR deletion, that transaction may also retire at most the now-empty declared-scope leaf and now-empty tenant parent: it locks surviving parent before child, proves zero current/history versions, zero descendant counters, zero execution/reference/cleanup-cursor ownership, exact-matches parent and child generations, generation-CAS deletes the child, and releases its manifested counter-row charge. A recreated logical key receives the parent's next never-reused generation, so a delayed adapter/cleanup writer cannot ABA. At most 1,000 combined terminal units run per tick, and the per-kind eligible count/oldest age participates in its computed drain/readiness deadline. Counter drift, leaked empty counter, reused generation, over-cap legacy seed, missing mutation adapter, oldest eligible deadline breach, unversioned target, or subject-index residue disables affected emission/finalization rather than truncating history. Tests erase a user and organization before/after epoch freeze, page materialization, grant, terminalization, and history cleanup, including shared non-user targets, cross-tenant equal UUIDs, counter-only near-cap preflight, partial seed crash, and add/retire/delete/recreate scope-counter churn with delayed old-generation writers.

Each generated event kind fixes complete event/group/execution root overhead plus, for every matched fan-out subscriber `i`, a positive per-target causal bound `1<=r_i<=8` rows/`1<=b_i<=16 KiB` including child/effect, nested outbox, future reconciliation tuple, ambiguity, and cleanup. Admission freezes **all** matched subscriber registry IDs/epochs/counts `N_i` under their sorted scope/counter locks and completes the same historical-epoch scan before root creation. Every target version declares either no secondary queue or one immutable generated destination-window ID/generation and positive maximum encoded outbox charge. The scan freezes, for each subscriber/destination pair, `N_{i,d}` plus the sorted target-identity/component-ordinal/token digest and summed destination bytes, with `Σ_d N_{i,d}` equal to that subscriber's queued-target subset and never greater than `N_i`; external-call targets contribute to `N_i` but to no destination histogram. Each matched trust group `g` separately freezes one peer-outbox destination-window ID/generation, maximum encoded charge, and named group component `G_g=1`; those fixed group transports are part of `R_event/B_event` causal overhead but require their own destination demand/rate tokens. The accepting transaction computes `R_total=R_event+Σ_i(R_i+N_i×r_i)` and `B_total=B_event+Σ_i(B_i+N_i×b_i)`, including every trust-group transport and execution, then locks the union of sorted destination windows and reserves every matched-group component plus every named `N_{i,d}` row/byte/rate-token component under the fixed 32-slot rolling rule. Mixed destinations are therefore explicit, not charged to a later page or inferred from mutable target state. Each `N_i<=10,000`, each per-subscriber shape must fit the strictest organization slice, and the aggregate must fit the exact source organization/tenant/system and environment `queue_other_general` counters; unknown/nonpositive terms or any overflow reject before root/event/transport/execution creation. One immutable root reserves that complete aggregate, so a later page never seeks capacity and multiple wildcard/fan-out subscribers cannot each consume a hidden `T`. Under each frozen epoch and typed scope locks, a subscriber keyset-materializes at most 32 sorted historical target identities per transaction into immutable `event_subscriber_effects`, maintaining its stable high-water/cursor/count/digest until that epoch's exact union is proven; current add/remove/ABA churn cannot alter or livelock the snapshot, and an unknown/nonhistorical/non-pageable source blocks launch. Each child stores registry kind/ID/epoch plus target kind/digest, scoped subscription/recipient/strategy/queue identity, frozen target/config/credential version, input digest, deterministic attempt/idempotency key, and `pending | leased | effect_started | completed | failed_terminal | ambiguous`; a secondary-queue child must exact-consume its frozen destination-window generation, component ordinal, rate-token ID, and row/byte charge, while an external-call child must have all destination-component fields null. For an external call, one grant permits exactly one SDK call with hidden retries disabled and a hard abort deadline. For a secondary-queue target, the event-child transaction instead inserts-or-exact-verifies the deterministic `queue_job_outbox` row and settles that event child atomically; only the durable-outbox-dispatcher touches Redis, so no duplicate direct-enqueue transport state exists. Success, proven pre-send failure, provider idempotency/status reconciliation, and response-loss ambiguity settle independently; the parent completes only after every matched execution's exact materialized child set is terminal or the guarded target-specific no-retry acknowledgment below. Target add/remove/reorder before a later page, below/above-cursor insert, ABA and sustained churn, exact history-cap, single-subscriber `N_i-1/N_i/N_i+1`, mixed external/two-destination histograms, destination aggregate `matched-group + Σ_i N_{i,d}` at `31/32/33` and byte boundaries, multi-subscriber aggregate `R/B-1/= /+1`, cursor blockers/cleanup, and crash-before/after histogram freeze, atomic destination reservation, each registry mutation/page/grant/call/settlement, and child→queue-outbox→Redis response-loss prove no missed, duplicate, cross-destination, later-charged, or unreserved effect.

The guarded no-retry acknowledgment is a generated **effect-row** reconciliation lane shared by `event_subscriber_effects` and `queue_handler_effects`, not an ActionLog correctness receipt and not one receipt component per fan-out target. Every effect row's admitted row/byte bound pre-reserves an inline nullable tuple containing canonical UUIDv7 `reconciliation_request_id`, expected execution/effect ID, attempt and generation, handler/target/config/credential/input digests, exact environment/scope coordinates, nullable indexed acknowledging actor, permission-snapshot digest, action exactly `acknowledge_no_retry`, allow-listed evidence kind plus bounded evidence digest, and database time. The immutable target/effect registry version declares whether acknowledgment is legal, its minimum ambiguity delay, authoritative evidence/status capability, exact scope permission, and terminal result mapping; an unknown effect type, generic absence-only evidence, or missing retained reconciler disables that target at generation/readiness. The authenticated operator command or separately typed operation capability takes the subject fence and exact scope/effect locks, reauthorizes the declared permission, verifies the UUIDv7 window, retained registry implementation, expected attempt/generation/digests, `effect_started|ambiguous` state, elapsed minimum, evidence, and that no live runtime, provider-status operation, transport, or automatic retry authority can still act. One guarded OLD→NEW CAS writes the tuple, moves the existing effect enum to `failed_terminal` with immutable result code `acknowledged_no_retry`, advances the exact parent, and permanently forbids replay; no new state-enum member is introduced. Every terminal/parent/cleanup predicate treats that row as `failed_terminal` while requiring the tuple for this result code. The record explicitly says the external effect may have happened and only declines another attempt. Exact request replay returns the same tuple; changed reuse, actor/scope mismatch, stale attempt, concurrent late settlement, or a remaining retry authority fails without mutation. User erasure takes the same fence and may null only the actor coordinate after authority ends while preserving the non-PII proof digest. Tests cover lost command responses, conflicting UUID reuse, settlement versus acknowledgment, runtime/provider-status races, retained-v1 reconciler during v2 rollout, actor erasure, fan-out at `N_i=10,000`, and proof that no new reservation/receipt row or external call is created.

The durable events worker loads only stored executions whose trust-group event row, peer generic transport outbox, and execution-set digest exact-match the claimed group job, then loads the exact retained handler version; it never rematches the current registry. A database-only handler applies its writes and marks complete in one transaction. Effectful handlers use only the child-effect API above. BullMQ retry reloads the ledger, skips completed children/handlers, and cannot repeat an `effect_started` attempt. Each child obtains the trust group's ordinary side-effect permit, so event work shares—not multiplies—the declared fleet cap. Unclassified raw external I/O, hidden retry, or inner effect concurrency is a static/readiness failure. Before dispatch, claim, target materialization, and grant, the capability rechecks active tenant/organization/user scope, runtime generation, and GDPR/cutover authority. Nonterminal event/execution/effect rows are indexed GDPR barriers. Under the operation fence, one exact event-group cancellation transaction takes the group and peer-outbox locks, sets immutable no-new-start authority, terminal-cancels every still-pending/unclaimed execution in the frozen at-most-36 execution set, freezes a digest of every terminal/leased/effect-started/ambiguous member, and CASes the peer to `detach_pending` kind `event_group_no_replay`; it commits all of those transitions or none. A leased member blocks final absence until normal no-more-side-effects or matching runtime termination; ambiguous child effects remain independently retained but are no longer startable/replayable through this group transport. The common slotless remove/status/zero-pass protocol then reaches `transport_detached`. Erasure completes only after every remaining execution/effect settles or uses the guarded target-specific no-retry lane. Tests pause/crash at logical cancel → detach pending → removal/absence, with multiple subscribers and multiple ambiguous effects, then at claim, materialization, grant, call, settlement, and concurrent user/organization erasure; they prove no late event enqueue, post-completion call, completed replay, cross-group effect, double local+durable dispatch, or missed wildcard.

The same discipline applies to every enabled ordinary legacy queue handler, not only event subscribers. Public direct/pager/scope transports retain their richer ledgers and are excluded only by exact generated handler IDs; any other exemption fails generation. The generated queue-durability migration adds exactly four protected tables: `queue_job_outbox`, `queue_handler_executions`, `queue_handler_effects`, and `durability_capacity_reservations`. `queue_job_outbox` includes the monotonic transport-release state, discriminated detach execution/effect/source/group/generation/times/absence digest, monotonic enqueue-attempt and terminal-removal generation/proved-through/cumulative-proof fields, terminal-removal absence-proved generation, current producer/remover runtime/start-attestation/checked Redis-server-run-ID/client-ID/generation/command-nonce/purpose/command-generation/database-generated binding-challenge nonce+time tuples plus allow-listed terminal-remove observed state, nonnegative Redis-client handoff count/chain/last-leaf fields, acknowledged-result or signed exact-tuple `RedisClientFenceReceiptV1` digest/outcome proofs, immutable destination-window generation/row-byte/rate-token charge and decrement-once detach-release time/digest, exact dispatchable/visible-recovery/detach candidate sort coordinates and partial candidate/detach/slot indexes described above. `queue_handler_effects` and `event_subscriber_effects` include the fixed inline reconciliation tuple/checks/indexes above. Checks require all-or-none state fields and forbid detached rewind; the security-barrier candidate view excludes `detach_pending|transport_detached`. Only fixed source, dispatcher enqueue/status, generation-fenced terminal remove/proof/absence, effect no-more-replay request, lock-held detach/remove/absence/final-slot-release, and terminal cleanup capabilities may change those columns. Each source records an immutable envelope; claim freezes handler/source/config and deterministic effects. External/file/provider effects use the grant API. Secondary-queue children atomically create exact nested outboxes; only the dispatcher touches Redis. The producer graph is acyclic at depth <=8. Database-only work and terminal marker share one transaction; messages-email records attempt before call and `emailSentAt` only after success. Redis loss, enqueue/remove response loss including delayed same-ID removal after an attempted re-add, worker crash, nested outbox boundaries, retry/stall/lock expiry, detach late-send races, and stale jobs prove one database transition plus one-or-ambiguous external effect. Any edge without durable source/reconciler is disabled.

Both durable ledger families are bounded and erasable without weakening ambiguity. The queue-durability migration's protected `durability_capacity_reservations` table has exactly two counter families per environment, `queue_generic_recurring` and `queue_other`. It stores exactly one `root` row per accepted parent plus deterministic `receipt_component` child rows as defined above; root uniqueness binds parent kind/ID/digest, while unique `(root_reservation_id,component_id)` binds each plural component. Each family has a hard ceiling of 1,000,000 rows and 2 GiB, and readiness proves configured ceilings sum to the physical 2,000,000-row/4-GiB bound and actual reserved+consumed usage never exceeds family, class, scope, or physical limits. A recurring generic source reserves from `queue_generic_recurring`; its execution, effects, nested outboxes, and receipt children consume that root and cannot switch family/class or open an unbound root. Manual and ordinary/event sources use the appropriate `queue_other` class. The accepting transaction locks hierarchical counters, derives a conservative root bound and exact future-component manifest from frozen subscriber/target epochs and payload bounds, refuses overflow, and atomically inserts root+parent plus any initial child. Later deterministic child materialization transfers one named pre-reserved component without new admission; descendants cannot exceed the root. Terminalization releases unused/unmaterialized components once impossible, while retained live rows remain consumed. Settlement, ambiguity recording, GDPR, and terminal cleanup are permitted at ceilings. Only fixed guard-owner root reserve/component-transfer/consume/release/reconcile capabilities mutate rows; direct DML, negative/overflow, caller family/class/bounds/component ID, switching, and candidate-view exposure fail. Nonterminal, leased, `effect_started`, or `ambiguous` causal rows never age-delete. Terminal causal rows store database `terminal_at`, minimized result digest and retention class; fixed capabilities keyset-delete at most 1,000 only after 30 database-time days and zero child/transport/reference/key dependencies. User/organization GDPR first proves zero nonterminal effects, then exact-subject deletes/redacts terminal coordinates through root/child indexes; free-form scans are forbidden. Readiness reconciles hierarchical counters, roots, child transfers, and physical samples and fails drift. Tests exhaust families with preaccepted roots before child materialization, materialize plural receipts at saturation, prove non-borrowing/descendant binding, and cover hostile DML, crash/reconcile, million-row plans, cleanup races, GDPR, key retirement, and exact boundaries.

The two physical capacity families are non-borrowable and `queue_other` is internally partitioned into three non-borrowable admission classes whose exact ceilings sum to its family ceiling: `queue_other_critical` is 100,000 rows/256 MiB, `queue_other_manual` is 50,000 rows/128 MiB, and `queue_other_general` is 850,000 rows/1,664 MiB. Critical is a generated closed allow-list limited to initial payment settlement/status sources, operation-GDPR/lifecycle finalization parents and descendants, the generated fixed at-most-64 infrastructure-counter set, at-most-40 `public_chat_scope_population` children, and at-most-40,001 generic-schedule-storage hierarchy rows, each charged at its exact encoded bound; it is not selectable by a request, module, event name, or arbitrary producer. The critical ceiling and startup seed reserve enough encoded headroom for that complete maximum infrastructure set before enabling ordinary admissions. Generic authenticated and cutover-remediation manual fires use manual. All other event/queue sources plus ordinary public-command and generic-scheduler undo/redo receipt-only reservations use general. Every accepted parent's conservative causal reservation includes the maximum future correctness receipts, ambiguity acknowledgments, reconciliation slots, cleanup markers, and terminal children it can require. In particular, public reply-job admission creates a `queue_other_general` reservation with fixed components for its metering and notification reconciliation slots plus protected receipts even though reply execution/effects remain in their richer public-chat ledgers and never become generic queue rows. A later reconcile/ack/cleanup consumes that already-bound component and never seeks new class admission; an exact duplicate consumes nothing. A source and all descendants retain one family/class, and no class borrows an idle floor. Settlement, cancellation, ambiguity recording/acknowledgment, receipt cleanup, and release of accepted work therefore require no new admission and remain possible when every class is full. Generation fails an effect class whose future terminal/reconciliation receipt bound is unknown.

Capacity is scope- and tenant-isolated. Recurring **projection** limits reserve counter/overlap headroom: organization 1,000 schedules/90,000 rows/180 MiB, tenant aggregate 2,000/180,000/360 MiB, system 1,000/90,000/180 MiB, and environment 10,000/900,000/1,792 MiB. Actual `queue_generic_recurring` usage, including counters and old revisions, has ceilings organization 100,000/200 MiB, tenant 200,000/400 MiB, system 100,000/200 MiB, environment 1,000,000/2 GiB. Within `queue_other`, organization caps are critical 10,000/25 MiB, manual 5,000/12 MiB, general 85,000/166 MiB; tenant aggregate is critical 20,000/50 MiB, manual 10,000/24 MiB, general 170,000/332 MiB. Tenant-scoped work uses the tenant aggregate. System is critical 20,000/51 MiB, general 85,000/166 MiB, authenticated manual zero, plus a controller-remediation-only manual slice 2,000/8 MiB. Counter rows cover every hierarchy/window. Admission locks them after source/receipt identity, charges organization work to organization+tenant, rejects before monopoly, and counts no duplicate. Reconciliation verifies counters against roots/children; GDPR does not move capacity. Revision/scope churn fixtures hit projection and actual boundaries while another tenant/system reserves.

No counter row is outside physical accounting. Fixed environment/family/class/retention/storage counters have a generated maximum of 64 rows/64 KiB and are precharged to `queue_other_critical`; the at-most-40,001 dynamic generic-storage hierarchy rows are likewise critical infrastructure; recurring causal scope/release counters consume the recurring family headroom; `queue_other` tenant/scope/actor/release counters consume the exact class they govern. Creating a dynamic counter first locks its surviving parent, increments that parent's `next_child_generation`, charges the exact encoded row/bytes, and inserts the child with the allocated generation plus the parent's current generation; inability to perform the complete CAS rejects the originating admission. Every reservation/source freezes the complete applicable counter ID/generation chain. Actor-window counters are eligible for exact deletion 24 hours after their last counted acceptance with zero live roots/children; declared-scope/tenant/release/storage counters require zero descendant counters, schedules, roots, children, slots, and active lifecycle references. The terminal-retention daemon uses sorted parent→child counter locks, generation-CAS deletion, and rechecks zero after waiting. A same-logical-key recreation allocates a strictly newer child generation from its still-live parent; if the parent itself was deleted and recreated, the changed parent generation makes the entire descendant chain different even when its new local allocator begins again. Fixed ancestry never deletes and its allocator never rewinds. A delayed writer must exact-match every frozen ancestor/child generation and therefore cannot ABA a deleted counter. Family/class/physical reconciliation counts every counter/root/child and actual encoded bytes; stored-schedule reconciliation independently counts every non-strict schedule charge against its storage hierarchy. Readiness fails any uncharged row, reused generation, or projection/stored-headroom drift. Churn tests create/delete/recreate actors, tenants, organizations, scopes, disabled schedules, and tombstones at every physical boundary, pause old writers across every ancestor reuse, and prove bounded rows/bytes plus no ABA.

Authenticated manual admission has additional durable abuse and fairness bounds. A new request is accepted only for a canonical UUIDv7 `Idempotency-Key`; it point-loads an existing deterministic receipt first, but if none exists applies the same database-time future-five-minute/old-24-hour gate as public commands. Under one scope+actor advisory lock and the reservation indexes, a new request must remain within 100 accepted manual triggers per actor+scope per rolling 24 database-time hours, 1,000 per scope per rolling 24 hours, four unclaimed/nonterminal manual sources per schedule, and 64 per scope. Exact retries consume no budget. Saturation returns `429` with bounded database-time `Retry-After` and creates no receipt, reservation, outbox, or Redis job. There is no anonymous/system manual API actor; the controller-only preinstall remediation lane is separately discriminated and charged to the manual class. When a claimed job finds a different active execution, it performs no authoritative mutation and moves to a deterministic 60-to-120-second database-time-derived delayed window. Because one schedule can contribute at most four such jobs and one scope at most 64, a continuous hostile flood cannot keep the C1 ready head occupied; another schedule's ready fire progresses once the bounded head is delayed. Tests sustain flood/retry/revision/actor rotation across two tenants and prove caps, exact duplicate freedom, non-borrowing, bounded queue churn, and progress for the quiet tenant.

An acquired but full family/class/scope counter is the typed `capacity_exhausted` no-source deferral, distinct from `capacity_contended`: it inserts no reservation/outbox, advances no recurring `next_run_at`, pointer, or last-materialized coordinate, and moves only `generic_materialize_after` to a bounded database-time fair retry. A pointed same-revision unclaimed source uses the separate `outstanding_fire` deferral; it verifies that source and leaves its pointer, reservation, outbox, `next_run_at`, and immutable envelope unchanged while moving only error/retry time. The enabled-schedule 30-day projection is admission planning, not a claim that retained old revisions can never make instantaneous capacity full. Revision/disable-near-capacity and competing-scope tests prove both deferrals recover without cursor loss or starvation.

Database acceptance is deliberately wider than Redis readiness. For `scheduler-execution`, the durable dispatcher enforces exactly four non-borrowable environment transport-release slots: one system and three tenant-domain. At most one tenant slot is visible/nonterminal across a tenant and its child organizations, one per exact scope, and one per schedule. A preclaim source is release-eligible only while its exact current schedule has `generic_active_execution_id IS NULL`; a claimed/resume source is eligible only when its unique execution ID is that exact active pointer. Pending outboxes outside the window—including a waiting successor behind a different active execution—remain authoritative but not Redis-visible and own no release slot. The metadata view and `scheduler_release_window` counter persist lane → least-recently-released tenant → child scope → workload-class order; never-served sorts first and recurring → authenticated manual → remediation rotates while empty classes skip.

An independent indexed stale-source candidate is cleanup, not Redis readiness. It selects only unclaimed recurring/manual/remediation scheduler sources whose frozen schedule incarnation/revision/scope/entry/digests no longer equal the locked current row or whose row is disabled/deleted; current sources merely waiting behind an active execution are excluded. Under the full scheduler hierarchy and outbox-ID lock, one causal transaction terminal-cancels that immutable source, releases only its unused reservation components, clears the waiting pointer only if it still exact-points to that source, records the immutable source-terminal digest, and CASes the peer outbox to unclaimed `detach_pending` with its frozen nullable slot tuple. If the outbox was never visible, no-send history and null slot are proved; if it was visible/ambiguous, the ordinary no-more-send/runtime and removal proof remains required. The detach cursor advances past every locked/malformed candidate, so revision/disable/delete does not scan unpointed sources and old authenticated-manual or legacy-remediation work cannot persist forever. Crash at terminal-cancel/detach-pending is atomic or repeats by digest. Fixtures revise and disable before first dispatch for recurring, authenticated manual, and remediation sources, including four manual sources, a permanent remediation receipt, a previously visible job, and a current source behind an active execution that must remain untouched.

`queue_job_outbox` has protected monotonic `transport_release_state` exactly `dispatchable | visible | detach_pending | transport_detached`, with required `transport_detach_kind` exactly `claimed_no_replay | unclaimed_terminal_source | event_group_no_replay` while pending/detached; nullable kind-discriminated `transport_detach_execution_id`, `transport_detach_effect_digest`, `transport_detach_source_terminal_digest`, `transport_detach_event_group_id`, and `transport_detach_execution_set_state_digest`; positive `transport_detach_generation`, `transport_detach_started_at`, `transport_detached_at`, and `transport_absence_proof_digest`; nullable all-or-none `transport_release_slot_id`/positive `transport_release_slot_generation`; and required `transport_destination_window_id`, positive `transport_destination_window_generation`, positive row/byte charge, plus nullable all-or-none `transport_destination_released_at`/lowercase SHA-256 release digest. Transport provenance is explicit and uses disjoint enqueue and terminal-removal chains. Bigint `transport_enqueue_attempt_generation` and `transport_enqueue_proved_through_generation` start at zero and require `0<=provedThrough<=generation`; required lowercase SHA-256 `transport_enqueue_proof_chain_digest` starts at the generated genesis digest; and one current producer command shape is present exactly while `generation>provedThrough`; its command generation equals the enqueue-attempt generation. `binding_pending` is exact `{ dispatcher_runtime_id, runtime_generation, start_attestation_digest, client_claim_id, client_claim_identity_digest, registered_identity_verification_digest, registered_connection_state_digest, redis_server_run_id, redis_client_id, client_generation, command_nonce, purpose='enqueue', command_generation, binding_challenge_nonce, binding_challenge_at }` with `database_tuple_digest`, `current_command_tuple_digest`, `registered_command_state_digest`, `controller_root_binding_ack_digest`, `controller_root_bound_at`, acknowledged-result fields, and controller-fence fields null. The registrar-only bind CAS fills those five fields to make `registered`; only a registered database tuple plus its exact fsynced root commit marker may send. A normal result is a protected acknowledged tuple consumed only by controller `reconcile_result`; ambiguity may add only registrar-authored all-or-none `{ controller_fence_receipt_digest, controller_fence_tuple_digest, controller_fence_outcome, controller_fence_verified_at }` with a sufficient outcome. Starting attempt `N` is one guarded CAS from `generation=N-1=provedThrough`: it increments generation, installs only `binding_pending`, and performs no Redis call until the controller registration CAS and its exact root commit marker both commit. Attempt `N+1` is forbidden until controller result reconciliation and registrar fold have consumed its exact acknowledged normal result, or a registrar-committed fence receipt whose entire registered tuple and `purpose='enqueue'`/`commandGeneration=N` match and whose outcome is exactly `killed_then_absent | already_absent | server_incarnation_retired`; `run_id_changed_unproved`, runtime death, socket close, or elapsed time is insufficient. The controller result-fold CAS, or the guarded sufficient-fence fold after its immutable controller commitment, hashes domain-separated `(priorChain,N,producer,acknowledgedResultOrControllerFenceCommitmentDigest)` into the chain, sets `provedThrough=N`, and clears the current tuple; only the already-clear two-store result path may atomically start `N+1`. A response-lost/possible-send attempt therefore cannot be overwritten by a restarted dispatcher. The row also owns generated `redis_client_handoff_count`, `redis_client_handoff_chain_digest`, and `redis_client_last_handoff_leaf_digest`; genesis is count zero/null leaf, and every normal/fence fold atomically advances the owner chain with the independently advancing root-claim handoff ordinal before clearing the tuple. Bigint `transport_terminal_remove_generation`, `transport_terminal_remove_proved_through_generation`, and `transport_terminal_absence_proved_generation` also start at zero and require `0<=absenceProved<=provedThrough<=generation`; required lowercase SHA-256 `transport_terminal_remove_proof_chain_digest` starts at its generated domain-separated genesis digest. The current terminal-remover command has the same `binding_pending -> registered` shapes and controller-only result/fence commitment rules: its base contains exact removal generation, remover runtime ID/generation/start-attestation, client claim ID/claim-identity/identity-verification/registered-connection-state digests, Redis server run ID, Redis client ID/generation and command nonce, `purpose='terminal_remove'`, allow-listed observed BullMQ state, observed enqueue generation, retained-envelope digest, database-generated binding-challenge nonce, and binding-challenge database time; its registered phase adds database-tuple/current-command/registered-command-state digests plus controller root-binding acknowledgment/datetime, and ambiguity adds the four controller fence commitment fields. It exists exactly while remove `generation>provedThrough`; any committed receipt must exact-match the complete registered tuple and removal generation. Starting removal `M` is one guarded CAS from `generation=M-1=provedThrough` with a completed enqueue chain and exact retained-envelope equality under one of two disjoint predicates: redispatch has observed matching `completed|failed`, or `detach_pending` has exact kind/generation/no-more-send proof and an inventoried matching `waiting|delayed|prioritized|waiting-children|active|completed|failed` root. A same-ID foreign/mismatched envelope, unknown state, or unsuccessful active/foreign removal remains live corruption/blocking and is never deleted. The CAS installs the exact observed-state/envelope `binding_pending` tuple and performs no Redis removal until the controller bind CAS makes it registered and the exact root commit marker is fsynced. No add/re-add or removal `M+1` may begin while `M` is unproved. An acknowledged result from the non-buffering, non-retrying exact-remove adapter is folded only through controller result reconciliation; otherwise only a registrar-committed controller fence receipt matching `purpose='terminal_remove'`/`commandGeneration=M` and outcome `killed_then_absent | already_absent | server_incarnation_retired` may fold it. After either sufficient proof, and never after `run_id_changed_unproved` or runtime termination alone, a fresh status plus page-zero-to-EOF absence pass under the outbox lock may CAS `absenceProved=M`. If the key remains, absence stays at its earlier value and a later full visit must grant `M+1`. No add/re-add is legal unless remove `generation=provedThrough=absenceProved` and the current remover tuple is null. Thus a lost remove/status response cannot leave an old same-ID command able to delete a replacement. After obtaining a root-bound `RedisClientGenerationClaimV1`, and before any effectful command on its fresh nonreconnecting socket, the fixed dispatcher adapter issues only literal `INFO SERVER` and `CLIENT ID` on that same socket, validates one canonical server `run_id` and client ID, allocates a never-reused client generation/command nonce, and supplies them to the guarded attempt/removal CAS. That first commit includes claim ID, claim-identity digest, registered-identity-verification digest, and registered-connection-state digest, with registered-command/controller-binding/result/fence fields null; the controller exact-reads it, fsync-binds the command digest into the root claim, and the registrar-only second database CAS stores the immutable registered-command-state digest plus controller root-binding acknowledgment digest/database time. Every dispatcher Redis client generation has that controller/root-store `RedisClientGenerationClaimV1`, and every signed fence receipt exact-binds its claim ID/identity-verification/claim-identity/registered-connection-state and historical registered-command-state digests plus controller root-binding acknowledgment, and is manifested with `enableOfflineQueue:false`, `autoResendUnfulfilledCommands:false`, `maxRetriesPerRequest:0`, no reconnect retry strategy, that fixed identity preflight, and one effectful command at a time. Any add/remove response ambiguity immediately marks that client generation draining, ends the slice, forbids another command on it, force-closes the local socket, and starts a narrow connection-fence proof. The data-plane daemon has no `CLIENT LIST`, `CLIENT KILL`, or admin credential; its only client subcommand is `CLIENT ID`, and its read-only `INFO` metadata exposure is an explicitly accepted/fingerprinted role capability used to obtain the server run ID.
