Only its signed, exact-tuple `RedisClientFenceReceiptV1` with a sufficient outcome is connection-scoped no-more-send/no-more-remove, and it permits the dispatcher runtime to continue only on a fresh client generation. A protected controller/root-store lineage per environment+producer role holds at most two unresolved/live generation claims total. After a first ambiguity it marks that generation retired-unproved and may authorize exactly one fresh current generation for other outbox IDs; if that replacement also becomes ambiguous, both slots are retired-unproved and no third connection/effect is legal until a sufficient fence receipt clears one. Restart first reloads/reconciles those claims and cannot reset the allocator or cap. The affected ID remains barred until its own proof completes; under the qualified healthy profile that proof completes within 15 database-time seconds and the row folds/rechecks on a later slice. If a sufficient fence receipt is not persisted by 15 seconds, the supervisor terminates the exact dispatcher runtime, but runtime termination alone never substitutes for the receipt; the affected row remains barred and its oldest-eligible/readiness deadline fires while other IDs may use a new proved-disjoint client generation. No force-close, runtime restart, or elapsed age by itself clears an attempt/removal. Tests lose add and remove responses before/after server receipt, pause the old client, deliver its buffered command before the controller helper fences it, prove same-run exact-ID absence, rotate, and show no old command can act after the fresh state/absence check; they also cover binding-pending no-send, hostile direct writes to every controller field, acknowledged-result/root-reconciliation/database-fold crashes, run-ID mismatch with no retirement proof followed by late sufficient retirement proof, signed old-container retirement, partition/replacement/failback, wrong purpose/generation/nonce/runtime/claim/connection digest, delayed receipt replay, and two consecutive response-loss generations with helper unavailable plus supervisor restart, proving no third client and the `49+49+20=118` budget. A Redis state read before the database transaction is candidate information only. Each enqueue or redispatch visit first takes its destination's complete database hierarchy; for scheduler work that is lifecycle/storage/schedule→source→outbox session lock→release counter→destination window when cursor or transport-demand state must CAS. While already holding the outbox lock, one transaction revalidates current replay authority and either starts/freeze-grants exact attempt `N`, chooses detach, or makes no transport grant; it commits before Redis I/O and retains only the outbox session lock. Universally, a first attempt on `dispatchable` atomically starts `N` and CASes `dispatchable -> visible`; a non-scheduler destination requires the scheduler slot tuple null, while scheduler additionally acquires its first slot in that transaction. A recovery attempt on already-`visible` exact-retains the existing nullable slot tuple and leaves state visible. If any proof fails, neither attempt nor state/slot changes. Thus an ordinary/event add with a lost response is already discoverable only by the visible-recovery sublane, never stranded as dispatchable. The frozen attempt then point-loads the deterministic BullMQ ID and exact-verifies its envelope: absent permits exactly one add under attempt `N` only when the terminal-removal equality above also holds; matching `waiting|delayed|prioritized|waiting-children|active` performs no add and records/folds a normal `no_send_already_visible` end proof for `N`. BullMQ parent/dependency/FlowProducer options are statically forbidden by every generated producer manifest; an observed matching `waiting-children` row is therefore treated as visible for duplicate prevention but emits typed transport-corruption telemetry and fails affected readiness until repaired, and it never weakens the database claim/effect gate. Matching `completed|failed` performs no add, records/folds `no_send_terminal_present`, and, only once the enqueue-attempt chain is complete, starts the exact terminal-removal generation above before any remove call. After terminal-removal proof and generation-matched absence it performs no schedule/source/execution read or authoritative transition, releases the lock, and starts a wholly new visit from the full hierarchy; a schedule mutation may win between visits and must be observed. A same-ID envelope mismatch or unreadable/unknown state performs no add, emits bounded typed telemetry, leaves the candidate due, and normal-ends/folds `N` as no-send; it never pretends the preexisting Redis object is safe. Remove/status ambiguity leaves the exact removal generation and remover tuple live, changes no enqueue-attempt field, and bars re-add; the dispatcher releases/yields until acknowledged removal or exact no-more-remove proof permits the locked absence step. A late reappearance after a proved absence cannot rewind either chain: a new full-hierarchy visit observes its current state and, if terminal, must grant the next removal generation before any later add. Only an actual add call with possible-send may leave exact attempt `N` ambiguous; acknowledged add normal-ends/folds that attempt. The restarted visit revalidates the existing scheduler slot/generation rather than acquiring a second slot and may freeze `N+1` only when the enqueue chain is proved through, the terminal-removal generation equals both its proved-through and absence-proved generations with no current remover, the source remains replayable, and the active pointer is null for an unclaimed source or exact-equal to the resumed execution; a different active pointer starts no attempt. No path reacquires schedule/storage/fence locks while holding the outbox lock, and no Redis observation made before the frozen database grant authorizes a call. Only a visible/nonterminal `scheduler-execution` outbox admitted by the four-slot window may own a release-slot tuple. A still-dispatchable scheduler source and every non-scheduler destination require both slot fields null. The claimed kind is for one ordinary queue-handler execution and requires its execution ID/effect digest while forbidding source/group fields. The unclaimed kind requires an immutable terminal-cancellation source digest, forbids execution/effect/group fields, and proves no execution. The event-group kind requires exact group ID plus frozen execution-set state digest, forbids single execution/effect/source fields, and proves group no-new-start plus no startable member while retaining any bounded pre-reserved ambiguous set. Detach freezes the nullable slot tuple; detached never returns to an earlier state or changes it. For a non-scheduler destination the dispatcher takes the outbox-ID session advisory lock before its final database grant. For `scheduler-execution`, it follows the complete hierarchy through the exact schedule, then takes the outbox-ID session lock, then locks/rechecks the release-window counter before the final grant; no scheduler dispatcher path takes that counter before the outbox lock. After commit it retains the outbox lock through Redis success/pre-send/ended-ambiguous CAS. Local mode uses its queue-coordinator lock with the same destination-specific post-lock preflight. The scheduler grant proves either no execution plus null active pointer or an existing unique execution equal to the active pointer. If a different/non-null active pointer appears, the transaction leaves the outbox `dispatchable` with null slot, acquires/releases no slot, records no transport attempt/generation, and performs no Redis call or cursor-service claim. The schedule eligibility proof, one-per-schedule slot check, slot ID/generation acquisition, and universal first-attempt/`dispatchable -> visible` CAS are one transaction while the outbox lock is already held; the lock remains held through the subsequent transport outcome, so no competing final grant can bypass it. A fixed no-more-replay capability may CAS to `detach_pending`: the claimed lane requires the unique claimed execution and frozen effect manifest proving no ungranted/startable child and every remaining child terminal or the one exact non-replayable `effect_started|ambiguous` grant; the unclaimed lane requires an already committed revision/disable/expiry/stale-source terminal cancellation, exact no-execution proof, and no live waiting/active pointer to that source; the event-group lane requires the atomic group cancellation/state digest above. That committed CAS makes every candidate/producer/status/claim path reject new enqueue or execution before any absence proof.

The detach worker uses the same global order: for a scheduler source it first locks/reloads the storage/fence and schedule authority, then acquires/holds the outbox-ID lock, and only then locks/rechecks the `scheduler_release_window` counter when a nonnull slot must be released; every other destination begins with the outbox lock and never touches that counter. It exact-matches kind/generation/source/group/frozen nullable slot tuple and the kind-specific single-execution/effect, source-terminal, or event-group state proof. Before absence proof it requires `transport_enqueue_proved_through_generation=transport_enqueue_attempt_generation`; if one current enqueue attempt remains, only its exact acknowledged result or sufficient signed `RedisClientFenceReceiptV1` for the full producer tuple and that enqueue generation may be folded into the cumulative chain under the held lock. Possible-send age, Redis absence, runtime death, `run_id_changed_unproved`, or a receipt for a different tuple/generation is insufficient. Every exact Redis remove is first granted as terminal-removal generation `M` under the held outbox lock and uses the same non-buffering, non-retrying adapter and proof chain above. An acknowledged remove may fold `M`; a lost response leaves `M` live until a sufficient signed fence receipt exact-matches the remover tuple and removal generation. Only with `transport_terminal_remove_generation=transport_terminal_remove_proved_through_generation=transport_terminal_absence_proved_generation`, no current remover, and a generation-matched page-zero-to-EOF absence pass may detachment continue. Only after exact retained-envelope equality, the adapter status-reconciles and point-removes the deterministic root job through `waiting|delayed|prioritized|waiting-children|active|completed|failed` without recursively deleting unknown children; generated manifests forbid BullMQ parent/dependency/FlowProducer options, and an unremovable or foreign-dependency `waiting-children` object remains a typed corruption/readiness and deletion blocker rather than authorizing broad cleanup. Only the final transaction may CAS `detach_pending -> transport_detached`; after the already-held outbox lock, a nonnull scheduler slot tuple takes its release counter, exact-matches its live generation, and decrement-once releases it, while a null tuple performs a checked zero scheduler-slot release. The transaction then locks the immutable destination window, exact-matches its generation and this outbox's unreleased one-row/byte/rate-token coordinates, decrement-once releases only the live row/byte transport demand without refunding the rolling token, writes the domain-separated release digest, and commits detached+both applicable releases atomically; it never releases the separate retained causal root/class charge. This is transport settlement only: source/group/execution/root/capacity/effect ambiguity/GDPR/outcome/manual-ack obligations stay retained and indexed until exact business settlement. A detached/stale delivery ACKs/no-ops and cannot claim/grant/replay; later effect adjudication cannot reattach or reacquire a slot. Ordinary terminal/revision/disable/receipt-expiry/stale-source/event-group cleanup uses the same pending→locked no-more-send→enqueue-chain-complete→terminal-removal-chain-complete→generation-matched absence→detached protocol with its exact discriminated proof. Duplicate/delayed scheduler copies retain their one slot until proof; non-scheduler and never-visible sources retain none. Within one qualified scheduler-destination slice, the persisted outer alternation gives detach every second causal unit. With all four possible slot detaches—one system plus three tenant—continuously eligible and unlocked, they therefore complete within the first eight alternating causal units of that slice; all three tenant detaches complete inside the same bound even when system remains eligible, after which tenant fairness chooses a new tenant before refilling the prior one. A blocker advances the detach inspection cursor without claiming completion and is governed by the destination's oldest-eligible deadline. Tests pause mutation holding the schedule before dispatcher/detacher outbox acquisition and pause dispatcher/detacher after schedule but before outbox, counter after outbox, plus crash before/after pending CAS, immediately before Redis send, during possible-send, after one ambiguous producer crash, after its proof fold and a second ambiguous producer crash, after terminal-key generation-fenced removal/absence then outbox-lock release while a schedule mutation wins before full-hierarchy reacquire, after detach removal/before final CAS, and after detach; detach one event group with multiple subscriber executions/ambiguities, every other non-scheduler destination with a null slot, and both never-visible and visible scheduler sources with null/non-null slot tuples; race revision/disable/manual-receipt expiry/stale-source cancellation before and after visibility with zero execution; race an active-pointer claim before candidate selection, between selection and final grant, and after visibility; create three tenants with long-lived active executions plus waiting successors and prove none of those successors takes a slot while a fourth tenant and system progress; sustain dispatchable+visible-recovery+detach eligibility through within-slice alternation, cursor wrap, and crash; lose a remove/status response, attempt a same-ID re-add while the old remover remains live, then deliver the old remove and prove re-add stayed barred; also inject late delivery, settle later ambiguity, and prove no provenance overwrite, lock inversion, database-state-only or Redis-absence-only release, double release/reattach/replay, or cursor loss.

Dynamic notification recipient expansion is an exact event fan-out class and therefore uses the same immutable registry epoch, complete pre-reservation, and ceiling formula as other fan-out; paging is not permission to seek capacity later. Its manifest fixes positive per-recipient causal bound `r_notify` rows/`b_notify` bytes plus root overhead `R0_notify`/`B0_notify`, and admission freezes/counts the versioned same-scope recipient union before root creation with `N_notify=min(10,000,floor((85,000-R0_notify)/r_notify),floor((166 MiB-B0_notify)/b_notify))`. Unknown bounds or a count above `N_notify` reject before parent/reservation/event creation. For an accepted source, each transaction freezes at most 32 exact historical-epoch recipients under membership/user locks into pre-reserved child rows, advances a stable high-water/count/digest, and dispatches only committed children. Membership or erasure races revalidate per target; a page rejection remains recoverable and does not lose the parent. Fixtures cover `N_notify-1/N_notify/N_notify+1`, bounded rejection of a synthetic >100,000-recipient registry, crash between page commit and child dispatch, and bounded-memory/transaction progress without exceeding subject, lock, or causal-capacity limits.

Workflow activity definitions are untrusted tenant input. Production removes arbitrary `{{env.*}}` interpolation except a tiny generated non-secret typed allow-list and launch-disables `CALL_API`, arbitrary command/event/function dispatch, and arbitrary webhook/email activities until each has a generated per-activity capability binding exact target/endpoint+method, input/output/header schema, scope rederivation, creator/approver permission, least-privilege credential, frozen version, deadline, and effect class. Server-owned authorization/scope headers cannot be overridden; API credentials are short database-time-expiring, recovered after crash, and never admin-wide or `expiresAt:null`; responses are bounded and minimized. Publish and every execution reauthorize the exact capability. Hostile definitions cannot select another command/event/tenant, forge SSE/events, read process secrets, call internal/private/metadata destinations, or persist secrets/results.

Workflow event triggers are default-deny projections, not wildcard access to raw domain events. The generated event registry gives each exact event/version a sensitivity class, `workflowTriggerable` flag, source feature/permission, and one versioned per-subscriber projection schema that maps only approved fields; `excludeFromTriggers`, unknown events, raw wildcard-only matches, and schema/projection drift fail closed. Workflow create/update/publish/enable freezes creator, independent approver where required, service capability, source feature/scope, projection version, and allowed target activities; each execution reauthorizes all of them against the current tenant/organization and source entity before persisting an instance. Only the mapped minimized projection is stored or exposed—never raw payload or `__trigger.eventPayload`. A workflow-only user without customer-account read authority cannot capture signup/update/login emails or other source-feature PII, and permission revocation closes pending triggers.

Webhook create/rotate reveals an encrypted-at-rest versioned signing secret once and only to `webhooks.manage`; list/detail/delivery/log/outbox/Redis/error responses permanently redact it, and only the assigned delivery grant may decrypt the frozen version. Each webhook target is same-tenant-and-organization re-read under locks with its active subscription epoch, normalized HTTPS URL, secret digest, and minimized typed-scope audit coordinates. The shared safe transport used by delivery and send-test pins validated public DNS/TLS, rejects private/link-local/metadata/mixed answers, revalidates every allowed redirect (or disables redirects), streams a bounded response under one hard deadline, and performs zero hidden retries. Legacy arbitrary payload/response rows are backfilled to indexed tenant/organization/user coordinates and minimized request/result digests or retired under retention/GDPR proof. Reparent/deactivate/rotation, DNS/redirect rebinding, slow/chunked response, SSRF test-route, crash, and lost-response fixtures settle through the child ledger without leaking the secret.

| Service role | Exact launch process and cap |
|---|---|
| web app | Existing standalone server command; one replica; HTTP only; `AUTO_SPAWN_WORKERS=false` and no scheduler/reconciler authority. |
| private control API | Same standalone image/server on internal port 3002 with `CRM_RUNTIME_ROLE=control`; one replica; middleware allow-lists only Noli link-cancellation/status and GDPR/finalizer routes. Public app denies those routes. |
| MCP | Existing `node /app/packages/cli/bin/mercato ai_assistant mcp:serve-http --port 3001`; one replica; separately scoped database role. |
| public-chat target worker | `node /app/packages/cli/bin/mercato queue worker customers-public-chat-replies --concurrency=5`; one replica; effective concurrency exactly five with four non-borrowable validated sweep slots and one non-borrowable direct-job slot acquired before authority; no-slot claims move delayed 5–15 seconds. |
| generic scheduler service | `node /app/packages/cli/bin/mercato scheduler serve --worker-concurrency=1 --materialize-interval-seconds=5 --materialize-batch-size=100`; one replica/process identity; the supervised DB-only materializer and `scheduler-execution` C1 worker share the manifested pool/client caps. It installs no recurring Redis state and accepts only generic registry-bound fires; public-chat schedules/targets are rejected, so generic backlog or a hung command cannot delay the strict sweep. |
| global public-chat pager worker | `node /app/packages/cli/bin/mercato queue worker customers-public-chat-sweeps --concurrency=1`; one replica; effective concurrency exactly one; accepts only the static system/environment pager envelope materialized by the singleton canonical Job Scheduler, advances one durable scope cursor, and creates/enqueues at most one exact scope target binding per execution/minute. No generic or organization command can address this queue. |
| delivery worker group | New `queue worker --manifest-group=delivery --global-concurrency=3`; one replica; exact queues `events-delivery`, `notifications`, and `messages-email`; per-queue claim cap one and at most three handlers/child effects past the no-authority permit. It alone receives bounded delivery credentials/grants and a read-only attachment mount. |
| search worker group | New `queue worker --manifest-group=search --global-concurrency=2`; one replica; exact queues `events-search`, `fulltext-indexing`, and `vector-indexing`; per-queue claim cap one and at most two handlers/child effects past the permit. It alone receives search/pgvector/embedding configuration. |
| workflow worker | New `queue worker --manifest-group=workflow --global-concurrency=1`; one replica; exact queues `events-workflow` and `workflow-activities`; only this role receives the reviewed, registry-limited workflow capabilities. |
| account-cleanup worker group | New `queue worker --manifest-group=account-cleanup --global-concurrency=1`; one replica; exact queues `events-account-cleanup`, `customer-accounts-cleanup-sessions`, and `customer-accounts-cleanup-tokens`; database-only cleanup authority and no provider credentials. |
| payment worker group | New `queue worker --manifest-group=payment --global-concurrency=2`; one replica; exact queues `events-payment`, `payment-gateways-webhook`, `payment-gateways-status-poller`, and `stripe-webhook`; per-queue claim cap one, at most two handlers/child effects past the permit, and only payment/integration credentials. |
| durable outbox dispatcher | New exact `node /app/packages/cli/bin/mercato durability outbox-dispatch --daemon`; one replica; database advisory singleton, one fixed environment `outbox_dispatch_cycle`, and exactly 16 fixed destination windows: five event-group queues plus the eleven ordinary non-public queues. The cycle row is the crash-stable between-window owner: deterministic ordinal round-robin gives each window one bounded service slice and cannot begin another window while an active slice exists or repeat a completed window until all 16 are serviced. Before any candidate/effect, one transaction CAS-installs the cycle row's header-only `{sliceGeneration,activeWindowOrdinal,activeWindowGeneration,start,deadline}` and that window's separate active half `{activeGeneration,immutableStartingCursorAndSelectorSnapshots,perSublaneInspectedAndCompletedCounts=0}`. The window's live cursors/selectors are persistent state and are neither copied into nor reset by the cycle header. One slice metadata-keysets candidates in pages of at most 32, processes at most 256 independent causal units, spends at most 2.5 database-time seconds, and gives each Redis/database operation the smaller of its reviewed two-second bound and remaining slice budget; no batch transaction or shared transport result can couple two outbox IDs. Each unit commits its outbox outcome together with that generation's cursor/mode/count CAS where applicable. At end/deadline one transaction exact-matches both generations, clears only the cycle header and window active half, and persists the serviced bit/next ordinal; the advanced window cursors/selectors remain nonnull for the next slice. A crash resumes from the committed unit cursor while time remains; after deadline it runs only the final CAS. A crash after a Redis effect but before its outcome/cursor CAS may re-inspect only that one ID, whose attempt/removal chain forces reconciliation, never replay the whole slice. The daemon starts no new slice after 50 seconds, so one healthy complete cycle is at most 40 seconds and every continuously eligible window is sliced at least once per minute independent of traffic. A transport-response-ambiguous ID commits its exact attempt/remover plus cursor/mode state, marks that Redis client generation retired-unproved, and ends/finalizes the slice early; a later slice may use only the one permitted replacement in that role/slot lineage, and a second unresolved generation bars further transport rather than rotating a third. Each window has independent indexed `dispatchable`, already-`visible` recovery, and `detach` cursor/epoch/wrap/LRS/oldest-eligible coordinates, a crash-stable outer `next_unit_kind='enqueue | detach'`, and a crash-stable inner `next_enqueue_kind='dispatchable | visible_recovery'`. The outer selector alternates nonempty enqueue and detach units; an enqueue unit uses the inner selector, which alternates fresh dispatchable grants with visible-state recovery/removal. At either level, an indexed-empty chosen sublane may fall through to its sibling while preserving the empty sublane as next preference. Candidate selection reads the window coordinates without retaining its row lock. A causal unit takes the deterministic outbox/session lock before the destination window row when both are needed; a failed outbox try-lock may advance only the window cursor in a separate short CAS and never holds the window while waiting for that outbox. Every inspected candidate—success, blocked lock, malformed row, CAS loss, or transport ambiguity—generation-CAS advances only that sublane's inspection cursor and both persisted selectors; authority/enqueue fields remain unchanged on a blocker, and wrap occurs only after an indexed EOF proof. A separate indexed minimum probe refreshes each oldest-eligible coordinate without resetting its cursor. Thus one locked or corrupt head cannot be selected every cycle or conceal a later row, and restart cannot reset preference or position. On the qualified production profile, with all three state classes continuously eligible and unlocked, each destination must complete at least 256 causal units per healthy minute: at least 64 dispatchable, 64 visible-recovery, and 128 detach units under the two-level alternation; an empty class lends its units to siblings. The hard 4,096-row/32-MiB destination reservation and at-most-32-new-rows/minute admission are valid only while that measured floor holds. Let `I_dispatchable`, `I_visible`, and `I_detach` be each sublane's complete indexed candidate inspection population from the persisted cursor through one wrap, including locked, malformed, CAS-lost, and currently eligible rows; each is bounded by the 4,096 destination cap. Dispatchable and visible-recovery each have deadline `2 + ceil(I_kind / 64)` minutes, detach has `2 + ceil(I_detach / 128)` minutes, measured from the oldest eligible row. Thus a row unlocking just behind the cursor is charged the full blocker/cursor distance rather than an unlocked-only count, and full Redis loss for a saturated destination must recover within the visible-recovery deadline. A Redis client fence unproved for 15 seconds, floor miss, cursor stall, cap/rate drift, or oldest-eligible deadline breach disables new affected-destination source admission and fails readiness while accepted settlement/detach/cleanup continue. Scheduler recurring/manual/remediation rotation occurs inside the dispatchable sublane of the single `scheduler-execution` window. It polls at least every 60 seconds independent of visitor traffic and Redis scheduling, so saturated event/payment/detach traffic cannot starve a newly eligible scheduler slot, cleanup, or quiet unrelated destination. Queue-prefix/command ACL covers those exact 16 non-public-specialized destinations; its database role sees only the dispatchable, visible-recovery, and detach metadata candidate views, cycle/window metadata, and exact enqueue-attempt-chain/terminal-removal-chain/Redis-state/ambiguous/three-cursor/two-level-mode CAS plus ID+generation-bounded detach-pending, lock-held terminal-key remove/status/absence/revalidation, and final detached+nullable-slot-release CAS, with no payload-wide read, claim, grant, effect, or terminal authority. Saturated continuous dispatchable+visible-recovery+detach on payment/event plus late scheduler/quiet-destination, a full 4,096-row one-destination Redis-loss backlog, exact rolling-ring admission at 31/32/33 live tokens, `acceptedAt=now-59.999s` versus `now-60.000s`, multi-row `K` all-or-none reservation with no boundary refund, 32-versus-64 arrival/service boundaries, 4,095 blocked/malformed rows before an unlocking row across wrap, oldest-deadline breach, manifest-digest drift, crash before/after slice claim, after an outbox effect before cursor CAS, at deadline, before final slice CAS, and at every row-cursor/ordinal/outer-mode/inner-mode flip, plus two-second timeout tests prove the measured drain and fairness bounds. |
| independent strict authority reconciler | New exact `node /app/packages/cli/bin/mercato customers public-chat-reconcile --daemon`; one replica; database advisory singleton and bounded cursors. It has four independently budgeted duties: (1) repairs/proves the one global pager row/Job Scheduler and public next identities, (2) keysets at most 40 population/scope registrations and verifies desired/lifecycle/cap invariants while advancing past blockers, (3) maintains ambiguous pager/scope bindings through ended-or-terminated plus exact absence proof, and (4) before scope work, runs the environment-owned global processable-release cursor for at most 25 independent short release units or five database-time seconds, whichever comes first, at least once per minute. A blocker advances only that lane's cursor/oldest state and cannot couple another job; each successful unit takes the full ordered locks, exact-decrements once, and commits independently. It never runs a scope sweep or directly enqueues a reply target. |
| public-chat retention daemon | Exact `mercato customers public-chat-retention-sweep --daemon --interval-seconds 60 --quota-batch-size 10000 --receipt-batch-size 1000 --terminal-batch-size 1000`; one replica/process identity; database singleton; five fixed quota/receipt/event-queue-terminal/schedule-tombstone/registry-history capabilities and their metadata cursors only; no systemd timer, in-app cron, or per-tick process/role. |

The controller has no public/data-plane network or raw Docker socket; only the helper may perform maintenance-fence- and manifest-bound image pull/verify, network/volume/secret setup, create/recreate/start/inspect/stop/kill/remove, and exact one-shot operations. |

Renewal desired state, last success/expiry margin, image, timer, locks, and post-topology continuity are readiness evidence. |

The controller is a digest-pinned, checksum-verified host artifact installed under a versioned read-only path and run as a dedicated system user with systemd hardening (`NoNewPrivileges`, strict filesystem/home/tmp/device/kernel protections, explicit writable paths and address families). Each controller generation receives only three fresh never-reused route-specific database credential files derived from NOLOGIN registrar/Noli-verifier/ack templates, controller/Noli verification keys, acknowledgment/runtime signing keys, and five distinct mode-`0660` Unix sockets for deployment/migration, runtime termination, Noli-artifact acceptance, acknowledgment signing, and durable Redis-client lineage/fencing; each socket has a different OS group/capability secret, peer-credential check, request schema/rate/size limit, and route allow-list. Compose bind-mounts the first four client sockets only into their exact approved migration/control/runtime clients. The fifth socket is mounted only into the exact manifested owners of the 49 Redis client slots. At runtime-start the controller creates a generated ordered set of fresh per-slot 128-bit opaque capabilities whose digests and exact `(environmentId,role,clientSlotId,clientKind,manifestOrdinal,runtimeId,runtimeGeneration)` mappings are bound into the start attestation/root store. Their raw bytes remain encrypted under the root-store key for exact same-peer/same-runtime replay until an authenticated delivery acknowledgment for that set is fsync-tombstoned; response loss or controller crash never regenerates or substitutes a capability, and no route other than that same attested runtime may retrieve them. Only bootstrap `get_capability_set` and `ack_capability_set` omit a slot capability: they require the exact Unix peer/cgroup, already claimed runtime-start attestation and its capability-manifest digest; get idempotently decrypts/returns the same ordered set, and ack exact-matches its set digest and fsync-tombstones delivery. Every later request carries one capability; the controller exact-matches it under that peer/runtime attestation, consumes/uses only its mapped slot, and never accepts a caller-chosen role, slot, kind, or ordinal. This distinguishes multiple producer/Worker command/Worker blocking slots owned by one process while preventing cross-process/role use; it accepts only bounded `get_capability_set | ack_capability_set | claim | register_identity | bind_command | reconcile_result | report_ambiguous | fence_status | close_clean` schemas, at most 16,384 command bind/reconcile operations and 512 lifecycle operations per environment-minute; `claim`, `register_identity`, `report_ambiguous`, `fence_status`, and `close_clean` each consume one lifecycle unit, exact idempotent response-loss retries consume none, capability-set get/ack use a separate 100-runtime/minute bootstrap bucket, and helper completion is internal rather than charged, and never accepts an outcome, Redis command/key/host, foreign subject, deployment, runtime-death, Noli, acknowledgment, or database mutation request. Bootstrap capability delivery grants no Redis/root operation; every Redis-client verb is rejected until the delivery acknowledgment is durable. Controller code derives the role/slot/runtime/claim and helper action from peer credentials, root store, and the protected database candidate view. `reconcile_result` accepts only the peer-derived current subject/command locator: the controller exact-reads the protected acknowledged database result, exact-matches the live root command binding, and fsyncs a **prepared, non-current** root transition that clears the command and retains its domain-separated result-resolution digest. It then invokes the fixed registrar fold, which atomically folds/clears the owning database tuple and advances the database tail anchor to that prepared-root digest; only after commit does the controller fsync the root commit marker. The caller cannot supply an outcome, result digest, chain value, or clear instruction. A crash before, between, or after those boundaries resumes idempotently by DB-old/prepared-discard or DB-new/prepared-commit, and neither store admits the next command until both show the prior command folded and clear. A full-fleet fixture spends 49 successor claims, 49 registrations, 49 ambiguity reports, 49 fence completions, and up to 49 closes (245 lifecycle units) inside one database-time minute without rate rejection, while a 513th non-idempotent lifecycle operation is rejected before root/Redis state. There is no generic controller socket sidecar; app/worker roles mount only this least-privilege fifth socket when their manifested client slot requires it. PostgreSQL exposes no TCP host port: its socket directory is bind-mounted to one root/controller-group host path, `pg_hba.conf` requires SCRAM for the three per-generation controller logins, and the controller's three one-connection clients reach only that local Unix socket; the fifth route reuses the registrar client through the three fixed bind/result-fold/fence capability functions and adds no database principal or connection. Other containers neither mount that socket nor those credentials.

The root Docker helper exposes a separate peer-authenticated socket. Deployment, mutation, and destructive lifecycle requests carry the active maintenance-fence ID, installed service/image-graph digest, exact service/one-shot ID, and operation nonce. `redis-readiness-v1`, `redis-client-register-v1`, `redis-client-fence-v1`, and `redis-client-unregistered-fence-v1` are the only ordinary-serving exceptions: they bind the current installed deployment/controller generation and manifest digest; client fencing additionally binds an active root-store client claim and exact database-registered command/connection tuple. They grant no deployment verb, while a `server_incarnation_retired` outcome still requires the separately authenticated maintenance/deployment retirement proof. It supports only fixed schema-validated verbs for allow-listed digest pull/load verification, declared network/volume/secret creation, manifest-exact container create/recreate/start/inspect/stop/kill/remove, and manifest-exact migration/certificate one-shots and the long-lived retention service lifecycle; all image, command, environment names, secret source/destination, mount source/destination/mode, network, capability, user, and resource values are derived from the installed manifest, never request text. Arbitrary exec/Compose flags, shell, host path, command/env/mount/network/image substitution, privilege changes, registry target, and Docker API proxying are impossible. One additional argument-free `redis-readiness-v1` verb launches the exact digest-pinned short-lived probe on the Redis network with a root-owned one-use admin credential, returns only a bounded helper-authenticated `RedisClientHelperObservationV1(kind='readiness')` body covering exact Redis version/run-ID, TLS/certificate/SAN/expiry, ACL/key-prefix fingerprints without secrets, persistence/AOF status, memory, exact maxclients/client count, and disk watermark. The controller independently verifies it and prepares `RedisReadinessVerificationV1`, but does not publish or consume readiness yet. The helper must first destroy its credential/container, commit the exact helper completion and credential tombstone, prove stable-run zero readiness-user/name inventory, and fold the readiness claim into its admin-lineage accumulator; only one deployment-readiness CAS binding both the verification digest and matching `readinessCompletionReceiptDigest` may then become ready; it consumes one readiness/emergency-generation slot inside the 20-client admin reserve. It cannot accept a Redis command, key, host, network, image, or output selector. A second fixed `redis-client-register-v1` verb is callable only by the controller for one live reserved claim. The controller supplies no caller-chosen Redis command. The request returns the once-issued raw challenge plus run/client hints; the controller first hashes the challenge and exact-matches the immutable claim digest, and the helper parses the canonical live SETNAME suffix rather than deriving an unavailable preimage. Using one fresh nonreconnecting TLS admin-probe socket, the helper reads one authoritative canonical server run ID and the complete client inventory through the same 128-record/768-byte-record/96-KiB fail-closed parser used by fencing; the observed run/client pair, never the hints, is authoritative. It requires exactly one record in the entire inventory with the claim's exact SETNAME challenge, expected ACL username, and generated role/slot mapping, requires that record's ID and the run ID exact-match both hints, rejects any second challenge/name match even with a different ID, then re-reads the same server run ID on that same probe socket before returning a bounded helper-authenticated observation to the controller. The controller independently validates it and signs `RedisClientIdentityVerificationV1`; a missing/wrong/duplicate ID, absent or reused challenge, cross-role/user/slot record, wrong run hint, disconnect, reroute, or run-ID change fails without registering the claim. On controller/helper crash or lost response, the root-retained encrypted unconsumed challenge, exact-hash-matched to the immutable digest, permits only an idempotent repeat for the same observed ID; successful consumption tombstones the challenge before reply so it can never authorize another connection. The controller consumes the challenge once, fsync-persists the verification digest and named registered-connection subrecord in the root claim, and only then may the database create a command `binding_pending` tuple. The raw challenge is never stored in application/database rows or accepted again. A third fixed `redis-client-fence-v1` verb is callable only by the controller for one of two root-store-registered forms sharing `{ environmentId, role, clientSlotId, clientKind, runtimeId, runtimeGeneration, startAttestationDigest, clientClaimId, clientClaimIdentityDigest, registeredIdentityVerificationDigest, registeredClientNameDigest, expectedAclUsername, registeredConnectionStateDigest, redisServerRunId, redisClientId, clientGeneration }`. The command form additionally exact-matches database `{ subjectKind, subjectId, bindingGenerationOrNull, registeredCommandStateDigest, controllerRootBindingAckDigest, controllerRootBoundAt, commandNonce, purpose: 'enqueue' | 'terminal_remove' | 'strict_direct_enqueue' | 'strict_scope_enqueue' | 'strict_pager_upsert' | 'strict_transport_remove', positive commandGeneration }`. The connection-only form is exactly `purpose='connection_capacity_fence'` with subject/binding/registered-command/nonce/command-generation fields null and is valid only for a retired-unproved non-effectful or command-free claim. Either form may carry an already-registered `serverRetirementProofDigest` only for changed incarnation; no caller supplies a command, key, host, or unregistered ID. The helper launches one digest-pinned short-lived failure probe with a root-owned one-use admin credential and uses exactly one nonreconnecting TLS socket for the complete proof. It first exact-reads the Redis server `run_id`. If it equals the registered run ID, the same socket issues only `CLIENT KILL ID <registeredId>` when present, reads the complete bounded client inventory, and proves both that exact ID is absent and that zero inventory record whose exact canonical-name bytes recompute to the retained `registeredClientNameDigest` for this claim also has the expected ACL username/slot mapping; a twin/reconnect with a new ID therefore blocks sufficiency. It then finally re-reads the same `run_id` on that socket. `maxclients` is exactly 128; inventory parsing is capped at 128 records, 768 bytes per record, and 96 KiB total, and overflow, duplicate/unknown mandatory fields, truncation, disconnect, reroute, or a changed final run ID returns only `run_id_changed_unproved` and signs no sufficient absence. If the initial run ID differs, it issues no kill: run-ID change alone is never retirement proof. Before either changed-incarnation outcome, it always re-reads `run_id` on the same nonreconnecting socket. `server_incarnation_retired` requires initial and final IDs equal to the same current run distinct from the registered old run, plus a controller/root-retained signed proof exact-binding that old run and the single manifested Redis container identity to its stop/kill/remove/absence generation and a deployment fence that forbids reattach or failback. Missing proof or any initial/final mismatch returns only `run_id_changed_unproved`; the affected command or connection claim stays barred. It destroys credential/container and returns a bounded helper-authenticated observation. The controller independently schema/bounds/nonce/authentication-verifies that observation against the root and protected database candidate. Only for `killed_then_absent | already_absent | server_incarnation_retired` does it sign `RedisClientFenceReceiptV1`, which binds the entire registered tuple including the immutable `registeredIdentityVerificationDigest`, registered-connection-state digest and, for command form, registered-command-state digest, optional retirement-proof digest, both initial/final observed run IDs, database time, probe image, and inventory/retirement digest. For `run_id_changed_unproved` it signs no controller receipt and may only tail-anchor the helper-observation digest as bounded non-authoritative attempt telemetry. A fourth fixed `redis-client-unregistered-fence-v1` verb accepts only a controller-derived `delivered_unknown` reserved claim after exact runtime termination, container/cgroup absence, slot-capability revocation, and host egress-fence proof. It accepts no caller run/client hint or command. The controller supplies the root-decrypted claim challenge to the one-use helper, which derives the exact SETNAME and performs the stable-run, full-inventory, twin rejection, optional exact-ID kill, repeated-inventory, and final-run protocol defined by `RedisClientUnregisteredFenceReceiptV1`; changed incarnation requires the exact proof for the claim's expected run. Missing prerequisites or uncertainty returns only a typed insufficient observation and leaves the slot consumed. Helper Redis credentials come from a fixed installed pool, never dynamic ACL-user creation: exactly 16 disabled usernames `noli-spec065-helper-01` through `noli-spec065-helper-16` map one-to-one to gate permits, with fixed additional users `noli-spec065-readiness`, `noli-spec065-broker`, and `noli-spec065-emergency`. The broker itself uses a named nonreconnecting root-controller two-generation state with exact registered run/client IDs: one active broker and at most one ambiguous replacement consume two reserved admin slots, while one active readiness/emergency probe and at most one ambiguous replacement consume two more. This state is an exact `global_anchor` helper-control subrecord—not a 50th application lineage—and is included in the helper/global/checkpoint digests. A replacement broker may kill/prove absence of the old exact ID. If its own response becomes ambiguous, an independently usable `noli-spec065-emergency` credential is already enabled and AEAD-sealed only in the root/recovery store, never mounted into any ordinary helper or data container; its digest/generation and allowed `INFO SERVER`, bounded `CLIENT LIST`, exact-ID `CLIENT KILL`, and fixed-pool `ACL SETUSER` surface are fingerprinted. A digest-pinned emergency probe uses that credential to fence both broker IDs and re-establish the broker, then proves its own exact ID absent. Its exact run/client ID is root-registered before any admin command; one ambiguous emergency socket permits exactly one replacement, and two ambiguous emergency generations bar a third until a maintenance-fenced Redis retirement/restart proves the old incarnation absent. Emergency-secret rotation is maintenance-fenced, tail-anchored, overlaps old/new only until zero old emergency clients, and is restore-tested before revocation. No third broker or emergency socket is legal. Before assigning a permit, the broker idempotently `CLIENT KILL USER`s that pool user, verifies zero such clients, applies the generated least-privilege ACL with one fresh 256-bit password, and enables it only after the credential-generation/root-tail transition commits. Completion first fsyncs the helper record, erases the probe's local secret, then the broker kills every connection for that exact pool user, applies `off resetpass` and the deny ACL, verifies zero matching inventory, and only then tail-anchors credential tombstone and releases the permit. Controller/broker crash recovery replays kill/disable/zero-inventory for every assigned or uncertain pool member before reuse; a lost broker response coalesces to the same credential generation, never re-enables the old password, and an unavailable broker leaves the permit occupied. The generated ACL fingerprint requires exactly these 19 admin identities: 16 disabled-or-currently-assigned helper users, one disabled-or-currently-assigned readiness user, the broker user, and the always-preprovisioned root-only emergency user. Their credential generations/digests and enabled/disabled matrices exact-match root state, so no crash can accumulate users or reusable secrets. Registration and fence probes share one persisted per-environment 16-permit helper gate, while four of the 20 admin/health/failure reserve slots remain unavailable to that gate for active+replacement broker state and active+replacement readiness/emergency state. At most 98 legitimate claim-bound requests may wait. A lineage may have at most two pending-or-active requests only when they target its two distinct slot-consuming claim IDs; each claim admits one exact verb/command-generation/request-nonce request, an exact retry coalesces to it, and a conflicting request is rejected. The selector orders old-claim fence deadlines before replacement registration, then all requests by earliest database deadline and FIFO/claim ID, creates the 15-second database challenge only when a permit becomes active, gives every probe a hard two-second end-to-end bound, and never grants more than 16 concurrent probes. Therefore even 49 old-claim fences plus 49 replacement registrations start within 12 seconds and finish within 14, without serial per-lineage waves; the at-most-one-second root checkpoint barrier keeps the complete healthy bound at 15 seconds, while 49 simultaneous replacement registrations finish within eight seconds and readiness retains a separate slot. Before replying, each helper fsyncs one bounded root-only completion record keyed by request nonce and containing its authenticated observation or typed no-observation end. A lost response/status retry returns that exact record. If none exists, the controller may release the permit only after the helper credential/container/TLS client are all exact-proved absent, appending a typed failed-attempt digest; controller death is not required. Completion consumption tombstones into the fixed gate replay accumulator, and crash never authorizes overlap or duplicate execution. The full worst case is `98 data + 16 register/fence + 2 broker + 2 readiness/emergency = 118 < maxclients=128`. These probes grant no additional data-plane authority or access to inventory/kill/raw INFO beyond the separately fingerprinted identity preflight granted to the exact manifested owners of all 49 client slots; only effectful producer roles receive command-binding authority. Registration/unregistered-recovery fixtures crash before challenge delivery, after the pre-response `delivered_unknown` commit, after partial/lost response, after connect/SETNAME and before hints, and before/after runtime/egress fence, then exercise correct same-socket challenge consumption plus wrong reported run, wrong live ID, absent ID, duplicate/reused/lost-response challenge, simultaneous twin-name sockets, cross-role/ACL-user/slot ID, controller/helper crash, 49 simultaneous replacements under the shared helper gate, disconnect, and run-ID rotation at every lookup boundary. Fence fixtures rotate/restart/reroute before initial run read, between run read and kill, during inventory, and before final run re-read; only one-socket same-incarnation proof succeeds. Normal-serving ambiguity with no maintenance fence, substitution, cross-role/subject/purpose/generation reuse, run-ID change without exact old-container retirement, partition/replacement/failback, client-ID reuse across server restart, same-name/user twin or reconnect during fencing, strict direct/scope/pager delayed-command delivery, connection-only worker/client recovery, inventory count/record/byte overflow, extra-command/key exfiltration, malformed output, lost cleanup, and probe overlap, broker crash before/after enable/kill/disable, stale helper password reuse, all 16 occupied permits, readiness, broker ambiguity, and first-emergency response loss during full occupancy, and any twentieth admin username tests fail closed. The controller itself never mounts `/var/run/docker.sock`.

`RedisClientHelperObservationV1` is exact JCS, at most 8 KiB encoded, and has common unsigned `{ schema="noli.redis-client-helper-observation", version=1, kind, environmentId, controllerGeneration, manifestDigest, helperBuildDigest, probeImageDigest, requestNonce, databaseChallengeIssuedAt, observedAt, body, authenticationKeyId }` plus `authentication`. `kind` is exactly `readiness | identity | fence | unregistered_fence | admin_run_bind | admin_identity | admin_recovery`. The controller creates a one-use 256-bit helper key and 128-bit nonce under the persisted helper-gate request; the helper computes `preimage=UTF8("noli:redis-client-helper-observation:v1") || 0x00 || UTF8(RFC8785_JCS(unsigned))`, then `inner=SHA256(preimage)` as the raw 32 bytes and `authentication=base64url_no_padding(HMAC_SHA256(helperKeyBytes,inner))`; it never HMACs hex/base64 text and destroys the key after returning the observation. The controller independently verifies key/nonce, exact helper image/build, JCS/bounds, no duplicate/unknown keys, and a 15-second database-time challenge window before accepting the body; the helper observation is never itself database authority. Readiness body is exact `{ redisVersion, redisImageDigest, redisContainerGenerationDecimal, redisContainerName, redisContainerPlanDigest, redisContainerId, redisContainerCreationAttestationDigest, initialObservedRunId, finalObservedRunId, tlsProtocol, tlsCipher, certificateChainDigest, sanSetDigest, certificateNotAfter, aclFingerprintDigest, keyPrefixFingerprintDigest, appendOnly, appendFsyncMode, persistenceStatus, maxmemoryBytesDecimal, usedMemoryBytesDecimal, maxclientsDecimal="128", connectedClientsDecimal, diskFreeBytesDecimal, diskWatermarkStatus }`; both run IDs must match on its one probe socket; the root helper exact-verifies that the five nonnull container fields byte-equal the sole current `running` lifecycle projection and that the signed container-creation attestation exact-binds the current Docker ID/image/name/plan before inserting those values; all quantities are bounded canonical decimal strings, and no secret, raw ACL rule, or client inventory appears. Identity body is exact `{ claimId, claimIdentityDigest, connectionChallengeDigest, clientNameDigest, expectedAclUsername, role, clientSlotId, clientKind, runtimeId, runtimeGenerationDecimal, clientGenerationDecimal, observedRedisServerRunId, observedRedisClientId, firstObservedRunId, finalObservedRunId }`, with `observedRedisServerRunId = firstObservedRunId = finalObservedRunId`, challenge/name/user/slot already verified, and the later root/registered-connection `redisServerRunId` required to equal that same value. Fence body is exact `{ claimId, claimIdentityDigest, registeredIdentityVerificationDigest, registeredClientNameDigest, expectedAclUsername, registeredConnectionStateDigest, registeredCommandStateDigestOrNull, subjectKindOrNull, subjectIdOrNull, bindingGenerationOrNull, commandNonceOrNull, purpose, commandGenerationDecimalOrNull, registeredRedisServerRunId, registeredRedisClientId, clientGenerationDecimal, initialObservedRunId, finalObservedRunId, inventoryDigestOrNull, serverRetirementProofDigestOrNull, outcome }`; command and connection-only null rules are those above, Unregistered-fence body is exact `{ claimId, claimIdentityDigest, connectionChallengeDigest, clientNameDigest, expectedAclUsername, role, clientSlotId, clientKind, runtimeId, runtimeGenerationDecimal, clientGenerationDecimal, expectedRedisServerRunId, observedRedisClientIdOrNull, initialObservedRunId, finalObservedRunId, inventoryDigestOrNull, serverRetirementProofDigestOrNull, runtimeTerminationReceiptDigest, slotCapabilityRevocationDigest, egressFenceDigest, outcome }`. `unregistered_killed_then_absent` requires initial=final=expected run, one observed ID, nonnull final-inventory digest and null retirement proof; `unregistered_already_absent` requires the same except observed ID null; `unregistered_server_incarnation_retired` requires stable initial=final distinct from expected, observed ID/inventory null, and the exact expected-run retirement proof; every other branch is `unregistered_unproved`, sets both authority evidence digests null, and cannot close the claim. Admin-run-bind body is exact `{claimId,claimIdentityDigest,credentialGenerationDecimal,credentialDeliveryState:'delivered_unknown',runBindingMode:'bootstrap_unbound',redisContainerGenerationDecimal,redisContainerCreationAttestationDigest,expectedAclUsername,canonicalClientNameDigest,observedRedisClientId,initialObservedRunId,finalObservedRunId,helperProcessIdentityDigest,outcome}`; both container fields exact-match the claim and sole current running lifecycle state. `run_bound` requires equal canonical run IDs and the exact same-socket SETNAME/CLIENT-ID observation after only authentication, exact SETNAME, `INFO SERVER`, and `CLIENT ID`; `run_bind_unproved` carries no authority and requires process/container plus credential cleanup. The controller tail-anchors the former digest before any LIST/KILL/ACL command. Admin-identity body is exact `{claimKind,claimId,claimIdentityDigest,currentAdminClaimStateDigest,credentialGenerationDecimal,credentialDeliveryState:'delivered_unknown',runBindingMode,runAttestationDigestOrNull,redisContainerGenerationDecimal,redisContainerCreationAttestationDigest,runBindObservationDigestOrNull,runBindResumeAuthorizationDigestOrNull,expectedRedisServerRunId,expectedAclUsername,registeredClientNameDigest,currentAclFingerprintDigest,observedRedisClientId,initialObservedRunId,finalObservedRunId,inventoryDigest,helperProcessIdentityDigest,outcome}`. `admin_identity_registered` requires initial=final=expected run, exact prior claim-state/name/user/credential/profile, and one nonreconnecting socket that performed authentication, SETNAME, `INFO SERVER`, `CLIENT ID`, read-only `ACL GETUSER`, and one complete bounded `CLIENT LIST`; the inventory contains exactly one record matching that observed ID+canonical name+user and no name/user twin.
