`RedisReadinessVerificationV1`, `RedisClientIdentityVerificationV1`, `RedisClientFenceReceiptV1`, and `RedisClientUnregisteredFenceReceiptV1` are separate controller-signed JCS envelopes with exact common unsigned `{ schema, version=1, issuer="noli-host-controller", audience, environmentId, controllerGeneration, manifestDigest, keyId, receiptNonce, databaseIssuedAt, databaseExpiresAt, helperObservationDigest, body }` plus base64url-no-padding 64-byte Ed25519 `signature`. The controller Ed25519-signs the exact RFC 8785 JCS bytes of `unsigned` directly, with `schema`, `audience`, `issuer`, and `version` providing domain separation; readiness uses schema/audience `noli.redis-readiness-verification`/`noli.crm.redis-readiness-commit-v1`, copies the exact readiness body, is at most 8 KiB, expires after 30 database-time seconds, and is single-consume by deployment/controller generation; identity uses schema/audience `noli.redis-client-identity-verification`/`noli.crm.redis-client-register-v1`, copies the exact identity body, is at most 4 KiB, expires after 30 database-time seconds, and is single-consume by claim ID/challenge digest. Fence uses `noli.redis-client-fence-receipt`/`noli.crm.redis-client-fence-commit-v1`, copies the exact fence body plus `controllerRootBindingAckDigestOrNull`, `controllerRootBoundAtOrNull`, `databaseTupleDigestOrNull`, `probeEvidenceDigestOrNull`, and is at most 8 KiB; for `killed_then_absent | already_absent`, inventory digest and `probeEvidenceDigest` are both nonnull/equal while retirement proof is null and registered/initial/final run IDs are equal; for `server_incarnation_retired`, retirement-proof digest and `probeEvidenceDigest` are nonnull/equal while inventory digest is null; `run_id_changed_unproved` never produces this signed envelope: the controller retains only the authenticated helper-observation digest in bounded root telemetry, leaves `fenceReceiptDigest` and every database fence field null, and may later sign only a fresh sufficient attempt; it expires after 60 database-time seconds for initial controller commitment, after which the committed digest/chain remains durable. Command form requires all three added database-binding fields nonnull; connection-only requires them null. `RedisClientUnregisteredFenceReceiptV1` uses schema/audience `noli.redis-client-unregistered-fence-receipt`/`noli.crm.redis-client-unregistered-fence-commit-v1`, copies the exact unregistered-fence body, is at most 8 KiB, expires after 60 database-time seconds for its one lineage transition, and is signed only for the three sufficient unregistered outcomes. The controller exact-matches root-retained delivery state/challenge, runtime termination, capability revocation, host egress fence, expected run, helper evidence, and no database command/registered-identity tuple before signing; it never upgrades `unregistered_unproved`. Issuer, audience, current nonrevoked key, nonce, freshness, helper-observation digest, claim/manifest/controller generation, all tuple fields, signature preimage, and sufficient-outcome/null rules are exact-matched before any root or registrar CAS. Wrong key/audience/issuer/nonce/time/schema/version, alternate JSON/number/time encoding, duplicate/unknown field, oversized body, stale/current-command replay, helper/controller signature substitution, and readiness/identity/registered-fence/unregistered-fence cross-kind substitution fixtures fail; cross-language golden vectors cover unsigned JCS, helper-HMAC domain preimages/digests and controller unsigned-envelope JCS/signatures.

`RedisServerIncarnationRetirementProofV1` is the only old-incarnation authority. It is a controller-signed RFC8785-JCS envelope, at most 8 KiB, with exact unsigned `{ schema='noli.redis-server-incarnation-retirement-proof', version=1, issuer='noli-host-controller', audience='noli.crm.redis-server-retirement-v1', environmentId, controllerGeneration, manifestDigest, keyId, receiptNonce, databaseIssuedAt, databaseExpiresAt, body }` plus 64-byte base64url Ed25519 signature over the exact unsigned JCS. Body is closed `{ redisServiceId, oldRedisServerRunId, oldContainerGenerationDecimal, oldContainerName, oldContainerPlanDigest, oldContainerId, oldContainerCreationAttestationDigest, oldContainerStartIntentDigest, oldContainerStartAttestationDigest, oldBootstrapReadinessState, hostBootId, redisImageDigest, volumeIdentityDigest, networkIdentityDigest, maintenanceFenceId, retirementGenerationDecimal, nonReattachGenerationDecimal, terminalAction, stopRequestedAt, stoppedAtOrNull, killedAtOrNull, removedAt, containerAbsentAt, replacementContainerIdOrNull, replacementRedisServerRunIdOrNull }`; all old-container fields byte-equal the retired lifecycle projection, and every referencing claim's immutable container generation/creation-attestation digest must byte-equal this proof before it can acquire or consume a reference; `terminalAction` is exactly `stopped_removed_absent | killed_removed_absent` with matching time null rules, and every identity exact-matches the installed manifest/controller observation. Creation requires the continuously held maintenance fence, stop-or-kill, remove, complete old-container absence, and an incremented non-reattach generation that the controller root store and deployment state make irreversible before signing. `redisServerIncarnationRetirementProofDigest=D('noli:redis-server-incarnation-retirement-proof-digest:v1',completeSignedEnvelope)` is root-persisted by old run/container/retirement generation before reply and is the exact fence evidence; expiry is at most five database-time minutes for first use, while a consumed digest remains durable. Unknown key/audience/host boot/container/image/volume/network/fence, partial lifecycle, failback/reattach, stale generation, alternate replacement, response loss, controller crash, signature replay, and old-run proof applied to another client all fail closed.

`RuntimeRedisEgressFenceProofV1` is a controller root-store record created only after a claimed runtime termination. Its exact body is `{environmentId,runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,startAttestationDigest,containerId,cgroupIdentity,networkNamespaceIdentity,sourceAddressOrNull,firewallRuleGenerationDecimal,firewallRuleFingerprint,controllerGenerationDecimal,maintenanceFenceId,nonReopenGenerationDecimal,installedAt,verifiedAt}` and `runtimeRedisEgressFenceDigest=D('noli:runtime-redis-egress-fence:v1',body)`. Creation requires container/process/cgroup absence, monotonic non-reopen generation, an installed host rule denying that exact cgroup/network/source identity, a second independent inventory proving the rule fingerprint/effective order, and controller state forbidding identity reuse or recreation under the old runtime generation. Missing/stale rule, identity reuse, rule reorder, reboot loss, firewall-backend drift, source-address reuse, or controller restart blocks the proof and readiness.

Per-runtime state is exact `{runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,currentProofDigestOrNull,supersessionAccumulatorSequenceDecimal,supersessionAccumulatorCountDecimal,supersessionAccumulatorRootDigest}` with count=sequence and at most one current raw proof. `runtimeRedisEgressFenceAccumulatorGenesis=D('noli:runtime-redis-egress-fence-accumulator-genesis:v1',{environmentId,runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal})`. Each inner step is discriminated: replacement is `D('noli:runtime-redis-egress-fence-accumulator:v1',{kind:'replace',priorRootOrGenesis,supersessionSequenceDecimal,supersededProofDigest,replacementProofDigest})`; terminal removal is `D('noli:runtime-redis-egress-fence-accumulator:v1',{kind:'terminal_remove',priorRootOrGenesis,supersessionSequenceDecimal,currentProofDigest,runtimeZeroReferenceProofDigest})`. `runtimeEgressFenceZeroReferenceProofDigest=D('noli:runtime-redis-egress-fence-zero-reference:v1',{runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,liveClaimCandidateSetDigest,pendingCallCandidateSetDigest,capabilityDeliveryTerminalStateDigest,runtimeTerminationReceiptDigest,provedAt})` requires both candidate sets to hash literal empty arrays and the capability state terminal. Replacing a rebooted/drifted rule exact-CASes/folds the old current proof and installs exactly one new proof; final removal folds the last proof and deletes its raw bytes only in the terminal-removal CAS.

The outer bounded state is `redisClientRuntimeEgressFenceStateDigest=D('noli:runtime-redis-egress-fence-state:v1',{liveEntries,compactionAccumulatorSequenceDecimal,compactionAccumulatorCountDecimal,compactionAccumulatorRootDigest})`, where at most 2,048 entries sort by `(runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal)` and are exact `{runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,perRuntimeStateDigest}`. Its genesis is `redisClientRuntimeEgressFenceStateAccumulatorGenesis=D('noli:runtime-redis-egress-fence-state-accumulator-genesis:v1',{environmentId,contract:'spec-065-v1'})`; after inner terminal removal, `D('noli:runtime-redis-egress-fence-state-accumulator:v1',{priorRootOrGenesis,compactionSequenceDecimal,runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,finalPerRuntimeStateDigest,runtimeZeroReferenceProofDigest})` atomically folds and deletes that live entry. Runtime admission pauses at the cap. This outer digest is mirrored in the control row and included directly in global state and the checkpoint; no historical per-runtime object survives outside the fixed accumulator.

`RedisClientGenerationClaimV1` is a canonical fsync-safe controller root-store record, not an in-memory counter. Every one of the 49 manifested steady client **slots**—producer/control, worker command, and worker blocking—has a deterministic `(environmentId,role,clientSlotId)` lineage. Those 49 role/slot/kind/manifest-ordinal keys are immutable for `spec-065-v1`; a future topology may disable a slot but cannot delete, rename, renumber, or reuse its lineage. Any reviewed contract migration carries every retired high-water/terminal accumulator into an ever-seen-lineage tombstone before adding a new key; remove/reintroduce and rename-back fixtures prove deterministic claim IDs cannot be reused. The claim ID is UUIDv5 under RFC URL namespace `6ba7b811-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8` with exact UTF-8 name `noli:redis-client-generation:v1:<environmentId>:<role>:<clientSlotId>:<generationDecimal>`; it plus immutable `claimIdentityDigest` bind JCS exact `{ contract, environmentId, role, clientSlotId, clientKind, clientGenerationDecimal, predecessorGenerationOrNull, runtimeId, runtimeGenerationDecimal, startAttestationDigest, connectionChallengeDigest, expectedRedisServerRunId, issuedAt }`. `expectedRedisServerRunId` is the exact 40-hex run ID from the current committed readiness verification at allocation; registration must observe that incarnation or fail. The controller creates one 128-bit random base64url-no-padding connection challenge per claim and stores its digest in the immutable identity plus an AEAD-sealed raw value/nonce as `connectionChallengeCiphertextOrNull` in the mode-0700 root state. A new claim begins `challengeDeliveryState='undelivered'`. Before writing any response byte, the controller must tail-anchor a distinct `undelivered -> delivered_unknown` lineage transition; only then may it return the raw challenge, and an exact same-peer retry decrypts/returns that same value without another state change. Thus `undelivered` proves no response byte was attempted, while every sent, partially sent, response-lost, or crash-ambiguous claim is pessimistically `delivered_unknown`. The ciphertext is bound to claim ID/identity digest/runtime/slot as associated data; successful identity registration changes delivery state to `consumed` and tombstones it atomically, and no replacement challenge is legal for that generation. Mutable canonical state is the envelope `{ body, currentStateDigest }`, where `body` is exact `{ state, challengeDeliveryState, registeredAtOrNull, retiredAtOrNull, fencedAtOrNull, redisServerRunIdOrNull, redisClientIdOrNull, connectionChallengeCiphertextOrNull, registeredIdentityVerificationDigestOrNull, registeredClientNameDigestOrNull, expectedAclUsernameOrNull, registeredConnectionStateDigestOrNull, currentCommandTupleDigestOrNull, currentRegisteredCommandStateDigestOrNull, currentControllerRootBindingAckDigestOrNull, currentControllerRootBoundAtOrNull, lastCommandResolutionDigestOrNull, databaseHandoffCountDecimal, databaseHandoffAccumulatorDigest, terminalDatabaseHandoffLeafDigestOrNull, fenceAttemptGenerationDecimal, fenceAttemptProofChainDigest, lastFenceAttemptOutcomeOrNull, lastFenceAttemptArtifactDigestOrNull, fenceReceiptDigestOrNull, priorStateDigest }`. `currentStateDigest = SHA256(UTF8("noli:redis-client-claim-state:v1\\0") || UTF8(JCS(body)))`; `currentStateDigest` is excluded from `body` and therefore never hashes itself. Genesis uses the generated domain-separated prior digest. `databaseHandoffCountDecimal=0` requires `databaseHandoffAccumulatorDigest=redisClientClaimHandoffGenesis` and `terminalDatabaseHandoffLeafDigestOrNull=null`; a positive count requires the exact accumulator step for every ordinal and a nonnull terminal leaf only after the zero-reference handoff. Every later CAS compare-matches the prior envelope's `currentStateDigest`, stores that value as the proposed body's `priorStateDigest`, hashes the proposed body exactly once, and never rewrites the identity digest. Fence-attempt generation starts at zero with the generated genesis chain; each helper attempt increment-one uses the exact `fenceAttemptSubjectDigest`, artifact kind/digest, and outcome defined below; registered and unregistered attempts cannot collide. `run_id_changed_unproved` may update only this root telemetry and cannot set `fenceReceiptDigest` or any database controller-fence field; a later sufficient attempt advances the chain again and may set the terminal receipt. Wrong/stale generation, chain, or late result cannot overwrite a newer attempt; kind is the manifested `producer_effectful | producer_control | worker_command | worker_blocking`, `challengeDeliveryState` is exactly `undelivered | delivered_unknown | consumed`, state is exactly `reserved | registered_current | retired_unproved | fenced | closed_clean`, generations are positive/never reused, and only `fenced|closed_clean` stop consuming a slot. `closed_clean` without a connection receipt is legal only from `reserved+undelivered`; every `delivered_unknown` claim requires the unregistered recovery fence below, and every registered claim requires a controller/helper connection-only proof of same-run exact client-ID/name absence or proved old-incarnation retirement after every command binding is clear. QUIT/local close/process exit alone can only produce `retired_unproved`. One CAS per lineage advances a permanent high-water and permits at most two slot-consuming claims, at most one `reserved|registered_current`, and no successor except the prior generation. When both slots are empty, allocation generation is exactly `highWater+1` and `predecessorGenerationOrNull` is null only for generation one, otherwise the prior high-water even though that historical claim is compacted. When a retired-unproved slot 1 remains and slot 2 is empty, replacement generation is exactly `highWater+1` and its predecessor is exactly slot 1's claim generation—including after a later-generation former slot 2 was compacted—rather than blindly naming `highWater`; this is the only live-predecessor exception. Exact retry must match generation and predecessor byte-for-byte, and neither coordinate is caller-selected. Thus a first one-way-loss may create one replacement, a failed replacement bars a third connection even across process restart, and the 49-old+49-replacement bound covers non-effectful Worker clients as well as producers. Every client reserves a claim before connect, sets exact `CLIENT SETNAME noli-spec065-v1:<claimId>:<rawChallenge>` on that same fresh socket before `INFO SERVER`/`CLIENT ID`, then submits only the reported ID/run ID to the transport-fence controller route; both must equal the claim's expected incarnation and helper observation. The controller's fixed registration helper must inventory that exact live ID and verify its one-use challenge, expected ACL username, and generated role/slot mapping; only its signed `RedisClientIdentityVerificationV1` can consume the challenge and register the claim. Redis server run ID is exactly Redis's 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters (`^[0-9a-f]{40}$`) with no prefix, case folding, truncation, or whitespace. TypeScript/helper/controller compare the string byte-for-byte; every owning PostgreSQL `redis_server_run_id` field is `varchar(40)` with generated `octet_length(value)=40 AND value COLLATE "C" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{40}$'`, and every claim, helper body, signed receipt, retirement proof, snapshot, migration, and fingerprint shares it. Golden negatives cover 39/41 characters, uppercase, nonhex, prefix, 39-hex-plus-space, 40-hex-plus-space, explicit casts, truncation, ORM round-trip, and equality/index behavior. Redis client ID is canonical positive unsigned-decimal text in the inclusive range `1..18446744073709551615`, with no sign, whitespace, exponent, fraction, or leading zero; TypeScript parses/compares it only as `bigint`, never `number`, and JCS carries it as a string. Every owning PostgreSQL field is `varchar(20)`, never `bigint`, with generated check `value ~ '^[1-9][0-9]{0,19}$' AND value::numeric <= 18446744073709551615`; every direct/strict/outbox tuple, snapshot, and fingerprint exact-matches that physical/wire contract. Golden vectors cover `9007199254740991`, `9007199254740992`, and `18446744073709551615` plus overflow/noncanonical rejection. The controller computes the named subrecord `registeredConnectionStateDigest = SHA256(UTF8("noli:redis-client-connection-state:v1\\0") || UTF8(JCS({ claimId, claimIdentityDigest, registeredIdentityVerificationDigest, registeredClientNameDigest, expectedAclUsername, environmentId, role, clientSlotId, clientKind, runtimeId, runtimeGenerationDecimal, startAttestationDigest, clientGenerationDecimal, redisServerRunId, redisClientId, registeredAt })))` and stores it in the root state; the subrecord never contains its own digest and is immutable for that connection. For a command it likewise computes `registeredCommandStateDigest = SHA256(UTF8("noli:redis-client-command-state:v1\\0") || UTF8(JCS({ claimId, claimIdentityDigest, registeredConnectionStateDigest, subjectKind, subjectId, bindingGenerationOrNull, commandNonce, purpose, commandGenerationDecimal, bindingChallengeNonce, bindingChallengeAt })))`; this named command snapshot never contains its own digest or a not-yet-created database time and is immutable for that command even though later claim-state-chain digests change. The initial database `binding_pending` CAS itself creates immutable 128-bit `bindingChallengeNonce` and database `bindingChallengeAt`; these are part of the pending base and are never caller supplied. The controller computes `controllerRootBindingAckDigest = SHA256(UTF8("noli:redis-client-root-binding-ack:v1\\0") || UTF8(JCS({ claimId, registeredCommandStateDigest, currentCommandTupleDigest, databaseTupleDigest, bindingChallengeNonce, bindingChallengeAt })))`, with `controllerRootBoundAt=bindingChallengeAt`. It can therefore write/fsync the complete final root transition as **prepared but not current** before calling the registrar bind CAS. Every exact JSON key, lowercase UUID/hex representation, signed-decimal/time wire form, and null rule is generated and cross-language golden-tested. A client is forbidden to reconnect outside its lineage. For an effectful slot, a healthy client may execute sequential commands but root store binds at most one current command. The runtime's first guarded database CAS creates only `binding_pending` with the complete base tuple including claim ID, claim-identity digest, registered-identity-verification digest, registered-connection-state digest, subject/binding, run/client identity, nonce, purpose, generation, and the database-generated binding challenge/time; all registered-command, controller-binding, result, and fence fields are null. The controller exact-reads that row, computes the command/ack subrecords above, and fsyncs a prepared root envelope containing `currentCommandTupleDigest`, `currentRegisteredCommandStateDigest`, `currentControllerRootBindingAckDigest`, and `currentControllerRootBoundAt`. The registrar-only bind function then atomically CASes the owning row to `registered` with those exact values **and** advances the database tail anchor to that prepared-root digest; only afterward does the controller fsync its commit marker and reply. The prepared envelope is not current/send authority before the database CAS, and registered database state is not send authority before the matching root commit marker. DB-old/root-prepared discards; DB-new/root-prepared completes the marker without recomputing time or digest. The helper receipt and database fold bind the immutable claim-identity digest, identity-verification digest, registered-connection-state digest, and that command's historical registered-command-state digest, never a later mutable claim-state digest. Worker command/blocking slots require `currentCommandTupleDigest`/`currentRegisteredCommandStateDigest`/`currentControllerRootBindingAckDigest`/`currentControllerRootBoundAt` null and use a connection-only fence over claim identity, identity-verification digest, registered client-name digest, expected ACL username, and registered-connection state/run/client/role/runtime/slot/generation, with no subject or command fields, solely for connection-capacity safety. Normal database result reconciliation occurs only through the fifth-socket `reconcile_result` route: the controller exact-reads the protected acknowledged result, exact-matches both stores, and fsyncs a prepared root transition that clears `currentCommandTupleDigest`, `currentRegisteredCommandStateDigest`, `currentControllerRootBindingAckDigest`, and `currentControllerRootBoundAt` while writing the domain-separated `lastCommandResolutionDigest`. The registrar-only fold then atomically folds/clears the owning database tuple and advances the database tail to that prepared-root digest; only afterward does the controller fsync the root commit marker. A crash at either boundary is idempotently resumed; the process-wide gate admits no next command until both root and database current-command shapes are clear. After a normal result, command history remains only in the immutable owner handoff chain/last leaf, the claim handoff accumulator, `lastCommandResolutionDigest`, and prior claim-state chain; all four active command/binding fields are null, so a later connection-only close/fence is well typed. Only an unresolved exact command retains all four active command/binding fields across retire/fence transitions. Connection loss, graceful drain without server-side absence, or ambiguity CASes the claim retired-unproved before a successor. Command-form sufficient fencing is deliberately two separately tail-anchored phases so the owning row's controller commitment is observable and crash-recoverable. First, `controllerFenceVerifiedAt` is the receipt's already signed `databaseIssuedAt`—never the later PostgreSQL commit instant—and the controller computes the fence tuple, fsyncs a prepared root transition that retains the complete current command while adding its fence commitment, calls `public_chat_redis_client_commit_fence_v1` to atomically CAS the four all-or-none controller-fence fields plus control tail and one lineage row, then fsyncs that root commit marker. Second, it computes the command-resolution/folded-database-chain digests from that immutable commitment, fsyncs a distinct prepared root transition that clears the current command/fence fields and writes `lastCommandResolutionDigest`, and calls the fixed fence branch of `public_chat_redis_client_fold_result_v1` to atomically fold the database chain, clear the entire current tuple, and advance the next control-tail/lineage state before fsyncing the second root marker. Neither phase authorizes another send or client generation; DB-old/root-prepared discards and DB-new/root-prepared completes the matching marker, including a crash after fence commitment but before fold. Connection-only fencing has no owning command row or persisted command-fence phase and uses one prepared `lineage_anchor` transition to terminal state. An unproved attempt advances only prepared-root telemetry plus standalone tail and leaves the claim retired/uncommitted. A crash after claim/before socket, identity read/before registration, database binding-pending/before root binding, database bind/before root commit marker, acknowledged result/before root result reconciliation, root result reconciliation/before database fold, sufficient receipt/before fence preparation, root fence preparation/before database commitment, database fence commitment/before its root marker, or committed fence/before the distinct fold transition never frees/resets the slot: recovery exact-reconciles both stores and either completes the next CAS or leaves it barred. An unregistered socket is never effect-authorized, but it cannot strand a lineage. A `delivered_unknown` reserved claim may enter `unregistered_recovery` only after the controller has tail-anchored that slot's monotonic capability-revocation digest, obtained the exact runtime-termination receipt, removed the container/cgroup, installed and fingerprinted an egress-deny fence for its network identity, and thereby proved no delayed process can open a new socket. The controller decrypts the retained challenge only into the one-use helper request; no runtime hint is accepted. On one nonreconnecting helper socket, the helper reads the current run, inventories the exact claim-bound name/expected ACL user/role/slot, rejects twins, kills the sole matching ID if present, repeats the full inventory, and performs the final run read. Stable expected run plus zero final matches yields `unregistered_killed_then_absent | unregistered_already_absent`; a stable different run yields `unregistered_server_incarnation_retired` only with the exact proof for `expectedRedisServerRunId`; any run change, twin, missing runtime/egress fence, or uncertain inventory is insufficient. The separately signed `RedisClientUnregisteredFenceReceiptV1` binds the claim identity, challenge/name digests, expected user/role/slot/run, observed ID-or-null, both run reads, inventory-or-retirement evidence, runtime-termination, per-slot capability-revocation, and egress-fence digests, and outcome. Its `lineage_anchor` transition tombstones the challenge and closes/fences the claim. A still-undelivered claim may instead close through a domain-separated no-byte-emitted root/database proof; no null-evidence close is legal after `delivered_unknown`. Terminal `closed_clean|fenced` records first require the terminal database-handoff leaf when handoff count is positive and zero current root/DB command or receipt reference, then compact into a fixed per-lineage accumulator `{ compactionSequence, compactedCount, compactedRootDigest, clientGenerationHighWater }`; fsync old-root→new-root CAS precedes record deletion, stale root/sequence and old-generation replay fail, and only the at-most-two slot-consuming records plus fixed accumulator remain. Canonical cross-language golden fixtures for claim challenge/identity, identity-verification receipt, uint64 client-ID strings, genesis/state-body CAS, monotonic fence-attempt chain including unproved→sufficient recovery, connection subrecord, command subrecord, binding acknowledgment, result reconciliation, and compaction roots; compaction/replay, predecessor/high-water ABA, every crash boundary, two asymmetric-loss generations plus restart and repeated nominal drain/QUIT-response loss across all command/blocking slots, `CLIENT LIST<=118` with helper admission, and stale/wrong identity or registered-state digest, state-chain ABA, role/slot/command mismatch prove no third client or unbound effect.

All Redis-client digests use one exact rule unless a signature/HMAC rule above explicitly applies: `D(domain,value)=sha256:<lowercase hex SHA256(UTF8(domain) || 0x00 || UTF8(RFC8785_JCS(value)))>`; every earlier `domain\\0` or direct `SHA256(UTF8(domain\\0)||UTF8(JCS(value)))` notation means this same `D(domain,value)` wire value, with one zero byte and never two text characters. Every digest below is the resulting 71-character `sha256:` string.

`redisClientSlotCapabilityDigest=D('noli:redis-client-slot-capability:v1',{runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,manifestOrdinal,role,clientSlotId,clientKind,capabilityBase64url})`; `runtimeRedisClientSlotCapabilityManifestDigest=D('noli:redis-client-slot-capability-manifest:v1',entriesSortedByManifestOrdinalWithoutRawCapability)`, where every entry is exact `{manifestOrdinal,role,clientSlotId,clientKind,capabilityDigest}`; and `redisClientSlotCapabilityDeliveryAckDigest=D('noli:redis-client-slot-capability-delivery-ack:v1',{runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,manifestDigest,deliveryGenerationDecimal,deliveredAt})`. `redisClientSlotCapabilityRevocationDigest=D('noli:redis-client-slot-capability-revocation:v1',{runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,manifestOrdinal,capabilityDigest,revocationGenerationDecimal,reason,claimIdOrNull,runtimeTerminationReceiptDigestOrNull,revokedAt})`. Reason is exactly `unregistered_recovery | runtime_terminated_unacked`; the first requires a nonnull exact claim ID and null termination digest, while the second requires null claim ID and the exact runtime-termination receipt digest. Both are monotonic and permanently reject the capability. `redisClientCapabilityDeliveryStateDigest=D('noli:redis-client-capability-delivery-state:v1',{runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,manifestDigest,deliveryGenerationDecimal,state,terminalReasonOrNull,sealedCapabilitySetDigestOrNull,deliveryAckDigestOrNull,runtimeTerminationReceiptDigestOrNull,runtimeRedisEgressFenceDigestOrNull,zeroPendingCallClaimProofDigestOrNull,revokedSlots,changedAt})`, where `revokedSlots` sorts by manifest ordinal and each is exact `{manifestOrdinal,capabilityDigest,revocationGenerationDecimal,revocationDigest}`. State is exactly `prepared | delivered_unacked | acked | tombstoned`. Nonterminal states require every terminal proof/reason null; sealed-set digest is nonnull exactly for `prepared|delivered_unacked`, and delivery acknowledgment is nonnull exactly for `acked`. Tombstoned state requires `terminalReasonOrNull='acked_shutdown' | 'terminated_unacked'`, exact runtime-termination, runtime-egress-fence, and zero-pending-call/claim proof digests, and null sealed set; `acked_shutdown` retains the matching acknowledgment, while `terminated_unacked` requires acknowledgment null and a revocation entry for every manifest slot before sealed bytes are destroyed. A per-slot revocation while `acked` immediately bars every later fifth-socket request for that capability but does not itself tombstone the set. `capabilityDeliveryTombstoneProofDigest=D('noli:redis-client-capability-delivery-tombstone-proof:v1',{runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,runtimeTerminationReceiptDigest,runtimeRedisEgressFenceDigest,pendingCallCandidateSetDigest,liveClaimCandidateSetDigest,provedAt})`; both candidate-set digests use the exact checkpoint member schemas below and must hash literal empty arrays while the control-row lock is held; every relevant claim/call mutation also requires that same first lock, so the empty snapshots cannot race. This proof authorizes the terminal state and sealed-byte destruction; it is distinct from the later compaction zero-reference proof, which additionally proves no remaining sealed-artifact reference. Runtime death in `prepared|delivered_unacked` therefore has a closed fail-safe terminal path and cannot strand sealed capabilities. After ACK, the controller deletes encrypted raw capabilities but retains the closed digest map and acknowledgment until that tombstone, so restart can authenticate presented capabilities.

`claimIdentityDigest=D('noli:redis-client-claim-identity:v1',identityObject)`, `connectionChallengeDigest=D('noli:redis-client-connection-challenge:v1',{claimId,challengeBase64url})`, `clientNameDigest=D('noli:redis-client-name:v1',{claimId,canonicalClientName})`, `helperObservationDigest=D('noli:redis-client-helper-observation-digest:v1',completeObservationIncludingAuthentication)`, and each readiness/identity/fence artifact digest is `D('noli:redis-client-controller-envelope-digest:v1',completeSignedEnvelopeIncludingSignature)`. `registeredConnectionStateDigest=D('noli:redis-client-connection-state:v1',{claimId,claimIdentityDigest,registeredIdentityVerificationDigest,registeredClientNameDigest,expectedAclUsername,environmentId,role,clientSlotId,clientKind,runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,startAttestationDigest,clientGenerationDecimal,redisServerRunId,redisClientId,registeredAt})`, where `registeredAt` is exactly the signed `RedisClientIdentityVerificationV1.databaseIssuedAt`, not local or later database time. `registeredCommandStateDigest=D('noli:redis-client-command-state:v1',{claimId,claimIdentityDigest,registeredConnectionStateDigest,subjectKind,subjectId,bindingGenerationOrNull,commandNonce,purpose,commandGenerationDecimal,bindingChallengeNonce,bindingChallengeAt})`; `databaseTupleDigest=D('noli:redis-client-database-tuple:v1',bindingPendingProjection)`; `currentCommandTupleDigest=D('noli:redis-client-current-command:v1',{claimId,claimIdentityDigest,registeredIdentityVerificationDigest,registeredConnectionStateDigest,databaseTupleDigest})`; and `controllerRootBindingAckDigest=D('noli:redis-client-root-binding-ack:v1',{claimId,registeredCommandStateDigest,currentCommandTupleDigest,databaseTupleDigest,bindingChallengeNonce,bindingChallengeAt})`. The connection, command, and acknowledgment objects are exactly these closed objects and never contain their own digest.

`bindingPendingProjection` is the closed object `{common,detail}`. Common is exact `{purpose,owningEntityKind,owningRowId,subjectKind,subjectId,bindingGenerationOrNull,producerRole,runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,startAttestationDigest,claimId,claimIdentityDigest,registeredIdentityVerificationDigest,registeredConnectionStateDigest,redisServerRunId,redisClientId,clientGenerationDecimal,commandNonce,commandGenerationDecimal,bindingChallengeNonce,bindingChallengeAt}`. IDs/digests/run/client fields use the canonical contracts above; `bindingChallengeNonce` is a database-generated 128-bit value encoded as exactly 22 base64url-no-padding characters in `varchar(22)` with `octet_length=22` and C-collation regex `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22}$`, and `bindingChallengeAt` is the same transaction's database timestamp. Both are present from `binding_pending` through registered/fence commitment and clear only with the whole current command. Runtime callers cannot supply either.

The detail union is exact: `{purpose:'strict_direct_enqueue',replyJobId,dispatchGenerationDecimal,transportJobId,expectedEnvelopeDigest}`; `{purpose:'strict_scope_enqueue',scheduleId,scopeTargetId,targetBindingGenerationDecimal,transportJobId,expectedEnvelopeDigest}`; `{purpose:'strict_pager_upsert',scheduleId,pagerBindingGenerationDecimal,transportJobId,expectedEnvelopeDigest}`; `{purpose:'strict_transport_remove',scheduleId,strictSubjectKind,strictSubjectId,bindingGenerationDecimal,transportJobId,observedTransportState,retainedEnvelopeDigest}`; `{purpose:'enqueue',outboxId,destinationQueue,transportJobId,expectedEnvelopeDigest,enqueueAttemptGenerationDecimal}`; or `{purpose:'terminal_remove',outboxId,destinationQueue,transportJobId,removeGenerationDecimal,observedTransportState,observedEnqueueGenerationDecimal,retainedEnvelopeDigest}`. Detail purpose must equal common purpose; common owner/subject/binding/generation is rederived from the named row and must equal its detail. Binding generation is null only for the two outbox forms; observed transport state is one generated BullMQ state and is present only in the two remove forms. No owner transport/envelope field may be omitted or added.

An acknowledged result is the closed object `{purpose,owningEntityKind,owningRowId,commandGenerationDecimal,commandNonce,registeredCommandStateDigest,transportJobId,adapterOutcome,observedTransportStateOrNull,observedEnvelopeDigestOrNull,databaseRecordedAt}` exact-read from the protected owner row. Literal digest domains by purpose are `noli:redis-client-acknowledged-result:strict-direct-enqueue:v1`, `noli:redis-client-acknowledged-result:strict-scope-enqueue:v1`, `noli:redis-client-acknowledged-result:strict-pager-upsert:v1`, `noli:redis-client-acknowledged-result:strict-transport-remove:v1`, `noli:redis-client-acknowledged-result:enqueue:v1`, and `noli:redis-client-acknowledged-result:terminal-remove:v1`; `acknowledgedDatabaseResultDigest=D(domainForPurpose,result)`. Outcomes are respectively `added | already_matching | pre_send_failed`, `added | already_matching | pre_send_failed`, `upserted | already_matching | pre_send_failed`, `removed | already_absent | pre_send_mismatch | pre_send_failed`, `added | no_send_already_visible | no_send_terminal_present | pre_send_failed`, and `removed | already_absent | pre_send_mismatch | pre_send_failed`. Only the closed typed `adapterOutcome` and, where its purpose requires one, the canonical observed transport state/envelope enter authority; raw RESP2/RESP3 client reply values are neither persisted in this protected result nor hashed, and may appear only in redacted non-authoritative diagnostics. Observed state/envelope are nonnull exactly for an already-present/mismatch/no-send transport observation. Unknown outcome, caller-provided result, or null-matrix mismatch fails.

Every owning reply-job, strict-schedule, and queue-outbox row has generated nonnegative `redis_client_handoff_count`, nonnull `redis_client_handoff_chain_digest`, and nullable `redis_client_last_handoff_leaf_digest`; count zero requires the owner-specific genesis and null last leaf, while count positive requires last leaf. `redisClientOwnerHandoffGenesis=D('noli:redis-client-owner-handoff-genesis:v1',{owningEntityKind,owningRowId})`. Each normal-result or fence fold computes `resolutionDigest` is the exact `acknowledgedDatabaseResultDigest` for a normal fold or `D('noli:redis-client-fence-resolution:v1',{controllerFenceReceiptDigest,controllerFenceTupleDigest,controllerFenceOutcome,controllerFenceVerifiedAt})` for a fence fold. `databaseHandoffCommandLeafDigest=D('noli:redis-client-database-handoff-command-leaf:v1',{claimId,purpose,owningEntityKind,owningRowId,commandGenerationDecimal,registeredCommandStateDigest,resolutionDigest,priorOwnerHandoffChainDigest,ownerHandoffOrdinalDecimal,priorClaimHandoffAccumulatorDigest,claimHandoffOrdinalDecimal})`; owner ordinal is exactly that row's prior count+1, while claim ordinal is independently the root claim's prior handoff count+1. `foldedDatabaseChainDigest=D('noli:redis-client-owner-handoff-chain:v1',{priorChainDigest,ownerHandoffOrdinalDecimal,databaseHandoffCommandLeafDigest})`; the same database transaction increment-one stores owner count, chain, last leaf, folds the purpose-specific proof chain with that leaf, and clears the current tuple. The prepared root transition advances the claim's fixed `{databaseHandoffCountDecimal,databaseHandoffAccumulatorDigest}` with `D('noli:redis-client-claim-handoff-accumulator:v1',{priorRootOrGenesis,claimHandoffOrdinalDecimal,databaseHandoffCommandLeafDigest,foldedDatabaseChainDigest})`, where `redisClientClaimHandoffGenesis=D('noli:redis-client-claim-handoff-genesis:v1',{environmentId,claimId})` is the sole count-zero genesis.

The security-barrier `public_chat_redis_client_reference_candidates_v1` union exposes only current tuples from reply-job dispatch, strict-schedule transport, queue-outbox enqueue, and queue-outbox terminal-remove rows. Each member is exact `{owningEntityKind,owningRowId,purpose,commandGenerationDecimal,claimId,claimIdentityDigest,databaseTupleDigestOrNull,currentCommandTupleDigestOrNull,controllerFenceTupleDigestOrNull}` and sorts by C-collated `(owningEntityKind,owningRowId,purpose,commandGenerationDecimal)`; pending rows require both tuple digests null, registered/fence-committed rows require both nonnull, and each source has a matching partial index on `(claim_id,owning_row_id)` for nonnull current tuples. `candidateViewSnapshotDigest=D('noli:redis-client-reference-candidate-set:v1',sortedMembers)`, including the literal empty array. Every function that creates `binding_pending` first locks the control row and then the manifest-derived lineage row, re-queries `public_chat_redis_client_reference_candidates_v1` while those locks are held, requires the literal empty set for that claim, and only then locks/updates its owner; terminal/unknown/inactive claims or any existing pending/registered/fence-committed tuple are rejected. Because every creator and terminal handoff takes the same lineage lock, two cross-table owners cannot concurrently install current tuples for one claim. The terminal-handoff registrar uses that same order, then locks every indexed candidate member and re-queries the union in the same transaction; only exact empty permits `zeroLiveDatabaseReferenceProofDigest=D('noli:redis-client-zero-live-database-reference:v1',{claimId,candidateViewSnapshotDigest,provedAt})`, where `provedAt` is that transaction's database time. It atomically advances tail+lineage to terminal and makes every later reference insertion fail. `databaseHandoffLeafDigest=D('noli:redis-client-terminal-database-handoff-leaf:v1',{claimId,databaseHandoffCountDecimal,databaseHandoffAccumulatorDigest,zeroLiveDatabaseReferenceProofDigest})` is nonnull exactly when count is positive and is stored in the claim/capsule by that same transition. A folded owner chain contains only immutable digest history, not a live claim ID/command reference; the fold releases that direct reference while the root accumulator preserves membership. The terminal capsule may therefore immediately fold into the fixed lineage accumulator after this atomic handoff instead of retaining one capsule per historical reference. Concurrent binding creation, phantom candidate, changed partial-index predicate, cross-row/current tuple, response loss, chain rollback, missing leaf, mismatched owner/result, and fold/terminal-handoff crashes fail closed.

`registeredTupleDigest=D('noli:redis-client-registered-tuple:v1',{claimId,claimIdentityDigest,registeredIdentityVerificationDigest,registeredClientNameDigest,expectedAclUsername,registeredConnectionStateDigest,registeredCommandStateDigestOrNull,controllerRootBindingAckDigestOrNull,controllerRootBoundAtOrNull,databaseTupleDigestOrNull,redisServerRunId,redisClientId,clientGenerationDecimal})`; its four command fields are all null for connection-only form and all nonnull for command form. `controllerFenceTupleDigest=D('noli:redis-client-controller-fence-tuple:v1',{claimId,registeredIdentityVerificationDigest,registeredConnectionStateDigest,registeredCommandStateDigestOrNull,controllerRootBindingAckDigestOrNull,databaseTupleDigestOrNull,controllerFenceReceiptDigest,controllerFenceOutcome,controllerFenceVerifiedAt})`. `unregisteredFenceSubjectDigest=D('noli:redis-client-unregistered-fence-subject:v1',{claimId,claimIdentityDigest,challengeDeliveryState:'delivered_unknown',connectionChallengeDigest,clientNameDigest,expectedAclUsername,role,clientSlotId,clientKind,runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,clientGenerationDecimal,expectedRedisServerRunId,runtimeTerminationReceiptDigest,slotCapabilityRevocationDigest,egressFenceDigest})`. `fenceAttemptSubjectDigest` is exactly `D('noli:redis-client-fence-attempt-subject:v1',{kind:'registered',registeredTupleDigest})` for a registered claim or `D('noli:redis-client-fence-attempt-subject:v1',{kind:'unregistered',unregisteredFenceSubjectDigest})` for delivered-unknown recovery; no other subject form exists. `redisClientFenceAttemptGenesis=D('noli:redis-client-fence-attempt-genesis:v1',{environmentId,claimId})`; every next `fenceAttemptProofChainDigest=D('noli:redis-client-fence-attempt-chain:v1',{priorChain,attemptGenerationDecimal,fenceAttemptSubjectDigest,attemptArtifactKind,attemptArtifactDigest,outcome})`, where `attemptArtifactKind` is exactly `helper_observation | helper_probe_failure | signed_fence_receipt`. `lastFenceAttemptArtifactDigest` is the exact helper-observation digest for an unproved observed attempt, helper-completion digest for an early probe failure, or complete signed receipt-envelope digest for a sufficient attempt; only the last case may also set `fenceReceiptDigest`. `redisClientCommandResolutionGenesis=D('noli:redis-client-command-resolution-genesis:v1',{environmentId,claimId})`; `lastCommandResolutionDigest=D('noli:redis-client-command-resolution:v1',{priorResolutionDigestOrGenesis,registeredCommandStateDigest,controllerRootBindingAckDigest,resolution,foldedDatabaseChainDigest})`, where resolution is exactly `{kind:'acknowledged_result',acknowledgedDatabaseResultDigest}` or `{kind:'controller_fence',controllerFenceReceiptDigest,controllerFenceTupleDigest,controllerFenceOutcome,controllerFenceVerifiedAt}` with a sufficient outcome.

The terminal capsule is the closed RFC8785 object `{environmentId,role,clientSlotId,clientKind,claimId,clientGenerationDecimal,terminalState,claimIdentityDigest,registeredIdentityVerificationDigestOrNull,registeredConnectionStateDigestOrNull,lastCommandResolutionDigestOrNull,fenceReceiptDigestOrNull,databaseHandoffCountDecimal,databaseHandoffLeafDigestOrNull,terminalAt}` and its canonical bytes must be at most 2,048 bytes. `terminalState` is exactly `fenced | closed_clean`; identity-verification and connection-state digests are both null only when the claim never registered and otherwise both nonnull; `fenceReceiptDigestOrNull` is nonnull for every registered terminal claim and every `delivered_unknown` unregistered terminal claim, and names the registered or unregistered receipt as appropriate; it may be null only for an `undelivered` no-byte-emitted close. `lastCommandResolutionDigestOrNull` is nonnull exactly when a command was resolved. `databaseHandoffCountDecimal` is nonnegative and `databaseHandoffLeafDigestOrNull` is nonnull exactly when that count is positive; the leaf proves all direct references were folded/released into immutable owner and claim accumulators, so it is not itself a live database reference. `terminalAt` is the signed proof's `databaseIssuedAt`, or the root/database no-byte-emitted proof time for the sole undelivered close case. `terminalCapsuleLeafDigest=D('noli:redis-client-terminal-capsule:v1',capsule)`; `redisClientLineageAccumulatorGenesis=D('noli:redis-client-terminal-accumulator-genesis:v1',{environmentId,role,clientSlotId})`; and each next `D('noli:redis-client-terminal-accumulator:v1',{priorRootOrGenesis,compactionSequenceDecimal,claimGenerationDecimal,capsuleLeafDigest})` is retained with sequence/count/high-water.

The 49-entry lineage map is a fixed array sorted by generated manifest ordinal, each entry exact `{role,clientSlotId,clientKind,manifestOrdinal,generationHighWaterDecimal,slotConsumingClaims,activeCurrentClaimIdOrNull,terminalAccumulatorSequenceDecimal,terminalAccumulatorCountDecimal,terminalAccumulatorRootDigest}`. `slotConsumingClaims` has length `0..2`, is sorted by numeric generation, and each member is exact `{claimId,clientGenerationDecimal,state,currentStateDigest}` with state exactly `reserved | registered_current | retired_unproved`; active ID is null or names the sole reserved/registered-current member; terminal accumulator count equals sequence because every compaction advances both by exactly one. `redisClientLineageMapDigest=D('noli:redis-client-lineage-map:v1',array)`.

A parsed `CLIENT LIST` inventory is the closed object `{redisServerRunId,records}`. Each record is exact `{redisClientIdDecimal,inventoryClientNameDigest,aclUsername,flagsSorted,selectedDatabaseDecimal}` derived respectively from Redis fields `id`, the losslessly decoded complete `name` bytes, `user`, the byte-sorted unique flag characters from `flags`, and `db`. `inventoryClientNameDigest=D('noli:redis-client-inventory-name:v1',{nameBase64url})`, where `nameBase64url` is base64url without padding of those exact `0..128` decoded bytes and empty name is the empty string; this is deliberately distinct from claim-bound `clientNameDigest`. For registered twin exclusion after the raw challenge is tombstoned, the helper parses only names that satisfy the exact ASCII `noli-spec065-v1:<lowercase-claim-uuid>:<22-char-base64url-challenge>` grammar, requires the embedded claim ID equal the known claim ID, computes `clientNameDigest` over each candidate's decoded canonical name, and compares it to the retained `registeredClientNameDigest`; no digest is reversed and no unavailable name bytes are assumed. For unregistered recovery, the still-sealed challenge supplies the exact canonical name. IDs are canonical uint64 decimal strings, database is a canonical nonnegative decimal string, usernames obey the generated byte bound, and no address, file descriptor, age, idle time, buffer size, command, library, or network counter enters authority. Records sort by numeric uint64 client ID and duplicate IDs, malformed escape decoding, or overlong names fail. `redisClientInventoryDigest=D('noli:redis-client-inventory:v1',inventory)`. `redisServerIncarnationRetirementProofDigest=D('noli:redis-server-incarnation-retirement-proof-digest:v1',completeSignedEnvelopeIncludingSignature)`.

The six AEAD associated-data forms use the sole closed key set `{environmentId,purpose,subjectId,runtimeIdOrNull,runtimeGenerationOrNull,roleOrNull,clientSlotIdOrNull,generationOrNull}`. `runtime_capability_set` is exact `{environmentId,purpose:'runtime_capability_set',subjectId:runtimeId,runtimeIdOrNull:runtimeId,runtimeGenerationOrNull:runtimeGenerationDecimal,roleOrNull:null,clientSlotIdOrNull:null,generationOrNull:deliveryGenerationDecimal}`. `connection_challenge` is exact `{environmentId,purpose:'connection_challenge',subjectId:claimId,runtimeIdOrNull:runtimeId,runtimeGenerationOrNull:runtimeGenerationDecimal,roleOrNull:role,clientSlotIdOrNull:clientSlotId,generationOrNull:clientGenerationDecimal}`. `helper_observation_key` is exact `{environmentId,purpose:'helper_observation_key',subjectId:observationRequestNonce,runtimeIdOrNull,runtimeGenerationOrNull,roleOrNull,clientSlotIdOrNull,generationOrNull:credentialGenerationDecimal}`; `observationRequestNonce` is the primary request nonce except for the second bootstrap admin-identity stage, where it is exactly `identityRequestNonceOrNull`. Its runtime/role/slot fields are all nonnull for an application-claim-bound request and all null for readiness/admin run-bind/admin identity/admin recovery. The bootstrap pair has distinct subject IDs and separately allocated AES nonces/sealed values; swapping stage, nonce, key, or AAD fails. `emergency_credential` is exact `{environmentId,purpose:'emergency_credential',subjectId:'noli-spec065-emergency',runtimeIdOrNull:null,runtimeGenerationOrNull:null,roleOrNull:null,clientSlotIdOrNull:null,generationOrNull:credentialGenerationDecimal}`. `helper_permit_credential` is exact `{environmentId,purpose:'helper_permit_credential',subjectId:requestNonce+':'+permitOrdinalDecimal,runtimeIdOrNull:null,runtimeGenerationOrNull:null,roleOrNull:null,clientSlotIdOrNull:null,generationOrNull:credentialGenerationDecimal}`. `admin_claim_credential` is exact `{environmentId,purpose:'admin_claim_credential',subjectId:adminClaimId,runtimeIdOrNull:null,runtimeGenerationOrNull:null,roleOrNull:null,clientSlotIdOrNull:null,generationOrNull:credentialGenerationDecimal}`. No alternate key name, omitted key, extra key, purpose, or null shape is legal. `sealedValueDigest=D('noli:redis-client-sealed-value:v1',{purpose,associatedData,sealedValue})` over the exact sealed object; `sealedCapabilitySetDigest=D('noli:redis-client-sealed-capability-set:v1',{runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,deliveryGenerationDecimal,sealedValuesSortedByManifestOrdinal})`, where each member is exact `{manifestOrdinal,capabilityDigest,sealedValueDigest}`. `emergencyCredentialDigest=D('noli:redis-client-emergency-credential:v1',{credentialGenerationDecimal,credentialBytesBase64url})`, where the raw 32 bytes encode as exactly 43 base64url-no-padding characters; `sealedEmergencyCredentialDigest=D('noli:redis-client-sealed-emergency-credential:v1',{credentialGenerationDecimal,credentialDigest,sealedValueDigest})`. `helperPermitCredentialDigest=D('noli:redis-client-helper-permit-credential:v1',{permitOrdinal,requestNonce,credentialGenerationDecimal,credentialBytesBase64url})` and `adminClaimCredentialDigest=D('noli:redis-client-admin-claim-credential:v1',{claimId,credentialGenerationDecimal,credentialBytesBase64url})`; both raw credentials are exactly 32 bytes/43 base64url characters. Their sealed digests are `D('noli:redis-client-sealed-helper-permit-credential:v1',{permitOrdinal,requestNonce,credentialGenerationDecimal,credentialDigest,sealedValueDigest})` and `D('noli:redis-client-sealed-admin-claim-credential:v1',{claimId,credentialGenerationDecimal,credentialDigest,sealedValueDigest})`. The latter admin-claim formula and `admin_claim_credential` AAD apply exactly to broker/readiness claims. An emergency claim creates no second seal: its three credential fields exact-reference one active/allowed-retiring `emergencyCredentialState` tuple and its sealed object keeps purpose `emergency_credential`; kind confusion, resealing it as `admin_claim_credential`, or an uncounted extra secret fails schema and reference scans.

`rootKeyDigest=D('noli:redis-client-root-key:v1',{keyId,keyBytesBase64url})`, where key bytes are exactly 32 bytes encoded as 43 base64url-no-padding characters and the raw value never leaves the mode-0700 root/recovery stores. `redisClientKeyringDigest=D('noli:redis-client-keyring-state:v1',{initialized,keyringGenerationDecimal,activeKeyIdOrNull,activeKeyDigestOrNull,activeNonceHighWaterDecimalOrNull,retiringKeyIdOrNull,retiringKeyDigestOrNull,retiringNonceHighWaterDecimalOrNull,recoveryState})`; `recoveryState` is exact `{copyGenerationHighWaterDecimal,committedCopyManifest,candidateIntentDigestOrNull,rollbackAccumulatorSequenceDecimal,rollbackAccumulatorCountDecimal,rollbackAccumulatorRootDigest,hostRecoveryNonceHighWaterDecimal}`; the committed manifest is null only at uninitialized genesis and otherwise exact `{copyGenerationDecimal,immutableRecoveryPath,keyIdsAndDigestsSorted,recoveryCopyBytesDigest,keyringRecoveryCopyDigest,keyringRecoveryRestoreProofDigest,hostRecoveryKeyId,hostRecoveryKeyVersion}`. `keyringCommittedCopyManifestDigest=D('noli:redis-client-keyring-committed-copy-manifest:v1',committedCopyManifest)` and null is legal only at genesis. `keyringCandidateRollbackAccumulatorGenesis=D('noli:redis-client-keyring-candidate-rollback-genesis:v1',{environmentId,contract:'spec-065-v1'})`; count=sequence, copy high-water is zero at genesis and never rewinds; all fields are covered by keyring/global/checkpoint digests. each nonnull key digest is exactly `rootKeyDigest` for that ID. Uninitialized generation zero requires every active/retiring field null; initialized positive generation requires the complete active triplet and either a complete immediately-prior retiring triplet or all retiring fields null.

`redisClientCapabilityDeliveryStateSetDigest=D('noli:redis-client-capability-delivery-state-set:v1',{liveEntries,compactionAccumulatorSequenceDecimal,compactionAccumulatorCountDecimal,compactionAccumulatorRootDigest})`, where `liveEntries` has at most 2,048 members sorted by `(runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal)` and each member is exact `{runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,stateDigest}`. The accumulator starts at `redisClientCapabilityDeliveryAccumulatorGenesis=D('noli:redis-client-capability-delivery-accumulator-genesis:v1',{environmentId,contract:'spec-065-v1'})`, requires count=sequence, and advances by `D('noli:redis-client-capability-delivery-accumulator:v1',{priorRootOrGenesis,compactionSequenceDecimal,runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,terminalStateDigest,zeroReferenceProofDigest})`. `capabilityDeliveryZeroReferenceProofDigest=D('noli:redis-client-capability-delivery-zero-reference:v1',{runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal,runtimeTerminationReceiptDigest,runtimeRedisEgressFenceDigest,liveClaimSetDigest,pendingCallSetDigest,sealedSecretReferenceSetDigest,provedAt})` is legal only when the three named sets are literal empty and every slot capability is revoked or the set was acknowledged then tombstoned. A `capability_set_compact` global transition atomically removes that one tombstoned live entry, advances the fixed accumulator and control tail/digest, and deletes any no-longer-referenced sealed bytes; response loss resumes the same step. Runtime-start admission pauses at 2,048 entries until reconciliation compacts eligible tombstones. The control column `redis_client_capability_delivery_state_digest` equals this aggregate digest, so restarts cannot accumulate an unbounded per-runtime tombstone set.

Helper control state is exact `{requestHighWaterDecimal,pendingRequests,adminRequests,permits,brokerLineage,readinessEmergencyLineage,completionAccumulatorSequenceDecimal,completionAccumulatorCountDecimal,completionAccumulatorRootDigest,emergencyCredentialState,redisContainerLifecycleState,readinessPublicationState}`; `requestHighWaterDecimal` equals control column `redis_client_helper_gate_high_water` at genesis and after every transition/readiness check. Pending requests sort by numeric sequence and are exact `{requestSequenceDecimal,requestNonce,verb,claimIdOrNull,commandGenerationDecimalOrNull,deadline,state}`, where verb is `register_identity | registered_fence | unregistered_fence`, state is `queued | active | cleanup_required`, and command generation is nonnull only for command-form registered fence. `adminRequests` has at most two members sorted by sequence and each is exact `{requestSequenceDecimal,requestNonce,verb,adminClaimId,credentialGenerationDecimal,sealedObservationKeyDigest,identityRequestNonceOrNull,sealedIdentityObservationKeyDigestOrNull,databaseChallengeIssuedAt,deadline,state,pausedSocketIdentityDigestOrNull,runBindObservationDigestOrNull,resumeAuthorizationDigestOrNull,adminIdentityObservationDigestOrNull,identityCommitAuthorizationDigestOrNull,completionDigestOrNull}`, where verb is `readiness | admin_run_bind | admin_identity | admin_recovery`, state is `queued | active | awaiting_run_bind_commit | resumed | awaiting_identity_commit | cleanup_required | completed`, and completion digest is nonnull exactly for completed. It occupies the matching shared admin-lineage claim, uses the same monotonic request high-water, and is tombstoned into the completion accumulator before that claim can be reused. An ordinary readiness/recovery or attested `admin_identity` request has both identity-key fields null and may authenticate exactly one observation with its primary nonce/key. A bootstrap `admin_run_bind` request is created with a distinct 128-bit `identityRequestNonceOrNull` and independently generated/sealed 256-bit identity-observation key; both are nonnull from enqueue through identity commit, every other verb requires them null, and the two one-use HMAC keys have distinct `helper_observation_key` AAD subjects. The primary key authenticates only `admin_run_bind`, is destroyed after that observation, and can never authenticate identity; the identity key authenticates only the later `admin_identity` observation whose common request nonce equals `identityRequestNonceOrNull`, then is destroyed. Both sealed digests remain root-replayable until the matching CAS/cleanup tombstones them; no key or nonce is reused. Only bootstrap-unbound run binding may enter `awaiting_run_bind_commit`: the helper retains one paused nonreconnecting TLS socket after AUTH/SETNAME/INFO/ID, stores its process/socket identity plus authenticated run-bind observation, and performs no LIST/KILL/ACL. After the controller tail-CASes the observed run into the claim, `adminRunBindResumeAuthorizationDigest=D('noli:redis-client-admin-run-bind-resume:v1',{requestSequenceDecimal,requestNonce,identityRequestNonce,adminClaimId,redisContainerGenerationDecimal,redisContainerCreationAttestationDigest,pausedSocketIdentityDigest,observedRedisServerRunId,runBindObservationDigest,boundAdminClaimStateDigest,expiresAt})` is written atomically by that same `admin_run_bind` claim/helper-control CAS and returned once; exact verification moves to `resumed` and only that same socket continues. Timeout, helper/controller crash, wrong socket/run/state, replay, or reconnect moves to cleanup_required and requires credential/process/container cleanup; it never resumes on a fresh socket. An attested identity request moves directly from active to `awaiting_identity_commit`; a resumed bootstrap request moves there only after the fixed identity observation. `adminIdentityCommitAuthorizationDigest=D('noli:redis-client-admin-identity-commit-authorization:v1',{requestSequenceDecimal,runBindRequestNonceOrNull,identityObservationRequestNonce,adminClaimId,pausedSocketIdentityDigest,adminIdentityObservationDigest,adminIdentityRegistrationDigest,registeredConnectionStateDigest,expiresAt})` is written atomically by the matching `admin_identity_register` claim/helper-control CAS and returned once. `identityObservationRequestNonce` is the primary nonce for attested identity and the distinct identity nonce for bootstrap; `runBindRequestNonceOrNull` is nonnull only for bootstrap. Exact verification on that paused socket permits only the now-registered claim profile; missing/wrong/replayed authorization or a changed socket/run enters cleanup, and no pre-CAS observation authorizes mutation. `permits` is the fixed 16-entry ordinal array, each exact `{permitOrdinal,state,requestNonceOrNull,credentialGenerationDecimalOrNull,credentialDigestOrNull,sealedCredentialDigestOrNull,aclFingerprintDigestOrNull,credentialEnabled,completionDigestOrNull}` with state `free | active | cleanup_required`; free requires all nullable fields null and `credentialEnabled=false`, active requires credential/sealed-credential/ACL digests nonnull and enabled true, and cleanup retains the exact digests and sealed value plus actual enabled state until kill/disable/zero-inventory proof; sealed bytes are deleted only in the completion-tombstone CAS and remain replayable for an exact same-generation lost delivery. It is at most 8 KiB, duplicate outer/body coordinates exact-match, and `redisContainerCreationAttestationDigest=D('noli:redis-client-container-creation-attestation:v1',completeSignedEnvelopeIncludingSignature)`. It may enter `redis_container_creation_attest` only when a database-time validation within five minutes is stored in the unique fsynced prepared transition for the exact current planned container generation. That global transition exact-verifies the stopped returned ID/name/plan against `redisContainerLifecycleState.currentOrNull`, stores one raw `redis_container_creation_attestation` artifact owned by `{ownerKind:'redis_container_generation',ownerId:containerGenerationDecimal}` at reference count one, advances the root/database tail, and single-consumes its nonce before start; at most one current container-owner creation artifact exists. Once stored, delayed crash recovery/readiness uses the exact committed digest after envelope expiry. The helper may then start only that stopped container. Each matching `readiness_complete` requires the digest in its verification/pending state and folds it into the run attestation, but only marks publication consumption and retains the container-owner raw bytes, signing-key reference, and reference count unchanged; sole `redis_container_retire` deletes/releases them exactly once after its exact retirement proof; no container with missing/wrong attestation may start or supply run authority. When a maintenance-fenced server-incarnation retirement must clear saturated ambiguous emergency generations, normal rotation is forbidden. `emergencyCredentialServerResetDigest=D('noli:redis-client-emergency-credential-server-reset:v1',{environmentId,emergencyCredentialStatePriorDigest,oldEmergencyExternalReferenceSetDigest,retiredServerProofSetDigest,currentContainerRetirementProofDigest,redisContainerLifecycleCoreStatePriorDigest,redisContainerLifecycleCoreStateRetiredDigest,containerRetirementAccumulatorRootDigest,replacementContainerAbsenceDigest,newCredentialGenerationDecimal,newCredentialDigest,newSealedEmergencyCredentialDigest,newOnlyRedisEmergencyAclFileDigest,recoveryCopyDigest,recoveryRestoreProofDigest,controllerGenerationDecimal,manifestDigest,resetAt})`. Its old reference set must equal exactly the emergency claims covered by the signed server-retirement receipt and both state reference counts; every admin request, observation key, staged artifact, or other old-credential reference is already tombstoned/zero before preparation. With the old Redis/container proved stopped/removed/non-reattachable and the replacement container/listener also absent, the controller creates only emergency generation `highWater+1`, first fsyncs its candidate-bound intent, writes and restore-verifies only its recorded recovery material, advances the intent to material-verified, derives the recorded new-only ACL file containing neither old hash, and fsyncs a unique prepared reset root record consuming that intent and binding all receipt/reset/state/reference/recovery/file/fence values before writing that file. Only after preparation does it write/fsync/verify the new-only file while both Redis instances remain absent. While the signed absence envelope is still fresh and before stage one, the controller fsyncs the unique `RedisEmergencyServerResetOperationV1` exact record `{operationId,replacementBasisDigest,phase:'prepared'|'container_retired'|'credential_reset'|'plan_allocated'|'complete',adminServerIncarnationRetiredReceiptDigest,emergencyCredentialServerResetDigest,emergencyCredentialStatePriorDigest,emergencyCredentialStateNextDigest,redisContainerLifecycleCoreStatePriorDigest,redisContainerLifecycleCoreStateRetiredDigest,currentContainerRetirementProofDigest,containerRetirementAccumulatorRootDigest,replacementContainerAbsenceDigest,replacementContainerGenerationDecimal,replacementContainerName,replacementContainerPlanDigest,maintenanceFenceId,controllerGenerationDecimal,manifestDigest,absenceAdmittedAt}`. Fresh signature/DB-time validation and nonce consumption occur once in `prepared`; later stages may use that already-admitted proof after expiry only while the exact operation ID, fence, prior stage digest, and expected database/root state match. An active operation ID is a global-anchor exclusion flag that permits only its next named stage, recovery/status, and marker transition. The reset then uses exactly three ordered global commits under the continuously held non-start fence: (1) `redis_container_retire` consumes `currentContainerRetirementProofDigest`, exact-matches the prepared lifecycle prior, advances the named retirement accumulator, releases creation evidence, produces the bound retired digest with current null, and fsync-advances the operation to `container_retired`; (2) `emergency_credential_server_reset` consumes the matching signed retirement receipt, exact-matches both lifecycle digests and the retained replacement-absence proof, folds every covered admin claim, replaces both prior credential tuples with exactly `{generationHighWaterDecimal:newGeneration,activeOrNull:newCredentialWithReferenceCountZero,retiringOrNull:null,redisEmergencyAclFileDigestOrNull:newOnlyDigest}`, records the reset digest without changing container lifecycle, and advances to `credential_reset`; (3) ordinary `redis_container_plan_allocate` consumes the admitted proof under this operation, increments container high-water once, installs its exact replacement name/plan as `planned`, and advances to `plan_allocated`; after the commit marker it releases the absence raw/signing-key reference and marks complete. No other transition or container/listener start may interleave. Neither old hash is ever re-enabled; old sealed/recovery material is deleted only after the root commit marker, and only after that marker may the helper create the deterministic replacement name from `replacementContainerPlanDigest`; its post-create attestation binds the returned immutable Docker container ID, exact image/config/network/volume plan and new ACL-file digest before start, and only then may it start Redis; before any bootstrap claim, a separate root-helper stable-run check must exact-match disk bytes to normalized live `ACL GETUSER` state for all 19 users, prove only the fresh emergency hash is accepted and every covered old identity remains disabled, and tail-anchor that post-start ACL verification digest. Before stage-one database commit, authenticated rollback may restore the exact prepared old state and tombstone the operation/proof nonce. Once stage one commits, container-retirement accumulator progress is irreversible and recovery is forward-only through the exact remaining stages; at each boundary DB-old/root-next-stage replays only that stage, DB-new completes only its marker/phase advance, and both Redis instances remain absent until plan allocation is committed. A crash after the marker during replacement create/attest/start inventories the deterministic name and plan, accepts at most one exact stopped matching container, records its returned-ID attestation, and resumes start; a running, multiply matched, wrong-plan, or unattested container blocks and is never adopted. Activation, each arrow, rotation, saturated server reset, response-loss, ACL-file corruption, container-start-before-commit, and reference increment/decrement goldens prove no generation-zero deadlock or secret outside the two-generation state.

`redisClientHelperGateGenesis=D('noli:redis-client-helper-gate-genesis:v1',{environmentId,contract:'spec-065-v1'})`; completion accumulator count equals sequence and each step is `redisClientHelperCompletionAccumulatorDigest=D('noli:redis-client-helper-completion-accumulator:v1',{priorRootOrGenesis,completionSequenceDecimal,requestNonce,completionDigest})`. `redisClientHelperControlDigest=D('noli:redis-client-helper-control:v1',helperControlState)`, and the control column `redis_client_helper_gate_accumulator_digest` plus manifest/checkpoint helper digest equal it. Golden/crash fixtures cover both admin lineages, broker-to-emergency recovery, two ambiguous generations, credential overlap/revocation, high-water equality, and every permit/completion boundary.

`redisClientRetirementAccumulatorGenesis=D('noli:redis-client-retirement-accumulator-genesis:v1',{environmentId,contract:'spec-065-v1'})`. `redisClientRetirementStateDigest=D('noli:redis-client-retirement-state:v1',{liveEntries,compactionAccumulatorSequenceDecimal,compactionAccumulatorCountDecimal,compactionAccumulatorRootDigest})`, where live entries sort by retirement-proof digest and are exact `{retirementProofDigest,oldRedisServerRunId,oldContainerGenerationDecimal,oldContainerName,oldContainerPlanDigest,oldContainerId,oldContainerCreationAttestationDigest,oldContainerStartIntentDigest,oldContainerStartAttestationDigest,retirementGenerationDecimal,signingKeyId,rawReferenceCountDecimal,state:'retained'}` with full verified signed bytes stored in the bounded raw-artifact set. Count equals sequence. When and only when the exact raw reference count is zero, `retirementProofCompactionLeafDigest=D('noli:redis-client-retirement-compaction-leaf:v1',{retirementProofDigest,oldRedisServerRunId,oldContainerGenerationDecimal,oldContainerName,oldContainerPlanDigest,oldContainerId,oldContainerCreationAttestationDigest,oldContainerStartIntentDigest,oldContainerStartAttestationDigest,retirementGenerationDecimal,signingKeyId})` and the next accumulator root is `D('noli:redis-client-retirement-accumulator:v1',{priorRootOrGenesis,compactionSequenceDecimal,compactionLeafDigest})`; one tail-anchored global transition advances the accumulator, removes the live entry and raw bytes, and releases the signing-key retention reference. No compacted entry remains in `liveEntries`, so state size is bounded by live references rather than lifetime churn. The control `redis_client_retirement_state_digest` equals this object, and key revocation is barred until every proof signed by that key is either still verifiable in `liveEntries` or committed in this accumulator.

`redisClientTerminalAccumulatorSetDigest=D('noli:redis-client-terminal-accumulator-set:v1',entries)`, where all 49 manifest-ordered entries are exact `{manifestOrdinal,terminalAccumulatorSequenceDecimal,terminalAccumulatorCountDecimal,terminalAccumulatorRootDigest}` with count=sequence. This is a checkpoint-only projection: control `redis_client_checkpoint_terminal_accumulator_digest` changes only in the all-49 checkpoint CAS and may intentionally lag later one-lineage compaction until replay; a lineage transition never rewrites it. `redisClientReadinessProjectionOrNull` is null exactly when all eight fixed readiness columns are null, otherwise exact `{readinessGenerationDecimal,readinessVerificationDigest,readinessCompletionReceiptDigest,readinessRunAttestationDigest,readinessManifestDigest,readinessServerRunId,readinessControllerGenerationDecimal,readinessPublishedAt}` and byte-equals `readinessPublicationState.currentOrNull` after the field-name projection. `redisClientGlobalStateDigest=D('noli:redis-client-global-state:v1',{rootInitialized,keyringDigest,readinessProjectionOrNull,capabilityDeliveryStateDigest,runtimeEgressFenceStateDigest,helperControlDigest,retirementStateDigest,checkpointTerminalAccumulatorDigest})`; control `redis_client_global_state_digest` exact-matches this object after each global or checkpoint transition.

Journal subjects are closed. `redisClientGlobalSubjectDigest=D('noli:redis-client-global-subject:v1',subject)`, where subject is exactly `{scope:'environment',environmentId}` for keyring/helper/admin/retirement state or `{scope:'runtime',environmentId,runtimeId,runtimeGenerationDecimal}` for capability-delivery/egress state. `redisClientLineageSubjectDigest=D('noli:redis-client-lineage-subject:v1',{environmentId,manifestOrdinal,role,clientSlotId})`. `redisClientCommandSubjectDigest=D('noli:redis-client-command-subject:v1',{environmentId,manifestOrdinal,claimId,owningEntityKind,owningRowId,purpose,commandGenerationDecimal})`. `redisClientCheckpointSubjectDigest=D('noli:redis-client-checkpoint-subject:v1',{environmentId,generationDecimal})`.

The literal global transition kinds are `capability_set_prepare | capability_set_delivery | capability_set_ack | capability_slot_revoke | capability_set_tombstone | capability_set_compact | egress_fence_create | egress_fence_replace | egress_fence_terminal_remove | egress_fence_state_compact | aead_nonce_allocate | keyring_candidate_bind | keyring_candidate_verify | keyring_activate | keyring_rotate | keyring_retiring_remove | keyring_candidate_rollback | emergency_credential_candidate_bind | emergency_credential_candidate_verify | emergency_credential_activate | emergency_credential_rotate | emergency_credential_retiring_remove | emergency_credential_server_reset | emergency_credential_candidate_rollback | redis_container_operation_admit | redis_container_operation_abort | redis_container_plan_allocate | redis_container_creation_attest | redis_container_start_prepare | redis_container_start_commit | redis_container_retire | redis_container_operation_complete | helper_request_enqueue | helper_permit_activate | helper_completion_commit | helper_completion_tombstone | readiness_commit | readiness_complete | readiness_abort | readiness_attestation_retire | admin_claim_allocate | admin_credential_delivered_unknown | admin_run_bind | admin_identity_register | admin_claim_retire | admin_claim_fence | admin_claim_compact | admin_recovery_phase_commit | admin_server_incarnation_retire | retirement_proof_create | retirement_reference_acquire | retirement_reference_release | retirement_proof_compact | proof_preparation_rollback`.
