No numeric/unknown/vendor extension is accepted under version 1.

`RedisClientControlProjectionV1` is exact `{checkpointSequenceDecimal,checkpointRootDigest,checkpointLineageMapDigest,checkpointTerminalAccumulatorDigest,rootInitialized,keyringGenerationDecimal,keyringDigest,activeKeyIdOrNull,activeKeyDigestOrNull,activeNonceHighWaterDecimalOrNull,retiringKeyIdOrNull,retiringKeyDigestOrNull,retiringNonceHighWaterDecimalOrNull,readinessGenerationDecimalOrNull,readinessVerificationDigestOrNull,readinessCompletionReceiptDigestOrNull,readinessRunAttestationDigestOrNull,readinessManifestDigestOrNull,readinessServerRunIdOrNull,readinessControllerGenerationDecimalOrNull,readinessPublishedAtOrNull,capabilityDeliveryStateDigest,runtimeEgressFenceStateDigest,helperHighWaterDecimal,helperControlDigest,retirementStateDigest,globalStateDigest}`. `RedisClientLineageProjectionV1` is exact `{manifestOrdinal,role,clientSlotId,clientKind,generationHighWaterDecimal,claimSlot1OrNull,claimSlot2OrNull,activeClaimIdOrNull,terminalAccumulatorSequenceDecimal,terminalAccumulatorCountDecimal,terminalAccumulatorRootDigest}` using the exact scalar claim-slot schema above. `RedisClientOwnerCommandProjectionV1` is exact `{owningEntityKind,owningRowId,purpose,commandGenerationDecimal,databaseTupleDigestOrNull,currentCommandTupleDigestOrNull,registeredCommandStateDigestOrNull,controllerRootBindingAckDigestOrNull,controllerRootBoundAtOrNull,acknowledgedDatabaseResultDigestOrNull,controllerFenceTupleDigestOrNull,controllerFenceReceiptDigestOrNull,handoffCountDecimal,handoffChainDigest,lastHandoffLeafDigestOrNull}`. Variant state is exactly `global_anchor:{control}`, `lineage_anchor:{control,lineage}`, `command_anchor:{control,lineage,owner}`, or `checkpoint:{control,lineages}` with all 49 lineage projections in manifest order.

Every prepared transition value is exact `{schemaVersion:1,variant,kind,subject,expectedTailSequenceDecimal,expectedTailRootDigest,priorState,nextState,changedPaths,artifactDigestOrNull}`. Subject and kind must be one compatible pair above; prior/next state must be the compatible closed projection; `changedPaths` is the C-collated unique array of RFC6901 leaf paths whose canonical prior/next values differ and no other path; kind-specific artifact/null and OLD→NEW rules are the exact schemas in this contract. The tail coordinates are expected-old only, avoiding a self-hash: for an ordinary append the new sequence is expected+1 and the new tail root is the resulting record digest; checkpoint publication instead uses the checkpoint root under the frozen-sequence protocol. `redisClientTransitionStateDigest=D('noli:redis-client-transition-state:v1',transitionValue)`. An append-record preimage is exactly `{environmentId,sequenceDecimal,priorRecordDigest,kind,subjectDigest,stateDigest}` and `redisClientRecordDigest=D('noli:redis-client-record:v1',recordPreimage)`; the stored transition must recompute the subject/state digests byte-for-byte. A segment-root preimage is exactly `{environmentId,generationDecimal,genesisRoot,lastSequenceDecimal,lastRecordDigest,recordCountDecimal}` and `redisClientSegmentRootDigest=D('noli:redis-client-segment-root:v1',segmentRootPreimage)`; for an empty segment count is `0`, last sequence is checkpoint sequence, and last-record digest equals genesis root.

Checkpoint collection schemas are literal. `redisClientLiveClaimSetDigest=D('noli:redis-client-live-claim-set:v1',members)`, with at most 98 members sorted by `(manifestOrdinal,clientGenerationDecimal)` and each exact `{manifestOrdinal,claimId,clientGenerationDecimal,state,currentStateDigest}`. `redisClientTerminalRecordSetDigest=D('noli:redis-client-terminal-record-set:v1',members)`, with at most 49 members sorted the same way and each exact `{manifestOrdinal,claimId,clientGenerationDecimal,terminalCapsuleLeafDigest}`. `redisClientRawArtifactSetDigest=D('noli:redis-client-raw-artifact-set:v1',members)`, whose members sort by `(artifactKind,artifactDigest)` and are exact `{artifactKind,artifactDigest,ownerKind,ownerId,referenceCountDecimal}`; artifact kind is `readiness_verification | readiness_completion | identity_verification | registered_fence_receipt | unregistered_fence_receipt | server_retirement_proof | runtime_termination_receipt | runtime_egress_fence | helper_observation | helper_completion | admin_helper_closure | admin_recovery | promoter_handoff | admin_server_incarnation_retired_receipt | admin_terminal_credential_tombstone | helper_pool_credential_tombstone | helper_pool_closure | admin_negative_authentication_proof | redis_container_generation_absence | redis_container_creation_attestation | redis_container_start_intent | redis_container_lifecycle_operation | redis_container_retirement_witness | keyring_candidate_intent | emergency_credential_candidate_intent`. `redisClientSealedSecretSetDigest=D('noli:redis-client-sealed-secret-set:v1',members)`, whose members sort by `(purpose,subjectId,generationDecimal)` and are exact `{purpose,subjectId,generationDecimal,keyId,sealedValueDigest,referenceCountDecimal}` for one of the closed AEAD purposes. `redisClientFenceAttemptStateSetDigest=D('noli:redis-client-fence-attempt-state-set:v1',members)`, whose members sort by `(manifestOrdinal,claimId)` and are exact `{manifestOrdinal,claimId,attemptGenerationDecimal,attemptProofChainDigest,lastOutcomeOrNull,lastArtifactDigestOrNull}`. `pendingCallCandidateSetDigest=D('noli:redis-client-pending-call-candidate-set:v1',members)` uses the exact reference-candidate members/sort above; `liveClaimCandidateSetDigest` is the corresponding runtime-filtered live-claim member array; `sealedSecretReferenceSetDigest` is the corresponding subject-filtered sealed-secret member array. Every empty set hashes the literal empty array.

A checkpoint preimage is exactly `{environmentId,generationDecimal,journalSequenceDecimal,priorCheckpointRootDigest,liveClaimSetDigest,terminalRecordSetDigest,rawArtifactSetDigest,retirementProofStateSetDigest,sealedSecretSetDigest,capabilityDeliveryStateSetDigest,runtimeEgressFenceStateDigest,helperGateStateDigest,lineageAccumulatorSetDigest,fenceAttemptStateSetDigest,lineageMapDigest,keyringStateDigest,keyringRecoveryStateDigest,emergencyCredentialRecoveryStateDigest,containerLifecycleOperationStateDigest,globalStateDigest}` and `redisClientCheckpointRootDigest=D('noli:redis-client-checkpoint-root:v1',checkpointPreimage)`. The alias equalities are exact: retirement proof state equals `redisClientRetirementStateDigest`; capability delivery equals `redisClientCapabilityDeliveryStateSetDigest`; runtime egress equals `redisClientRuntimeEgressFenceStateDigest`; helper gate equals `redisClientHelperControlDigest`; lineage accumulator equals `redisClientTerminalAccumulatorSetDigest`; lineage map equals `redisClientLineageMapDigest`; keyring equals `redisClientKeyringDigest`; keyring recovery equals its embedded `recoveryState`; emergency recovery equals `emergencyCredentialState.recoveryState`; container operation equals `redisContainerLifecycleState.activeOperationOrNull` including literal null; global equals `redisClientGlobalStateDigest`. Unknown members, alternate sort keys, omitted empty arrays, or a stale alias fail checkpoint verification.

A generation-manifest preimage is exactly `{environmentId,generationDecimal,priorManifestDigest,checkpointRootDigest,segmentRootDigest,databaseTailSequenceDecimal,databaseTailRootDigest,checkpointLineageMapDigest,capabilityDeliveryStateDigest,runtimeEgressFenceStateDigest,retirementStateDigest,helperControlDigest,checkpointTerminalAccumulatorDigest,keyringDigest,globalStateDigest}` and `redisClientGenerationManifestDigest=D('noli:redis-client-generation-manifest:v1',generationManifestPreimage)`. `redisClientRecordGenesis=D('noli:redis-client-record-genesis:v1',{environmentId,contract:'spec-065-v1'})`, `redisClientCheckpointGenesis=D('noli:redis-client-checkpoint-genesis:v1',{environmentId,contract:'spec-065-v1'})`, `redisClientManifestGenesis=D('noli:redis-client-generation-manifest-genesis:v1',{environmentId,contract:'spec-065-v1'})`, the already-defined `redisClientHelperGateGenesis`, and `redisClientCheckpointTerminalAccumulatorGenesis=D('noli:redis-client-checkpoint-terminal-accumulator-genesis:v1',{environmentId,contract:'spec-065-v1'})`; no implicit empty or ellipsis domain exists. `CURRENT` is exact UTF-8 RFC8785 JCS `{version:1,generationDecimal,manifestDigest}` plus one LF and no other bytes.

All decimal fields above are canonical nonnegative strings unless explicitly positive; UUIDs are lowercase; timestamps are canonical UTC milliseconds; digests/domains are literal; object keys and null rules are closed; and arrays use the stated order before JCS. Cross-language golden and negative vectors cover every preimage, raw zero byte, order, empty/genesis/root step, signed-versus-unsigned boundary, registration-time equality, inventory and retirement equality, uint64 limits, capsule null matrices/2,048-byte boundary with maximum-length identifiers, map/checkpoint/segment/manifest/CURRENT splice, and every unknown/duplicate/alternate encoding.

Every container/one-shot starts behind a bootstrap barrier. Before a successful controller-persisted runtime-start claim and exact role/manifest/pool/ACL/origin verification, it may open only its registry-owned claim database client—which occupies one of the role's already-budgeted ordinary slots—and its local nonready health endpoint; that client is synchronously transferred as the first ordinary pooled connection or closed with exact `pg_stat_activity` zero before any other pool/lock client exists, and it cannot bind public/control/MCP ports, construct Redis/provider clients, load provider secrets, run DI startup hooks, claim/produce jobs, or mutate domain data. The controller releases the serving gate only after the claim is durable; timeout or controller loss closes and zero-proves it before an effect-free exit. Tests pause the controller after container start with seeded queues and requests and prove zero binds, claims, schedules, writes, or calls and a full-fleet startup/restart peak no higher than 113 backends.

Its root store lives on a dedicated mode-`0700` persistent volume/path and uses checksummed append records plus write-temp/fsync/atomic-rename/directory-fsync before any success response. Root-secret material uses a versioned environment keyring, never the application digest keyring. After the explicit uninitialized first-install state, it contains exactly one active and at most one retiring 32-byte AES-256-GCM key. Active key ID is literal `k` plus the positive canonical keyring-generation decimal; a retiring key, when present, uses the immediately prior generation, so the never-rewound generation makes ID reuse impossible. A second rotation is forbidden until the retiring key has zero references and is removed; generation `9223372036854775807` is exhausted and blocks candidate creation before any nonce, recovery write, or external effect. Sealed values are exact `{version:1,algorithm:'AES-256-GCM',keyId,nonceBase64url,ciphertextBase64url,tagBase64url}` with a 96-bit nonce equal to the per-key positive monotonic counter encoded as exactly 12-byte big-endian/base64url-no-padding. Allocation increment-one advances that key's `0..79228162514264337593543950335` nonce high-water in the same prepared-root/database-tail CAS before sealing or returning bytes; rollback/reuse is impossible, exhaustion requires rotation before allocation, and no per-seal registry row exists. It uses a 128-bit tag, and RFC8785-JCS associated data `{environmentId,purpose,subjectId,runtimeIdOrNull,runtimeGenerationOrNull,roleOrNull,clientSlotIdOrNull,generationOrNull}`. It seals only undelivered slot capabilities, connection challenges, helper-observation keys, helper-permit credentials, admin-claim credentials, and the active/retiring emergency credential under the six exact AAD forms above. The bounded keyring, fixed nonce high-waters, initialized flag, nonnegative keyring generation, and keyring digest use the same fsync/checkpoint protocol and exact-match the protected runtime-policy control-row triplets. Genesis has generation zero and no key; the fenced, recovery-verified one-shot activation tail-anchors `k1` before any claim or readiness. Before any first-activation, rotation, or retiring-removal recovery write, the controller fsyncs the sole bounded per-environment `KeyringCandidateIntentV1` exact record `{operationKind:'activate'|'rotate'|'retiring_remove',operationId,priorKeyringStateDigest,priorCommittedCopyManifestDigestOrNull,candidateCopyGenerationDecimal,candidateKeyringGenerationDecimal,candidateKeyId,candidateRootKeyDigest,sealedCandidateKeyDigestOrNull,hostRecoveryKeyId,hostRecoveryKeyVersion,recoveryEncryptionAlgorithm:'AES-256-GCM',recoveryNonceBase64url,recoveryTagBase64url,candidateStagingPath,finalImmutableRecoveryPath,encryptedRecoveryCopyBytesBase64url,recoveryCopyBytesDigest,keyringRecoveryCopyDigest,keyringRecoveryRestoreProofDigestOrNull,liveSealedReferenceSetDigest,maintenanceFenceId,controllerGenerationDecimal,manifestDigest,phase:'candidate_bound'|'material_verified'}`. `candidateCopyGenerationDecimal` is exactly prior copy high-water+1 and `finalImmutableRecoveryPath` is the manifest-derived immutable `keyring-copy-g<candidateCopyGenerationDecimal>-<operationId>.enc`; exhaustion blocks before bind. Activate/rotate require candidate key generation=prior keyring generation+1, the corresponding `kN` ID/root digest, and nonnull sealed-candidate digest; retiring-remove requires candidate key generation/ID/root digest equal the unchanged current active tuple and sealed-candidate null. `priorCommittedCopyManifestDigestOrNull` is null iff activate at genesis; rotate/remove require it nonnull and byte-equal `keyringCommittedCopyManifestDigest` of the current manifest. `recoveryCopyBytesDigest=SHA256(exact staged encrypted bytes)` and is the rollback leaf's staging-bytes digest. `keyringCandidateIntentDigest=D('noli:redis-client-keyring-candidate-intent:v1',completeExactIntent)`; candidate bind below installs it. `sealedCandidateKeyDigestOrNull` is nonnull for activate/rotate and equals `D('noli:redis-client-keyring-sealed-candidate:v1',{operationId,candidateKeyId,candidateRootKeyDigest,hostRecoveryKeyId,hostRecoveryKeyVersion,recoveryNonceBase64url,recoveryTagBase64url,recoveryCopyBytesDigest})`; it is null for retiring-remove, so it never creates an uncounted retiring-key reference. `keyringRecoveryCopyDigest=D('noli:redis-client-keyring-recovery-copy:v1',{environmentId,operationKind,operationId,priorCommittedCopyManifestDigestOrNull,candidateCopyGenerationDecimal,candidateKeyringGenerationDecimal,candidateKeyId,candidateRootKeyDigest,hostRecoveryKeyId,hostRecoveryKeyVersion,recoveryEncryptionAlgorithm,recoveryNonceBase64url,recoveryTagBase64url,finalImmutableRecoveryPath,recoveryCopyBytesDigest,liveSealedReferenceSetDigest})`; the host recovery key version is a positive canonical decimal from the installed manifest, nonce is the next committed 96-bit big-endian high-water encoded as 16 base64url characters, tag is exactly 16 bytes/22 characters, and the closed encrypted payload is `{schema:'noli.keyring-recovery-copy',version:1,environmentId,keyIdsAndRawKeysSorted,liveSealedReferenceSetDigest}` with AAD `{environmentId,operationId,operationKind,hostRecoveryKeyId,hostRecoveryKeyVersion,finalImmutableRecoveryPath}`. Intent/ciphertext is capped at 128 KiB; staging is UUID-specific create-exclusive and cannot equal/overwrite the committed immutable path; its nonce is burned on every rollback. `liveSealedReferenceSetDigest=D('noli:redis-client-live-sealed-reference-set:v1',members)` where members are the complete six-purpose sealed-secret projection sorted by `(purpose,subjectId,generationDecimal,keyId,sealedValueDigest)` and rechecked unchanged in the publication CAS; rotation retains existing ciphertext under the retiring key and seals only new values under active, never nondeterministically reseals. Each kind has a unique fsynced prepared record exactly equal to its digest preimage plus candidate-intent digest, accepts only its named OLD→NEW projection/changed-field mask, and consumes its proof once; DB-old restores the prior pointer and rolls back staging, DB-new completes marker/pointer/manifest publication and idempotent deletion. Missing key, key-ID/generation mismatch, second rotation during overlap, nonce-high-water rollback/reuse/overflow, tag/AAD swap, rollback, corrupt backup, response loss, restart, and restore all fail closed without regenerating a secret. The Redis-client lineage subjournal is fixed-size, not an unbounded history. Its snapshot includes every live claim envelope; every terminal claim that cannot yet compact because a database reference remains; every uncommitted identity/fence raw artifact; every signed Redis-server retirement proof with exact old-run/container key, live claim/database reference count, and consumption state until zero, plus its fixed old-run accumulator after compaction; creation, reference consume/release, and compaction are tail-anchored, and restart before first or last claimant use retains verifiable full signed bytes; every live member of the exact six-purpose AEAD sealed-secret set, including unconsumed connection challenges, undelivered capability sets, observation keys, replayable helper/admin credentials, and active/retiring emergency credentials with reference counts; every live runtime's closed delivered `{capabilityDigest -> manifestOrdinal/role/slot/kind}` map, set-delivery acknowledgment/tombstone state, and termination/zero-call retention gate; all pending/active helper-gate requests, permits, one-use authenticated-observation keys/nonces, completion tombstones, and fixed replay accumulator/high-water; each fixed per-lineage terminal accumulator; every monotonic fence-attempt chain; the exact 49-lineage generation-high-water map; the global journal sequence; and the prior checkpoint root. Once the registrar has committed a receipt/terminal handoff digest and the database cumulative chain owns its immutable claim/receipt leaf, the controller may replace the raw artifact/full terminal record with a fixed at-most-2,048-byte capsule, but that capsule is only a crash-recovery staging object. The lineage remains allocation-barred until the exact terminal-accumulator step is committed in both the root record and its database lineage row and the staged capsule is deleted. At most one terminal capsule may exist per lineage, and no successor claim generation may be allocated while it exists; thus the numeric worst case is exactly 49 staged capsules. Uncommitted artifacts remain limited by the two slot-consuming claims per lineage. Proof-bearing preparation is atomic. `PreparedProofNonceMemberV1` is exact `{nonceKind:'signed_artifact'|'retirement_proof'|'replacement_absence'|'helper_closure'|'candidate_intent',noncePurpose:'receipt_nonce'|'candidate_recovery_nonce',ownerId,nonceDigest}` with `nonceDigest=D('noli:redis-client-prepared-proof-nonce:v1',{nonceKind,noncePurpose,ownerId,rawNonce})`; `candidate_recovery_nonce` is legal only with `candidate_intent`, and every other kind requires `receipt_nonce`. `PreparedProofReferenceMemberV1` is exact `{referenceKind:'signed_artifact_raw'|'signing_key'|'retirement_proof_raw'|'helper_closure_raw'|'replacement_absence_raw'|'candidate_intent_raw'|'candidate_staging'|'recovery_material',ownerId,artifactDigestOrNull}`; `artifactDigestOrNull` is null iff `referenceKind='signing_key'`, whose `ownerId` is the exact signing-key ID, and is otherwise the referenced canonical artifact digest. `retirementProofDigestsSorted` has 0..4 unique canonical digests and `helperClosureDigestsSorted` has 0..16, each in ascending UTF-8 byte order. `admittedNoncesSorted` has 0..23 unique members sorted by UTF-8 byte order of `(nonceKind,noncePurpose,ownerId,nonceDigest)`; `acquiredReferencesSorted` has 2..26 unique members sorted by UTF-8 byte order of `(referenceKind,ownerId,artifactDigestOrNullOrEmpty)`. Duplicate tuples, duplicate `(nonceKind,noncePurpose,ownerId)` nonce sources, or duplicate `(referenceKind,ownerId)` resources are invalid. At preparation `acquiredReferencesSorted` byte-equals this exact union: `{referenceKind:'signed_artifact_raw',ownerId:operationId,artifactDigestOrNull:signedArtifactDigest}`; `{referenceKind:'signing_key',ownerId:signingKeyId,artifactDigestOrNull:null}`; for each retirement digest `R`, `{referenceKind:'retirement_proof_raw',ownerId:R,artifactDigestOrNull:R}`; for each helper-closure digest `H`, `{referenceKind:'helper_closure_raw',ownerId:H,artifactDigestOrNull:H}`; when replacement absence digest `A` is nonnull, `{referenceKind:'replacement_absence_raw',ownerId:operationId,artifactDigestOrNull:A}`; and when candidate-intent digest `C` is nonnull, exactly `{referenceKind:'candidate_intent_raw',ownerId:operationId,artifactDigestOrNull:C}`, `{referenceKind:'candidate_staging',ownerId:operationId,artifactDigestOrNull:C}`, and `{referenceKind:'recovery_material',ownerId:operationId,artifactDigestOrNull:C}`. At preparation `admittedNoncesSorted` byte-equals this exact union, with each member's `nonceDigest` recomputed by the formula above from the named raw nonce: the primary signed artifact's `receiptNonce` as `{nonceKind:'signed_artifact',noncePurpose:'receipt_nonce',ownerId:signedArtifactDigest,nonceDigest}`; each retirement proof `R`'s `receiptNonce` as `{nonceKind:'retirement_proof',noncePurpose:'receipt_nonce',ownerId:R,nonceDigest}`; each helper closure `H`'s outer `receiptNonce` as `{nonceKind:'helper_closure',noncePurpose:'receipt_nonce',ownerId:H,nonceDigest}`; the nonnull replacement-absence artifact `A`'s `receiptNonce` as `{nonceKind:'replacement_absence',noncePurpose:'receipt_nonce',ownerId:A,nonceDigest}`; and the nonnull candidate intent `C`'s exact `recoveryNonceBase64url` as `{nonceKind:'candidate_intent',noncePurpose:'candidate_recovery_nonce',ownerId:C,nonceDigest}`. A member is present exactly when its named source object is present; each source contributes exactly one member, and no source may be encoded under another kind or purpose. Only these owner-admitted fields are included: helper body `requestNonce`, request/generation high-waters, AEAD allocation nonces, and every other nonce already owned by a prior state are explicitly excluded. Both arrays are immutable and checkpointed. `PreparedProofOwnerV1` records `{operationId,preparedTailSequenceDecimal,signedArtifactKind,signedArtifactDigest,signingKeyId,retirementProofDigestsSorted,helperClosureDigestsSorted,replacementAbsenceDigestOrNull,candidateIntentDigestOrNull,preOperationExternalStateDigestOrNull,admittedNoncesSorted,acquiredReferencesSorted,state:'prepared'|'committed'}`. `preOperationExternalStateDigestOrNull` is nonnull exactly for lifecycle-operation admission and byte-equals the closed external-state snapshot stored in the active projection; it is null for every other owner. `preparedProofOwnerDigest=D('noli:redis-client-prepared-proof-owner:v1',{operationId,preparedTailSequenceDecimal,signedArtifactKind,signedArtifactDigest,signingKeyId,retirementProofDigestsSorted,helperClosureDigestsSorted,replacementAbsenceDigestOrNull,candidateIntentDigestOrNull,preOperationExternalStateDigestOrNull,admittedNoncesSorted,acquiredReferencesSorted})`; mutable `state` is excluded, so prepared→committed does not change the digest. In one fsynced transition it stores the receipt raw bytes, acquires its signing-key reference, and acquires the complete zero-through-four retirement-proof and other raw references; partial acquisition is impossible. `proof_preparation_rollback` is legal only while the database remains at the recorded OLD tuple and after exact restoration of pre-operation external state; its `tombstonedNoncesSorted` and `releasedReferencesSorted` must byte-equal the owner's two immutable arrays. In one idempotent transition it tombstones every admitted nonce, releases precisely the acquired proof/key references, deletes receipt/helper/absence raw bytes and candidate staging/recovery material, advances `D('noli:redis-client-proof-preparation-rollback:v1',{priorRootOrGenesis,sequenceDecimal,operationId,preparedProofOwnerDigest,releasedReferencesSorted,tombstonedNoncesSorted,rolledBackAt})`, and deletes the owner. After database commit `proof_preparation_rollback` is forbidden. For lifecycle-operation admission, the committed owner and both arrays remain checkpointed throughout the initial abortable phase: `redis_container_operation_abort` consumes the complete arrays and deletes the owner, while the first non-abortable stage consumes/releases its named members and deletes the owner only after that stage's marker. For every other proof-bearing transition, the success marker releases the identical complete set after terminal accumulation. Checkpoint includes every live prepared/committed owner and rollback root. Before acknowledging **every** generation allocation, challenge or capability-set delivery/ack/tombstone/compaction, identity registration, command bind/result reconciliation, retire/fence/close, helper-gate/readiness/admin recovery, retirement-proof creation/reference/compaction, runtime-egress create/replace/terminal-remove/state-compaction, AEAD nonce/keyring/emergency-credential rotation, and terminal compaction transition, the controller writes/fsyncs a prepared root record at tail `S+1`. For each bind, normal-result fold, fence commitment, or later fence fold, the matching fixed registrar function acquires locks only in the order control row → manifest-derived lineage row → owning protected row, then atomically CASes that owner, the control-policy tail from `(S,tailRoot)` to `(S+1,newTailRoot)`, and exactly that one lineage row in one database transaction. Fence commitment and fence fold are two explicit consecutive prepared records/transactions as defined above; neither is split into an unanchored database-only or root-only mutation. Every prepared record carries one authenticated, closed transition variant. `public_chat_redis_client_commit_root_v1(kind='tail_transition',variant='global_anchor')` locks and CASes only the control row and accepts exactly the literal closed global-kind registry below, not a second prose whitelist; each capability, runtime-egress, AEAD/keyring/emergency-credential, helper/readiness/admin, and retirement subtype updates only its exact fixed scalar digest/high-water/readiness fields and requires all lineage coordinates null. Variant `lineage_anchor` locks the control row plus exactly the manifest-derived lineage row for claim allocation/challenge/identity/retire/close/unproved-fence/per-lineage compaction, updates only its fixed claim/high-water/accumulator fields, and requires a nonnull exact role/slot/ordinal; generation allocation additionally advances the lineage high-water. `command_anchor` is not callable through this generic function and exists only inside the fixed bind/result/fence registrar transaction described above, always with the same control → lineage → owner lock order. `checkpoint` is the only multi-lineage variant and locks all 49 rows in manifest order. Variant/subtype, role, slot, ordinal, owner, old/new digests, and changed-column mask are derived from the authenticated prepared record and database tuple, never caller-selected; a global transition cannot alter a lineage, and a lineage transition cannot alter another/global-only state. The control-row lineage-map digest is explicitly the checkpoint projection, not a current map: after any later transition, startup/readiness begins from that checkpoint map, verifies and replays every anchored tail record through the database tail sequence, and requires the resulting 49 entries to exact-match the current lineage rows. The tail root and affected fixed row are current and may never lag a command, fence telemetry, registration, retire, close, or compaction transition. The controller then fsync-marks that exact prepared record committed before returning success. DB-old/root-prepared discards; DB-new/root-prepared commits; any missing/conflicting prepared record or root rollback behind the DB tail fails closed. An isolated real-PostgreSQL soak on the one registrar connection must sustain at least 20,000 such single-transaction transitions per minute for 24 hours while the configured route admits at most 16,384, with p99 queueing inside the stated command/helper deadlines and bounded WAL, TOAST-free rows, dead tuples, vacuum lag, and table/index bytes under the declared root/database budget. Thus the database anchors every safety transition, not merely periodic checkpoints. After at most 1,024 claim/register/bind/reconcile/fence/helper-gate transitions or 8 MiB since its prior checkpoint, the controller takes one global Redis-subjournal append barrier. It acknowledges no transition after the frozen sequence while held; bounded callers wait/retry without effect authority. The healthy barrier budget is one database-time second. Under that barrier it writes a canonical checkpoint of at most 64 MiB plus an empty digest-anchored segment, fsyncs both, fsyncs the generation manifest, then fsyncs the prepared generation directory and its parent before any database change. It then calls `public_chat_redis_client_commit_root_v1(kind='checkpoint')`, which atomically CASes old `(redis_client_tail_sequence=S, redis_client_tail_root_digest=oldTail, prior checkpoint sequence/root)` to `(redis_client_tail_sequence=S, redis_client_tail_root_digest=newCheckpointRoot, redis_client_checkpoint_sequence=S, redis_client_checkpoint_root_digest=newCheckpointRoot)`, while locking the 49 lineage rows in manifest order, exact-verifying their canonical map and terminal-accumulator-set digests, storing them as `redis_client_checkpoint_lineage_map_digest` and `redis_client_checkpoint_terminal_accumulator_digest`, and recomputing/storing `redis_client_global_state_digest` over the new checkpoint terminal digest in that same CAS; no 49-entry JSON value is rewritten per command. The empty new segment's genesis prior root is exactly `newCheckpointRoot`, so the first prepared append is `S+1` over that value; only afterward does one atomic rename publish a tiny `CURRENT` pointer followed by directory fsync. A crash before the database CAS discards the unpublished generation; a crash after it but before pointer publication exact-matches the prepared generation and completes publication. Only after both stores agree may the prior generation be unlinked and the barrier released; queued transitions then append only to the published new segment before receiving success. A crash on any boundary therefore has no acknowledged post-snapshot append that is unreachable from the database-selected generation. The database mirror makes wholesale rollback to an older internally valid root fail closed even for Worker-only lineages; fixtures restore the last checkpoint after exactly one and 1,023 post-checkpoint transitions, including a live registered socket, and startup refuses reuse. Peak storage honestly includes two 64-MiB published checkpoints, one 64-MiB prepared checkpoint, two 8-MiB segments, and bounded manifests/capsules under a 256-MiB hard volume/admission watermark; effect admission pauses before the checkpoint or artifact bound is exceeded while reconciliation/compaction remains served. Recovery accepts exactly one monotonic database/root/pointer/segment chain; stale snapshot, high-water rollback, ABA, torn pointer rename, lost directory fsync, deletion-before-publish, the first post-checkpoint append, and every claim/register/bind/result/fence/gate/egress transition racing each prepare/DB-CAS/pointer/unlink boundary fail or resume without a lost acknowledged state. A 24-hour soak at the maximum 16,384 bind/reconcile operations per minute with long-lived `registered_current` clients, the exact worst-case 49 retained 2,048-byte terminal capsules, and periodic crashes stays below 256 MiB and preserves every live root/database reconciliation fact. Startup verifies monotonic sequence/checksums, reconciles every partial root-store/database commit through the exact idempotent status/CAS protocols, reacquires the maintenance-fence authority, and fails local health closed on corruption or unknown state; it never rewrites a conflicting record. During deployment the controller drains last and remains available to attest, provision/demote identities, resolve death, and finish acknowledgment/Noli commits; its own upgrade uses a second root-owned maintenance fence and complete recovery before data-plane readiness. Tests restart/crash it before/after every fsync and DB CAS, steal/swap each socket credential, attempt Docker-socket escape/arbitrary exec/mount/image substitution, corrupt/truncate/reorder the root store, rotate keys/three DSNs, and prove recovery or fail-closed behavior without duplicate signatures, false termination, or unobserved process authority.

All queue-capable services receive literal `QUEUE_STRATEGY=async` plus a role-specific secret-backed Redis URL containing a nonempty ACL username and password; the shared Redis parser and async queue adapter preserve both fields, require and preserve verified TLS options, redact them from errors/logs/config output, and forbid the current production localhost fallback. There is no local-memory/file/default-user transport. Redis is a reviewed version and image digest in the manifest, private Docker-network only with no host port, TLS 1.3 on `tls-port` with plaintext `port 0`, per-environment root-owned CA/server key and fixed SAN/server-name verification for every client, overlap-tested certificate rotation/expiry readiness, persistent AOF on a permission-restricted backed-up volume, `appendfsync everysec`, finite `maxmemory` below the host/cgroup reserve, `maxmemory-policy noeviction`, and AOF disk free-space/watermark readiness. AOF acknowledgment is not accepted as business durability: every enabled producer recovers from the protected database outbox/source described above.

One injected process-scoped registry caches BullMQ Queue objects and shares one producer/control command client per queue-capable process; every Worker uses exactly one command and one blocking client per consumed queue, no QueueEvents client exists unless separately manifested, and all are closed on drain. Raw `new Queue`, `new Worker`, `new QueueEvents`, `new IORedis`, per-request/per-event connection creation, and unclosed clients fail static generation and readiness. Exact steady-state clients are web 1, control 1, MCP 1, public target 3, generic scheduler 3, global public-chat pager worker 3, delivery 7, search 7, workflow 5, account-cleanup 7, payment 9, durable outbox dispatcher 1, and strict reconciler 1: 49 total. The outbox dispatcher count is its one ordinary data client. The 20 admin/health/failure reserve is partitioned into the persisted shared 16-permit registration/fence gate, two slots for root-broker active+ambiguous-replacement state, and two slots for readiness/emergency active+ambiguous-replacement state; provisioned helper clients are included in—not added to—that reserve. Redis `maxclients` is pinned to exactly 128: every one of the 49 steady slots has its own controller root-store lineage, a full partition may leave at most 49 first-generation sockets half-open while at most 49 second-generation replacements connect, and the 20 broker/admin/readiness/registration/fence clients must still work (`49+49+20=118`, leaving 10 additional hard reserve). The root controller installs and fingerprints host bridge/firewall connection ceilings before container start: each data-plane container source identity may hold no more concurrent Redis TLS connections than that runtime's manifested steady slot count, old and replacement runtimes each retain only their own count, the helper subnet is capped at 16, the broker identity at two, and readiness/emergency identity at two. Rules live in the host `DOCKER-USER`/nftables chain keyed by controller-observed container cgroup/IP and fail closed on identity/rule drift; a compromised container can occupy only its own already-budgeted slots, not exhaust fleet/admin capacity. Startup refuses any other value; the bounded helper parser refuses more than 128 records or 96 KiB, and a full-fleet asymmetric half-open/replacement test plus simultaneous broker-response and first-emergency-response loss proves the reserved replacement remains available while neither a data nor broker lineage admits a third client. Repeated clean drain and lost QUIT/close acknowledgment across every producer/control/Worker command/Worker blocking slot must either obtain same-run exact-ID absence and compact normally or consume one of its two lineage generations—never accumulate an untracked socket. Every envelope has the manifested byte/depth/cardinality/retention/backlog cap before allocation, enqueue, and claim. High-volume request/event and hostile raw-connection tests keep `CLIENT LIST` flat at the per-container/role and global caps through half-open replacement; oversize/nested payloads and full queues fail one edge without exhausting Redis memory/AOF disk or blocking other queues.

Every manifested role is health-gated on its authenticated ACL and exact BullMQ command/key-prefix access for only its queue group and exact BullMQ version. Redis ACL is explicitly prefix/command isolation, not semantic producer-versus-consumer authority because BullMQ scripts share commands and keys; the protected database candidate view, ID/digest-only Redis envelope, claim/grant/CAS capabilities, and reconciler are the actual authority boundary. A compromised role may corrupt only its allowed transport prefix and consume only its externally enforced manifested connection allotment; it cannot read protected payloads, exhaust another role/helper reserve, or claim/settle another database execution, and exact reconciliation repairs or quarantines the transport. Real-Redis tests prove each role can perform required producer, consumer, blocking, delayed, pause/drain, and status commands while cross-group queues/commands/default-user authentication fail. Every data-plane ACL denies `CLIENT KILL`, `CLIENT LIST`, and broad administrative `CLIENT`. Every exact owner of one of the 49 manifested client slots—including producer/control, Worker command, and Worker blocking slots—receives only `CLIENT|SETNAME`, `CLIENT|ID`, and read-only `INFO` in addition to that slot's BullMQ-required non-admin commands. Its generated fixed adapter sets only the claim challenge name, invokes literal `INFO SERVER`→canonical `run_id` and `CLIENT ID`→canonical ID on the same nonreconnecting socket, and registers the resulting identity before any BullMQ command or block. Because Redis ACL cannot limit `INFO` by section, compromise of any slot owner may read the server's non-secret INFO metadata; the threat/readiness model explicitly accepts and inventories that disclosure for all 49 slots while keys, payloads, credentials, client inventory, kill, mutation outside required scripts, and cross-prefix authority remain unavailable. Roles with no manifested Redis slot deny the complete identity preflight, and only exact effectful producer roles receive controller command-binding authority. Only the root-owned one-use helper credential can perform fixed registration inventory or fence inventory/kill, and it is destroyed after the signed receipt. Positive and negative real-Redis ACL fixtures exercise SETNAME/INFO/ID and exact expected ACL-user/role/slot registration for every manifested slot, reject wrong challenges and cross-slot/user IDs, and reject identity preflight, LIST, KILL, raw cross-prefix commands, and helper credentials for every role without that slot. All data-plane containers set `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `no-new-privileges`, no host networking, no `NET_RAW`, and manifest-exact egress; the controller inventories effective capabilities and networks. The control container joins a distinct internal control network reachable only by nginx and its exact bind-mounted controller client sockets; web/MCP/target-worker/generic-scheduler/strict-schedule/delivery/search/workflow/account-cleanup/payment-worker/outbox-dispatcher/reconciler/retention data-plane networks have no route to `control:3002`. Nginx exposes only exact mTLS/fleet-authenticated control locations, strips every caller-supplied proxy-identity header, adds one secret/certificate-bound proxy assertion unavailable to other containers, and forwards to control. Control independently verifies that assertion plus end-to-end Noli service identity/signed artifact or exact active GDPR operation before body-derived authority; every other path is denied, port 3002 has no host binding, `AUTO_SPAWN_WORKERS=false`, and ordinary app returns `404` for internal paths. The controller inventories Redis config/image/volume/client budget plus every service command, effective worker concurrency/handler/retry set, image, replica, network, queue, database role, origin fingerprint, and runtime attestation in preinstall/deployment/drain receipts. A hostile low-trust container cannot sniff/ARP-spoof or route to another role's plaintext because Redis/PostgreSQL TCP is verified TLS; fixtures attempt packet capture, ARP spoofing, cross-network reachability, certificate substitution, and extra TLS connections from every role before/during half-open replacement. Any floating/digest-mismatched image, incomplete client/ACL/backlog budget, unreadable/ephemeral/evicting Redis, or AOF/disk/memory readiness failure blocks deployment.

Email attachments use one controller-inventoried authoritative volume and canonical path, replacing the divergent `process.cwd()/storage/attachments` versus `/uploads` assumptions. Only the exact app/control writer receives the required write mount; the delivery role receives a read-only mount and no path outside it. Ownership/mode, backup/restore, byte digest, retention/GDPR deletion, legacy-path migration, and volume/image/topology fingerprints are deployment evidence. Upload, restart/recreate, delivery with attachment, missing/corrupt byte failure, and GDPR row-plus-byte deletion are end-to-end fixtures; silently skipping an attachment is forbidden.

The independent strict reconciler is not a BullMQ worker and never depends on generic `scheduler-execution`. It owns one fenced singleton lease and four bounded duties in fixed order: run the global at-most-25/5-second processable-reservation release slice from the quota-environment cursor; repair/prove the one system pager row plus canonical Job Scheduler/current-next identities while proving zero per-scope recurring transport; reconcile the at-most-40 generation-fenced population children against the desired/strict/quota/unreleased-processable union and scope rows with `<=4` per tenant; and repair pager/scope ambiguity through exact liveness/transport absence. Its cursor advances past every blocker and completes a healthy full scope pass within 40 minutes. The pager worker alone selects/enqueues one scope target per fire; the generic worker rejects every public owner/queue. Redis outage is observable/degraded, never guessed absence. Real-Redis tests flush scheduler state, saturate all 40 scopes, hold corrupt/locked scope and release rows, sustain generic backlog, restart each service, and prove both cursor wraps/recovery, the seven-minute all-unlocked release drain, exactly one global scheduler, 45-minute healthy target-start bound, 4+1 target isolation, and no duplicate provider attempt.

Graceful shutdown is part of correctness. Web/MCP first fail readiness and stop accepting new requests, with a 60-second grace and no background claims. The private control API fails readiness/stops new operations but retains exact in-flight fence/finalizer work with a 300-second grace. The generic scheduler service first stops beginning materializer ticks and finishes only its current short row transaction, then public target, its generic C1 worker, global pager worker, and all five least-privilege groups pause every BullMQ intake, move no-permit active jobs back to delayed with the version-pinned token transition, prove zero claimed waiters, refuse every new grant/child, keep each permit-owning session-lock connection and abortable client alive through bounded no-more-side-effects settlement, and have `stop_grace_period: 300s`, exceeding the 240-second invocation plus settlement reserve. The retention daemon stops beginning ticks and finishes only its current transaction within 60 seconds. The strict reconciler and durable outbox dispatcher stop opening scopes/pages/rows, persist their cursors, and finish only the current bounded row/transport-plus-CAS unit within a 60-second grace; a page is never the shutdown unit. The controller waits for signed drain evidence; if a process exceeds grace it records exact force termination and issues the matching runtime termination receipt before cleanup may rely on death. Routine deploy, SIGTERM, Redis restart/power-loss, and image replacement tests prove no avoidable 4,200-second ambiguity, late call, or lost acknowledged business work.

### PostgreSQL privilege boundary

Production never gives an application container the cluster bootstrap/owner credential. The audited role transition creates NOLOGIN `crm_database_owner`, `crm_schema_owner`, and `crm_guard_owner` roles, transfers `ALTER DATABASE crm OWNER` to the first, ordinary schemas/tables/sequences to the second, and security/guard/`SECURITY DEFINER` objects to the third. A one-shot LOGIN `crm_migrator` is `NOINHERIT` and may `SET ROLE` only to those three owners plus the nonprivileged `crm_runtime_role_policy_owner` while the controller maintenance fence is held; it can never `SET ROLE crm_runtime_role_executor`, and exact membership/`SET` option/ACL fingerprints are readiness evidence; outside that one-shot it is `NOLOGIN`/expired and unmounted. Runtime privilege templates are separately enumerated for app, private control (GDPR/finalizer/Noli cancellation only), MCP, public worker, generic scheduler, global public-chat pager worker, delivery, search, workflow, account-cleanup, payment, durable-outbox-dispatcher, strict reconciler, and retention daemon, and every data-plane process start/restart/one-shot receives a **fresh never-reused directly granted LOGIN principal and secret**, with a controller-derived allow-listed name such as `crm_app_p_<opaque-runtime-suffix>`; per-service or per-deployment shared identities and stable runtime passwords are forbidden. The public app cannot execute GDPR/finalizer/cancellation capabilities, and the control runtime cannot execute ordinary public/widget/MCP/provider capabilities. Every login is `NOINHERIT NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOREPLICATION` and has no membership in an owner, migrator, bootstrap, another runtime, or controller role.

The host controller uses three non-overlapping NOLOGIN capability templates rather than bootstrap/migrator authority. `crm_runtime_registrar`, `crm_noli_artifact_controller`, and `crm_ack_controller` cannot authenticate directly. Initial offline installation—and thereafter the still-current fenced controller—provisions three fresh never-reused per-controller-generation LOGINs (`crm_controller_registrar_p_<opaque>`, `crm_controller_noli_p_<opaque>`, and `crm_controller_ack_p_<opaque>`) with only the corresponding template's direct grants, one connection each, short registration expiry, and separate generated secrets; old generations become `NOLOGIN`, lose grants, have backends terminated/zero-proved, and are retired before successor readiness. The registrar template has only `CONNECT`/schema `USAGE` plus fixed-search-path provision/demote/retire, typed receipt functions, the metadata-only Redis-fence/result candidate union, and the four exact bind/result-fold/fence/root-tail-or-checkpoint CAS functions; it cannot select/mutate base rows, choose an outcome, or run arbitrary role DDL. The Noli template has only `CONNECT`/`USAGE` plus kind-specific verified-artifact acceptance; the acknowledgment template has only `CONNECT`/`USAGE`, the security-barrier candidate view, and `public_chat_ack_commit_signed_v1`. None can cross routes, and stable controller passwords are forbidden. App/control/MCP/worker/scheduler roles cannot call any controller function except their one exact runtime-start claim capability. Before a process starts, the registrar persists and later binds its exact `session_user`, service role, environment, deployment generation, image, and signed runtime-start digest in the typed receipt ledger. Every ordinary capability function rederives the latest claimed mapping from `session_user` and exact-matches the active scope generation rather than accepting a caller's generation. Maintenance demotion sets old principals `NOLOGIN`/connection-limit zero, revokes their grants, terminates all pooled backends, and proves zero `pg_stat_activity` rows before enabling new principals; retirement promptly drops them after zero backends and a durable exact termination/aborted-provision fact; live leases and domain rows resolve later from that immutable fact and never require the catalog role; immutable receipts retain only principal text and keyed fingerprint with no `pg_authid`/ownership/membership/FK dependency. Registration/revocation/termination, Redis identity registration plus command bind/result-reconciliation/fence commitment/root-tail-and-checkpoint anchoring, Noli artifact acceptance, and signed-ack tests prove a hostile runtime cannot self-register, revoke a peer, forge death/Redis fence/signed Noli input, write a valid-looking identity/binding/result/fence/root-anchor commitment, or invoke a controller CAS.

A separate NOLOGIN `crm_runtime_role_executor` is the small stable provisioning trust root. It is nonsuperuser/no-bypass/no-database-create/no-replication, has only minimum `CREATEROLE`, exact runtime-template `GRANT OPTION`, and `pg_signal_backend` membership, owns only three fixed-search-path core functions, is never granted to a LOGIN, and is never mounted or reachable through `SET ROLE`. Provisioning first exact-checks live `password_encryption='scram-sha-256'` and the matching SCRAM-only `pg_hba.conf` fingerprint before generating/storing a verifier; drift creates no principal and blocks readiness, and a real provision/connect fixture proves the verifier is usable. A second NOLOGIN `crm_runtime_role_policy_owner` has no role attributes, `pg_signal_backend`, or grant option and owns only the generated service/template policy tables and pure validation/projection functions; the fenced migrator may `SET ROLE` only to this nonprivileged policy owner for ordinary policy migrations. The executor core independently enforces hard ceilings that policy cannot widen: generated opaque principal prefix, one exact template from an immutable executor allow-list, direct grants only, no owner/admin/default-role membership, bounded expiry and connection limit, safe identifier quoting, and fixed `LOGIN NOINHERIT NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOREPLICATION` attributes.

Registrar-only `public_chat_provision_runtime_principal_v1` accepts an allow-listed service role plus exact environment/deployment/runtime coordinates, derives the unique principal name itself, generates a 256-bit password internally, exact-matches the installed policy/body/ACL digests, installs the fixed direct-grant fingerprint, and returns the secret once over the root-owned controller channel for a mode-0600 mount; it accepts no caller role name, SQL, privilege list, membership, or password. A lost response makes that unclaimed principal unusable: the controller demotes it and provisions a different identity rather than reusing it. Registrar-only demotion sets the exact role `NOLOGIN CONNECTION LIMIT 0`, revokes its capability grants, terminates only matching backends, and proves zero sessions before a replacement may be created. Retirement promptly drops it after a durable exact termination/aborted-provision fact and zero backends; live leases and historical domain references retain only principal text/digest and resolve without the catalog role; receipt retention never depends on the catalog role. Each service/template, including the three controller routes and retention daemon, is capped at one live plus one retiring/unclaimed principal; a crash loop cannot provision a third until the retiring slot is safely removed. Dynamic SQL, statement/error/audit logging, controller root-store records, environment inspection, and crash paths redact the generated secret. Hostile service/name/Unicode/SQL inputs, grant escalation, direct registrar `CREATE/ALTER/DROP ROLE`, partial provisioning, lost-secret recovery, stale-backend termination, and premature drop tests all fail closed. Accelerated crash/restart soak tests bound `pg_authid`, controller root-store, and receipt rows while preserving historical principal text/digests.

Ordinary compatible policy upgrades never reactivate the bootstrap credential and cannot gain `CREATEROLE`: the fenced migrator updates only `crm_runtime_role_policy_owner` objects under exact expected old/new body, ACL, table, and migration-bundle digests, and may only narrow or reselect among executor-installed immutable privilege-set digests; it cannot name a new object/capability/grant. All core-policy compatibility fixtures pass before readiness. A new object privilege/GRANT OPTION or change to any stable executor core function or its owner/grants is **not** controller-automated. It requires a separately approved offline maintenance event with every data-plane/controller database client drained, a checked-in signed single-purpose SQL bundle, exact before/after fingerprints, local PostgreSQL operating-system administration rather than any reusable LOGIN or temporary owner membership, and immediate removal of that one-shot path before restart. The controller and Docker helper cannot invoke arbitrary SQL or create an upgrade LOGIN. Wrong digest, direct SQL via the registrar/migrator DSN, policy attempts to authorize arbitrary roles/grants or an otherwise valid new function/object, owner/ACL substitution, partial transaction, and post-upgrade registrar compatibility tests all fail closed.

`REVOKE CONNECT,TEMPORARY ON DATABASE crm FROM PUBLIC` is mandatory; `CONNECT` is regranted only to exact manifested roles, and no runtime/controller receives `TEMPORARY` (an audited migration one-shot may receive it only for a generated proven need and loses it before runtimes start). `PUBLIC` also loses schema creation plus existing and default table/sequence/function privileges. Every `SECURITY DEFINER` function has `EXECUTE` revoked from `PUBLIC`, exact `search_path=pg_catalog,<trusted-owned-schema>,pg_temp` with `pg_temp` explicitly last, and an enumerated caller grant; every relation, sequence, type, function, operator, cast, and dynamic target in its body is schema-qualified, while dynamic identifiers are internally derived, allow-listed, and safely quoted. Any unqualified dependency is a static-review/readiness failure. Runtime roles own no table, sequence, function, view, trigger, or schema and cannot alter/disable triggers, change `session_replication_role`, replace functions, grant privileges, or read another role's protected object. Ordinary allow-listed reads/writes are granted per service. Protected cutover, locator, job phase/subject, lease, receipt, acknowledgment, routing/config authority, lifecycle, association, Inbox graph, quota, and legacy-chat columns/tables have **no direct runtime DML grant**: one narrow owner-controlled definer routine derives scope from authenticated/server state, takes the complete ordered locks, re-reads OLD+NEW/database time, performs the exact column-diff mutation, and lets the trigger verify that function-owned transaction lane. Caller-settable custom GUC values are diagnostic context only and never authority; a caller that guesses every contract/generation/operation GUC still lacks direct DML and cannot make a definer routine accept a caller-derived scope. Trigger/private lane state is created and consumed only inside the routine and cannot outlive or cross its transaction.

PostgreSQL's raw advisory-lock surface is not a runtime capability. Reconciliation revokes `EXECUTE` from `PUBLIC` on every `pg_catalog.pg_advisory_lock*`, `pg_try_advisory_lock*`, `pg_advisory_xact_lock*`, `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock*`, shared variant, `pg_advisory_unlock*`, and `pg_advisory_unlock_all` overload for bigint and `(integer,integer)` keys; only the NOLOGIN guard/lock owner retains raw execution, with a narrowly documented migrator/controller exception where required. Runtime roles call fixed-search-path definer wrappers that accept typed authoritative coordinates rather than raw domains/keys, derive and exact-match `session_user`, active operation/scope/runtime registration, global order, nonblocking/timeout policy, and the manifested per-role bundle/cardinality cap before acquiring a complete sorted bundle. A caller cannot loop the wrapper across arbitrary valid resources, and release can unlock only its exact registered bundle on that backend. PostgreSQL upgrade/readiness fingerprints the complete `pg_proc` overload set and ACLs. Tests exercise every role/overload, known and guessed keys, repeated valid-wrapper exhaustion, shared/exclusive/xact/session paths, `unlock_all`, stale principals, and valid bounded acquire/release.

Compose uses service-specific allow-listed environment files and Docker secrets/credential files. App, private control, MCP, public worker, generic scheduler, global public-chat pager worker, all five least-privilege worker groups, durable-outbox-dispatcher, strict reconciler, retention daemon, and controller containers never receive `POSTGRES_USER`, the bootstrap password/DSN, a migration DSN, another service's password, or a common `.env.production` file containing them. Each runtime receives only its fresh process-specific one-use DSN; the controller receives separately mounted registrar/Noli-verifier/ack DSNs; image layers/config output never contain any DSN. The bootstrap credential remains only in initial PostgreSQL break-glass scope, is rotated after the existing-volume role transition, and is `NOLOGIN` outside a separately audited recovery procedure; migration credentials are unmounted and the migrator returns to `NOLOGIN` immediately after the fenced one-shot. Because `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` does not run for an existing volume, the reviewed deploy wrapper executes the idempotent database/schema/function ownership, role, default-ACL, credential-rotation, and login-state transition explicitly and records its fingerprint before guard install.

Startup and controller readiness exact-check `session_user`/`current_user`, its signed service/deployment mapping, `pg_roles` attributes and membership, role connection limits, every protected owner/ACL/default ACL, function owner/`prosecdef`/exact `proconfig`, fully qualified body dependencies/dynamic-target allow-lists, database CONNECT/TEMP ACL, complete advisory-lock `pg_proc` ACLs, view security-barrier/grants, process secret mounts/environment names, and absence of privileged DSNs. Tests connect as every actual runtime role and a still-pooled prior-generation role and attempt `SET ROLE`, forged `set_config` for every guard GUC followed by raw DML, wrong-scope/role capability calls, cross-role reads, direct protected INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, trigger disable/ALTER/DROP, `session_replication_role`, function replacement/search-path or temporary-table/type/operator shadowing, raw advisory-lock/try/shared/xact/unlock/unlock-all use and exhaustion, candidate-view/base-ledger overread, and GRANT/REVOKE; all fail, while each exact current-generation permitted definer entry point and controller view read succeeds. Any privilege/ownership/secret/session drift blocks enablement.

### Connection, advisory-lock, and shutdown budget

One central injected production pool registry owns **every** ORM, raw `pg`, event publisher/LISTEN, search/pgvector, transaction, session-lock, registrar/controller, and one-shot connection. An unregistered `new Pool`, `new Client`, default driver pool, per-module pool, or connection-string fallback is a forbidden pattern and startup inventory failure. Event publishers in every emitting role use that role's existing ordinary transaction lane for the protected row plus `pg_notify`; they never create a publisher pool. Only the web/SSE process enables the bridge and reserves one dedicated LISTEN client inside its role cap; all other roles reject bridge startup. Every container DSN connects directly to PostgreSQL with `ssl=on`, TCP plaintext rejected, `hostssl`-only SCRAM rules, TLS 1.3 `verify-full`, a root-owned environment CA/server key, exact SAN/manifested server name, and overlap-tested rotation/expiry readiness, or to a one-to-one session-mode proxy providing the same verified TLS and authenticated upstream; the host controller's permission-restricted local Unix socket is the sole non-TCP exception; transaction/statement pooling, forced-user pooling, multiplexing, and any proxy that changes `session_user` or backend affinity are forbidden.

With exactly one replica per launch service, hard maxima and physically separate settlement semaphores/lanes are: app 12 short connections (seven ordinary, four critical dispatch/settlement, one web-only LISTEN) plus four direct-dispatch session locks; private control six short (four ordinary, two finalizer/settlement) plus two lifecycle locks; MCP six total and no public admission/direct dispatch; public worker 12 short (seven ordinary, five settlement) plus five locks; delivery eight short (five ordinary, three settlement) plus three locks; search six short (four ordinary, two settlement) plus two locks; workflow four short (three ordinary, one settlement) plus one lock; account-cleanup four database-only short and zero settlement plus one lock; payment six short (four ordinary, two settlement) plus two locks; generic scheduler six short (four ordinary, two settlement) plus one lock; global public-chat pager worker six short (four ordinary, two settlement) plus one lock; strict reconciler four short (three ordinary, one settlement) plus one lock; durable outbox dispatcher four short (three ordinary, one transport-settlement) plus one lock; retention daemon two; and controller registrar/Noli-verifier/ack one connection each. Discovery/polling cannot check out a settlement lane. These totals are respectively 16+8+6+17+11+8+5+5+8+7+7+5+5+2+3 = **113** concurrent runtime connections. Migration uses at most two only while runtimes are drained. PostgreSQL `max_connections=160` is an exact pinned launch setting and leaves 47 connections unavailable to ordinary runtime work for health, administration, migration/drain, and failure settlement; exact per-principal `CONNECTION LIMIT`s, lane-specific pool configs, and exhaustion tests enforce the manifest.

A worker invocation uses **one** dedicated lock-pool connection to acquire its complete sorted execution/notification/scope advisory-lock set, including both notification users when distinct; it never opens one connection per lease or lock. Public HTTP admission likewise passes a four-slot direct-dispatch semaphore, obtains one of the four dedicated app lock connections plus one critical settlement permit before committing a dispatch binding, and otherwise accepts the durable message without granting/sending a direct nudge so the independent schedule recovers it. MCP cannot originate public admission or direct dispatch. A private-control link-lifecycle/GDPR/finalizer batch must first obtain one of its two dedicated lifecycle-lock connections plus one of the two reserved finalizer/settlement permits; it never borrows an ordinary transaction connection for the lock lifetime, and inability to obtain both starts no mutation. Before committing any external/local send grant, the owning role has both its lock connection and a permit from the phase's dedicated settlement pool; inability to obtain either within five seconds leaves work due without a grant or call. Once granted, the reserved settlement permit cannot be consumed by discovery, polling, or new work, so pool exhaustion cannot strand an already-sent effect. Connection loss triggers the existing no-new-side-effect/termination-proof rule.

Production enables no recursive/unbounded GDPR subject discovery. Every enabled worker has generated, fingerprinted exact organization/user subject paths, maximum subject cardinality, and maximum session-advisory-lock count in the role manifest. Per invocation the caps are: app direct dispatch 16, private control 40, public worker 16, every generic group child 40, generic scheduler 16, global public-chat pager worker 16, strict reconciler 40, durable outbox dispatcher 8, and controller registrar maintenance work 8; MCP, retention, controller Noli-verifier, and controller acknowledgment use zero session advisory locks. With the exact session-lock connection/concurrency caps above, the displayed worst case is app `4×16=64` + control `2×40=80` + public `5×16=80` + delivery `3×40=120` + search `2×40=80` + workflow `1×40=40` + account `1×40=40` + payment `2×40=80` + generic scheduler `1×16=16` + strict schedule `1×16=16` + reconciler `1×40=40` + dispatcher `1×8=8` + controller registrar `1×8=8` = **672 simultaneous session advisory locks**.

Public jobs have zero payload users and at most two trusted notification users. Private control and generic paged materializers process at most 32 users/targets per transaction. The complete bundle is derived and rejected before the first acquire; wrappers sort and nonblockingly acquire all locks on one session and insert all leases atomically or none. The pinned launch settings require `max_connections=160`, `max_locks_per_transaction>=64`, and `max_prepared_transactions=0`, yielding at least `64×(160+0)=10,240` lock-table entries by the PostgreSQL sizing rule. A generated SQL/transaction census reserves an additional hard **1,024** concurrent entries for relation, row-transaction, and transaction-advisory locks, including the retention daemon and generic schedule materializer transaction-scoped environment locks, so the manifested worst case is `672+1,024=1,696`, below one half (`5,120`) of capacity. Readiness recomputes these values from live settings and the complete manifest and fails on any exact-setting drift, lower computed capacity, higher consumer cap, unknown lock caller, or reserve overflow. Any future worker/SQL path must update the census; a wrapper-cap exhaustion test proves rejection before partial acquisition.

Pool/lock tests run more than four concurrent HTTP admissions/direct nudges, five simultaneous two-user alerts, the exact 3/2/1/1/2 concurrent worst-case 32-subject jobs in the five groups, two concurrent 32-user private-control batches, and generic-scheduler/strict-schedule/reconciler/dispatcher/controller work; exhaust every ordinary lane while proving reserved settlement remains available; terminate one lock connection; reach every wrapper cap; and prove fallback plus settlement of every already-granted effect. They also feed a 2,048-UUID legacy payload to five concurrent jobs, inject partial acquisition failure, and prove preflight rejection, zero partial leases, healthy GDPR/controller access, no deadlock, and eventual public progress. Startup tests reject the hidden raw max-5 pool, ORM default max-50 pool, per-module event publisher pool, non-web LISTEN client, search default pool, transaction/forced-user proxy, and mixed session identity. A live web bridge consumes exactly the one reserved LISTEN slot, all publishers remain inside ordinary role pools, repeated peak sampling proves session-advisory lock rows <=672, all other manifested lock/proclock entries <=1,024, total lock entries <=1,696, and backends <=113; a synthetic 1,024-entry transaction reserve still leaves measured capacity above the half-table threshold.

### Approved launch constants

| Contract | Value |
|---|---:|
| Visitor token lifetime | 30 days |
| Public/agent message | 1–4,000 characters |
| Visitor name / widget name / business name | 100 characters |
| Normalized email | 254 characters |
| Greeting / welcome / description | 500 characters |
| Allowed origins | 25 entries, 2,048 characters each |
| Transcript page | 100 messages |
| Provider context | 40 messages and 16,000 total characters |
| Provider output | 1,024 tokens; 4,000 persisted characters |
| Result metadata / sanitized error | 16 KiB serialized / 500 characters |
| Pre-provider lease / provider abort / stale-provider threshold | 60s / 45s / 75s |
| External ambiguity ceiling | 4,200 seconds |
| Dispatch no-new-start / possible-send retire / active-execution reclaim / per-call abort / start headroom | 30s / 90s / 300s / 5s / 10s |
| Global recovery pager / scope population / target slots / sweep batch | one scope selection per minute; 40/environment and 4/tenant; four sweep + one direct; 25 candidate jobs |
| Outstanding processable reply jobs / healthy recovery bounds | 160/environment; 16/tenant; 4/scope; 2/conversation / 45-minute scope target start; 180-minute fourth preexisting job start |
| Provider starts | 60/widget/hour; 300/org+tenant/hour |
| New sessions | 20/widget/hour; 100/org+tenant/hour |
| Visitor messages | 120/widget/hour; 600/org+tenant/hour; 30/conversation/hour; 500/conversation lifetime |

These are approved launch defaults, not placeholders. Changing a security/spend/storage bound requires tests, release notes, and an explicit review; environment variables cannot silently loosen them.

## Migration & Compatibility

1. Build packages because the generator loads entity metadata from `dist`. The mandatory launch target is an isolated clone of the controller-pinned production PostgreSQL image/major/settings—currently the checked-in production family is PostgreSQL 17 with pgvector, and the floating `pgvector/pgvector:pg17-trixie` tag must be replaced by a reviewed image digest before evidence is accepted. The controller deployment receipt records and readiness exact-matches image digest, `server_version_num`, `pgvector`/`pgcrypto` and every installed extension version, database encoding, locale/collation provider/name/version, timezone, `standard_conforming_strings`, transaction/read-committed settings, `max_connections`, `max_locks_per_transaction`, `max_prepared_transactions`, and role/ACL fingerprint. Use only isolated databases named exactly `crm`, `open-mercato`, and `openmercato`; never inherit a Railway or production `DATABASE_URL`. PostgreSQL 16 may remain an additional portability matrix but cannot substitute for the complete PostgreSQL 17 launch matrix.
2. Before adding public-chat entities, run the existing generator through a customers-only resolver for each database basename. `.snapshot-crm.json` currently has 27 unique tables and is missing the two shipped Customer Service tables. `.snapshot-open-mercato.json` and `.snapshot-openmercato.json` each have 16 unique tables and are missing 13 shipped customer tables; the former also contains duplicate snapshot entries. Every emitted table must map exactly to committed migrations `Migration20260409154143`, `Migration20260426003147`, `Migration20260614130000`, `Migration20260614140000`, and the five additive Customer Service migrations.
3. For each reconciliation pass, keep only the generator-owned snapshot correction and remove the newly generated duplicate migration artifact with `apply_patch`; never edit or repurpose its SQL. Repeat generation must say `customers: no changes`, and every reconciled snapshot must contain exactly 29 unique customer tables.
4. Add the cutover-state, global-locator, session, message-order, reply-job, quota-event, receipt-consumption, runtime-receipt-policy, outbound cancellation-acknowledgment, and operation-user-barrier scalar-ID entities plus exactly three additive fields on two existing managed Customer Service tables: `customer_service_knowledge.public_chat_eligible boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`, `customer_service_settings.public_chat_alert_recipient_connection_id uuid NULL` (scalar, no FK), and `customer_service_settings.public_chat_alert_settings_epoch bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` with a nonnegative check. Rebuild packages and generate once against the isolated `crm` database. Retain exactly one narrow additive customers migration containing the ten new tables, their specified indexes, and only those three existing-table alterations plus `.snapshot-crm.json`; it includes locator active/retired checks and indexes, shared prompt and notification-routing epochs, session `outstanding_processable_jobs` bound, reply-job processable population/reservation generation/release time+digest and global covering partial release index, immutable Noli-binding-integrity mismatch tuple/action slot and candidate index, direct-dispatch strict Redis command generation/full checked `varchar(40)` run-ID+`varchar(20)` client-ID+nonce+purpose, database-generated `varchar(22)` binding-challenge nonce+database time, current-result-or-signed-fence chain, Redis-client handoff count/chain/last-leaf, and recovery index, reply-job CS reverse unique indexes, phase/prompt/notification digest-key and epoch proof tuples, quota retention/time/index checks, receipt-ledger two-stage preinstall/journal plus required `event_fanout_registry_seed_digest` and completion `preinstall_guard_fingerprint_digest`, non-runtime `control_reservation_id`/`control_slot_ordinal` checks and unique peer index, environment runtime-death/compaction candidate index and runtime/link typed claims, the runtime-policy `runtime_role | control_plane | redis_client_lineage | control_reservation` discriminator/null matrices; environment/runtime and anchor/receipt/ack rolling windows; immutable hard caps, generation allocator/ancestry, operation/fence/scope/manifest coordinates, at-most-eight ordinal maps, reserved/consumed bitmaps and row/byte charges, 80%-warning, issued-generation, and sparse-compaction-root fields; runtime start/termination Redis slot-count and capability-manifest fields; control-row Redis root-initialized flag, tail/checkpoint sequences+roots, checkpoint-lineage-map/global/capability/runtime-egress/helper/retirement/terminal digests and helper high-water, the exact all-null/all-nonnull eight-field readiness family (`redis_client_readiness_generation`, verification/completion/attestation/manifest digests, canonical server run ID, controller generation, and published-at), keyring generation/digest plus active/retiring `varchar(20)` key-ID/digest and `numeric(29,0)` nonce-high-water triplets; 49 lineage role/slot/kind/ordinal identities, generation high-water, two scalar claim-state families, active claim, terminal accumulator fields; and every exact partial uniqueness/CAS support index, outbound-ack base/final-unsigned pending/signed checks plus required control-reservation/slot join and uniqueness, and operation-user barrier active-authority/source-union indexes and guards. Authenticated bootstrap of a tokenless row creates an immediately expired/revoked null-hash allocator and marker; public access still fails closed. New public sessions always persist a digest/expiry plus a different marker. Code recognizes the marker prefix as non-authenticating state and never compares it as a legacy token.

Query-token support is removed in `0.6.0`; authenticated detail returns the deprecated `visitor_token` key with only `null` in `0.5.x`, then removes the key in `0.6.0`.

No old value is trusted for AI context, contact-page transcript/history access, summary/search/export, lifecycle mutation, or future projection.
